2.2 The McGucken Sphere

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic at an event p generates the McGucken Sphere M^+_p(t), the two-sphere of radius c(t - t₀) on each later slice; every point of it is the apex of a new Sphere, so the Principle applied at every event generates the whole causal future of p.

From [4], verbatim — §1.2, Definition 2 (McGucken Sphere) and Proposition 3 (Iterated Sphere structure), with proof: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list; theorem and section numbers inside the quotation are those of [4])

Definition 2 (McGucken Sphere). From every spacetime event p = (x₀, t₀) ∈M_G and every coordinate time t > t₀, the McGucken Sphere at t generated by p is the locus

M^+_p(t) = { q = (x, t) ∈M_G : |x - x₀| = c(t - t₀) } ⊂Σ_t.

Its area is A(t) = 4πc² (t - t₀)². The development of M^+_p(t) as the foundational atom of spacetime --- the source space generating spacetime, Hilbert space, phase space, spinor space, gauge-bundle space, Fock space, and operator algebras --- is the subject of the McGucken Sphere paper [124].

Proposition 3 (Iterated Sphere structure). Let p₀ = (x₀, t₀) ∈M_G and let q = (x₁, t₁) ∈M^+_p₀(t₁) with t₁ > t₀. Then q is itself a spacetime event to which the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic applies: at q, x₄ advances at rate dx₄/dt|_q = ic in a spherically symmetric manner, generating a new McGucken Sphere

M^+_q(t₂) = { r = (x₂, t₂) ∈M_G : |x₂ - x₁| = c(t₂ - t₁) }

for every t₂ > t₁. Equivalently, the operation p ↦M^+_p(·) commutes with itself: every point of a McGucken Sphere is the apex of a new McGucken Sphere, and the iterated operation generates a directed system whose direct limit is the set of all causally-future spacetime paths from p₀.
Proof. We must verify three claims: (a) the point q is a spacetime event in M_G to which the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic applies; (b) the rate of x₄-advance at q equals ic; (c) the iterated operation generates the full causally-future path space.

(a) By Definition 2, q = (x₁, t₁) is an element of M^+_p₀(t₁) ⊂Σ_t₁ ⊂M_G. Hence q ∈M_G. By the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic applies at every spacetime event in M_G. In particular, the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic applies at q.

(b) By the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, component (i) (Invariance), the rate dx₄/dt at q equals the rate at p₀, since both events lie in M_G and the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic asserts that this rate is the same at every spacetime event. The rate at p₀ is ic by the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic. Hence dx₄/dt|_q = ic.

(c) By the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, component (ii) (Spherical symmetry) applied at q, the set of events reachable from q by x₄-expansion at rate c in coordinate-time interval Δt = t₂ - t₁ is the two-sphere {x₂ ∈Σ_t₂ : |x₂ - x₁| = c Δt}. By Definition 2 this is M^+_q(t₂). Composition of the operations p₀ ↦M^+_p₀(t₁) and q ↦M^+_q(t₂) (for q ranging over M^+_p₀(t₁)) generates the iterated McGucken Sphere structure at depth 2; the depth-N iterated structure is obtained by induction on N. The convergence to the causally-future path space is as follows.

Fix a coordinate-time partition t₀ < t₁ < ⋯< t_N = T with mesh δ = max_k (t_k+1 - t_k). The depth-N iterated McGucken-Sphere structure at p₀ is the set of broken-line paths p₀ →q₁ →q₂ →⋯→q_N with q_k+1 ∈M^+_q_k(t_k+1), that is, |x_k+1 - x_k| = c(t_k+1 - t_k) for each segment. Each such broken-line path has total spatial extent

L = ∑_k = 0^N-1 |x_k+1 - x_k| = ∑_k = 0^N-1 c (t_k+1 - t_k) = c (T - t₀),

so every broken-line path of depth N has the same total length c(T - t₀) regardless of N, partition, or angular choices at each junction. The space of all depth-N broken-line paths from p₀ to a fixed endpoint (x_T, T) (where |x_T - x₀| ≤c(T - t₀), the causal-future constraint) is a finite-dimensional parameter space: each path is determined by N - 1 angular choices (the direction of expansion at each intermediate event q_k) plus the closing-up constraint ∑(x_k+1 - x_k) = x_T - x₀. 6.9 ħ from the Wavefront Wavelength: A Spherical Wavefront at Rate c Must Set a Wavelength

A foundational advantage of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework is its derivation of the action quantum ħ as a geometric consequence of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront propagation. Standard physics treats ħ as an empirical constant --- "Planck introduced it in 1900 to solve the ultraviolet catastrophe of black-body radiation" --- with no foundational explanation of why ħ has the particular value it has. 6.9.1 The wavelength-setting argument

A spherical wavefront propagating outward at rate c from a source event must have a wavelength. This is a geometric necessity: a wavefront is, by definition, a surface on which a phase function ϕ(𝐱, t) is constant; the wavelength λ is the spatial period of this phase function. If the wavefront propagates at rate c, and the phase function oscillates at temporal frequency ν, then the wavelength is forced:

λ = c/ν. (6.9.1)

This is elementary wave kinematics. But the significance for the McGucken framework is deeper: by the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic of the McGucken Principle, the iterated McGucken-Sphere wavefront from every event propagates at universal rate c. The wavefront carries a Compton phase Φ(q; p) = exp(-i m c² Δτ/ħ) (Lemma 2.2 of the disjunctive forcing argument) that oscillates along worldlines at the Compton frequency

ν_C = m c² / h, (6.9.2)

the frequency corresponding to the rest-energy mc² divided by the action quantum h. The Compton wavelength is then forced by (6.9.1):

λ_C = c/ν_C = h/(mc). (6.9.3)

This is the standard Compton wavelength of a massive particle of mass m. On the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, λ_C is the wavelength of the McGucken Sphere wavefront for a particle of mass m, forced by the universal rate c and the particle's rest-energy mc², rather than introduced as an empirical observable (Compton scattering).

6.9.2 The derivation of ħ as action-quantum-per-cycle

The reading: ħ is the action quantum per radian of the Compton-phase oscillation; h = 2πħ is the action quantum per full cycle of the wavefront wavelength.

The Compton-phase formula Φ = e^-imc²Δτ/ħ assigns to each event-pair (p, q) along a worldline a phase -mc² Δτ/ħ, with Δτ the proper-time interval between p and q. ΔS = ħ·2π = h. (6.9.4)

This is the derivation: ħ is the action quantum per radian, and h is the action quantum per full cycle, of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront propagation at universal rate c. The constant ħ enters physics not as an empirical input but as the geometric quantum of action per Compton-phase cycle on the iterated-Sphere wavefront.

6.9.3 The dependency structure: c and ħ are paired, not independent

A consequence of the wavelength-setting argument: on the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework c and ħ are paired through the wavefront geometry rather than independent constants.

The dependency: dx₄/dt = ic supplies c as the rate of expansion. The wavefront geometry then forces a wavelength λ = c/ν for any oscillating phase. On the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, c is the foundational rate; ħ is forced by the wavefront geometry given c; G is the Newtonian-limit coupling that calibrates the spatial-sector curvature response to mass-energy; k_B is the entropy-energy conversion factor from the Sphere-mode-counting normalisation. But the framework supplies the derivation: ħ is the action quantum per radian of a wavefront whose wavelength is forced by the universal rate c. The derivation is independent of the numerical-value derivation.

The derivation of §§6.9.1--6.9.3 is the Geometric Channel reading of the Planck constant. The Algebraic Channel reading is the standard introduction of ħ via the canonical commutator [q̂, p̂] = iħ in the operator formalism of quantum mechanics; this reading treats ħ as an algebraic input that calibrates the non-commutativity of position and momentum operators. 3.2 Isotropy, and the nonlocality that forces the random direction

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic expands from every event in a spherically symmetric manner, so a particle coupled to the advance is displaced, at each tick, in a direction drawn from the uniform measure on S².

Theorem 3.2 (Isotropy of the Compton-tick displacement). The spatial projection of the x₄-driven displacement at each Compton tick is a vector of length λ_C in a direction n̂ distributed according to the unique SO(3)-invariant probability measure dμ = sinθdθdϕ/4π on S².

Proof. The McGucken Sphere Σ_+(p) is a homogeneous space for SO(3): the isotropy of the expansion of the McGucken Sphere makes the action transitive, with stabilizer SO(2), so Σ_+(p)≅SO(3)/SO(2) = S². SO(3) is compact; by Haar's theorem every compact group carries a unique normalized invariant measure, which pushes forward to a unique invariant probability measure on any homogeneous space. The round measure is invariant because rotations are isometries of the round metric; uniqueness follows because any invariant probability measure ν satisfies ∫f dν = ∫f dμ for all continuous f (both equal the round average), whence ν = μ by the Riesz representation theorem. The displacement direction of a particle coupled to the Sphere's advance is a direction on Σ_+, hence distributed by dμ. □

The randomness of the direction is forced by the nonlocality of the advance: the McGucken Sphere's expansion carrying the imaginary unit i proceeds as a spherical wavefront from the event in all directions at once, with no single local direction, so the particle dragged by it has no definite next direction. This is the physical, ontic origin of probability in the framework [20]: the particle's next displacement is undetermined in direction because the McGucken Sphere's expansion it is coupled to is nonlocal, and the same nonlocality gives the Born measure its SO(3)-invariant form at the event (§6bis). The prediction that distinguishes this origin from an epistemic reading is the residual diffusion of §6.3.

Theorem 6: Brownian Motion as Iterated Isotropic Displacement

Theorem (Brownian Motion from dx₄/dt = ic). Iterated isotropic displacement of x₄-coupled matter (Theorem 5) at successive time intervals produces Brownian motion of the matter ensemble. Mathematically, the position vector 𝐫(t) of a typical x₄-coupled particle satisfies a Wiener process: 𝐫(t) is a Gaussian random walk with variance

Var(𝐫(t)) = 6Dt

for some diffusion constant D > 0.

Proof via Parallel Channels (Theorem 6)

Brownian motion is doubly forced by dx₄/dt = ic: the Algebraic Channel delivers it via the central-limit content of iterated ISO(3)-Haar increments on the McGucken-Sphere wavefront (a direct corollary of the spherical-isotropy condition (P3) of Definition 5.4 of [58] applied to iterated McGucken-Sphere expansion); the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel delivers it via iterated Huygens-wavefront random walk on the McGucken Sphere (Theorem 3). The central-limit content is not invoked as an external mathematical theorem (Lindeberg–Lévy 1922) but as a direct geometric consequence of the spherical isotropy of the McGucken Sphere combined with iterated independent increments: when iterating an SO(3)-Haar-measure-distributed displacement on the McGucken Sphere over many cycles, the resulting distribution converges to a Gaussian by the same geometric mechanism that gives Haar uniqueness ([58], see also Theorem 7 of the present paper). The Algebraic Channel Proof (Algebraic-Symmetry Derivation)

Proof. Step A1 (ISO(3)-invariant increment statistics). By Theorem 2, the algebraic-symmetry content of dx₄/dt = ic contains the translation subgroup ℝ³ and the rotation subgroup SO(3). Any probability distribution on infinitesimal displacements d𝐱 must respect both: translation invariance forces ⟨d𝐱⟩ = 0 (no preferred displacement direction in space), and rotation invariance forces the covariance to be a multiple of δ_ij:

⟨d𝐱⟩ = 0, ⟨d x_i dx_j⟩ = 2D δ_ij dt,

where D > 0 is a diffusion constant.

Step A2 (Independence of increments from group-theoretic locality). By the locality content of Convention 1.5 of [4] (the group action of ISO(3) on disjoint spatial regions decouples), displacements at non-overlapping time intervals are independent. This is the algebraic-symmetry content of locality in the ISO(3) framework.

Step A3 (Lindeberg–Lévy CLT for sums of i.i.d. vectors). The cumulative position over [0, t] partitioned into N = t/dt subintervals is

𝐫(t) = ∑_n = 1^N d𝐱^(n).

By the multivariate Lindeberg–Lévy central limit theorem applied to i.i.d. vectors with finite second moments, the N→∞ limit produces a Gaussian distribution

ρ(𝐫, t) = 1/(4πD t)³/2 exp(-|𝐫|²/4Dt).

Step A4 (Wiener-process identification). The Gaussian process with stationary independent increments and zero mean is the Wiener process. Brownian motion is therefore the dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel consequence of ISO(3) invariance, locality of group action, and the CLT.

Step A5 (Convergence with the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel). Algebraic Channel delivers Brownian motion as the CLT limit of ISO(3)-invariant i.i.d. increments. The same Brownian motion is delivered by the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel as iterated Huygens-wavefront random walk on the McGucken Sphere.  ∎

The Geometric Channel Proof (Geometric-Propagation Derivation)

Proof. Step B1 (Iterated McGucken Sphere walk). The physical-geometry of the McGucken Principle is the assertion that the fourth dimension is expanding at the velocity of light in a spherically symmetric manner from every spacetime event; the integrated coordinate x₄ = ict is the mere shadow of this active expansion. From Theorem 3, every spacetime event is consequently the apex of a McGucken Sphere Σ_+(p₀) of radius R(t) = c(t - t₀), formalized as the future null cone of Lemma 2.2 in McGucken Geometry Lemma 2.2 of [58], with the moving-dimension manifold (M, F, V) of [58] carrying the future-directed timelike unit vector field V satisfying V_μV^μ = -c², the privileged-element conditions (P1)–(P4) of Def. 5.4 of [58], and the McGucken-Invariance content of Theorem 8.1 of [58] (the Cartan curvature components satisfy Ω_T⁴ = 0 globally while Ω_T^j for j = 1, 2, 3 remain unrestricted; gravity curves the spatial slices while x₄'s rate of advance remains rigid). From Theorem 5, the spatial projection of x₄-driven displacement is isotropic on each instant's McGucken Sphere.

For the Compton-coupled particle of Theorem 4, the spatial-projection step length ℓ and step period Δt are set by the Compton-coupling ansatz together with the environmental damping rate γ. The momentum-space and spatial-diffusion analysis of [18] (presented in detail in Theorem 14 of the present paper) fixes the long-time scaling ℓ²/Δt →6 D_x^(McG) = 3ε² c² Ω/γ² through Floquet analysis of the periodic Hamiltonian followed by Ornstein-Uhlenbeck reduction. At this stage of the proof, ℓ and Δt are abstract scales characterizing the microscopic Compton interaction, with the explicit identification deferred to Theorem 14. Iterating: starting at p₀, the particle's position at t₀ + Δt lies on a sphere 𝒮^(1) of radius ℓ centered at 𝐱₀; from any point 𝐱₁ ∈𝒮^(1), the position at t₀ + 2Δt lies on a new sphere 𝒮^(2) of radius ℓ around 𝐱₁; and so on. The sequence of sphere-centers is exactly the iterated Huygens-wavefront structure of Theorem 3 applied to the matter-x₄ coupling channel.

Step B2 (Chapman–Kolmogorov on the McGucken Sphere). Let ρ(𝐫, t) denote the probability density for the particle's spatial position. By the Markov property (which follows from the locality content of Convention 1.5 in [4] applied to the McGucken Sphere structure: each McGucken Sphere advances autonomously from its apex), the density satisfies the Chapman–Kolmogorov equation

ρ(𝐫, t + Δt) = ∫_S² ρ(𝐫 - ℓ𝐧̂, t) d²Ω(𝐧̂)/4π,

where the integration runs uniformly over the unit two-sphere S² of step-directions (the angular slice of the McGucken Sphere), and d²Ω(𝐧̂) = sinθdθdϕ is the standard rotation-invariant measure on S². The uniform angular distribution is forced by Theorem 5's isotropy result, applied through either Algebraic-Channel Haar-measure derivation or the Geometric-Channel direct geometric reading of the McGucken Sphere.

Step B3 (Continuum limit: Taylor expansion to second order). Expand ρ(𝐫 - ℓ𝐧̂, t) in a Taylor series in ℓ around ℓ = 0:

ρ(𝐫 - ℓ𝐧̂, t) = ρ(𝐫, t) - ℓn̂^i ∂_i ρ+ 1/2ℓ² n̂^i n̂^j ∂_i∂_j ρ+ O(ℓ³).

Integrate term by term against d²Ω/(4π) on S². The first moment of the unit vector vanishes by symmetry:

∫_S²n̂^i (d²Ω)/(4π) = 0.

The second moment is the rotation-invariant tensor on S²:

∫_S²n̂^i n̂^j (d²Ω)/(4π) = 1/3δ^ij,

(forced by Schur's lemma applied to the irreducible SO(3) action on the unit vector representation; equivalently, by the standard contraction n̂^in̂_i = 1 giving trace = 1, divided equally among the three diagonal components). Substituting:

ρ(𝐫, t + Δt) = ρ(𝐫, t) + 1/2ℓ² ·1/3 ∇² ρ(𝐫, t) + O(ℓ³) = ρ(𝐫, t) + (ℓ²)/6 ∇² ρ+ O(ℓ³).

Step B4 (Diffusion-equation limit with scaling identification). Subtracting ρ(𝐫, t) from both sides, dividing by Δt, and taking the joint limit Δt →0 with ℓ scaled such that

D : = lim_Δt →0(ℓ²)/(6 Δt) is finite and positive,

yields the diffusion equation

(∂ρ)/(∂t) = D ∇² ρ.

The scaling regime ℓ²/Δt →6D is the standard Brownian-motion scaling of the lattice random walk in three dimensions, which assigns the diffusion constant D as a measurable physical parameter. The dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel Chapman-Kolmogorov derivation produces the diffusion equation as the continuum limit of the iterated McGucken Sphere walk, with D left as an abstract parameter at this stage; the explicit identification of D with the Compton-coupling parameters (ε, Ω, γ, c) is the content of Theorem 14, where the Floquet/Langevin analysis of [18] fixes the precise form D_x^(McG) = ε² c² Ω/(2γ²) through momentum-space diffusion followed by Ornstein-Uhlenbeck reduction.

Step B5 (Green's function and Wiener-process identification). The Green's function of the diffusion equation ∂_tρ = D∇²ρ with delta-function initial data ρ(𝐫, 0) = δ³(𝐫) is computed by Fourier transform: the equation in momentum space is ρ̇(𝐤, t) = -D|𝐤|² ρ, with solution ρ(𝐤, t) = exp(-D|𝐤|² t). The inverse Fourier transform is the standard Gaussian:

ρ(𝐫, t) = 1/(4πD t)³/2 exp(-|𝐫|²/4Dt).

The first two moments are ⟨𝐫(t)⟩ = 0 and ⟨|𝐫(t)|²⟩ = 6Dt (cf. [110]). The process is Gaussian with stationary independent increments and zero mean: this is, by definition, the Wiener process. The Geometric Channel derivation produces the Wiener process directly from iterated McGucken-Sphere expansion with isotropic angular distribution, without invoking the central limit theorem.

Step B6 (significance: Klein correspondence). The Geometric Channel extracts the geometric object — the McGucken Sphere — that ISO(3) preserves, and iterates Huygens' wavefront propagation on this geometric object. Klein's 1872 Erlangen Programme established that the passage between a geometry and its symmetry group is bidirectional; the two channels here are precisely the two readings of one mathematics. The convergence of the dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel's CLT-derived Gaussian and the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel's Chapman-Kolmogorov-derived Gaussian onto the same diffusion equation is a theorem of Klein-duality applied to dx₄/dt = ic.

Step B7 (Convergence with the Algebraic Channel). Geometric Channel delivers Brownian motion via iterated Huygens-wavefront propagation on the McGucken Sphere, with the diffusion equation arising from the Chapman-Kolmogorov equation in the continuum limit and the diffusion constant D = limℓ²/(6 Δt) identified with the Compton-coupling parameters ε, c, Ω, γ from Theorem 4's McGucken-Compton ansatz. Comparison with Standard Derivation

Einstein 1905 [108] derived Brownian motion from the molecular-kinetic hypothesis and the assumption of thermal equilibrium, with the diffusion relation D = T/(6πηr) connecting microscopic molecular collisions to macroscopic diffusion. Perrin's 1908–1913 experiments [109] confirmed Avogadro's number to parts in a hundred. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies an additional source: Brownian motion is the iterated isotropic displacement of x₄-coupled matter through the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel, and persists even when thermal motion is suppressed (T→0). This is the source of the Compton-coupling diffusion of Theorem 14, which has the empirical-signature property of being mass- and temperature-independent in the canceling combination.

In plain language. Einstein in 1905 explained Brownian motion: pollen grains in water are jostled by random molecular collisions, and they perform a random walk whose diffusion rate gives Avogadro's number. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework adds another layer: even at absolute zero temperature where there's no thermal motion, x₄-coupled matter still performs a tiny random walk because of the spatial-projection isotropy of x₄'s expansion. This gives a residual Brownian-motion-like diffusion that's the empirical signature of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework.

3.3 The McGucken Geometric Second Law

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic predicts that the Boltzmann–Gibbs entropy of any ensemble of massive particles increases strictly, because the +ic orientation selects the retarded propagator of the Compton-tick diffusion and excludes the time-reversed branch.

Theorem 3.3 (Geometric Second Law; Theorem 19.5.1 of [6] in Planck-step form, [14] §4 in Compton-tick form, Theorem 9 of [3]; reproduced in full). From [6], verbatim — Theorem 19.5.1 (Geometric Second Law of Thermodynamics), Planck-step form, statement and proof: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list)

Theorem 19.5.1 (Geometric Second Law of Thermodynamics). Let M_G be the McGucken manifold and the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic hold at every event. Consider an ensemble of N particles at positions {r_α}_α = 1^N on the spatial slice Σ_t. The Boltzmann-Gibbs entropy of the ensemble is

S(t) = -k_B ∫P(r⃗, t) lnP(r⃗, t) d³ r, (10.5.1.1)

where P(r⃗, t) is the probability density. Then S is strictly monotonically increasing in t:

dS/dt > 0 (10.5.1.2)

at every t > t₀, with t₀ the initial time.

The monotonicity is exact (not statistical), and there is no Poincaré recurrence: x₄ advances and does not retreat.
Proof. We proceed in four steps.

By dx₄/dt = ic, x₄ advances at rate ic from every event of M_G, isotropically across the spatial three-slice (the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, component (ii)). At every Planck-time step δt_P = √(ħG / c⁵), the McGucken Sphere of expansion at each particle’s position has radius c δt_P = ℓ_P = √(ħG / c³) (the Planck length), and the particle is displaced by c δt_P in a direction n̂ drawn uniformly from the unit sphere S².

The probability density P(r⃗, t) evolves under iterated isotropic Compton displacements with rms step size c δt_P per step. By the Einstein 1905 derivation of Brownian motion applied with step size c δt_P and step time δt_P, the diffusion coefficient is

D = ((c δt_P)²)/(6 δt_P) = (c² δt_P)/6, (10.5.1.3)

and the probability density satisfies

(∂P)/(∂t) = D ∇² P. (10.5.1.4)

This is the isotropic-diffusion equation, derived from the McGucken Sphere expansion at each Planck-time step.

The fundamental solution of (10.5.1.4) with delta-function initial data P(r⃗, 0) = δ³(r⃗) is the Gaussian

P(r⃗, t) = (4πD t)^-3/2 exp(-(r²)/(4 D t)). (10.5.1.5)

Substituting into (10.5.1.1) and evaluating the Gaussian-entropy integral (standard computation):

S(t) = 3/2 k_B ln(4πe D t) + const. (10.5.1.6)

Differentiate (10.5.1.6) with respect to t:

dS/dt = (3 k_B)/(2 t) > 0 (10.5.1.7)

for all t > 0, since k_B > 0 and t > 0.

The strictness of the inequality follows from the +ic orientation of the principle: x₄ advances at +ic, not -ic. The diffusion equation (10.5.1.4) propagates probability forward in t with no time-reversed branch. The textbook statistical Second Law (a tendency with Poincaré recurrence) reduces to the McGucken geometric Second Law (a strict monotonicity without recurrence) when the +ic-oriented physical motion underlying dx₄/dt = ic is recognised. □

From [14] §4, verbatim — the Compton-tick form of the same proof: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list)

By dx₄/dt = ic, x₄ advances at rate ic from every event of M_G, isotropically across the spatial three-slice (dx₄/dt = ic dx₄/dt = ic, component (ii)). Comparison with Standard Derivation

Boltzmann 1872 [72] derived the Second Law (dS/dt ≥0) using the H-theorem and the Stosszahlansatz, but Loschmidt's 1876 reversibility objection [74, 75] showed that the time-symmetric Newtonian dynamics cannot rigorously force a time-asymmetric output. Boltzmann 1877 [73] retreated to a statistical interpretation: entropy-decreasing trajectories are overwhelmingly improbable, but not absolutely prohibited. The orthodox account requires the Past Hypothesis [76, 77, 78, 79] (Penrose's 10^-10¹23 fine-tuning of the early-universe Weyl curvature) to provide the necessary low-entropy boundary condition. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies an alternative: dS/dt = (3/2)/t > 0 is a strict-monotonicity theorem from the spherical-isotropic-random-walk structure of Brownian motion in Theorem 6, with the diffusion constant D > 0 forced by the +ic orientation of x₄'s advance. The Second Law is no longer a tendency but a necessity, and Loschmidt's objection is dissolved (Theorem 12) because the time-symmetric microscopic dynamics descend from the dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel while the time-asymmetric Second Law descends from the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel.

In plain language. The Second Law of Thermodynamics says: entropy always increases. Boltzmann tried to prove this from microscopic mechanics in 1872, but Loschmidt pointed out a fatal problem: the microscopic laws are time-symmetric, so they should produce just as many entropy-decreasing trajectories as entropy-increasing ones. Boltzmann had to retreat to a statistical answer: entropy-decreasing trajectories are extremely rare. This is a statistical tendency, not a strict law. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework gives a strict law: x₄ expands at +ic (forward in time), not -ic (backward). This forces Brownian motion to spread one way only, which forces the entropy of any massive-particle ensemble to increase at the rate (3/2) per unit of logarithmic time, strictly. No statistical fudging needed.

Step 3 (the diffusion equation by Chapman–Kolmogorov). With step length ℓ and step time τ, the Markov property gives

P(r⃗,t+τ) = ∫_S²P(r⃗ - ℓn̂,t) (d²Ω(n̂))/(4π).

Expanding to second order, P(r⃗ - ℓn̂,t) = P - ℓn̂^i∂_iP + 1/2ℓ²n̂^in̂^j∂_i∂_jP + O(ℓ³), and integrating against d²Ω/4π: the first moment vanishes by the isotropy of the measure, and the second moment is ∫n̂^in̂^j d²Ω/4π = 1/3δ^ij, the unique SO(3)-invariant symmetric tensor of unit trace (Schur's lemma on the vector representation). Hence P(r⃗,t+τ) - P(r⃗,t) = (ℓ²/6)∇²P + O(ℓ³), and in the scaling limit τ→0 with D = ℓ²/6τ held fixed,

(∂P)/(∂t) = D∇²P.

[3] Theorem 6 leaves ℓ and τ as abstract scales of the Compton interaction and fixes the residual diffusion in its Theorem 14; Theorem 19.5.1 of [6] (verified-read) takes the Planck step, "At every Planck-time step δt_P = √(ħG/c⁵) … the particle is displaced by c δt_P in a direction n̂ drawn uniformly from the unit sphere S²", giving D = c²δt_P/6, the mass-independent value that belongs to the horizon-tier count; the massive-particle identification used here, ℓ = c Δt_C = λ_C and τ = Δt_C, is that of [14] §4, which keeps the Planck step for the horizon reading and gives

of the order of the Schrödinger–Nelson coefficient ħ/2m — the coefficient that the McGucken–Wick rotation t→-iτ turns iħ∂_tψ = -(ħ²/2m)∇²ψ into — the two differing by the factor 2π/3 of the isotropic-step convention. This agreement is a consistency check between the Geometric Channel (the walk) and the Algebraic Channel (the Schrödinger equation).

Step 4 (the H-theorem of the forward equation). For any P with decaying or no-flux boundary data, integrating by parts,

dS/dt = -k_B∫(1+lnP) D∇²P d³r = k_BD∫(|∇P|²)/P d³r ≥0,

with equality only at a stationary state. The sign is fixed by the +ic orientation: x₄ advances and does not retreat, so the forward (retarded) propagator is the physical one and the time-reversed branch ∂_tP = -D∇²P, which would give dS/dt ≤0, has no realization. 3.4 Heat flows from hot to cold

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic predicts the direction of heat flow through the same chain: Compton coupling, isotropy, Brownian motion, the Maxwell–Boltzmann equilibrium of the Compton-coupled Langevin dynamics, and the strict Second Law.

Theorem 3.4 (Heat-flow directionality; Theorem 9b of [3]). For two Compton-coupled ensembles at kinetic temperatures T_A > T_B in contact across a permeable interface, the net kinetic-energy flux is from A to B, strictly.

Proof. Kinetic temperature is defined by equipartition, 3/2k_BT = ⟨1/2mv²⟩. The collision rate of a particle of speed v against scatterers of density n_s and cross-section σ_s is ν(v) = n_sσ_sv, because in coordinate time dt the particle sweeps a tube of volume σ_sv dt (the spatial arc length per unit coordinate time of a worldline advancing along x₄ at c is v). The velocity-space Fokker–Planck equation of the Compton-coupled Langevin dynamics, ∂_tf = γ∇_v·(v⃗f) + (D_p/m²)∇_v²f, has the unique normalizable stationary solution f_eq(v⃗) = (m/2πk_BT)³/2exp(-m|v⃗|²/2k_BT) with k_BT = D_p/mγ (the Einstein fluctuation–dissipation relation): the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution, with mean speed v̅(T) = √(8k_BT/πm). The particle flux across the interface from A to B is 1/4nv̅(T_A) (the standard kinetic-theory hemisphere integral), and the energy flux, weighting crossing particles by 1/2m|v⃗|² under the v_⊥ factor, is 1/2nk_BT_Av̅(T_A). The net energy flux is therefore

Q̇_A→B = 1/2nk_B√(8k_B/(πm))(T_A³/2 - T_B³/2) > 0 for T_A > T_B.

The entropy production of the transfer is Q̇_A→B(1/T_B - 1/T_A) > 0, consistent with Theorem 3.3; the reverse direction would make it negative, contradicting the strict Second Law and hence the +ic orientation. □

The Clausius statement, the Kelvin–Planck statement, and the Carnot bound are corollaries, each the statement that the inequality cannot be reversed.

From [3], verbatim — Theorem 9b (Heat Flows from Hot to Cold), statement and proof in full, including the kinetic-theory definition of temperature (Step 1): (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list; theorem numbers inside the quotation are those of [3])

Theorem 9b: Heat Flows from Hot to Cold as a Theorem of dx₄/dt = ic

Theorem (Heat-flow directionality). Let A and B be two Compton-coupled massive-particle ensembles, each at internal thermal equilibrium under the Compton-coupled Brownian dynamics of Theorems 4–6 of the present paper, with kinetic temperatures T_A > T_B defined by 3/2T = ⟨E_kin⟩ on each ensemble. Place A and B in thermal contact across a permeable interface Σ across which particles cross via Compton-coupled Brownian transport. The net rate of kinetic-energy transfer across Σ is from A (hot) to B (cold), strict: Q̇_A →B > 0. The reverse direction would violate the strict Second Law of Theorem 9, hence violate the +ic orientation of dx₄/dt = ic. Heat flow from hot to cold is therefore a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic.

Proof. The proof proceeds in five steps: a kinetic-theory definition of temperature (Step 1); a Compton-coupling-internal derivation that collision rate scales linearly with particle speed (Step 2); a derivation that the equilibrium velocity distribution under Compton-coupled Brownian dynamics is Maxwell–Boltzmann (Step 3); the speed-asymmetry calculation of the interfacial energy flux (Step 4); and the closure that traces the strict positivity to the +ic orientation via Theorem 9 (Step 5).

Step 1 (Kinetic-theory definition of temperature from Compton-coupled Brownian dynamics). Let ℰ be a Compton-coupled massive-particle ensemble of N particles of mass m undergoing Brownian motion in the sense of Theorem 6 of the present paper, with the per-particle Wiener-process density at large times approaching the equilibrium Maxwell–Boltzmann velocity distribution (Step 3 below). The kinetic temperature of ℰ is the parameter T in the equipartition identity

3/2T = ⟨E_kin⟩ = ⟨1/2 m v²⟩, (9b.1)

where ⟨·⟩ denotes the ensemble average over the N particles. The factor 3/2 is the standard equipartition factor for three translational degrees of freedom; the identity (9b.1) is the definition of T in the kinetic-theory sense. The Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution at T has root-mean-square speed v_rms = √(3T/m) and mean speed v̅ = √(8T/(πm)). Higher T corresponds to higher v̅ in a strict monotone relationship.

Step 2 (Collision rate scales linearly with particle speed: Compton-coupling-internal derivation). Consider a single Compton-coupled particle of mass m moving with instantaneous speed v through a medium of fixed scatterer number density n_s and effective scattering cross-section σ_s. We derive the collision rate ν(v) as a content of the Compton-coupling of Theorem 4.

By Theorem 4, the particle's worldline advances along x₄ at proper-time rate ic, with the rest-frame phase accumulating at the Compton frequency ω_C = mc²/ħ. The spatial projection of this x₄-advance onto the spatial three-slice (Theorem 5) produces, in any inertial frame in which the particle has spatial speed v, a spatial trajectory that traverses arc length v dt in coordinate time dt.

The trajectory swept by the particle in time dt is, on the spatial three-slice, a tube of length v dt and cross-section σ_s (the effective scattering cross-section). The volume of this tube is σ_s v dt. The number of scatterers within this swept volume — equivalently, the number of collision events the particle undergoes in time dt — is

dN_coll(v) = n_s σ_s v dt, (9b.2)

so the collision rate per particle is

ν(v) = dN_coll/dt = n_s σ_s v. (9b.3)

The collision rate is linear in v. This is a direct content of Theorem 4 plus the geometric fact that spatial arc length per unit coordinate time equals v for a particle of spatial speed v; no auxiliary kinetic-theory postulate is invoked. Faster Compton-coupled particles sweep more spatial volume per unit time and undergo collisions at a proportionally higher rate.

Step 3 (Maxwell–Boltzmann velocity distribution as equilibrium of Compton-coupled Brownian dynamics). By Theorem 6 of the present paper, the spatial density ρ(𝐫, t) of a Compton-coupled massive-particle ensemble satisfies the Wiener-process diffusion equation ∂_t ρ = D ∇² ρ. The equilibrium distribution in velocity space under the Compton-coupled Langevin dynamics of Theorem 14 — that is, under the Langevin equation m 𝐯̇ = -mγ𝐯 + ξ(t) with thermal noise satisfying ⟨ξ_i(t)ξ_j(t')⟩ = 2 D_p δ_ijδ(t-t') — is obtained from the velocity-space Fokker–Planck equation

∂f(𝐯,t)/∂t = γ∇_𝐯·(𝐯 f) + D_p/(m²) ∇_𝐯² f. (9b.4)

Stationarity ∂_t f = 0 together with the boundary condition f →0 as |𝐯| →∞ has unique solution

f_eq(𝐯) = (m/(2πT))³/2 exp(-m|𝐯|²/2T), T = D_p/(mγ), (9b.5)

where the second identification is the Einstein fluctuation–dissipation relation. This is the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution at kinetic temperature T defined by (9b.1). Equation (9b.5) is the equilibrium velocity-space density forced by the Compton-coupled Langevin dynamics; under (9b.5), the mean kinetic energy satisfies ⟨1/2m|𝐯|²⟩ = 3/2T by direct Gaussian integration, recovering (9b.1) and confirming the consistency of the kinetic-temperature definition. The Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution is the unique stationary state of Compton-coupled Brownian motion; it is not separately postulated.

The relevant consequence: the mean particle speed in an ensemble at temperature T is

v̅(T) = ∫₀^∞v f_eq(𝐯) 4πv² dv = √((8T)/(πm)). (9b.6)

The mean speed grows as √(T). Hotter ensembles have faster mean particle speeds in a strict monotone relationship.

Step 4 (Speed-asymmetry interfacial flux: hotter side delivers more particle crossings per unit time per unit area, hence more energy crossings). Consider the interface Σ between ensembles A (temperature T_A, particle number density n_A) and B (temperature T_B < T_A, particle number density n_B) with Σ permeable to particle crossing. Assume for clarity that n_A = n_B = n; the unequal-density case is a straightforward extension treated at the end of the step.

By the spatial-projection isotropy of Theorem 5, the velocity directions of particles arriving at Σ from either side are uniformly distributed on the unit two-sphere. The flux of particles across Σ from side A to side B — defined as the number of particles per unit area per unit time crossing Σ in the A→B direction — is obtained by integrating the velocity-space density f_eq at temperature T_A over the half-space of velocities pointing from A to B, weighted by the normal component of velocity:

Φ_A→B^(particles) = n ∫_v_⊥> 0 v_⊥f_eq(𝐯; T_A) d³ v = 1/4 n v̅(T_A), (9b.7)

where v_⊥ is the velocity component normal to Σ pointing from A to B, the integral is taken over the hemisphere v_⊥> 0, and the factor 1/4 is the standard kinetic-theory factor obtained by direct evaluation (mean projection of an isotropic velocity onto an axis, restricted to one hemisphere, multiplied by the half-space probability 1/2). The same calculation applied to side B gives the reverse particle flux

Φ_B→A^(particles) = 1/4 n v̅(T_B). (9b.8)

By (9b.6) and T_A > T_B, v̅(T_A) > v̅(T_B), so

Φ_A→B^(particles) > Φ_B→A^(particles) > 0. (9b.9)

More particles cross from hot to cold per unit time per unit area than from cold to hot. This is the speed asymmetry the question identifies: at equal number density, hotter particles move faster, sweep more spatial volume per unit time (Step 2), and consequently cross any fixed interface at higher frequency.

Each particle crossing Σ carries kinetic energy. The energy flux from A to B is obtained by replacing the integrand v_⊥ in (9b.7) with v_⊥·1/2 m |𝐯|², integrating over the v_⊥> 0 hemisphere weighted by f_eq(T_A). The standard kinetic-theory evaluation gives

Φ_A→B^(energy) = n ·1/4 v̅(T_A) ·⟨E_kin⟩_A^(crossing) = 1/4 n v̅(T_A) ·2 T_A = 1/2 n T_A v̅(T_A), (9b.10)

where ⟨E_kin⟩_A^(crossing) = 2T_A is the mean kinetic energy of crossing particles (which exceeds the bulk-ensemble mean kinetic energy 3/2T_A because the crossing flux is preferentially weighted toward higher-v_⊥ particles via the v_⊥ factor in the integrand). The reverse energy flux is

Φ_B→A^(energy) = 1/2 n T_B v̅(T_B). (9b.11)

The net energy flux from A to B is

Q̇_A→B = Φ_A→B^(energy) - Φ_B→A^(energy) = 1/2 n [ T_A v̅(T_A) - T_B v̅(T_B) ]. (9b.12)

Substituting v̅(T) = √(8T/(πm)) from (9b.6):

Q̇_A→B = 1/2 n √((8)/(πm)) ( T_A³/2 - T_B³/2 ). (9b.13)

Since T_A > T_B > 0, T_A³/2 > T_B³/2 strict, and therefore

Q̇_A→B > 0 strict. (9b.14)

Energy flows from A (hot) to B (cold), with the inequality strict whenever T_A > T_B. The unequal-density case n_A ≠n_B replaces (9b.13) with 1/2√(8/(πm)) [n_A T_A³/2 - n_B T_B³/2], which is positive whenever the temperature gradient dominates the density gradient (the standard heat-conduction regime); the pure temperature-gradient case (9b.13) is the directionally clean result.

Step 5 (Closure: the strict positivity in (9b.14) traces to the +ic orientation via Theorem 9). The combined ensemble A ∪B is itself a Compton-coupled massive-particle ensemble (the union of two such), so by Theorem 9 the total kinetic-theory entropy of the combined ensemble satisfies dS_A∪B/dt > 0 strict. The contribution of the heat transfer (9b.13) to the entropy budget is

dS_A∪B/dt|_transfer = -Q̇_A→B/T_A + Q̇_A→B/T_B = Q̇_A→B(1/T_B - 1/T_A). (9b.15)

Since T_A > T_B, we have 1/T_B > 1/T_A, so (1/T_B - 1/T_A) > 0 strict. Combined with (9b.14), the transfer contributes

dS_A∪B/dt|_transfer > 0 strict. (9b.16)

The strict inequality in (9b.14) — that energy flows from hot to cold — is precisely the inequality that makes (9b.16) positive rather than negative, hence consistent with Theorem 9's strict-positive-entropy-production. The hypothetical reverse direction Q̇_A→B < 0 (energy flowing from cold to hot at a permeable interface, with no other change) would produce dS_A∪B/dt|_transfer < 0, violating Theorem 9. Since Theorem 9 traces directly to the +ic orientation of dx₄/dt = ic (the strict positivity D > 0 of the diffusion coefficient in the Wiener equation is the spatial-projection content of +ic, not -ic, expansion of the McGucken Sphere; see Theorem 9 Steps A3, B4), the directionality of heat flow traces to the +ic orientation in exactly the same way.

Equivalently: were dx₄/dt = -ic to hold, the Wiener-process diffusion coefficient D would carry the reverse sign, the equilibrium Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution (9b.5) would not be normalizable as a forward-time stationary state, the mean speed v̅(T) would be ill-defined as a +t-asymptotic quantity, and the interfacial flux calculation (9b.13) would invert. The + in +ic is load-bearing for the direction of heat flow.

Combining Steps 1–5: heat flow from hot to cold is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic via the chain Compton coupling (T4) → spatial-projection isotropy (T5) → Brownian motion (T6) → Maxwell–Boltzmann equilibrium velocity distribution (Step 3 above) → collision rate linear in speed (Step 2 above) → interfacial flux asymmetry (Step 4 above) → strict entropy-production closure (Step 5 above, via T9 and its +ic trace). The Clausius statement of the Second Law — no spontaneous process whose sole effect is the transfer of heat from a colder to a hotter body — is the inequality (9b.14) read in the contrapositive direction, and it is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic in the same sense. ∎

Diagnostic remark. The mechanism is what Maxwell 1860 [107] gave as the kinetic-theory explanation of heat conduction: hotter particles move faster, sweep more spatial volume per unit time, and consequently cross any fixed interface at a higher rate, delivering kinetic energy preferentially in the down-temperature-gradient direction. The McGucken framing identifies the source of every step in Maxwell's argument: Compton coupling (Theorem 4) supplies the universal mass-energy oscillation that gives every particle the same rate of x₄-phase accumulation; spatial-projection isotropy (Theorem 5) supplies the SO(3)-symmetric velocity-direction distribution; Brownian motion (Theorem 6) supplies the diffusive transport equation; the Maxwell–Boltzmann equilibrium (Step 3 of the present theorem) is the unique stationary state of Compton-coupled Brownian dynamics; the collision-rate-linear-in-speed (Step 2) is direct from the spatial arc length swept per unit coordinate time. The Maxwell 1860 calculation closes through Theorem 9's strict-positivity content, which carries the +ic orientation of dx₄/dt = ic. The physical fact "hotter particles move faster and hit more particles than slower ones" is, in the McGucken framing, the empirical surface of the deeper fact that the Compton-coupled x₄-advance produces Maxwell–Boltzmann equilibrium with strict monotone speed-temperature relationship.

Consequences for the Carnot, Kelvin, and Clausius statements. The Carnot cycle bound (Theorem proved in the Geometric-Channel Founders section), the Kelvin–Planck statement of the Second Law (no process whose sole result is the transfer of heat from a colder to a hotter body), and the Clausius statement (no spontaneous heat flow from cold to hot) are corollaries of the present Theorem 9b: each is the statement that the inequality (9b.14) cannot be reversed, with the irreversibility traced to the +ic orientation through Theorem 9. The hand-waved "+ic-monotonic content forces heat from hot to cold" of the earlier Carnot Step 3 derivation is replaced by the explicit chain of the present proof.

3.4bis The Carnot bound as a theorem of the Principle

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic predicts the Carnot efficiency bound η≤1 - T_C/T_H as the closed-cycle form of the strict Second Law of Theorem 3.3: a working substance returned to its initial state has advanced along x₄ through the cycle, and the entropy its Compton-coupled ensemble has produced in that advance cannot be returned.

Theorem 3.4bis (Carnot bound; Theorem (Carnot 1824 as Theorem of dx₄/dt = ic) of [3]; reproduced in full). The statement and proof are the author's, verbatim, from [3]; the present paper's restatement in its own numbering, and any steps it adds, follow the quotation.

From [3], verbatim — Theorem (Carnot 1824 as Theorem of dx₄/dt = ic), statement and proof: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list; theorem numbers inside the quotation are those of [3])

Theorem (Carnot 1824 as Theorem of dx4/dt = ic)

Statement. The Carnot cycle bound — that no heat engine operating between reservoirs at temperatures T_H and T_C can have efficiency exceeding η_Carnot = 1 - T_C/T_H — is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic via Geometric Channel reading of the +ic-monotonic content. The cycle is a closed geometric path on the indicator diagram of (P, V) states, with the orientation of traversal encoded by the +ic-monotonic direction of x₄-expansion. The work extractable from one complete cycle is bounded by the T_C/T_H factor because the heat-flow content carries the +ic orientation of the McGucken Sphere expansion that drove it.

Proof. The Carnot cycle traverses four legs in (P, V, T) phase space: isothermal expansion at T_H (heat absorbed Q_H), adiabatic expansion (T_H →T_C, no heat exchange), isothermal compression at T_C (heat rejected Q_C), and adiabatic compression (T_C →T_H, no heat exchange). The cycle is closed in (P, V) space; its enclosed area equals the net work W = Q_H - Q_C extracted per cycle.

Step 1 (the cycle as a McGucken Sphere trajectory). By Theorem 3 of the present paper (Huygens-wavefront propagation), every spacetime event is the apex of a forward McGucken Sphere Σ_+(p₀) of radius R(t) = c(t - t₀) > 0 for t > t₀. The traversal of the Carnot cycle is a sequence of equilibrium states {s₁, s₂, s₃, s₄ in (P, V, T) phase space connected by quasi-static transitions; each transition is a path on the McGucken manifold ℳ whose x₄-component advances monotonically at rate ic by the Principle. The cycle is closed in (P, V, T) but is not closed in x₄: the working substance advances by Δx₄ = ic ·t_cycle in the duration t_cycle required to complete the cycle, with the +ic orientation of this advance being the load-bearing geometry.

Diagnostic remark. Carnot's 1824 derivation [106] used the caloric theory — heat as a conserved fluid that "falls" from high to low temperature like water through a waterwheel. The caloric theory was later discredited by the mechanical equivalence of heat (Joule 1843, Mayer 1845); Carnot's result survived the discrediting because it depended only on the directionality of the heat flow, not on the conservation of caloric. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies the explanation: Carnot's "caloric falls from high to low temperature" was a phenomenological surrogate for the +ic-monotonic content of dx₄/dt = ic. The cycle bound survived because the directionality is real (it is the +ic orientation of x₄-expansion), even though the conserved-fluid mechanism Carnot invoked is incorrect. The Geometric Channel's geometric directionality content was correct from 1824; Carnot lacked only the language to name dx₄/dt = ic as the underlying mechanism.

4. Gravity as two derivationally disjoint theorem chains of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality. The Einstein field equations G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG/c⁴)T_μν are a theorem of this Principle along two channels that share no intermediate machinery beyond the Principle itself and two inputs named in Corollary 4.8 [4]. The Algebraic Channel uses symmetry and the calculus of variations and no thermodynamics; the Geometric Channel uses the Second Law, the area law, the Unruh temperature, and the Clausius relation, each of which is a theorem of §3.

4.1 The Algebraic Channel: the field equations with no thermodynamics

McGucken Principle anchor. The Algebraic Channel reads the integrated coordinate x₄ = ict as a label and asks which transformations leave dx₄/dt = ic invariant. The subgroup Diff_McG and the preserved foliation, with its empirics, are developed in §6.6 of [4]. Since x₄ advances at the same rate from every event in every spatial direction at every time, the Principle is invariant under translations along x₄, along x₁,x₂,x₃, and along t; under spatial rotations SO(3); and under Lorentz boosts SO^+(1,3), the latter automatic from the i in dx₄/dt = ic via the Lorentzian signature of §2.1. The combined invariance group is the Poincaré group ISO(1,3) = ℝ⁴⋊SO^+(1,3) (Theorem 8 of [4]; the Principle generates the group, [22]).

Theorem 4.1 (Factorization of Diff(M) and the Einstein field equations; Theorem 9 of [4]; reproduced in full). The statement and proof are the author's, verbatim, from [4]; the present paper's restatement in its own numbering, and any steps it adds, follow the quotation.

From [4], verbatim — Theorem 9 (Factorisation of Diff(M) via McGucken), statement and proof: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list)

Theorem 9 (Factorisation of Diff(M) via McGucken, imported from [23, §3]). Hilbert's diffeomorphism invariance of the gravitational action is factored by dx₄/dt = ic into two physically distinct components:
(a) A kinematic symmetry: Diff_McG(M_G)-invariance of the matter action, where Diff_McG(M_G) is the foliation-preserving subgroup of Diff(M_G) generated by vector fields ξ^μ = (ξ⁰(x⁰), ξ^i(x⁰, x^j)) with ξ⁰ depending only on the time coordinate x⁰.
(b) A constitutive identity: u^μu_μ = -c² enforced pointwise on every massive worldline.
Off shell, only Diff_McG(M_G) acts as a symmetry. On shell --- given the matter equations of motion --- the full Diff(M_G) is recovered, and the Einstein field equations G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG/c⁴) T_μν follow from Lovelock uniqueness plus Newtonian matching.
Proof of Theorem 9. We follow the structure of [23, §3], expanding each step.

Step 1 (the subgroup Diff_McG). The McGucken Principle the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic fixes the rate of x₄-advance to ic at every point of M_G. Under a diffeomorphism ϕ: M_G →M_G generated by a vector field ξ^μ, the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic requires dx₄/dt = ic to be invariant. The constraint is that ξ⁰ cannot depend on the spatial coordinates x^j in a way that varies the rate at different points of the same spatial slice; otherwise the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic would be broken because dx₄/dt would acquire spatial dependence. Hence ∂ξ⁰/∂x^j = 0 for j = 1, 2, 3, i.e., ξ⁰ = ξ⁰(x⁰) only. The spatial components ξ^j are unconstrained because the spatial sector is deformable (Definition 5(b)). The vector field is therefore of the form ξ^μ = (ξ⁰(x⁰), ξ^j(x⁰, x^k)), which defines Diff_McG(M_G).

Lemma 9.1. Diff_McG(M_G) is a strict subgroup of Diff(M_G).

Proof of Lemma 9.1. The general vector field on M_G has ξ⁰ = ξ⁰(x⁰, x^i) depending on all coordinates. Restricting ξ⁰ to depend only on x⁰ yields a strict subgroup, since vector fields with ∂ξ⁰/∂x^j ≠0 are not in the McGucken subgroup. □

Step 2 (the constitutive identity). By the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, every massive particle's worldline x^μ(τ) on M_G has dx₄/dt = ic. Parametrising by proper time τ via dτ² = -c^-2 g_μν dx^μdx^ν, the four-velocity is u^μ = dx^μ/dτ. The four-velocity budget identity

u^μu_μ = g_μν u^μu^ν = -c²

follows directly from the definition of τ: indeed g_μν u^μu^ν = (dx^μdx_μ)/dτ² = -c². The stress-energy tensor of a perfect fluid of such particles is

T^μν = (ρc² + p) (u^μu^ν)/(c²) + p g^μν, (T)

with the constraint u^μu_μ = -c² enforced pointwise.

Step 3 (Noether's second theorem applied to Diff_McG). Apply Noether's second theorem [81, ref. 37] to the matter action S_M[ϕ, g_μν] invariant under Diff_McG(M_G). Noether's second theorem is here the standard variational result applied to framework-derived inputs: the McGucken Lagrangian (Lemma 1 plus the derived least-action structure), the Diff_McG-symmetry, and the +ic foliation all descend from dx₄/dt = ic ([23, Theorem 30']; precise status in Remark 10.3.1.1). The variational theorem itself is general calculus of variations --- a tool, not re-derived from the Principle; what the Principle supplies are its inputs. Therefore the Algebraic Channel rests on no physical input external to dx₄/dt = ic for this step.

The conserved currents associated with Diff_McG-invariance are weaker than those of full Diff(M_G) because the symmetry group is smaller. Specifically: (S) spatial diffeomorphism invariance (ξ^j unconstrained, ξ⁰ = 0) yields the spatial conservation law ∇_i T^iν = 0 on each spatial slice Σ_t; (T-int) time-reparametrisation invariance (ξ⁰ = ξ⁰(x⁰), ξ^j = 0) yields the integrated time-conservation d/dt ∫_Σ_t T⁰ν √(h) d³ x = 0. The local conservation ∇_μT^μν = 0 in all four directions is not given by Diff_McG alone because Diff_McG is a strict subgroup (Lemma 9.1).

Step 4 (on-shell enhancement). Claim: given the matter equations of motion (relativistic energy equation and Euler equation) together with the constitutive identity (Step 2), the local conservation ∇_μT^μν = 0 holds in all four directions.

Proof of the on-shell enhancement. The perfect-fluid stress-energy tensor (T) gives, upon differentiation,

∇_μT^μν = ∇_μ[(ρc² + p) (u^μ)/(c²)] u^ν+ (ρc² + p) (u^μ)/(c²) ∇_μu^ν+ g^μν ∂_μp. (†)

Timelike projection. Contract (†) with u_ν and apply the constitutive identity u_νu^ν = -c² together with its consequence u_ν∇_μu^ν = 0 (from differentiating u_νu^ν = -c², a constant on the constraint surface):

u_ν∇_μT^μν = -c² ∇_μ[(ρc² + p) (u^μ)/(c²)] + 0 + u^μ∂_μp.

Expanding the first term:

-c² ∇_μ[((ρc² + p) u^μ)/(c²)] = -∇_μ[(ρc² + p) u^μ] = -(ρc² + p) ∇_μu^μ- c² u^μ∂_μρ- u^μ∂_μp.

Combining:

u_ν∇_μT^μν = -(ρc² + p) ∇_μu^μ- c² u^μ∂_μρ.

Setting this to zero gives the relativistic energy equation (the perfect-fluid matter EOM for energy conservation along the flow):

u^μ∂_μρ+ (ρ+ p/c²) ∇_μu^μ = 0. (Energy-EOM)

The timelike projection u_ν∇_μT^μν = 0 is therefore equivalent to the perfect-fluid energy equation, which is one of the matter EOMs.

Spatial projection. Project (†) orthogonal to u^ν using the spatial projector h^ν_λ = δ^ν_λ+ u^νu_λ/c² (with h^ν_λu^λ = 0 and h^ν_λh^λ_σ = h^ν_σ):

h^ν_λ∇_μT^μλ = (ρc² + p) (u^μ)/(c²) (h^ν_λ∇_μu^λ) + h^νμ ∂_μp,

where the first term of (†) drops out under the spatial projection because h^ν_λu^λ = 0, and the third term contracts to h^νμ∂_μp via h^ν_λg^λμ = h^νμ. Setting this to zero gives the relativistic Euler equation (the perfect-fluid matter EOM for spatial momentum):

(ρc² + p) u^μ∇_μu^ν = -h^νμ ∂_μp, (Euler-EOM)

where the projection h^ν_λ∇_μu^λ≡∇_μu^ν on the spatial subspace (using u_λ∇_μu^λ = 0) eliminates the redundant temporal component. The spatial projection h^ν_λ∇_μT^μλ = 0 is therefore equivalent to the relativistic Euler equation.

Span and conclusion. The timelike-projector -u^νu^λ/c² and the spatial-projector h^ν_λ = δ^ν_λ+ u^νu_λ/c² together span the full tangent space at every event:

-(u^νu_λ)/(c²) + h^ν_λ = -(u^νu_λ)/(c²) + δ^ν_λ+ (u^νu_λ)/(c²) = δ^ν_λ.

Hence the vanishing of ∇_μT^μν on both subspaces implies ∇_μT^μν = 0 identically. On shell — given the relativistic energy equation (Energy-EOM) and the relativistic Euler equation (Euler-EOM) as the perfect-fluid matter EOMs — the local conservation ∇_μT^μν = 0 holds in all four directions. The matter action becomes invariant under arbitrary diffeomorphisms acting consistently on metric and matter, recovering the full Diff(M_G) on-shell. □ (end of Step 4)

Step 5 (Einstein field equations from Lovelock). With ∇_μT^μν = 0 established, the geometric side of the field equations is forced by Lovelock's theorem [23, ref. 32]: in four dimensions, the unique divergence-free symmetric rank-2 tensor built from the metric g_μν and its first two derivatives, linear in second derivatives, is

L_μν = αG_μν + βg_μν, (Lovelock)

where G_μν = R_μν - 1/2 R g_μν is the Einstein tensor and α, β are constants. The priority of Lovelock as a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic operates through the McGucken-Invariance Lemma (Lemma 6): the McGucken-Invariance Lemma restricts the allowed geometric structure to one in which g_μν is the deformable-sector variable (spatial sector) coupled to matter through the universal Sphere geometry; the Lovelock uniqueness then applies to the divergence-free combinations on the four-dimensional manifold M_G. Setting L_μν = κT_μν with κ = 8πG/c⁴ and β = Λ gives

G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG)/(c⁴) T_μν. (Einstein field equations)

The tag (the Einstein field equations) is the standard abbreviation for the Einstein Field Equations: the foundational dynamical equations of general relativity, relating the geometric curvature of spacetime (encoded in the Einstein tensor G_μν and cosmological-constant term Λg_μν on the left) to the matter-energy content (encoded in the stress-energy tensor T_μν on the right). They are GR T11 of the book's 24-theorem gravitational chain.
Step 6 (Newtonian matching fixes κ). In the weak-field static limit g₀0 = -(1 + 2Φ/c²), g_ij = δ_ij, the dominant component of (the Einstein field equations) at 00 reduces to Poisson's equation ∇² Φ = 4πG ρ. The coupling constant κ = 8πG/c⁴ is forced by this matching. □ (end of Theorem 9)

From [4], verbatim — Corollary 9.2: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list)

Corollary 9.2. The Algebraic Channel derivation of the Einstein field equations rests on no mathematical input external to dx₄/dt = ic and Lovelock's theorem, plus the Newtonian matching condition fixing the coupling constant. The factorisation (a) of Theorem 9 (Diff-invariance) and (b) (constitutive identity) are both direct theorems of dx₄/dt = ic. The meaning is that the McGucken Principle is strictly stronger than Hilbert's diffeomorphism invariance: the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic determines which diffeomorphisms are off-shell symmetries (only Diff_McG) and explains why the full Diff(M_G) is recovered on shell (because the four-velocity budget is consistent with arbitrary reparametrisation of the worldline).

The Algebraic Channel is the invariance-group content of dx₄/dt = ic. Through Noether's theorem (itself a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic per [22]), every continuous symmetry generates a conservation law: energy (t-translation), momentum (spatial translation), angular momentum (spatial rotation), four-momentum (Lorentz), stress-energy conservation ∇_μT^μν = 0 (the on-shell enhancement of Diff_McG-invariance). The Algebraic Channel operates uniformly in Lorentzian signature; the reason established in [23, §5] is that the imaginary unit i is interior to the unitary representations exp(-isp/ħ), exp(-iHt/ħ) and cannot be exteriorised without dissolving the algebra.

From [19], verbatim — Theorem 5.5 (Master Equation), statement and proof: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list)

Theorem 5.5 (Master Equation) For any massive particle, the four-velocity satisfies g_μν u^μ u^ν = −c². The physics: every massive particle, embedded in a spacetime in which the fourth dimension is physically expanding at c from every event (Axiom 2.1), carries a four-velocity of magnitude c. The magnitude is fixed by the physics, not by a definitional choice. Proof. (a) Physical argument from Axiom 2.1. Axiom 2.1 states that the fourth dimension is expanding at c from every spacetime event. Every massive worldline of ℳ is embedded in this geometry. At spatial rest, a massive particle's only motion is the x₄-advance that the physics imposes at the particle's event: dx₄/dt = ic, with d x = 0. The four-velocity at spatial rest in flat space (Lemma 5.4, v = 0, γ = 1) has u⁰ = c, u^j = 0, hence g_μν u^μ u^ν |_rest = −(u⁰)² + | u |² = −c². The physical claim is that this magnitude is universal: a massive particle in spatial motion has redistributed some of its four-velocity from the x₄-advance budget into spatial motion, but the total Minkowski-magnitude squared remains −c², because every event of spacetime continues to participate in the c-rate fourth-dimension expansion (Axiom 2.1). The magnitude c is the physical c of the McGucken Principle, not a kinematic convention. (b) Formal verification at general velocity. By Lemma 5.4: u⁰ = γc, u^j = γv^j. Computing in flat space: η_μν u^μ u^ν = −(γc)² + γ²v² = −γ²c² + γ²v² = −γ²c²(1 − v²/c²) = −γ²c² · γ^(−2) = −c². The result is the formal statement of the universal magnitude c established in (a). (c) Curved spacetime. The proper-time differential reads c² dτ² = −g_μν dx^μ dx^ν in any spacetime. Dividing by dτ² and using u^μ = dx^μ/dτ: c² = −g_μν u^μ u^ν, i.e., g_μν u^μ u^ν = −c². By Lemma 5.2, the prefactor c² in the proper-time differential is the squared rate of the fourth-dimension expansion (Axiom 2.1). The Master Equation expresses, in any spacetime, that every massive worldline carries a four-velocity of physical magnitude c. ∎

From [19], verbatim — Theorem 7.1 (McGucken-Invariance Lemma), statement and proof: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list)

Theorem 7.1 (McGucken-Invariance Lemma) The physical fact of the fourth-dimension expansion at c holds globally on ℳ, regardless of the gravitational field. Formally: ∂(dx₄/dt)/∂g_μν = 0 for all metric components. In any chart (t, x₁, x₂, x₃) adapted to the foliation 𝓕 such that the coordinate x₄ along worldlines descends from the integrated form of Axiom 2.1 (x₄ = ict), the timelike block of the metric is gauge-fixed: g_tt = −c², g_tj = 0. Only the spatial-slice metric h_ij ≡ g_ij has dynamical degrees of freedom under mass-energy. The metric component count of ℳ reduces from ten to six. Proof. (1) The physics does not depend on the metric. Axiom 2.1 is the physical statement that the fourth dimension is expanding at c from every event. Its differential expression dx₄/dt = ic contains only the imaginary unit i (a fixed element of ℂ, encoding the perpendicularity of x₄ to the spatial directions) and the velocity of light c (a fundamental physical constant). Neither depends on the matter content of ℳ or on the gravitational field. Therefore ∂(dx₄/dt)/∂g_μν = ∂(ic)/∂g_μν = 0. Equivalently: the physics of Axiom 2.1 is unchanged by the presence of mass-energy. The fourth dimension expands at c at every event, in flat or curved spacetime alike. (2) Gauge-fixing of the timelike block. In any chart adapted to the foliation 𝓕, the coordinate x₄ along a worldline at spatial rest is identified with ict (the integrated form of the physics; the integration parametrized by coordinate time at fixed spatial point). The contribution to the line element from the timelike direction is computed by Proposition 3.1: −c²(dt)². Comparing with the generic form ds² = g_μν dx^μ dx^ν at spatial rest (d x = 0): ds² |_rest = g_tt (dt)² = −c²(dt)², hence g_tt = −c². Since the physics holds at every event (Axiom 2.1, globally on ℳ), this gauge-fixing is global. For the cross-terms g_tj: by Lemma 7.2 below, the foliation slices are orthogonal to the ∂_t-direction at every event in the adapted chart, hence g_tj = g(∂_t, ∂_j) = 0 for j = 1, 2, 3. (3) Component count. The metric tensor on ℳ has ten independent components: g_tt (one), g_tj (three), g_ij symmetric (six). By (2), the four timelike-block components are gauge-fixed by the physics. The remaining six are h_ij, unconstrained by the physics, carrying the dynamical degrees of freedom under mass-energy. ∎

Restatement in the present paper's notation. Hilbert's diffeomorphism invariance is factored by dx₄/dt = ic into (a) a kinematic symmetry, invariance of the matter action under the foliation-preserving subgroup Diff_McG generated by vector fields ξ^μ = (ξ⁰(x⁰),ξ^i(x⁰,x^j)), and (b) the constitutive identity u^μu_μ = -c² enforced pointwise on every massive worldline. Off shell only Diff_McG acts; on shell the full Diff(M) is recovered, and the Einstein field equations follow from Lovelock uniqueness plus Newtonian matching.

Proof. Step 1 (the subgroup). Under a diffeomorphism generated by ξ^μ, dx₄/dt = ic must remain the same at every point of a spatial slice. If ξ⁰ depended on x^j, the relabelling of t would vary across the slice and dx₄/dt would acquire spatial dependence; hence ∂ξ⁰/∂x^j = 0, ξ⁰ = ξ⁰(x⁰). The spatial components are unconstrained because the spatial sector is deformable. This defines Diff_McG, a strict subgroup of Diff(M).

Step 2 (the constitutive identity). Parametrizing a massive worldline by proper time, dτ² = -c^-2g_μνdx^μdx^ν, the four-velocity satisfies g_μνu^μu^ν = -c² — the Master Equation, Theorem 5.5 of [19], whose magnitude c is the rate of the advance at spatial rest and is "fixed by the physics, not by a definitional choice". The perfect-fluid stress tensor T^μν = (ρc² + p)u^μu^ν/c² + pg^μν carries this constraint pointwise.

Step 3 (Noether's second theorem on the smaller group). Applied to a matter action invariant under Diff_McG, Noether's second theorem yields the spatial conservation law ∇_iT^iν = 0 on each slice (from ξ^j unconstrained) and the integrated temporal law d/dt∫_Σ_tT⁰ν√(h) d³x = 0 (from ξ⁰ = ξ⁰(x⁰)). The local conservation ∇_μT^μν = 0 in all four directions is weaker than what full Diff(M) would give and is at this step unavailable. The variational theorem is a tool of the calculus of variations; what the Principle supplies are its inputs — the McGucken Lagrangian, the symmetry, and the +ic foliation.

Step 4 (on-shell enhancement). Differentiating the perfect-fluid tensor,

∇_μT^μν = ∇_μ[(ρc²+p)(u^μ)/(c²)]u^ν+ (ρc²+p)(u^μ)/(c²)∇_μu^ν+ g^μν∂_μp.

Contract with u_ν, using u_νu^ν = -c² and its consequence u_ν∇_μu^ν = 0:

u_ν∇_μT^μν = -(ρc²+p)∇_μu^μ- c²u^μ∂_μρ,

whose vanishing is the relativistic energy equation u^μ∂_μρ+ (ρ+ p/c²)∇_μu^μ = 0, a matter equation of motion. Project with h^ν_λ = δ^ν_λ+ u^νu_λ/c²:

h^ν_λ∇_μT^μλ = (ρc²+p)(u^μ)/(c²)∇_μu^ν+ h^νμ∂_μp,

whose vanishing is the relativistic Euler equation (ρc²+p)u^μ∇_μu^ν = -h^νμ∂_μp, the other matter equation of motion. Since -u^νu_λ/c² + h^ν_λ = δ^ν_λ, the two projections span the tangent space, so on shell ∇_μT^μν = 0 identically, and the matter action becomes invariant under the full Diff(M) acting consistently on metric and matter.

Step 4′ (full Diff(M)-invariance of the gravitational sector). The restriction of Step 1 concerns the matter foliation and does not fix the symmetry of the gravitational action. A gravitational action invariant only under Diff_McG would be the Hořava–Lifshitz family, with kinetic term K_ijK^ij - λK² and λ free; general relativity is the member λ = 1, and nothing in Diff_McG selects it. The Principle supplies the missing invariance: the McGucken Sphere expands at the same rate c from every event in every inertial frame (Theorem 8 of [4]; [17]), so the geometry carries no preferred foliation — a preferred slicing in the gravitational sector would single out a frame in which the expansion rate differed from c. The gravitational action is therefore a scalar under full Diff(M), forcing λ = 1.

Step 5 (Lovelock). With ∇_μT^μν = 0 and the gravitational action Diff(M)-invariant, Lovelock's theorem [23] gives, in four dimensions, the unique divergence-free symmetric rank-2 tensor built from g_μν and its first two derivatives, linear in second derivatives: L_μν = αG_μν + βg_μν. Setting L_μν = κT_μν with β = Λ gives G_μν + Λg_μν = κT_μν.

Step 6 (Newtonian matching). In the weak-field static limit g₀0 = -(1 + 2Φ/c²), g_ij = δ_ij, the 00 component reduces to Poisson's equation ∇²Φ = 4πGρ, forcing κ = 8πG/c⁴. This is the standard weak-field gauge; in the chart adapted to the foliation of the advance, the McGucken-Invariance Lemma (Theorem 7.1 of [19]) fixes g_tt = -c², g_tj = 0 and places the same potential in the spatial metric h_ij, with the matching unchanged. □

Corollary 4.2. The Algebraic-Channel derivation rests on no physical input beyond dx₄/dt = ic, Lovelock's theorem applied to a sector whose full invariance Step 4′ derives from the Lorentz covariance of the McGucken Sphere, and the Newtonian matching that fixes the coupling. No entropy, temperature, horizon, or arrow of time appears.

Proof. By inspection of Steps 1–6: Step 1 uses the invariance of dx₄/dt = ic under relabelling; Step 2 uses x₄ = ict and the definition of proper time; Step 3 uses Noether's second theorem, a theorem of the calculus of variations; Step 4 uses the algebraic identity u_ν∇_μu^ν = 0 and the projector h^ν_λ; Step 4′ uses Lemma 7.4.1; Step 5 uses Lovelock's theorem; Step 6 uses the weak-field limit. None of these steps contains a probability measure, a state count, a temperature, a null surface, or a direction of time; the Euclidean action underlying the variations is even in x₄ (Lemma 7.4.6). □

4.2 The Geometric Channel: the thermodynamic route, with every input a theorem

McGucken Principle anchor. The Geometric Channel reads dx₄/dt = ic as the active expansion of the McGucken Sphere and asks what the Principle generates when applied at every event. The wavefront Σ_+(p), Huygens' principle (every point of a Sphere is the source of a new Sphere, with the Principle supplying the physical mechanism — x₄'s spherical expansion at c from every event — that Huygens' construction states without mechanism), and the iterated-Sphere path structure are its objects. Four theorems, each derived from the Principle, culminate in the field equations.

Theorem 4.3 (Geometric Second Law). Identical to Theorem 3.3, used here as the first thermodynamic input.

Theorem 4.4 (Area law). Identical to Theorem 3.5, used here as the second input, with the coefficient fixed within the channel by Newtonian matching (Theorem 4.7).

Theorem 4.5 (Algebraic-Channel confirmation of the 1/4 by the Euclidean cigar; Theorems 15–16 of [3]). The Hawking temperature and the coefficient 1/4 follow from the Einstein–Hilbert action of Theorem 4.1 under the McGucken–Wick rotation of the horizon geometry.

From [56], verbatim — the Hawking temperature as the inverse spatial circumference of the real fourth axis around the horizon McGucken Sphere: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list)

The Simplest and Most Direct Instance: The Hawking Temperature as the Inverse Spatial Circumference of the Real Fourth Axis Around the Real Horizon Sphere

Before the reader proceeds to the historical reconstruction, the -closure theorems, and the senior-figure-admission cluster, the simplest and most direct instance of the McWick rotation accomplishing something the orthodox Wick rotation cannot is supplied here as an entry-level example. The reader is invited to extend the example to the fifteen additional -distinction instances catalogued throughout the present paper at every tier of physics.

The instance. The orthodox Wick rotation t → −iτ is invoked to make the Schwarzschild metric Euclidean. The Euclidean Schwarzschild metric carries a conical singularity at the horizon r = 2GM unless the imaginary time τ is periodically identified with period

> β_H = 8πGM = 1/T_H, >

with T_H = ħ c³ / (8π G M k_B) the Hawking temperature. The orthodox derivation by Gibbons and Hawking 1977 [34] supplies the numerical relationship β_H = 8π GM as a regularity condition on the complexified manifold. Real photons of real energy are then computed to be emitted by real astrophysical black holes at this temperature.

What the orthodox Wick rotation cannot do. Three questions remain open on the orthodox reading:

(i) Why is imaginary time periodic? The orthodox procedure supplies a consistency condition — "otherwise there is a conical singularity" — and stops. A consistency condition on a complexified coordinate that has, on the orthodox reading, no physical referent is not a physical mechanism. Periodicity of an imaginary coordinate is a vocabulary statement, not a physical statement.

(ii) What is the physical thing oscillating with period β_H? The orthodox formalism cannot say. No physical clock is identified as running with that period; the period is the circumference of a mathematical identification of points on a complexified manifold.

(iii) Why does the regularity of a calculational trick correspond to a real physical temperature that real Hawking photons carry away from real black holes? Gibbons-Hawking 1977 posits the correspondence; the connection between mathematical regularity in imaginary time and physical thermodynamic temperature in real Lorentzian time is asserted, not derived from a physical principle. This is the gap that Feynman 1965 flagged as "amusing", Huang 1998 and 2010 as "one of the great mysteries of physics", Zee 2003 and 2010 as "something profound that we have not quite understood", Mountain–Stelle 1999 as "there is no standard treatment of Wick rotation in the literature", Penrose 2004 as "manifestly contrary to GR", and Turok 2024 as "a prescription. It's a mathematical prescription, which makes it predictive."

What the McWick rotation does. The McWick rotation τ = x₄/c identifies τ as the arc-length coordinate on the real physical fourth axis of the McGucken manifold 𝓜_G, with the fourth axis x₄ physically expanding at +ic from every spacetime event per the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic. At the horizon r = 2GM, the geometric structure of Schwarzschild forces the radial proper-distance direction and the x₄-advance direction to interchange roles: the x₄-axis becomes spatially circumferential around the horizon Sphere, with physical spatial circumference

> L_x₄^horizon = 8πGM >

in units where c = 1, or equivalently L_x₄^horizon = 8πGM/c in dimensional form. The Hawking period in τ-units is the spatial circumference divided by c:

> β_H = L_x₄^horizon/c = (8πGM)/(c²) ·c = (8πGM)/c ·1/1 = 8πGM, >

restoring the units convention. The Hawking temperature is now the inverse of a real spatial circumference of a real axis around a real horizon Sphere — exactly as the temperature of any other thermal system is the inverse of a real characteristic length scale (the de Broglie thermal wavelength of an ideal gas, the period of a harmonic oscillator at thermal equilibrium, the wavelength of a photon mode in a cavity).
