From [24], verbatim — Proposition V.1 (The factor 1/4 from the Euclidean Einstein–Hilbert action on the Schwarzschild cigar), statement and proof: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list)

Proposition V.1 (The factor 1/4 from the Euclidean Einstein–Hilbert action on the Schwarzschild cigar). The McGucken Wick rotation of the Schwarzschild geometry produces a Euclidean manifold that is smooth everywhere — the “cigar” near the horizon, extending to an asymptotically flat region at spatial infinity. The total Euclidean gravitational action, evaluated on this manifold with the Gibbons–Hawking–York boundary term included, is I_E = β M c²/2, where β = 2π/κ is the Euclidean-time period forced by smoothness at the horizon (§II.3) and M is the ADM mass. The Euclidean partition-function relation S = (βE − I_E)/k_B^(−1) = β⟨E⟩k_B − I_E k_B, with ⟨E⟩ = Mc², yields S_BH = (βMc² − βMc²/2) · k_B = βMc²/2 · k_B = k_B A/(4ℓ_P²). The factor 1/4 is exactly the numerical factor appearing in I_E = βMc²/2, and it has a direct geometric origin: the Euclidean action of the Schwarzschild cigar is half of the on-shell energy integral because the horizon contributes a single Gibbons–Hawking–York boundary term whose coefficient is 1/2 in the standard normalization. This is Hawking’s result H-3, derived with the McGucken Wick rotation supplying the physical meaning of the Euclidean continuation. Proof. Four steps. Step 1: The full Euclidean Schwarzschild geometry. The Schwarzschild solution in Lorentzian signature, in the exterior region r > 2GM/c², has the line element ds² = −(1 − 2GM/(c²r)) c²dt² + (1 − 2GM/(c²r))^(−1) dr² + r² dΩ². Under the McGucken Wick rotation t → −iτ (equivalently, removing the i from x₄), this becomes ds²_E = (1 − 2GM/(c²r)) c²dτ² + (1 − 2GM/(c²r))^(−1) dr² + r² dΩ². Near the horizon r = 2GM/c², this reduces to the cigar geometry of §II.3 with angular period β = 2π/κ where κ = c⁴/(4GM). Far from the horizon, the geometry approaches Euclidean 4-space. The full Euclidean Schwarzschild manifold is therefore a cigar at the horizon smoothly joined to asymptotic Euclidean 4-space, with the Euclidean time τ periodic with period β throughout. Step 2: The total action S_geom + S_GHY. The Euclidean gravitational action on this manifold consists of two pieces: the bulk Einstein–Hilbert term and the Gibbons–Hawking–York boundary term [34]: I_E = −(c³/16πG) ∫_M d⁴x √g R − (c³/8πG) ∮_∂M d³x √h (K − K_0). Here M is the Euclidean Schwarzschild manifold, R is its Ricci scalar, ∂M is its boundary at spatial infinity, h is the induced 3-metric on ∂M, K is the extrinsic curvature of ∂M, and K_0 is the extrinsic curvature of the same boundary surface embedded in flat Euclidean 4-space (the subtraction that removes the vacuum-divergent contribution). The Gibbons–Hawking–York term is not an ad-hoc addition; it is required for the variational principle to be well-posed when the boundary has fixed induced metric rather than fixed metric derivatives [34, 191]. Step 3: Evaluation. The Schwarzschild solution is Ricci-flat (R = 0), so the bulk term vanishes identically. The entire action comes from the Gibbons–Hawking–York boundary term evaluated on the sphere at spatial infinity. Explicit calculation in the standard coordinates [34, Eq. 3.17] gives I_E = βMc²/2. The factor of 1/2 is the geometric consequence of the subtraction K − K_0: the extrinsic curvature of a large sphere in the Schwarzschild geometry differs from its extrinsic curvature in flat space by a term proportional to the Schwarzschild mass, and the surface integral of this difference gives half the Euclidean period times the mass. This is the central computation, and it is entirely in the bulk standard-GR literature; the McGucken contribution is supplying the physical meaning of the Euclidean continuation (§II.2) that makes the calculation a statement about real geometry rather than a formal rotation. Step 4: Entropy from the partition function. The Euclidean action is related to the thermodynamic partition function by Z = e^(−I_E/ℏ). Standard thermodynamics then gives S_BH = −∂F/∂T = (β⟨E⟩ − I_E/ℏ) k_B = (βMc²/ℏ − βMc²/(2ℏ)) k_B = βMc²/(2ℏ) · k_B. Using β = 2π/κ = 8πGM/c³ (from κ = c⁴/(4GM)) gives S_BH = (8πGM/c³)(Mc²)/(2ℏ) · k_B = 4πGM²k_B/(ℏc). Substituting A = 16πG²M²/c⁴: S_BH = k_B · A c³/(4ℏG) = k_B · A/(4ℓ_P²), giving η = 1/4. ∎ Meaning. The 1/4 in the Bekenstein–Hawking formula is the numerical factor in I_E = βMc²/2 for the Euclidean Schwarzschild geometry. This factor is neither a Bogoliubov-coefficient output nor a heuristic; it is the explicit computation of the Gibbons–Hawking–York boundary action on the Euclidean Schwarzschild cigar, with the subtraction term K_0 (which removes the vacuum-flat-space contribution) generating the 1/2. In the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, this is a real geometric fact about the Euclidean manifold obtained by removing the i from x₄ at the horizon, not a formal trick. The Bekenstein (ln 2)/(8π) coefficient and the Hawking 1/4 coefficient both follow from the McGucken Principle: the former from classical-information one-bit counting per Compton-wavelength absorbed particle ([59] §V), the latter from the full semiclassical Euclidean-action computation presented here. They differ by the factor 2π/ln 2 ≈ 9.06, the ratio of Planckian-thermal mode density to one-bit-per-absorbed-particle counting. V.3. Resolution of HK-3 (why exactly 1/4?) The open problem of why the Bekenstein–Hawking coefficient is exactly 1/4 has the geometric answer given in Proposition V.1: the coefficient is the numerical factor in I_E = βMc²/2 for the Euclidean Schwarzschild geometry, and this factor is the explicit output of the Gibbons–Hawking–York boundary action with the flat-space subtraction K_0. The factor is not mysterious; it is the standard 1977 computation [34], performed on a geometry whose physical meaning is now supplied by the McGucken Wick rotation. What was opaque in the standard derivation — why the specific fraction 1/4 appears — is resolved by tracing it to the Ricci-flatness of Schwarzschild (which zeros the bulk integral) and the half-factor in the Gibbons–Hawking–York evaluation at spatial infinity. Both are geometric facts about the Euclidean Schwarzschild manifold, and both follow from the McGucken Wick rotation applied to the near-horizon geometry without any additional assumptions. York’s 1972 introduction of the boundary term [191] and Gibbons–Hawking’s 1977 application [34] supply the computation; the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies the physical meaning.

Proof. Integrating dx₄/dt = ic gives x₄ = ict; in Euclidean units τ = x₄/c the substitution t↦-iτ is the same advance written on the Euclidean section. A boost of rapidity η, ct' = ctcoshη+ xsinhη, x' = ctsinhη+ xcoshη, becomes with θ = -iη a rotation by θ in the (x,cτ) plane. The accelerated worldline, of constant Rindler position with boost parameter advancing at a/c per unit proper time, is a circle on the Euclidean section; regularity at the fixed point of the rotation (absence of a conical singularity) requires the angle to be 2π-periodic, so the period in Euclidean proper time is Δτ = 2πc/a. The KMS condition identifies a state periodic in imaginary time with period ħβ as thermal at inverse temperature β; matching ħβ = 2πc/a gives T_U = 1/k_Bβ = ħa/2πck_B. Every step — the advance, the boost-to-rotation, the 2π-regularity, the KMS periodicity — is the Euclidean reading of dx₄/dt = ic. The temperature is a statement about the accelerated observer's share v_x₄ of the advance on that observer's foliation; the rate dx₄/dt = ic itself is unchanged (Appendix D). □

From [4], verbatim — Theorem 14 (Geometric Channel output: the Einstein field equations), statement and proof: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list)

Theorem 14 (Geometric Channel output: the Einstein field equations). Given the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, Theorems 11--13, the Clausius relation δQ = T dS, and the Raychaudhuri equation for null congruences, the Einstein field equations

G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG)/(c⁴) T_μν

hold at every spacetime point.

Proof. The argument is Jacobson's 1995 thermodynamic derivation [7], applied to a local Rindler horizon at every spacetime event p ∈M_G and underwritten by the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework Geometric Channel inputs (Theorems 11--13). The local Rindler horizon is not an external scaffold imposed on the manifold: by the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, component (ii), x₄ expands spherically at rate c from every event, and the null surface this expansion sweeps out is the McGucken Sphere's null cone (Definition 2); the local Rindler horizon through p is precisely a patch of that Principle-generated null structure as seen by a uniformly accelerated observer. Consider an arbitrary spacetime point p and a local Rindler horizon H through p: a null hypersurface generated by a null congruence with affine parameter λ and tangent vector k^μ. The horizon is the boundary of the past of a uniformly accelerated observer with proper acceleration a in the local neighbourhood of p. The Rindler horizon-generating Killing vector χ^μ is parallel to k^μ on H, with χ^μ = -aλk^μ in the affine parametrisation [7, eq. (1)] — the Rindler-Killing-vector affine-parameter relation that supplies the factor of a canceling against the Unruh temperature.

Step 1 (heat flux through H). The heat flux carried across H by matter, defined as the boost-energy flux past the Rindler observer, is

δQ = ∫_H T_μν χ^μdΣ^ν = -∫_H T_μν (aλ) k^μk^νdλdA, (Q-flux)

where dΣ^ν = k^νdλdA is the null-congruence area-element-times-affine-parameter measure, and the minus sign comes from χ^μ = -aλk^μ.

Step 2 (entropy change from the area law). By Theorem 12, the entropy associated with the horizon H at any cross-section is S = k_B A/(4ℓ_P²). The differential entropy change for an area variation δA is

δS = k_B/(4ℓ_P²) δA. (S-area)

On a null congruence, the area variation along the congruence at parameter λ relates to the expansion θ via d(δA)/dλ = θδA, equivalently δA = -∫(dθ/dλ) λdλdA in the focusing limit (Step 3 below).

Step 3 (area change from Raychaudhuri). The Raychaudhuri equation for the null congruence generating H is

(dθ)/(dλ) = -1/2θ² - σ_μνσ^μν - R_μν k^μk^ν,

where θ is the expansion, σ_μν the shear, and R_μν the Ricci tensor. At the chosen event p (with θ(0) = 0 and σ(0) = 0 for the locally-stationary horizon), the leading-order behaviour is dθ/dλ = -R_μν k^μk^ν. The integrated area change up to affine parameter λ:

δA(λ) = ∫₀^λθ(λ') dA dλ' = -∫₀^λλ' R_μν k^μk^νdA dλ', (Ray)

where the second equality uses θ(λ) = ∫₀^λ(dθ/dλ')dλ' = -λR_μν k^μk^ν at leading order.

Step 4 (Clausius relation). Equate δQ = T_U δS with T_U = ħa/(2πc k_B) from Theorem 13. Substituting from (Q-flux), (S-area), and (Ray):

-∫_H T_μν (aλ) k^μk^νdλdA = (ħa)/(2πc k_B) ·k_B/(4ℓ_P²) ·(-∫_H λR_μν k^μk^νdλdA).

The factor a on each side cancels; the factor λ inside each integral cancels; the minus sign on each side cancels:

∫_H T_μν k^μk^νdλdA = (ħ)/(8πc ℓ_P²) ∫_H R_μν k^μk^νdλdA.

Using ℓ_P² = ħG/c³:

(ħ)/(8πc ℓ_P²) = (ħc³)/(8πc ħG) = (c²)/(8πG).

But T_μν has units of energy density and the integration dλdA has units of length × area = volume, while R_μν has units of inverse area. For dimensional consistency on the contraction with null k^μ (which are dimensionless tangent vectors on the affine null congruence), the equality reads:

T_μν k^μk^ν = (c⁴)/(8πG) R_μν k^μk^νfor all null k^μ, (14.1)

with the remaining factor of c² coming from the unit-conversion between the energy-flux measure (which intrinsically carries c from the relativistic T_μν definition) and the inverse-area Ricci measure.

Step 5 (conclusion: all null vectors → tensor identity). Equation (14.1) holds for every null vector k^μ at every spacetime point. The Newman-Penrose-type completeness of null vectors in the tangent space, together with the symmetry of both T_μν and R_μν, forces

T_μν = (c⁴)/(8πG)( R_μν - 1/2 R g_μν + Λg_μν ),

where:
- the trace term -1/2 R g_μν is forced by the requirement ∇^μT_μν = 0 (from Step 4 of Theorem 9, the on-shell enhancement), which by the contracted Bianchi identity ∇^μG_μν = 0 singles out the Einstein tensor G_μν = R_μν - 1/2Rg_μν over the bare Ricci tensor;
- the cosmological-constant term +Λg_μν enters as an integration constant (allowed because ∇^μg_μν = 0 identically).

Rearranging the conclusion gives (the Einstein field equations). □

Restatement in the present paper's notation. Given Theorems 4.3, 4.4, 4.6, the Clausius relation δQ = T dS, and the Raychaudhuri equation for null congruences, G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG/c⁴)T_μν holds at every event.

The Clausius relation is listed as a hypothesis here, as in Theorem 14 of [4]; Corollary 10.2 derives it from the modular structure of the McGucken Sphere-cogenerated wedge algebra (Theorem 10.1), so that after §10 the hypotheses of this theorem reduce to Theorems 4.3, 4.4, 4.6, and the Raychaudhuri identity (differential geometry on the metric of §2.1); the identification of the horizon entanglement entropy with the area law of Theorem 3.5 is Proposition 10.3.

Proof. The construction is Jacobson's [7], reproduced in full, with each input a theorem of §3 and the local horizon generated by the Principle. By §2.2 the null surface swept by the expansion of the McGucken Sphere from an event is the Sphere's null cone; the local Rindler horizon through p is the patch of that null structure seen by a uniformly accelerated observer — the null plane that is the limit of the Sphere's cone from a source event at large affine distance behind p, where the cone's expansion θ = 2/r and shear vanish, which is why the equilibrium conditions θ(p) = σ(p) = 0 hold on it. Let H be this horizon, generated by a null congruence with affine parameter λ and tangent k^μ, and let the approximate boost Killing vector be χ^μ = -(a/c²)λk^μ on H.

Step 1 (heat flux). The boost-energy flux of matter across H is

δQ = ∫_HT_μνχ^μdΣ^ν = -∫_HT_μν(aλ)/(c²)k^μk^νdλdA.

LTD reading: this is the Compton-tick action of the matter McGucken Spheres crossing the Principle-generated null cone of the accelerated observer; the generators k^μ are the lightfronts of the x₄-expansion.

Step 2 (entropy change). By Theorem 4.4, δS = (k_B/4ℓ_P²)δA. LTD reading: δS is the change in the McGucken Sphere's Compton-tick cell count on H.

Step 3 (area change). The Raychaudhuri equation dθ/dλ = -1/2θ² - σ_μνσ^μν - R_μνk^μk^ν gives, at leading order about θ(0) = σ(0) = 0, θ(λ) = -λR_μνk^μk^ν and

δA = ∫₀^λθdA dλ' = -∫₀^λλ'R_μνk^μk^νdA dλ'.

LTD reading: the expansion θ is the focusing of neighbouring McGucken Sphere lightfronts, and its matter-driven convergence is the x₄-expansion being lensed by Compton-tick energy — the derived focusing of §2.4.

Step 4 (Clausius). Equating δQ = T_UδS with T_U from Theorem 4.6, the factors a, λ, and the minus signs cancel, leaving

∫_HT_μνk^μk^νdλdA = (ħc)/(8πℓ_P²)∫_HR_μνk^μk^νdλdA, (ħc)/(8πℓ_P²) = (c⁴)/(8πG).

In natural units (c = ħ = k_B = 1): T_U = a/2π, η = 1/4ℓ_P² = 1/4G, and the Clausius relation gives T_μνk^μk^ν = (η/2π)R_μνk^μk^ν = R_μνk^μk^ν/8πG, Jacobson's result; restoring units the two bookkeepings agree, the c⁴ being carried by the c^-2 of the Killing vector, the c³ of ℓ_P^-2, and the c^-1 of the Unruh temperature. LTD reading: the Clausius relation here is the statement that the Compton-tick heat crossing the horizon equals the Euclidean x₄-period temperature times the increment of the McGucken Sphere's state count; every factor is a theorem of the Principle.

Step 5 (all null vectors). Since the identity holds for every null k^μ at every event, and both tensors are symmetric — the null vectors span the tangent space, so a symmetric bilinear form vanishing on all of them is a multiple of g_μν (Theorem 14, Step 5 of [4]: "the Newman-Penrose-type completeness of null vectors in the tangent space, together with the symmetry of both T_μν and R_μν") — T_μν = (c⁴/8πG)(R_μν + fg_μν) for some scalar f. Local conservation ∇^μT_μν = 0 (Theorem 4.1, Step 4) with the contracted Bianchi identity ∇^μG_μν = 0 forces f = -1/2R + Λ with Λ constant. Hence G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG/c⁴)T_μν. □

4.3 The two channels and the McGucken–Wick rotation

McGucken Principle anchor. The McGucken–Wick rotation τ = x₄/c is a theorem of the Principle (Theorem 4 of [4]; the thirty-four Wick-rotation inputs of quantum field theory derived in [21]): integrating dx₄/dt = ic along any worldline gives x₄ = ic(t - t₀) with the imaginary unit a feature of the integration itself. The two channels are distinguished by their mode of reasoning — algebraic-symmetry reasoning on the label x₄ = ict versus geometric-propagation reasoning on the active wavefront — and each uses the Wick rotation internally when its argument requires the other signature (the Algebraic Channel in the cigar computation, the Geometric Channel in the diffusion equation). Applying the rotation to one derivation does not produce the other: the Lovelock derivation and the Clausius derivation share no intermediate object, and what relates them is common descent from dx₄/dt = ic. The rotation acts as a diagnostic between them: Algebraic-Channel objects (-c² in the master equation, iħ∂_t, e^iS/ħ) transform under it, while Geometric-Channel objects (the McGucken Sphere as a 2-surface of radius c(t-t₀), the iterated-Sphere flow, the mode count) are signature-invariant.

The McWick Rotation and How It Differs from the Wick Rotation

Before reconstructing the 121-year historical lineage of the Wick rotation, we state explicitly the distinction between the orthodox Wick rotation as introduced by Wick 1954 and the McWick rotation as established by the present paper and its corpus references. This distinction is one of the major themes of the present paper; every later argument — the dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel / the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel dual-channel architecture of §30.9, the dissolution of the Hawking-Susskind black-hole war of §30.9.10.7, the McGucken Measurement Theorem of Theorem 30.9.27.5 — depends on the distinction being stated explicitly at the outset. We articulate the distinction along six axes and then identify the deepest physics that the orthodox tradition missed.

The Concise Statement of the Differentiation

The differentiation can be stated in one sentence: the orthodox Wick rotation is a static analytic continuation in a complex plane that has no physical referent and no physical agent; the McWick rotation is a dynamic coordinate identity on the real four-manifold whose fourth axis is physically expanding at the velocity of light per dx₄/dt = ic, performed physically by every measurement apparatus at every quantum-registration event, and accompanied by motion along the rotated-into axis as a kinematic necessity of the axis's own motion. The one is a formal device of complex analysis; the other is the operational signature of the physical invariant of contemporary physics, with kinematic content (the rotated object acquires the motion of the axis), diagnostic content (separator of the dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel and the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel), and operational-physics (performed by every measurement apparatus and by every horizon) all unified in a single coordinate identity on the real four-manifold of physics.

This is the central conceptual content of the present paper. The 121-year historical reconstruction of Parts I–III, the McWick Rotation Theorem of Part IV, the six closures of Part V, the four-mysteries collapse of §30.7, the Erlangen Double-Completion and Hilbert Sixth Problem solution of §30.8, the McGucken Duality framing of §30.9 (including the Hawking-Susskind black-hole war dissolution of §30.9.10.7 and the McGucken Measurement Theorem of Theorem 30.9.27.5), and the Synthesis of §§37–42 are jointly the case for the McWick rotation as a and kinematically richer object than the orthodox Wick rotation — with the orthodox rotation as the static formal-device shadow of the McGucken rotation's dynamic real-manifold content.

§22. The McGucken-Wick Rotation Theorem

The closure of the 121-year gap is the McGucken-Wick (McWick) Rotation Theorem, established as Theorem 9 of [21]. We state the theorem here in the form required for the present paper's reconstruction, with the proof structure summarized.

Theorem 22.1 (McWick Rotation; cf. [21, Theorem 9])

Statement. Under the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, the substitution

t ⟼-iτ, τ∈ℝ (22.1)

is identically the coordinate identification

τ = x₄/c (22.2)

on the real four-dimensional McGucken manifold 𝓜 with coordinates (x₁, x₂, x₃, x₄) [bracket correction: the source prints (x₄, x₄, x₄, x₄)]. Specifically, for any function F of time,

F(t)|_t →-iτ = F(-iτ) = F(x₄/ic) = F((-ix₄)/c), (22.3)

with the second equality holding by the coordinate identification τ = x₄/c and the integrated coordinate shadow x₄ = ict.

Proof structure. The proof proceeds in three steps.

Step 1 (The integrated coordinate shadow). The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic has integrated solution

x₄(t) = x₄(0) + ict, (22.4)

which, taking x_4(0) = 0 at the spacetime event under consideration, gives x₄ = ict as the integrated coordinate shadow of the active expansion. The relation (22.4) is not a notational convention; it is the integral of the McGucken Principle, with x₄ a real coordinate on 𝓜 and t the projected time coordinate on the Lorentzian spacetime M_3,t.

Step 2 (Inversion of the integrated relation). Inverting (22.4) gives

t = x₄/ic = (-ix₄)/c = -i ·x₄/c. (22.5)

Setting τ:= x_4/c, the inversion (22.5) becomes

t = -iτ. (22.6)

Step 3 (Coordinate-identity status of the Wick substitution). The substitution t → −iτ used in the orthodox Wick-rotation literature is identically the relation (22.6), with τ ∈ ℝ a real coordinate. Equation (22.6) is not an analytic continuation from a complex parameter; it is a coordinate identity on the real four-manifold 𝓜, with τ = x₄/c a rescaling of the real x₄-coordinate by the constant c.

For any function F of time, the substitution F(t) → F(-iτ) is therefore the coordinate-identity rewriting of F in terms of the τ = x₄/c coordinate rather than the t coordinate. The Wick substitution is a coordinate change of perspective on the real four-manifold 𝓜, not an analytic continuation of a complex parameter. ∎

Consequences of the Theorem

The McWick Rotation Theorem 22.1 has immediate consequences for the interpretation of every Wick-rotation application discussed in Parts I and II of the present paper.

Consequence 1 (Lorentzian-Euclidean signature as coordinate-change of perspective). The substitution t → −iτ is not a signature change from Lorentzian to Euclidean. It is a coordinate-change of perspective on the same real four-manifold 𝓜, with one reading using the projected coordinate t = x_4/(ic) (and inheriting the explicit i from the projection) and the other reading using the direct coordinate τ = x₄/c (with the i absorbed into the integrated coordinate shadow x₄ = ict).

Consequence 2 (Path-integral correspondence). The Feynman path integral ∫ 𝒟γ exp(iS[γ]/ħ) and the Wiener-process expectation ∫ 𝒟ω exp(−S_E[ω]/ħ) are two coordinate-change readings of the same underlying iterated McGucken Sphere expansion on 𝓜. The Universal McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel Theorem of [57, Theorem 7.9] establishes this as a Grade-1 theorem.

Consequence 3 (Operator-correspondence). The operator-level identity (16.1) — U(t) = e^-iĤ t/ħ and ρ_β = (1/Z) e^-βĤ related by τ = βħ = it — is the operator-algebraic shadow of the geometric coordinate identity τ = x₄/c. The two operators generate translation along the same axis x₄ on 𝓜, read in two different coordinate conventions.

Consequence 4 (KMS condition and Matsubara periodicity). The KMS condition ⟨Â(τ)B̂⟩_β = ⟨B̂Â(τ+ iβħ)⟩_β and the Matsubara periodicity φ(τ + βħ) = ±φ(τ) are operator-algebraic and functional-integral encodings of the periodic identification of the x₄-axis at thermal equilibrium, with period cβħ on 𝓜.

Consequence 5 (Hawking temperature). The Hawking temperature T_H = ħκ/(2πc) is the empirical signature of the x₄-axis periodic identification at the horizon, with the factor 2π being the geometry of the McGucken Sphere closure on the Euclidean cigar.

Consequence 6 (OS reflection positivity). The Osterwalder–Schrader reflection-positivity axiom is the mathematical encoding of the x_4 → -x_4 symmetry of the McGucken manifold — equivalent to the fact that the McWick rotation is the coordinate identity τ = x₄/c on a real manifold whose fourth axis is a real continuous coordinate ([21, Theorem 19]).

Theorem 19.4: The Signature-Bridging Theorem for G_μν (Hilbert–Jacobson Agreement)

We now state and prove the dual-channel derivation of the Einstein field equations G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG/c⁴) T_μν as the gravitational-tier instance of the McGucken Duality, placing the Hilbert–Jacobson agreement alongside the Heisenberg–Feynman (Theorem 19.3) and Feynman–Wiener (Theorem 19) agreements as the third forced dual-channel agreement of dx₄/dt = ic.

Theorem 19.4 (Signature-Bridging for G_μν; cf. [3, Theorem 6.1], [17, Theorem 23]). Under the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, the Einstein field equations G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG/c⁴)T_μν admit two derivations from dx₄/dt = ic that share no intermediate machinery:

(i) the dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel — Hilbert variational derivation (Lorentzian signature). The Einstein–Hilbert action S_EH = (c⁴/16πG)∫d⁴ x √(-g) (R - 2Λ) is the unique diffeomorphism-invariant second-order scalar Lagrangian on the McGucken manifold, by Lovelock's theorem (Lovelock 1971 [23], reduced to its physics by Father-Symmetry classification of [16, Proposition 45]). Variation of S_EH with respect to the spatial-three-metric (the deformable slice, in the invariant/deformable split of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework; the x₄-axis is invariant) yields G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG/c⁴)T_μν. The route is purely Lorentzian and purely algebraic-symmetry-content, operating on the diffeomorphism-invariance content of dx₄/dt = ic.

(ii) The Geometric Channel — Jacobson thermodynamic derivation (Euclidean signature). By the Bekenstein–Hawking horizon-area entropy S_BH = (c³/4ħG) A applied to local Rindler horizons in the local-equilibrium limit (Jacobson 1995 [7]), the Clausius relation δQ = TδS applied across any local Rindler horizon — with T = ħa/(2πc ) the Unruh temperature of the accelerated observer at proper acceleration a and δS = (c³/4ħG) δA the entropy change associated with the area change δA — yields the Einstein field equations as a local thermodynamic identity. The route is Euclidean (operating through the imaginary-time periodicity of the Wick-rotated Schwarzschild section that fixes the Unruh temperature) and purely geometric-propagation-content, operating on the Compton-coupled Brownian dissolution of mode count on the McGucken-Sphere horizon screen.

The two routes share no intermediate machinery and proceed through derivationally disjoint logical chains. They converge on the same equation G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG/c⁴)T_μν as the same theorem of dx₄/dt = ic read through two derivationally distinct extraction procedures. The McGucken-Wick rotation τ = x₄/c is the universal coordinate identification on the real four-manifold that bridges the two signatures.

Proof. Algebraic Channel (Hilbert). By Theorem 23 of [4], the Einstein–Hilbert variational principle, applied to the unique diffeomorphism-invariant second-order scalar Lagrangian on a four-dimensional McGucken manifold with invariant x₄-axis and deformable spatial three-slice, yields G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG/c⁴)T_μν as the Euler–Lagrange equation. The uniqueness of the Einstein–Hilbert Lagrangian is forced by Lovelock 1971 (in its physics content, a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic via [16, Proposition 45]): in four spacetime dimensions with diffeomorphism invariance and second-derivative-at-most Lagrangian, the Einstein–Hilbert action is the unique (up to constants) scalar Lagrangian whose variational principle yields a second-order tensor field equation with the Bianchi identity preserved. The four-dimensions content is forced by the Disjunctive Forcing Theorem of [17, §X.7] from dx₄/dt = ic (the four-velocity budget u^μu_μ = -c² requires exactly four spacetime dimensions); the diffeomorphism-invariance content is forced by the moving-dimension geometry of [14, Defs. 5.1–5.4]. The Algebraic Channel derivation is therefore complete and uses only algebraic-symmetry content (diffeomorphism invariance + Lovelock uniqueness + Hilbert variational principle) of dx₄/dt = ic in Lorentzian signature.

Theorem 19.4.2 (The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Satisfies the Marolf Constraint on Emergent Gravity; Foundational Non-Locality is Intrinsic to the Principle)

We now establish a substantial result connecting the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's gravitational content to the most precise contemporary constraint on emergent-gravity programs: the Marolf Constraint [159], articulated by Don Marolf of UCSB and discussed at length by Sean Carroll on the Mindscape podcast with Daniel Harlow as a philosophical objection to any local-lattice substrate-emergence program for gravity [186] and again, by Ted Jacobson in his 2025 interview with Curt Jaimungal on Theories of Everything [1] [bracket correction: the source [3] attributes this interview to Sean Carroll and the Mindscape podcast; the speaker is Jacobson and the venue is Theories of Everything, verified against the transcript]. The Marolf Constraint is the sharpest contemporary result on what kind of foundational kinematics is admissible for any theory from which gravity is to emerge or descend. We demonstrate that the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic satisfies the constraint by virtue of the McGucken Sphere null-connectivity structure of Theorem 30 of the present paper.

The Marolf Constraint, stated precisely (verbatim from primary source). In the Theories of Everything interview [1] at approximately 44:00 to 45:46, Ted Jacobson [bracket correction: the source [3] reads "In the Mindscape podcast of 2024 [161] … Sean Carroll"] articulates the Marolf Constraint in primary-source form as the argument that gravity cannot emerge from a substrate of locally commuting operators at spacelike separation:

> "So there's a very interesting observation by Don Marolf of UCSB about a constraint on possible emergence of gravity. He made a pretty cogent argument that gravity cannot emerge, gravity I would say in spacetime also, from a system which has locally defined observables that can be simultaneously precise at space-like separation. So technically what he's saying is it can't be described by commuting operators... Marolf made the observation that if something really behaves like general relativity emerges that way, the Hamiltonian that governs its time translation has to be a flux integral at the boundary, let's say a large spatial boundary. And then he inferred from that that no system with that property can emerge if its starting point is based on local kinematics with observables that commute with each other at space-like separation... the concept of it is that there must be a non-locality built into the very structure from which spacetime and gravity are emerging." (Jacobson's exposition of Marolf's argument, [1] at ~44:00 to 45:46 [bracket correction: "Carroll exposition … [161] at ~43:30 to 45:50" in [3]])

Jacobson's second exposition of the Marolf Constraint [bracket correction: "Carroll's" in [3]], at approximately 1:07:14 to 1:10:10, articulates the boundary-unitarity content:

> "In general relativity, the symmetry is so huge that the way we coordinate space and time, the numbers we assign to label points in space and time are completely different... and one consequence it has is that the dynamics of everything inside a bulk of spacetime is generated in this mathematical sense by the Hamiltonian operator that actually is a surface integral at the boundary. Marolf calls it the gravitational flux integral. It's sort of analogous to the way you can measure the total electric charge in a region of space by surrounding that region with a big surface and measuring the flux of the electric field through the surface. And that'll tell you how much charge is inside there. Similarly, in gravity, if you measure the flux of this quantity, very far away, that includes everything in space, you'll know how much energy is in the space." (Jacobson's exposition of Marolf's gravitational flux integral and boundary unitarity, [1] at ~1:07:14 to 1:10:10 [bracket correction: "Carroll exposition … [161]" in [3]])

The content of the Marolf Constraint, condensed:

(MC1) Diffeomorphism invariance forces the Hamiltonian to be a boundary flux integral. In any theory genuinely realizing general relativity, the time-translation generator (the Hamiltonian) is a surface integral at the spatial boundary of the system — the gravitational flux integral, analogous to the Gauss-law surface integral measuring the total electric charge inside a region by integrating the electric flux through the bounding surface.

(MC2) Boundary-unitarity follows. Since the Hamiltonian is a boundary observable, the time-evolution of any observable in the bulk is governed entirely by the algebra of boundary observables. The bulk dynamics is "boundary unitary" — closed under time-evolution within the boundary observable algebra.

(MC3) Local-commuting kinematics at spacelike separation cannot produce (MC1)–(MC2). If the foundational substrate consists of locally defined observables that commute at spacelike separation (the standard structure of any naive lattice or local-quantum-field-theory substrate), there is no mechanism to produce the boundary-flux-integral Hamiltonian of (MC1). The bulk-to-boundary algebraic structure required by general relativity is incompatible with local-commuting substrate kinematics.

(MC4) Non-locality must be built into the foundational structure. Therefore: any theory from which gravity is to genuinely emerge or descend must have foundational non-locality — non-locality not at the emergent-gravitational level but at the foundational-kinematic level of the substrate itself.

The Marolf Constraint rules out the entire class of naive-lattice, local-discrete-substrate, condensed-matter-analogue, and local-quantum-field-theory emergent-gravity programs. It is the sharpest contemporary objection to any attempt to derive gravity from a local kinematic foundation.

Theorem 19.4.2 (The McGucken Principle Satisfies the Marolf Constraint). Under the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, the foundational kinematics of the McGucken manifold satisfies the Marolf Constraint (MC1)–(MC4) intrinsically — non-locality is built into the foundational structure of the principle via the McGucken Sphere null-connectivity at every spacetime event (Theorem 30 of the present paper). Specifically:

(i) The foundational kinematics of dx₄/dt = ic is the McGucken Sphere structure at every event. The principle places at every spacetime event p a spherically symmetric expansion of x₄ at rate c, producing the McGucken Sphere Σ_+(p) as the future null cone of p. The Sphere Σ_+(p) is a null hypersurface in the 4-manifold; every event on the Sphere is null-separated from p. This is the foundational kinematic structure of the principle — not derived, not emergent, but supplied directly by the active spherical expansion at +ic.

(ii) The McGucken Sphere is intrinsically non-local in Marolf's sense. Events that appear spacelike-separated in any 3D spatial-slice projection (e.g., Alice at 𝐱_A and Bob at 𝐱_B with |𝐱_A - 𝐱_B| macroscopic) are geometrically local on the 4D null surface Σ_+(p₀) of their common source event p₀. (iii) Therefore dx₄/dt = ic does not have locally-commuting observables at spacelike separation. The McGucken-Sphere null-connectivity structure means that observables associated with events on Σ_+(p₀) are correlated through the 4D null structure of the Sphere, not through the 3D spatial projection. The standard structure of a local-commuting substrate (operators at spacelike-separated 3D points commuting because they cannot communicate through 3D propagation) is not the foundational structure of dx₄/dt = ic. The foundational structure is the McGucken Sphere itself, which is intrinsically a 4D null surface with non-local 3D-slice projection. The Marolf Constraint condition (MC3) (failure of local-commuting kinematics at spacelike separation) is therefore satisfied at the foundational level.

(iv) The gravitational flux integral emerges from dx₄/dt = ic via the McGucken-Sphere asymptotic structure. The McGucken Sphere Σ_+(p) at a spacetime event p, taken in the asymptotic limit of large coordinate distance, becomes the asymptotic null infinity ℐ^+ of the spacetime — the boundary at which the gravitational flux integral of Marolf (and the ADM/Komar mass integrals of standard general relativity [162, 163]) is evaluated. The Hamiltonian-as-boundary-flux-integral content of (MC1) emerges naturally from dx₄/dt = ic because the principle's foundational kinematic object (the McGucken Sphere) is itself the locus of the boundary flux integral in the asymptotic limit. Diffeomorphism invariance on the McGucken manifold, established as the algebraic-symmetry content of dx₄/dt = ic in the Algebraic Channel derivation of Theorem 19.4 of the present paper, then forces the Hamiltonian to be a boundary integral on this asymptotic structure (MC1). The boundary-unitarity content of (MC2) follows from the algebraic closure of the boundary-observable algebra under time-evolution generated by the boundary flux integral.

(v) The McGucken Principle is therefore foundationally non-local in exactly Marolf's sense. The "non-locality built into the very structure" that Marolf identifies as required for any gravity-producing foundational substrate is, in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, the McGucken Sphere null-connectivity structure of dx₄/dt = ic itself. The non-locality is not added on top of a local substrate; it is constitutive of the principle.

(ii) is the content of Theorem 30 (Quantum Nonlocality as McGucken-Sphere Null-Separation) of the present paper applied to general spacetime-event pairs rather than only to entangled-photon detection events. Primary-Source Note on the Three-Mechanism Marolf Response and the Operator-Algebra Open Acknowledgment

The Marolf-constraint-satisfaction structure of Theorem 19.4.2 has its historical-first primary-source articulation in [21 §V] (April 12, 2026), where three mechanisms are identified by which dx₄/dt = ic supplies the kinematic non-locality Marolf requires:

(M1) Global single rate. "x₄'s expansion is a single global process, not a collection of local processes. The rate dx₄/dt = ic is the same everywhere — it is an invariant of the spacetime, not a field that varies from point to point. This means x₄'s expansion cannot be decomposed into independently specifiable local degrees of freedom" ([21 §V.2, mechanism (i)]).

(M2) Shared McGucken Sphere origins. "Two particles that share a common origin — that were once in local contact — remain connected through x₄'s expansion: they share a common McGucken Sphere. As they separate in the three spatial dimensions, they remain at the same x₄ coordinate (because x₄'s expansion carries them equally), and thus remain entangled" ([21 §V.2, mechanism (ii)]). This is the primary-source articulation of "all nonlocality begins as locality" — locality distributed into spatial nonlocality by x₄'s expansion.

(M3) Hamiltonian-as-boundary-flux content. "The total energy associated with x₄'s expansion through a region is encoded on the boundary of that region — the McGucken Sphere — precisely because x₄'s expansion is invariant and global, and the only measurable quantity is how the spatial metric deforms in response to it. This is analogous to the boundary-Hamiltonian property that Marolf identifies as the hallmark of gravitational theories" ([21 §V.2, mechanism (iii)]).

[21 §V.2 closing] explicitly acknowledges that the operator-algebra-level closure of the Marolf-constraint satisfaction remains open: "Whether this form of nonlocality rigorously satisfies Marolf's constraint — in particular, whether the operator algebra of observables on the McGucken Sphere fails to commute at spacelike separation in the required way — is an open question that requires further mathematical development. From [3], verbatim — Theorem 19.5 (Channel Asymmetry — the Algebraic Channel is Lorentzian-Locked, the Geometric Channel is Bi-Signature), statement and proof: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list; theorem numbers inside the quotation are those of [3])

Theorem 19.5: Channel Asymmetry — the Algebraic Channel is Lorentzian-Locked, the Geometric Channel is Bi-Signature

We now state and prove the diagnosis of the asymmetry between the two channels of the McGucken Duality. This diagnosis answers the question: why is the dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel mono-signature (uniformly Lorentzian) while the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel is bi-signature (admitting both Lorentzian and Euclidean readings)? The diagnosis is itself a theorem about the McGucken Principle, supplied in full by [3, §6.2] and adapted here.

Theorem 19.5 (Channel Asymmetry). Under the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, the algebraic-symmetry channel (the dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel) is Lorentzian-locked: it has only the Lorentzian-signature reading. The geometric-propagation channel (the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel) is bi-signature: it has both Lorentzian and Euclidean signature readings, related by the McGucken-Wick rotation τ = x₄/c. The asymmetry is forced by the status of the imaginary unit i in dx₄/dt = ic: the i is interior to the Algebraic Channel (it is the algebraic invariance content of the principle being read) and exteriorisable in the Geometric Channel (it can be moved from the interior of the path weight to the exterior coordinate frame via the McGucken-Wick rotation, becoming a real coordinate identification on the real four-manifold).

Proof in four steps.

Step 1 (Locate the imaginary unit i in dx₄/dt = ic). The principle dx₄/dt = ic contains a single load-bearing imaginary unit i, multiplying the rate c. The i is not a notational decoration; it is the algebraic record of x₄'s perpendicularity to the three spatial dimensions x₁, x₂, x₃ — the foundational geometric fact that the fourth direction of spacetime is not parallel to any spatial direction but is square-rooted-negative against the spatial three-slice. The i is what makes the four-velocity budget u^μu_μ = -c² hold with a negative sign in the time component (Proposition H.1), what makes the Minkowski line element (induced by x₄ = ict, the integrated coordinate shadow of dx₄/dt = ic) ds² = dx² + dy² + dz² - c² dt² have the (-,+,+,+) signature, and what makes the McGucken-Wick rotation a non-trivial rotation rather than a passive relabelling. The status of this i — whether it sits interior to a derivation as a fixed algebraic fact, or exterior to a derivation as a coordinate convention available for rotation — is the key to the signature asymmetry of the McGucken Duality.

Step 2 (The i is interior to the Algebraic Channel). Algebraic Channel reads dx₄/dt = ic as a statement about invariance: the rate ic is unchanged under translations, rotations, and Lorentz boosts that respect the McGucken-foliation structure. The unitary representations of these symmetries (Stone's theorem on translation, the Wigner classification on Poincaré, the Stone–von Neumann theorem on canonical commutation) involve operators of the form exp(-isp̂_i/ħ), exp(-iĤ t/ħ), exp(-iθĴ_z/ħ) — every one of which carries the i interior. The i in these unitary operators is the same i that appears in dx₄/dt = ic: it is the algebraic record of the perpendicularity of x₄ that propagates from the McGucken Principle into the operator algebra of Stone-theorem unitaries.

Applying the McGucken-Wick rotation to an Algebraic Channel unitary — that is, performing the exteriorisation operation that removes the i from the interior of the operator — replaces the unitary group with a different mathematical object: an exponentiated semigroup exp(-τĤ/ħ). The result is no longer an Algebraic Channel reading: a semigroup of self-adjoint exponentials is not a unitary representation of a symmetry group; it is a propagation-evolution kernel. The i is therefore not available for exteriorisation in the Algebraic Channel: it is the feature being read as the invariance content of the principle, and removing it would dissolve the Algebraic Channel entirely. Hence the Algebraic Channel is Lorentzian-locked. The Lorentzian signature is the i in dx₄/dt = ic read as the invariance content of the principle.

Step 3 (The i is exteriorisable in the Geometric Channel). Geometric Channel reads dx₄/dt = ic as a statement about propagation: the rate c drives spherical expansion of x₄ from every spacetime event, producing iterated McGucken Spheres on which wavefronts, paths, and entropies propagate. The i in dx₄/dt = ic enters the Geometric Channel through the phase-accumulation rule: each iterated McGucken Sphere path γ carries the phase factor exp(iS[γ]/ħ) by virtue of the Compton-frequency oscillation ω_C = mc²/ħ of x₄-phase along γ (Proposition L.3).

But here an option appears that is not available in the Algebraic Channel: the geometric propagation along iterated McGucken Spheres can be re-parameterised by treating the τ = x₄/c coordinate axis as a real positive coordinate rather than as an imaginary one. Under this re-parameterisation, the phase factor exp(iS[γ]/ħ) (Lorentzian reading, i interior) becomes the measure factor exp(-S_E[γ]/ħ) (Euclidean reading, i exteriorised onto the τ-axis as a real positive coordinate; Theorem 19, Step 3). The same iterated McGucken Sphere expansion generates both readings, with the i operating interior in the Lorentzian reading and exterior (on the τ-coordinate axis) in the Euclidean reading.

The McGucken-Wick rotation t →-iτ, τ = x₄/c — the physically forced rotation that exists because dx₄/dt = ic is a real physical statement about an actually expanding fourth dimension, not a formal analytic-continuation device on a complex t-plane — is, on this diagnosis, the exteriorisation operation on the i: it moves the i from the interior of the path weight (phase factor exp(iS/ħ)) to the exterior of the coordinate frame (real τ-axis on the real McGucken manifold). The McGucken-Wick rotation is therefore the operation by which Geometric Channel's bi-signature character is realised.

Step 4 (Closure: the asymmetry is forced). The asymmetry between the two channels is therefore not arbitrary but is forced by the position of the i in the principle. The Algebraic Channel reads the i as the invariance content, which makes the i interior and non-exteriorisable; the channel is Lorentzian-locked. The Geometric Channel reads the i as the phase, which makes the i exteriorisable onto the coordinate axis; the channel is bi-signature. The McGucken-Wick rotation is the exteriorisation operation that bridges the Geometric Channel's two signature-readings, and it is unavailable in the Algebraic Channel by the same reason.

This closes the diagnosis. The asymmetry observed empirically — the Algebraic Channel producing Heisenberg matrix mechanics (Lorentzian) and Hilbert variational G_μν (Lorentzian); the Geometric Channel producing both the Feynman path integral (Lorentzian) and the Wiener process (Euclidean), both the Lorentzian Schwarzschild metric and the Euclidean cigar — is the consequence of the position of the i in dx₄/dt = ic, read as invariance content (the Algebraic Channel) versus phase (the Geometric Channel).  ∎

corollary 19.5.1. The McGucken-Wick rotation is uniquely available to the Geometric Channel because the i is uniquely exteriorisable from the Geometric Channel. No formal analytic continuation can be performed on the Algebraic Channel without dissolving the channel itself; the symmetry content of dx₄/dt = ic is intrinsically Lorentzian. The bi-signature character of the Geometric Channel is therefore not a formal artifact of the path-integral formalism (as the orthodox tradition has read it for seventy-five years) but a feature of the geometric-propagation content of dx₄/dt = ic.

corollary 19.5.2. The three forced agreements (Heisenberg–Feynman, Feynman–Wiener, Hilbert–Jacobson) have different signature-structure depending on whether the Geometric Channel's Lorentzian or Euclidean reading is the partner of the Algebraic Channel in each agreement:

- Hilbert–Jacobson (gravitational instance, Theorem 19.4). The agreement is cross-signature cross-channel, bridged by the McGucken-Wick rotation.

The three agreements collectively exhibit the channel-asymmetric structure of the McGucken Duality across the three tiers of foundational physics.

Corollary 19.5.3: Wick Rotation Destroys the Algebraic Channel's Unitary Structure at the Measurement Event

We now state a restricted consequence of Theorem 19.5's channel asymmetry that follows directly from Theorem 19.5 Step 2 without further derivation: the McGucken-Wick rotation τ = x₄/c, considered as a formal mathematical operation, dissolves the dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel's integrity by exteriorizing the i from the interior of any Stone unitary exp(-iĤ t/ħ), producing a self-adjoint exponentiated semigroup exp(-τĤ/ħ) that is no longer a unitary representation of a symmetry group. This is established as Step 2 of Theorem 19.5 of the present paper. The consequence, applied at the apparatus-performed Wick rotation of Theorem 25, is:

Corollary 19.5.3 (Wick rotation destroys the dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel). Under the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, the Wick rotation τ = x₄/c — whether considered as a formal mathematical operation or as the apparatus-performed physical process at the registration event identified in Theorem 25 of the present paper — cannot be applied to the Algebraic Channel without dissolving the Algebraic Channel's integrity. Specifically: the substitution t →-iτ applied to the Stone unitary Û(t) = exp(-iĤ t/ħ) produces exp(-τĤ/ħ), which is a self-adjoint exponentiated semigroup rather than a unitary representation of a one-parameter symmetry group. The Wick rotation is therefore unavailable to the Algebraic Channel in the sense established by Theorem 19.5 Step 2: no formal analytic continuation that exteriorizes the interior i from an Algebraic Channel unitary preserves the Algebraic Channel's content.

Primary-source corpus articulation. The Wick-destroys-Algebraic Channel of this corollary receives its master primary-source articulation in [20, Theorem 30.9.2] as the bi-conditional diagnostic of the McGucken Duality: "a reading is the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel if and only if it has the McWick rotation as a non-trivial signature change without dissolving its structure; a reading is the Algebraic Channel if and only if applying the rotation dissolves its structure (converting a unitary representation into a self-adjoint contraction semigroup, which is no longer a Lie-group symmetry representation but a propagation kernel)." [20, Theorem 30.9.10.9.1] (the Cross-Field Wick-Rotation Response Corollary) supplies the explicit two-response classification: Algebraic Channel is destroyed and the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel is transported under the rotation, with the response on a given derivation determining its channel assignment. Corollary 19.5.3 of the present paper is the matter-tier specialization of [20, Theorem 30.9.10.9.1] applied to the Stone-unitary content of Û(t) = exp(-iĤ t/ħ).

Proof. Direct from Theorem 19.5 Step 2 of the present paper, with primary-source corpus articulation supplied by [20, Theorem 30.9.2 + Theorem 30.9.10.9.1]. Rigor grade: G1.

Physical interpretation at the measurement event (G2). Theorem 25 of the present paper identifies quantum measurement as the McGucken-Wick rotation τ = x₄/c performed physically by the apparatus's N ∼10²3 Compton-coupled degrees of freedom at localization rate Γ_Wick ∼Nω_C ∼10⁴7 s^-1. What this corollary does NOT establish. We list explicitly what is not claimed by Corollary 19.5.3, so as to avoid the overreach that an unqualified reading of the corollary might invite:

(i) No claim is made that the Wick rotation "transports the Geometric Channel" at the measurement event in a sense that supplies the Born density |ψ|² as a derived consequence of the apparatus's physical Wick operation. The transport of the Geometric Channel from Lorentzian to Euclidean signature (exp(iS/ħ) →exp(-S_E/ħ) under t →-iτ, Theorem 19.5 Step 3) is a mathematical signature-change on path-integral expressions; identifying this with the physical mechanism by which the apparatus extracts the Born density at a specific point on the spatial three-slice requires further derivation that the present paper does not supply in line.

(ii) No claim is made about the status of canonical conjugate observable pairs (Ĥ, t), (L̂_z, φ̂), (N̂, φ̂) beyond the position-momentum case. The energy-time pair is a Fourier conjugacy, not a canonical operator commutator (Pauli 1933 rules out a self-adjoint time operator on the standard Hilbert space). The angular-momentum-azimuthal-angle pair has well-documented domain incompatibilities (Judge 1963, Carruthers-Nieto 1968) under which the would-be Robertson-Schrödinger bound is empirically violated for sharp-L_z states. The number-phase pair has no self-adjoint phase operator on the Fock space (Susskind-Glogower 1964); the Pegg-Barnett 1989 formalism supplies a self-adjoint phase only on a truncated Hilbert space. The channel-conjugacy claim of Corollary 19.5.3 is therefore restricted to the position-momentum case (q̂, p̂) on the standard Schrödinger representation, where [q̂, p̂] = iħ holds rigorously with Stone–von Neumann uniqueness (Theorem 19.1 of present paper) closing the representation theory. Position q̂ is a geometric spatial-localization quantity (the Geometric Channel reading: where the particle is found on the spatial three-slice); momentum p̂ is the Stone-translation generator of spatial-translation invariance of dx₄/dt = ic (the Algebraic Channel reading via Theorem 4 of the present paper). The non-commutativity [q̂, p̂] = iħ has the channel-pairing reading at the operator level. Rigor grade: G1 for the position-momentum pair, with the channel-pairing reading consistent with the McGucken Duality of Theorem 19.5 but not constituting an independent derivation of [q̂, p̂] = iħ from the channel structure — the canonical commutator is itself a dual-channel derived theorem of dx₄/dt = ic per Theorem 19.3 of the present paper, with the i in the commutator traced to the perpendicularity content of x₄ = ict via [18, Theorem 10] (an external reference not derived in line in the present paper).

(iii) No claim is made that Geometric Channel and the Algebraic Channel are "perpendicular" in any sense beyond the algebraic-disjointness of derivation chains (Theorems 19.3, 19.4 of the present paper) and the operational distinction in their response to the Wick rotation (Theorem 19.5: the Algebraic Channel dissolves, the Geometric Channel's Lorentzian and Euclidean readings are related). Stronger "perpendicularity" claims — that the channels are perpendicular in the geometric sense that x₄ is perpendicular to (x₁, x₂, x₃), or that conjugate observables in QM are non-commuting because they are channel-perpendicular readings — require the operator-level bridge from the i in dx₄/dt = ic to the i in [q̂, p̂] = iħ supplied by [18, Theorem 10], which the present paper does not derive in line. - Pythagorean violation. On a Cartesian tile lattice, the number of lattice steps along the side of a square of side L is L/ℓ, and the number of steps along the diagonal of the same square is also L/ℓ (since the diagonal is traversed by alternating x̂ and ŷ steps), yielding effective diagonal-length L/ℓ·ℓ = L rather than L√(2) as required by Pythagoras.
- Rotational anisotropy. A measuring rod aligned with x̂ has lattice-length L/ℓ steps; the same rod rotated to a generic direction at angle θ to x̂ has lattice-length depending on θ via the lattice-traversal projection, yielding anisotropic length.

The four-cell architecture supplies the complete diagnosis of the Geometric Channel: every Geometric Channel of physics falls into one of the four cells, and the bridges relate the cells in a explicit way. The Bekenstein–Hawking entropy lives in (discrete, Euclidean) — Planck-scale resolution, McGucken-Wick-rotated. The smooth Schrödinger evolution lives in (continuous, Lorentzian). The Wiener process lives in (continuous, Euclidean). The horizon-mode count of the Bekenstein information bound lives in (discrete, Lorentzian). Each cell is independently supported by an orthodox-literature primary source and independently derived as a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic in the McGucken framework.

Falsifiability Content of Theorem 19.5.2

Three explicit empirical tests of the resolution-content diagnosis:

- Test A (the Planck length is Lorentz scalar). If any future measurement establishes that ℓ_P = √(ħG/c³) is not Lorentz-invariant — that some observer assigns a different Planck length than another inertial observer for the same fundamental physics — the Lorentz-invariance content of Theorem 19.5.2(iii) is refuted. To date no such measurement has been performed; the Lorentz-invariance of ħ, G, and c is established to high precision (the Planck constant ħ is the foundational constant of quantum mechanics with no frame-dependent variation observed; the gravitational constant G is the foundational constant of general relativity with no frame-dependent variation observed; the speed of light c is the foundational scalar of special relativity with frame-invariance tested to one part in 10¹7 in modern Michelson–Morley refinements [150, 151]).
- Test B (the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy is Lorentz-invariant). If any future measurement of black-hole horizon properties establishes that the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy S_BH = A/(4ℓ_P²) is observer-dependent in a frame-non-trivial way — that some observer reports S_BH different from another's by an amount not accounted for by the standard Lorentz-area transformation of horizons — the Lorentz-invariance content of Theorem 19.5.2(vi) at the horizon scale is refuted. To date no such measurement has been performed; the Lorentz-invariance of horizon area is established in classical general relativity [127, 144].
- Test C (chiral fermions on the McGucken manifold do not exhibit fermion-doubling). If any future theoretical or experimental analysis establishes that the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's continuum reading of chiral fermions on the Lorentzian 4-manifold combined with the Planck-scale discretization of x₄-stepping and Sphere mode count generates fermion doublers or breaks chiral symmetry, the Nielsen–Ninomiya dissolution content of Theorem 19.5.2(v) is refuted. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's commitment is that the chiral content lives in the dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel on the continuous 4-manifold, with the discrete content of the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel being orthogonal to it; no doublers are predicted and no chiral anomaly is predicted from the discreteness of the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel. The Standard Model's observed chiral structure (electroweak SU(2)_L, the absence of right-handed neutrino in the standard sector, the gauge-anomaly cancellation between fermion generations) is consistent with this prediction.

Restatement in the present paper's notation. (i) Every law derived in the Algebraic Channel is invariant under time reversal. (ii) The Second Law dS/dt > 0 has no Algebraic-Channel derivation. (iii) The Einstein field equations have derivations in both channels. (iv) Thermodynamics and gravity therefore share exactly the Geometric Channel, and every derivation of gravity that uses an entropy, a temperature, or the Second Law is a Geometric-Channel derivation.

Proof. (i) The Algebraic Channel derives from the symmetry group of x₄ = ict and the variational apparatus built on it (§4.1). The Poincaré group contains the orthochronous transformations only, but the Lagrangian objects it acts on — the metric η_μν, the Einstein–Hilbert scalar R√(-g), the matter actions — are even under t→-t, and the quantum objects — the unitary group U(t) = e^-iHt/ħ, whose inverse U(-t) lies in the same group, and the commutator [q̂,p̂] = iħ, invariant under the antiunitary T that sends t→-t, i→-i — are time-reversal invariant. Any theorem derived by symmetry and variation from these objects inherits the invariance. (ii) A strict monotone dS/dt > 0 is odd under t→-t. By (i) it cannot be a theorem of the Algebraic Channel. Its derivation in Theorem 3.3 uses the retarded propagator selected by the sign of +ic, which only the Geometric Channel reads. (iii) Theorem 4.1 is the Algebraic-Channel derivation; Theorem 4.7 is the Geometric-Channel derivation; Corollary 4.8 states their agreement. The field equations are time-reversal invariant, consistent with (i). (iv) follows from (ii) and (iii): the Geometric Channel is the only channel carrying thermodynamics, and it also carries gravity. A derivation of gravity from δQ = T dS uses S and T, which exist only in the channel carrying the +ic orientation. □

Corollary 5.2 (What "gravity is entropy" asserts, exactly). The equivalence is the statement that the Geometric-Channel derivation of the Einstein field equations runs through the thermodynamic quantities of §3. It holds in that channel. It is silent about the Algebraic Channel, in which the same field equations are derived with no entropy, temperature, or arrow. Gravity is therefore thermodynamic in the Geometric Channel and symmetry-derived in the Algebraic Channel; thermodynamics is Geometric-Channel only.

Proof. By Theorem 5.1(iii) the field equations have two derivations. The Geometric-Channel derivation (Theorem 4.7) takes the Second Law, the area law, and the Unruh temperature of §3 as inputs, so within that channel the field equations are consequences of thermodynamic quantities, which is the equivalence asserted. The Algebraic-Channel derivation (Theorem 4.1, Corollary 4.2) uses none of these quantities, so the equivalence makes no statement about it. By Theorem 5.1(ii) thermodynamics has no Algebraic-Channel derivation, so thermodynamics is Geometric-Channel only. □

Corollary 5.3 (Why gravity "already knows" thermodynamics). The agreement that Jacobson found between Einstein's equations and the Second Law is a consequence of the shared derivation: both are derived from the expansion of the McGucken Sphere — gravity from the horizon-area reading of the state count Ω (Theorem 3.5, Theorem 4.7) and the Second Law from the +ic-oriented growth of the same Ω (Theorem 3.3). Both descend from one premise, the expansion of the McGucken Sphere at c from every event, and the agreement is forced.

Proof. The Einstein field equations in the Geometric Channel are derived from the Clausius relation on the McGucken Sphere's null cone (Theorem 4.7 Step 4), in which δS is the increment of the count Ω on the horizon (Theorem 3.5) and the Second Law is the growth of the same count under the +ic-oriented advance (Theorem 3.3, Theorem 3.6). The two laws are therefore two statements about one quantity, the count Ω of the McGucken Sphere: the field equations state how its horizon reading changes when energy crosses the cone, and the Second Law states that its total reading never decreases. A law about how Ω changes and a law that Ω increases cannot disagree when both are derived from the advance of the McGucken Sphere that generates Ω; their agreement is forced by common descent, which is what Jacobson observed as general relativity having "known" about thermodynamics (§7.0 item 1). □

Corollary 5.4 (The arrow of time lives in the route, not in the field equations). The same equations arrive with the arrow (Geometric Channel) and without it (Algebraic Channel). The arrow is in the thermodynamic route to the equations because that route runs through the +ic-oriented expansion.

Proof. By Theorem 5.1(i) the field equations, having an Algebraic-Channel derivation (Theorem 4.1), are time-reversal invariant, so no arrow is in the equations themselves. The Geometric-Channel derivation (Theorem 4.7) uses the Second Law (Theorem 4.3) and the retarded null congruence of the McGucken Sphere's cone, both of which carry the +ic orientation of §2.2; by Theorem 5.1(ii) that orientation has no Algebraic-Channel expression. The arrow is therefore present in the Geometric-Channel route and absent from the output, which is the statement. □

5.1bis The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Reading of "gravity is attractive": a one-way statement on the same footing as "entropy increases"

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality. This subsection states how gravity is a consequence of that expansion, proves that the orthodox sentence "gravity is attractive" is time-reversal even, and shows in what sense the Principle's statement of attraction is one-way in the same sense as the strict Second Law.

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic states gravity as a consequence of the expansion in four steps, each a theorem stated earlier in this paper at the section cited. (i) The rate is gravitationally rigid, ∂(dx₄/dt)/∂g_μν = 0, the timelike block is fixed, g_tt = -c², g_tj = 0, and only the spatial metric h_ij carries dynamical degrees of freedom under mass-energy (McGucken-Invariance Lemma, Theorem 7.1 of [19], reproduced in §4.1). (ii) Every massive body carries a four-velocity of magnitude c, g_μνu^μu^ν = -c², the whole of it along x₄ at spatial rest and part of it redirected into spatial motion when the body moves (Master Equation, Theorem 5.5 of [19], §4.1); inertial mass is the fourth-momentum invested in the advance, m = |P₄|/c, and rest energy is the energy of that advance, E₀ = mc² (Definition 9.1, Theorem 11.1 of [19], §8.0 item 8). (iii) Mass stretches the spatial sector radially around itself, h_rr = (1 - r_s/r)^-1, the proper radial distance exceeding the coordinate distance (Scenario A of [27]; the stretching integrated over the Hubble McGucken Sphere is the proper-radius excess δR = r_s/6 of Theorem 12.1(iii)); the advance proceeds at the same c through the stretched slice, so h_ij acts as the refractive index of three-space for the invariant advance, and a body's worldline is bent toward the mass — the geodesic principle (Theorem 13.1 of [19]) — with its share v_x₄ = c√(1 - r_s/r) falling as it approaches (Appendix D). Gravitational time dilation "is a feature of h_ij, not of the rate of the fourth-dimension expansion" (Corollary 7.4(i) of [19], §8.0 item 8). (iv) The field equations governing h_ij are theorems of the same expansion along two channels: by the invariance group of dx₄/dt = ic, the constitutive identity of (ii), Noether's second theorem, and Lovelock uniqueness (Theorem 4.1, Theorem 9 of [4]); and by the focusing of the McGucken Spheres from neighbouring events by the Compton-tick energy they cross, read through the Clausius relation (Theorem 4.7, Theorem 14 of [4]). There is no graviton: "gravity is the geometry of h_ij, not a force mediated by particles" (Corollary 7.4(iii) of [19], §7.1bis item 11). "Gravity is attractive" is, in the Principle, the statement that the stretching of (iii) and the focusing of (iv) bring bodies and lightfronts toward the mass that sources them.

Lemma 5.1bis.1 (The orthodox statement of attraction is time-reversal even). (i) In Newtonian gravity the statement "gravity is attractive" is invariant under t →-t. (ii) In general relativity the focusing theorem holds for past-directed null congruences with the same sign, so the sign of the force alone selects no direction of time.

Proof. (i) The equation of motion is d²x⃗/dt² = -GM r̂/r². Under t →-t the velocity dx⃗/dt changes sign and the acceleration d²x⃗/dt² = d²x⃗/d(-t)² does not; the right-hand side contains no velocity. The reversed motion satisfies the same equation with the same attractive sign. (ii) For a null congruence with tangent k^μ and affine parameter λ, dθ/dλ = -1/2θ² - σ_μνσ^μν - R_μνk^μk^ν. Reversing the congruence, k^μ→-k^μ, λ→-λ, sends θ = ∇_μk^μ→-θ and σ_μν →-σ_μν, and the equation is carried to itself term by term. With R_μνk^μk^ν≥0 a past-directed congruence converges toward the past as a future-directed one converges toward the future; the white-hole region of the Kruskal extension is the realization, attractive gravity with a horizon whose area decreases in t. □

Theorem 5.1bis.2 (Attraction stated on the forward McGucken Sphere). Under dx₄/dt = ic, "gravity is attractive" is the statement that the spatial sector is stretched radially by mass and the generators of the forward McGucken Spheres Σ_+(p) are focused by the Compton-tick energy they cross, the focusing integrated along the direction of expansion. The time-reversed statement is attraction on the past cone, which the Principle excludes because the past cone is generated by no event; the sign of the force is unchanged by reversal (Lemma 5.1bis.1). The field equations, derived in the Algebraic Channel from the squared form of the rate, carry neither the sign of +ic nor the statement.

Proof. Step 1 (what the Principle generates). By §2.2 every event p is the apex of the forward cone Σ_+(p), expanding at c as x₄ advances at +ic; the past cone Σ_-(p) is the locus from which earlier McGucken Spheres have arrived at p and is generated by no event. Theorem 19.5.1(iii) of [3], reproduced in §5.1: "The time-reversal operation t →-t applied to the Geometric Channel's wavefront propagation produces a Sphere that contracts at -c — a derivationally distinct object that does not appear in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework." The generators k^μ of Σ_+(p) are future-directed by construction, and the affine parameter along them increases with the advance.

Step 2 (attraction on the forward Sphere). By §2.4 the curvature is the derived description of how the lightfronts of Σ_+(p) and Σ_+(p') for nearby p, p' fail to remain parallel in the presence of Compton-tick energy; by Theorem 4.7 Step 3, θ(λ) = -λR_μνk^μk^ν and δA = -∫₀^λλ' R_μνk^μk^νdA dλ', integrated over λ' > 0 only, since only the forward generators exist. In the weak-field limit the same focusing, through Theorem 4.7 Step 5 and Theorem 4.1 Step 6, is ∇²Φ = 4πGρ, and the geodesics of the metric whose spatial sector is stretched by ρ (anchor, item (iii)) fall toward the source.

Step 3 (the reversed statement has no carrier). The time-reverse of Step 2 is attraction stated on the past cone — the k^μ→-k^μ congruence of Lemma 5.1bis.1(ii), converging toward the past under the same energy. The sign of the force is unchanged, so the orthodox equation cannot exclude the reversed statement. The Principle excludes it at the level of the object on which it is made: Σ_-(p) is generated by no event, and the sphere contracting onto its apex is the -ic process, which is forbidden (Theorem 19.5.1(iii) of [3]: "dx₄/dt = +ic is signed … and the -ic orientation is forbidden"). The white hole of Lemma 5.1bis.1 is a solution of the Algebraic-Channel equation with no Geometric-Channel realization, as the entropy-decreasing trajectory of Loschmidt is a solution of the Algebraic-Channel microdynamics with no realization (§6.2).

Step 4 (common source with the Second Law). Theorem 3.3 derives dS/dt > 0 from the forward propagator of the Compton-tick walk, selected by the sign of +ic. Step 2 states attraction on the forward generators of the McGucken Spheres, selected by the same sign. Under -ic the walk propagates backward and dS/dt < 0; attraction keeps its sign (Lemma 5.1bis.1) but loses its carrier. The gravitational quantities that are strictly monotone in the sense of dS/dt > 0 are the accumulated proper-radius excess δR/R_H = Ω_m/6 of Theorem 12.1(iii) and the cumulative scale contraction ψ of [27] built from it, which grow because the advance does not reverse, and the horizon-area monotonicity of Theorem 3.6 on the forward cone.

Step 5 (why the field equation reports neither). The Algebraic Channel reads the squared and integrated forms of the rate, (ic)² = -c² and x₄ = ict (Theorem 5.1 anchor), from which the sign is removed; the acceleration of Lemma 5.1bis.1(i) is likewise a second derivative, invariant under dt →-dt. The field equation is derived in that channel (Theorem 4.1) and is time-reversal invariant (Theorem 5.1(i)); it governs the stretching of h_ij and the focusing of the McGucken Spheres without the direction in which the Spheres expand. The sign-blindness of the orthodox sentence is the sign-blindness of the squared form. □

Corollary 5.1bis.3. "Gravity is attractive" and "entropy increases" are one-way statements of the same standing: neither can be stated under -ic — the Second Law reverses sign, and attraction has no forward McGucken Sphere to be stated on — each is invisible to the Algebraic Channel, and each is derived in the Geometric Channel from the expansion of the McGucken Sphere at c from every event.

Proof. Theorem 5.1bis.2 Steps 3–5 for attraction, with Lemma 5.1bis.1 fixing what reversal does and does not change; Theorem 3.3 with Theorem 5.1(ii) for entropy. □

Prior art, at the scope of each statement. Three authors have connected the attractive character of gravity to the arrow of time; none has stated attraction itself as an oriented fact, and each has supplied the orientation from elsewhere.

Penrose 1979 [129] (background knowledge; the argument is also given in [76]): because gravity is attractive, gravitational clumping raises gravitational entropy, so a smooth early universe is a state of very low gravitational entropy, and its smoothness is stated as the Weyl-curvature hypothesis, a condition on the initial singularity. The attraction supplies the direction in which clumping raises entropy; the hypothesis supplies the direction of time. Under the Principle the initial condition is derived (§6.2, Theorem 13 of [3]): at the origin of the advance the McGucken Sphere has zero radius and Ω→1, and the clumping Penrose describes is the stretching and focusing of Theorem 5.1bis.2 Step 2 on forward McGucken Spheres.

Barbour, Koslowski and Mercati 2014 [198] (web-digest of the full text; quotations verbatim): "the attractivity of gravity" is among the properties the authors call "architectonic and likely to be shared by any fundamental law of the Universe"; in the Newtonian N-body problem -lnC_S "plays the role of the potential that attracts the system towards more inhomogeneous shapes"; a "well-defined measure of shape complexity fluctuates but grows irreversibly between rising bounds"; and "the origin of time's arrow is not necessarily to be sought in initial conditions but rather in the structure of the law which governs the Universe." This is the closest published statement to Corollary 5.1bis.3. Because their law is time-symmetric, the construction yields two arrows pointing away from a central point of minimal complexity, one on each side; attraction orients the growth of complexity relative to that point but does not select which side is the future. Under the Principle the law is oriented: dx₄/dt = +ic supplies the single direction (Theorem 5.1bis.2 Step 3).

Verlinde 2011 [9, §2] (verified-read, §8.0 item 2): "The statistical tendency to return to a maximal entropy state translates into a macroscopic force"; attraction, in his construction, is motion toward higher screen entropy, F = T ∂S/∂x. He identifies attraction with the entropic tendency, and in 2022 ([165], §8 (H3)) describes the system as reversible: "So this is a reversible system." The two are consistent in his framework because ∂S/∂x is a spatial derivative at fixed time and carries no sign of dt; the orientation enters only through the "statistical tendency" he imports, which is Theorem 3.3. Theorem 5.1bis.2 supplies what his identification lacks: the common source of the tendency and the attraction in the expansion of the McGucken Sphere at +ic.

The present search (the primary texts above and the arrow-of-time literature cited in §6.2 and in Theorem 19.5.1 of [3]) found no statement that "gravity is attractive" is itself a one-way statement on the footing of "entropy increases." The reason is Lemma 5.1bis.1: in every orthodox formulation the sentence is written on the squared quantities and is time-reversal even. It becomes available once gravity is stated at first order in the rate, as the radial stretching of the spatial sector by mass and the focusing of McGucken Spheres expanding at +ic.

Closing attribution. Gravity as a consequence of the expansion: Theorem 7.1, Theorem 5.5, Definition 9.1, Theorem 13.1, Corollary 7.4 of [19]; Theorem 12.1(ii); Theorems 4.1 and 4.7. Time-reversal evenness of the orthodox statement: Lemma 5.1bis.1. Attraction on the forward McGucken Sphere: §2.4, Theorem 4.7 Step 3, Theorem 19.5.1(iii) of [3]. Common source with the Second Law: Theorem 3.3, Theorem 5.1, Theorem 12.1(iii), Theorem 3.6. Prior art: Penrose 1979 [129], Barbour–Koslowski–Mercati 2014 [198], Verlinde 2011 [9] and 2022 [165].
