6. The McGucken Entropy S = k_B ln Ω, of which gravity, thermodynamics, and the Born rule are readings

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality. The entropy of physics is the logarithm of the count of distinguishable Compton-tick states of that Sphere.

6.1 Definition and the five readings

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic predicts one entropy: the state of the advance at an event is labelled by a direction n̂∈S² on the McGucken Sphere's cross-section together with the cycle index; the count of such states resolved on a region is Ω; the McGucken Entropy is

S_McG = k_BlnΩ.

Two quantities are kept apart: the cell count N(Σ) of a surface Σ of the McGucken Sphere, and the microstate count Ω(Σ) = e^N(Σ)/4 whose logarithm is the entropy, S = k_BN/4 on the horizon (Appendix A). Because the measure on the Sphere is the Haar measure of Theorem 3.2, S_McG inherits the two-channel reading of Theorem 5.1: through the Algebraic Channel it is a time-symmetric invariant; through the Geometric Channel it carries the +ic orientation, whence dS_McG/dt > 0.

Theorem 6.1 (The McGucken Entropy Identity; Theorem (The McGucken Entropy Identity) of [3], reproduced in full). The statement, proof, table of the five readings, and consequences are the author's, verbatim:

From [3], verbatim — The McGucken Entropy Identity: definition, theorem, proof, table of the five readings, and consequences (C1)–(C4): (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list; theorem numbers inside the quotation are those of [3])

The cascade analysis above identifies the same entropy formula appearing across multiple empirical sectors as the historical surface of a single fact. We elevate this fact to a formal named theorem on the order of the McGucken-Invariance Lemma [Theorem 8.1 of [58]] and the McGucken-Wick Rotation Theorem [Theorem 6 of [56]].

Definition (McGucken-Sphere Haar measure). Let p₀ = (𝐱₀, t₀) ∈M and let W(t) : = Σ_+(p₀) ∩Σ_t be the spatial cross-section of the McGucken Sphere at coordinate time t > t₀, the two-sphere of radius R(t) = c(t-t₀) centered on 𝐱₀ in Σ_t ≅ℝ³. The McGucken-Sphere Haar measure μ_W on W(t) is the unique normalized SO(3)-invariant probability measure on W(t) ≅S², with density 1/A(t) = 1/(4πc²(t-t₀)²) relative to the standard rotation-invariant surface measure on S². By Theorem 7 of the present paper, μ_W is forced by condition (P3) of Definition 5.4 of [58] combined with Haar's 1933 uniqueness theorem on the homogeneous space S² = SO(3)/SO(2), with the SO(3)-invariance being a direct geometry of dx₄/dt = ic (the foundational physical-geometric fact that the fourth dimension is expanding at velocity c in a spherically symmetric manner from every spacetime event). The McGucken-Sphere Haar-measure entropy of a sub-distribution ν≪μ_W on W(t) is the relative entropy

S_McG[ν] : = -∫_W(t) (dν)/(dμ_W) log((dν)/(dμ_W)) dμ_W,

which for ν = μ_W (the uniform Haar measure itself) equals lnA(t) + const (cf. Theorem 10 of the present paper).

Theorem (The McGucken Entropy Identity). Under the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic — the foundational physical-geometric fact that the fourth dimension is expanding at velocity c in a spherically symmetric manner from every spacetime event, with x₄ = ict the integrated coordinate shadow — the entropy formulas appearing in five apparently distinct empirical sectors of physics are five readings of one underlying quantity: the McGucken-Sphere Haar-measure entropy S_McG on the spatial-projection two-sphere W(t), under the Compton-coupling matter-interaction mechanism of Theorem 4. The five sectors and their readings are:

1. (1) Information theory: the Shannon entropy H_Shannon = -∑_i p_i logp_i [120] as the dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel algebraic-symmetry reading.
2. (2) Statistical mechanics: the Boltzmann–Gibbs entropy S_BG = -∑_i p_i logp_i [72, 119] as the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel Euclidean signature-reading, time-asymmetric with dS/dt = (3/2)/t > 0 (Theorem 9 of the present paper).
3. (3) Quantum mechanics: the von Neumann entropy S_vN = -Tr(ρlogρ) [123] as the dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel algebraic-symmetry reading of the density matrix on Hilbert space.

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic resolves the 150-year reversibility objection by placing the reversible microdynamics and the monotone Second Law in different channels of one Principle.

Loschmidt's objection (1876) to Boltzmann's H-theorem is that time-symmetric microdynamics cannot produce a strict monotone: for every entropy-increasing trajectory the time-reverse is equally valid. From [6], verbatim — Theorem 7.2 (Born rule from dx₄/dt = ic), statement and proof: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list)

Theorem 7.2 (Born rule from dx₄/dt = ic). Let ψ: ℝ³ → ℂ be the McGucken wavefunction of Definition 2.6, normalized so that ∫*ℝ³ |ψ|² d³x = 1. The unique density P: ℝ³ → ℝ{≥0} satisfying (R1)–(R4) is

P(𝐱) = |ψ(𝐱)|².

Proof. By (R4), P is bilinear in (ψ, ψ). The general bilinear form is

P(ψ) = a ψψ + b ψ^* ψ + c ψ ψ^* + d ψ^* ψ^* = a ψ² + (b + c) ψ^* ψ + d (ψ^*)²,

with coefficients a, b, c, d ∈ ℂ.

Phase invariance fixes the cross-term structure. By (R3), P(e^iα ψ) = P(ψ) for all α ∈ ℝ. Under ψ → e^iα ψ, ψ^* → e^-iα ψ^, the terms transform as: ψ² → e^2iα ψ², ψ^ ψ → ψ^* ψ, (ψ^)² → e^-2iα (ψ^)². Phase invariance for all α forces a = d = 0, leaving

P(ψ) = C ψ^* ψ, with C := b + c.

Reality fixes C to be real. By (R1), P ∈ ℝ. Since ψ ψ = |ψ|² ∈ ℝ_{≥0}, C must be real.

Non-negativity fixes C ≥ 0. By (R2), P ≥ 0. Since ψ ψ ≥ 0, C ≥ 0.

Normalization fixes C = 1. The case C = 0 gives P ≡ 0, excluded by the requirement that P be a probability density. Hence C > 0. The normalization ∫ |ψ|² d³x = 1 then fixes C = 1, giving

P(𝐱) = |ψ(𝐱)|². ▪

(d/dt) ∫_ℝ³ |ψ(x, t)|² d³x = 0.

For p ≠ 2 the L^p norm of a normalized solution to the Schrödinger equation is not in general preserved by unitary evolution; the proof is by direct computation. For a normalized 3D Gaussian wavepacket with spatial width σ(t) ~ ℏt/(2mσ_0) at large t, the L^p norm scales as ‖ψ_t‖_p ~ σ(t)^{3(2-p)/(2p)} ~ t^{-3(p-2)/(2p)} for p > 2 (verification: at p = 4 the L^p norm decays as t^{-3/4}, since ∫|ψ_t|⁴ d³x ~ σ(t)^{-3} and σ(t)^{-3/4} ~ t^{-3/4}). For p < 2 the exponent 3(2-p)/(2p) is positive and the L^p norm grows as a positive power of t — non-conserved in the opposite direction. Only p = 2 makes the exponent vanish, conserving the norm exactly. Lesovik (G. B. Lesovik, “Derivation of the Born rule from the unitarity of quantum evolution,” arXiv:1411.6992, 2014; [90]) gives the explicit derivation of the Born rule’s exponent 2 from precisely this unitarity argument on a given Hilbert space. In the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, Lesovik’s argument applies on the derived Hilbert space 𝓗 of Theorem 6.1, with the unitary evolution itself derived in Theorem 9.2, and the parallelogram-identity / inner-product structure of 𝓗 supplied internally by Lemma 7.6. The exponent 2 is therefore forced from the dynamical side as well: probability conservation under the unitary evolution of Theorem 9.2, which descends from dx₄/dt = ic, requires the bilinear L² norm whose existence on 𝓗 is internal to the dx₄/dt = ic framework via Lemma 7.6.

The exponent 2 in the Born rule is therefore overdetermined by two derivationally disjoint McGucken-internal routes that share no intermediate machinery between the McGucken Principle and the conclusion:

Metric Route (rank-2 metric route to bilinear density). dx₄/dt = ic → Lorentzian metric on Minkowski Space 𝕄₁,3 (Lemma 2.5) → rank-2 character of g_μν → natural bilinear pairing on (ψ, ψ) (Lemma 7.1) → P = |ψ|² (Theorem 7.2). Geometric machinery: metric tensor, rank counting, sesquilinear pairing on amplitudes.

Norm Route (rank-2 sesquilinear inner product route to L²-norm structure, McGucken-internal). dx₄/dt = ic → Lorentzian metric on Minkowski Space 𝕄₁,3 (Lemma 2.5) → rank-2 sesquilinear inner product on 𝓥 (Lemma 7.1) → parallelogram identity by direct two-line expansion (Lemma 7.6) → L²-norm structure on the McGucken-derived 𝓗 (Theorem 6.1); reinforced by unitarity (Theorem 9.2) preserving the L² norm exactly. Functional-analytic machinery: rank-2 sesquilinearity, parallelogram identity, Stone’s theorem on unitary groups, L^p norm-conservation analysis — all internal to the dx₄/dt = ic framework via Lemma 7.6.

Both routes start from dx₄/dt = ic; both routes end at P = |ψ|²; they share only the upstream principle and the rank-2 → sesquilinear chain (Lemma 2.5 → Lemma 7.1) before diverging. Metric Route operates through the density’s degree directly (rank-2 bilinear pairing → quadratic density). Norm Route operates through the norm structure and conservation (rank-2 sesquilinearity → parallelogram identity → L² norm → unitarity conservation). The two routes converge on the same exponent through entirely different mathematical structure, both descending from the same upstream physical principle, both internal to the dx₄/dt = ic framework.

Status of Jordan–von Neumann 1935 in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework. The Jordan–von Neumann theorem [89] historically established that a normed space admits an inner product if and only if its norm satisfies the parallelogram identity, with the corollary that among L^p spaces only L² is a Hilbert space. In the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, this theorem is unnecessary as upstream input: the inner product on 𝓗 is supplied directly by Lemma 7.1 from the rank-2 Minkowski metric, and the parallelogram identity follows by Lemma 7.6 as a McGucken-internal downstream consequence. Jordan–von Neumann therefore serves as a downstream consistency check — confirming that the McGucken-derived parallelogram-identity structure on the McGucken-derived 𝓗 is consistent with general functional analysis on L^p spaces — rather than as a foundational selection principle. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework derives the L² character of 𝓗 internally; Jordan–von Neumann’s historical theorem is cited as the standard functional-analytic correlate but is no longer used as upstream input to the cascade.

The architectural significance of this overdetermination is structural: no prior program in the foundations of quantum mechanics derived the Hilbert space from a physical principle upstream of the formalism, and none derived the parallelogram identity from a physical principle internal to the dx₄/dt = ic framework. Gleason (1957) derived the form of the Born rule on a given Hilbert space; the trace structure on the lattice of subspaces already encodes the inner-product-derived bilinearity. Jordan–von Neumann (1935) characterized the parallelogram identity on given L^p spaces; the result is a theorem about which Banach spaces admit inner products, with the L^p spaces themselves taken as input. Lesovik (2014) derived the Born rule from unitarity on a given Hilbert space; the Hilbert space hosting the unitary evolution is presupposed. Each of these results, in the orthodox tradition, takes the Hilbert space or the inner product as input and derives the exponent 2 from inside that input.

The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework operates one level upstream of all three programs: the Hilbert space itself is derived (Theorem 6.1) from dx₄/dt = ic, the inner product is supplied internally (Lemma 7.1) from the rank-2 metric, the parallelogram identity is internal to the dx₄/dt = ic framework (Lemma 7.6) by direct two-line algebra, and the orthodox inside-Hilbert-space arguments — Gleason, Jordan–von Neumann, Lesovik — all reinforce the exponent 2 with their inputs themselves traced back to dx₄/dt = ic. The exponent 2 has, in the McGucken framework, multiple internally-consistent derivations all descending from the same physical principle, with the Hilbert space as derived intermediate, the inner product as derived sesquilinear pairing, and the parallelogram identity as derived McGucken-internal algebraic consequence — rather than as primitive inputs. This is the exponent-2 overdetermination property of the dx₄/dt = ic framework: every functional-analytic argument that forces the exponent on a given Hilbert space (Jordan–von Neumann uniqueness, Lesovik unitarity, Gleason non-contextuality) is, in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, an argument whose Hilbert-space input and inner-product input are themselves theorems of dx₄/dt = ic — so each functional-analytic route to the exponent ultimately traces back to the same upstream principle as the geometric rank-2-metric route, and the parallelogram-identity step internal to Norm Route is itself a McGucken-internal consequence of rank-2 sesquilinearity (Lemma 7.6), not an external functional-analytic input.

Theorem 19.4.4.5: The Common Six-Step Methodology of Gravity-from-Entropy Programs — Convergence Diagnosis, the Field's Second Blind Spot, and What the Uniformity of Terminology Reveals

Preamble. Theorems 19.4.3 and 19.4.4 have identified Jacobson 1995 and Verlinde 2011 individually as proper subsets of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework. The present theorem generalizes the diagnosis. It states that every gravity-from-entropy program in the orthodox literature — Jacobson 1994 (entanglement entropy + Sakharov induction), Jacobson 1995 (local Rindler horizons + Clausius), Padmanabhan 2005–2012 (horizon degrees of freedom + equipartition), Verlinde 2010 (holographic screens + entropic force), Van Raamsdonk 2010 / Ryu–Takayanagi 2006 (entanglement entropy on AdS boundary), Parikh–Svesko 2018 (stretched light cones at every event), Alonso-Serrano–Liberati 2020 (causal-diamond thermodynamics), Bianconi 2024 (quantum relative entropy between two metrics) — executes the same six-step methodology in the same order, with the "differences" among the programs consisting only of the specific noun chosen for each slot. The convergence, when read against the linguistic uniformity of the field's popular presentations ("Entropy = Gravity," "Gravity from Entropy," "Entropic Gravity," "Thermodynamics of Spacetime"), is the sociological signature of a deeper physical fact that the field has systematically declined to articulate: the programs are not competing derivations of gravity from thermodynamics; they are competing readings of a single underlying object which none of them has named.

Under the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic that object is named. The McGucken Sphere at every event is simultaneously the null surface that Jacobson postulates, the holographic screen that Verlinde postulates, the entanglement-cutting surface that Ryu–Takayanagi postulate, the stretched light cone that Parikh–Svesko postulate, the causal diamond boundary that Jacobson 2015 and Alonso-Serrano–Liberati postulate, and the matter-induced metric surface that Bianconi postulates. Every one of the six slots in the common methodology is filled by dx₄/dt = ic as theorem rather than as postulate.

The present theorem states the diagnosis in four parts, supplies two comparative tables, unpacks the field's second blind spot (why nobody has asked the convergence question), and closes with the linguistic-uniformity evidence and the ontological read.

Theorem 19.4.4.5 statement (four parts).

(i) (Common six-step methodology.) Every orthodox gravity-from-entropy program executes the following six-step skeleton in the same order:

- (S1) Select a geometric object as arena — a null surface, horizon, screen, causal diamond, boundary, or matter-induced metric — postulated to exist at every event or at a distinguished subset of events.
- (S2) Attach an entropy to the arena — an area-law entropy, entanglement entropy, bit count, or quantum relative entropy — with the specific form and coefficient postulated rather than derived.
- (S3) Attach a temperature to the arena — the Hawking, Unruh, Tolman-redshifted, or equipartition-derived temperature — imported from horizon thermodynamics without derivation of the underlying mechanism.
- (S4) Invoke a thermodynamic identity — the Clausius relation δQ = T dS, the entropic force FΔx = TΔS, the Euclidean action W = -ħlnZ, or a variational entropy extremum — with the required local equilibrium postulated as a "very good approximation" rather than derived.
- (S5) Read off gravitational content — Einstein equations, Newton's laws, modified Einstein equations at low coupling, or a specific horizon-thermodynamic identity — via bookkeeping rearrangement of (S1)–(S4).
- (S6) Confess the undelivered inputs — the arena is undetermined, the entropy coefficient is a free parameter, the equilibrium is an approximation, the arrow of time is time-symmetric-in / time-asymmetric-out, the cosmological constant is undetermined, or ħ is auxiliary and rescalable.

(ii) (Program-by-program instantiation.) The four archetypal programs — Jacobson 1994, Jacobson 1995, Verlinde 2010, Bianconi 2024 — differ only in the specific noun that fills each of the six slots. No program departs from the six-step order or omits any step. Table 3 documents the instantiation explicitly.

(iii) (McGucken completion.) Under dx₄/dt = ic every slot in the common skeleton is closed as theorem: (S1) the McGucken Sphere at every event (Theorem 3), (S2) Planck-cell mode count on the wavefront delivering the Bekenstein–Hawking coefficient 1/4 (Theorem 15), (S3) the Hawking temperature from Euclidean cigar closure under the McGucken Wick rotation τ = x₄/c (Theorem 16), (S4) ISO(3) Haar isotropy as forced local equilibrium (Theorem 7), (S5) the Einstein field equations via Hilbert–Jacobson agreement at Tier 2 of the two-tier architecture (Theorem 19.4), (S6) every undelivered input of the orthodox programs answered as theorem: ħ as twin action-quantum reading of the wavefront, the Compton coupling as Theorem 4, the arrow of time as +ic orientation delivering strict Second Law dS/dt = (3/2)k_B/t > 0 (Theorem 9), Λ from cosmological x₄-expansion at H₀ (Theorem 18). Table 3 documents the completion slot-by-slot.

(iv) (Field's second blind spot.) The orthodox literature has posed and re-posed the question "how does my derivation of gravity from entropy differ from Jacobson's/Verlinde's/Bianconi's?" but has not posed the deeper question "why can we all derive gravity from entropy, along numerous 100%-different routes, all beginning with entropy and ending with gravity? What does this convergence mean about the physical reality that our different routes are collectively reading?" The absence of this question is the field's second blind spot. Einstein's 1949 admission that classical thermodynamics has not been reduced to mechanics [154] is the first blind spot the present paper closes as Theorems 7–9. The convergence question is the second, and the present theorem closes it as Corollary 19.4.4.5.1 below.

Proof of Theorem 19.4.4.5

Corollary 19.4.4.5.1: Ontological Reading of the Convergence — What the Uniformity Tells Us About Physical Reality

The convergence of the orthodox gravity-from-entropy programs on the same conclusion (gravitational content extracted from thermodynamics, via one of six variations on the same six-step skeleton) is not a coincidence, and it is not an artifact of overlapping technical vocabulary. It is the empirical signature of a foundational physical fact: gravity and thermodynamics are dual-channel readings of one underlying physical-geometric principle. The four programs each catch part of this principle and read off part of its consequences; none names the principle. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic names it.

Specifically: the convergence tells us that (i) there exists a single object at every spacetime event — the McGucken Sphere, the spherically-symmetric wavefront of x₄'s expansion at c — that is simultaneously the arena all four programs postulate; (ii) this object carries an entropy that all four programs identify with area; (iii) this object carries a temperature that all four programs identify with the Hawking/Unruh form; (iv) this object supports the equilibrium condition all four programs postulate as "extremely good approximation"; (v) this object's dynamics produces the Einstein field equations that all four programs recover. The programs did not stumble on gravity from entropy by four different accidents; they read the same wavefront by four different names. Once the name is supplied — dx₄/dt = ic — the convergence dissolves from mystery into forced consequence: any observer who identifies part of the wavefront's structure will derive part of gravity from part of thermodynamics, in the specific limit accessible to their vocabulary. Jacobson 1995 reads the null-surface face and gets Einstein equations from Clausius. Verlinde 2010 reads the screen face and gets Newton's laws from entropic force. Jacobson 1994 reads the entanglement-across-horizon face and gets S_BH from induced gravity. Bianconi 2024 reads the matter-induced-metric face and gets modified Einstein from quantum relative entropy. All four are correct within their scope; all four are proper subsets of the same underlying wavefront reading.

The convergence question the field has not asked is precisely the question the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework answers with a Corollary rather than with a theorem, because the answer requires no additional theorem: it requires only the observation that when six independent research programs starting from independent premises converge on the same conclusion via six variations on the same methodology, the shared substrate is not a coincidence to be catalogued but a physical fact to be named. The field has not named it because the field has not asked the question. The present corollary asks the question and names the answer: the substrate is dx₄/dt = ic, and the wavefront is the McGucken Sphere.

Corollary 19.4.4.5.2: Diagnosis of the Field's Silence — Why the Convergence Question Has Been Systematically Avoided

The sociological factors that have kept the convergence question off the agenda of the orthodox literature are diagnosable as follows. First, academic differentiation incentives: research programs are rewarded for staking distinct territory ("my derivation transcends Jacobson's because it derives inertia," "my theory is not horizon-based, unlike Verlinde and Jacobson," "my program uses entanglement entropy, not thermodynamic entropy"). The convergence question — "why do we all get gravity from entropy?" — is in tension with differentiation because it invites the answer "because we are all reading the same underlying object," which reduces the programs' claimed originality to a shared substrate they have not named. The differentiation incentive is stronger than the unification incentive at the publication level, and stronger still at the popular-media level, where video titles emphasize "Erik Verlinde: Why My Entropic Gravity Transcends Jacobson's" rather than "Why Jacobson and I Are Both Reading the Same Physical Object Without Naming It."

Second, terminological homonym-mistaken-for-difference: Bianconi's presentation of her "quantum relative entropy" as "not the horizon entropy of Verlinde or Jacobson" [190] is a homonym issue treated as a foundational one. Horizon entropy is entropy attached to a two-surface with the area-law form; quantum relative entropy on the Araki algebra of two metric-density operators reduces, in the horizon limit, to the same area-law form. The two entropies are not "unrelated"; they are the same object read on different mathematical substrates. Presenting them as unrelated is a linguistic convenience that hides the convergence. The same applies to the polymer-entropic-force reading of Verlinde 2010, the entanglement-entropy reading of Jacobson 1994, the Clausius-heat reading of Jacobson 1995, and the quantum-relative-entropy reading of Bianconi 2024. All four are readings of area-law entropy on a null-ish surface, differentiated by mathematical vocabulary rather than by underlying content.

Third, the two-decade proliferation of clickbait titles: The popular-media presentation of gravity-from-entropy programs has, over the last decade and a half, converged on a small vocabulary — "Entropy = Gravity," "Gravity from Entropy," "Entropic Gravity," "The Physicist Who Derived Gravity from Entropy," "Gravity Linked to Thermodynamics," "Intriguing Study Explains Gravity Through Quantum Entropy" — which is linguistically identical across programs that the presenters simultaneously insist are foundationally different. Sample video-title inventory (each program's popular presentation, chronological): "The Physicist Who Proved Entropy = Gravity" (Jacobson, Curt Jaimungal channel); "Erik Verlinde: Why My Entropic Gravity Transcends Jacobson's" (Verlinde, Jaimungal); "The Physicist Who (Unexpectedly) Derived Gravity From Entropy" (Bianconi, Jaimungal); "Entropic Gravity from Quantum Entanglement! | with Erik Verlinde" (Verlinde interview); "Emergence of Gravity from Quantum Information" (Verlinde talk title); "Gravity Linked to Thermodynamics in Black Holes" (Jaimungal channel summary); "Intriguing Study Explains Gravity Through Quantum Entropy" (Bianconi popular coverage). The vocabulary uniformity is the sociological signature of the convergence: presenters converge on the same terminology because they are, in fact, describing the same object.

The diagnostic conclusion is that the convergence question has been avoided not because it is difficult but because it is awkward: asking it makes the differentiation claims of individual programs harder to sustain. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's position is that the convergence is the more foundational fact than any of the differentiations, and the correct scientific response is to name the shared object rather than to catalogue the vocabulary variations. Naming the shared object is what Theorem 19.4.4.5 does.

Remark 19.4.4.5.1: The Verlinde-vs-Jacobson Dispute as Intra-Methodology, Not Inter-Methodology

Verlinde's stated distinction from Jacobson — "Jacobson basically assumed spacetime already, and just derived Einstein equations from it; I derive inertia as well, so my program is more fundamental" [12, 1:24–3:41] — is not a foundational difference but an intra-methodology one. Both programs execute the same six-step skeleton of Table 3. Verlinde substitutes a holographic screen at Φ = Φ₀ for Jacobson's local Rindler horizon (a swap within slot S1), substitutes a bit count with equipartition for Jacobson's S = ηA (a swap within slot S2), and substitutes the Compton-wavelength entropy jump for Jacobson's Raychaudhuri-focusing (a swap within slot S4). These are three lateral swaps within the same methodology; they do not constitute a distinct methodology. Verlinde's claim to "transcend" Jacobson is the claim that his substitutions in slots S1, S2, S4 yield F = ma as an additional output — which is a legitimate observation about the coverage of his substitutions but is not a claim to have derived gravity from a foundation Jacobson lacked. Both programs derive gravity from the same six-step methodology; Verlinde's derivation covers one additional cell of the output (inertia) that Jacobson's covers only implicitly. Neither program supplies the physical substrate that would ground the methodology.

Similarly, Bianconi's stated distinction — "my quantum relative entropy is not the horizon entropy of Verlinde or Jacobson" [190] — is a substitution within slot S2 (entropy attached to arena), not a departure from the six-step skeleton. Bianconi's arena (slot S1) is a matter-induced metric rather than a horizon; her entropy (slot S2) is quantum relative entropy on Araki algebras rather than area entropy; her thermodynamic identity (slot S4) is variational extremization rather than Clausius. These are three lateral substitutions, not a distinct methodology. The output (slot S5) recovers modified Einstein equations at low coupling — the same output all four programs deliver.

Remark 19.4.4.5.2: Are the Entropies Really Different?

A specific question posed in a 2026 dialogue cited in [3] without a locator: is Bianconi's "geometric quantum relative entropy" really "in no way whatsoever related to horizon entropy" as her popular presentations frame it? Are the entropies of Jacobson 1994 (entanglement across horizon), Jacobson 1995 (proportional to horizon area), Verlinde 2010 (holographic screen bit count), and Bianconi 2024 (quantum relative entropy between metric operators) really unrelated? Does "entropy" mean anything, or are these different entropies unrelated readings of the word?

The answer is that all four are the same object read on different mathematical substrates, and the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework identifies the common object:

- Entanglement entropy (J94): S_ent = -tr ρ_Ilnρ_I where ρ_I is the reduced density matrix on one side of a bipartition. In the horizon limit with Planck-scale cutoff, S_ent →A/(4ħG_ren).
- Area entropy (J95): S_area = ηA with η = (4ħG)^-1 fitted. In the Planck-cell counting limit, S_area = A/(4ℓ_P²).
- Holographic bit count (V10): N = Ac³/(Għ); converted to entropy via S = k_Bln2 ·N = k_B A/(4ℓ_P²) up to the factor 4ln2.
- Quantum relative entropy (B24): H(g̃G̃) = -Tr_Fln(G̃g̃^-1). In the horizon limit with the matter-induced metric near-horizon, this reduces to the area-law form.

All four converge on the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy S_BH = k_B A/(4ℓ_P²) in the horizon limit. The convergence is not accidental; it is forced by the fact that all four are readings of Planck-cell mode counting on a two-surface, which is the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's derivation of S_BH (Theorem 15). The mathematical substrates differ; the underlying object is identical. Bianconi's "geometric quantum relative entropy" is not the opposite of "horizon entropy" and it is not a special case of horizon entropy in any interesting sense — it is the same Planck-cell mode-counting object read on a different mathematical apparatus, delivering the same area-law behavior in the appropriate limit.

The linguistic contrast "quantum relative entropy versus horizon entropy" is a homonym confusion. The entropies are all the same physical object. The formalisms differ; the physics does not.

Theorem 19.4.4.6: The Priority Circle Dissolved — Gravity, Entropy, Nonlocality, and the Metric as Four Simultaneous Theorems of dx₄/dt = ic; The Convergence Question Answered as a Fan-Not-Chain Result

Preamble. Children of a common father resemble one another; this is a fact about the father, not a coincidence among the children. The family has been mistaken for a queue.

The present theorem is structured in five parts: (I) the Priority Circle diagnosis, (II) the shared-source resolution, (III) the metric-based impossibility theorem, (IV) the program-by-program contrast, (V) the children-of-one-father reading.

Theorem 19.4.4.6 statement (five parts).

(I) (The Priority Circle diagnosis.) Each orthodox gravity-from-entropy program takes as a primitive input a structure that another program claims to derive as an output. Consequently, no ordering of the programs exists in which every program is derived and none is assumed. The three archetypal cases:

- Jacobson 1995 [7] takes as input the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy formula S = A/(4ħG), the Unruh temperature T = ħκ/(2π), and the Clausius relation δQ = T dS; produces the Einstein field equations as output.

Each program's input is another program's output, and each program's output is another program's input. The circle is closed: none serves as a foundation. This is the primary-source content of Proposition 18.7bis.1 of [4] and is the diagnosis of why the convergence-across-programs has been a mystery for thirty years.

(II) (Shared-source resolution.) Under the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, the Priority Circle dissolves as follows. Gravity, entropy, thermodynamics, nonlocality, and the metric are five simultaneous theorems of the Principle, each descending directly from (dx₄/dt = ic) by its own chain of reasoning that does not pass through any of the others. - The thermodynamic arrow descends from the +ic orientation: the spherically-symmetric wavefront advance forces isotropic diffusion, and the strict Second Law dS/dt = (3/2)k_B/t > 0 (Theorem 9 of the present chain) is the Boltzmann–Gibbs entropy of the resulting Gaussian on the flat slice, generalized to arbitrary curved backgrounds by the McGucken Spacetime Entropy theorem (Theorem 10.5bis.3 of [4]): dS/dt = k_B D ℐ_h(P) + k_B⟨θ⟩, where the first term is the free-diffusion (Fisher-information) contribution and the second is the cosmological-expansion contribution — the thermodynamic and cosmological arrows as two terms of one identity.

(III) (Metric-based impossibility theorem.) By Theorem 17-ter of [4] (the Content-Asymmetry Theorem), the symmetry group 𝒢 of the integrated coordinate label x₄ = ict — the Lorentz group SO^+(1,3), the Poincaré algebra 𝔦𝔰𝔬(1,3), the CPT operator, and the internal gauge groups from which Algebraic Channel derives its theorems — is sign-blind on the +ic orientation. The involution i ↦-i is a field automorphism of ℂ over ℝ that leaves (ic)² = -c² and every algebraic structure erected upon it invariant. Consequently, no chain of reasoning conducted within any framework built exclusively on the metric and its symmetries can produce the arrow of time. This is the sharpest statement of why Jacobson 1995, Verlinde 2010, Verlinde 2016, and Bianconi 2024 all fail to derive the Second Law: each program is erected on the metric and its algebraic structure (Jacobson: metric + Killing vectors + Raychaudhuri; Verlinde: holographic screens in a metric space; Bianconi: metric's Lorentz-invariant eigenvalues and rank-2 tensor algebra); each imports the Second Law rather than deriving it; and this is not a defect of the specific programs but a theorem — no metric-based program could derive the arrow, because the arrow lives in the kernel of the projection that carries the active expansion to its preserved algebraic label. (IV) (Program-by-program contrast — the three archetypes as three reflections of one wavefront.) Under the shared-source resolution, the three archetypal programs are three distinct readings of the same dx₄/dt = ic wavefront, each catching a specific facet:

- Jacobson 1995: no action; reads horizon-thermodynamics at every local Rindler horizon; imports the Second Law, temperature, and horizon entropy from Bekenstein–Hawking–Unruh; produces Einstein's equations. Explicit moral: gravity is an equation of state; do not quantize.

(V) (Children of one father — the ontological read strengthened.) The convergence of the three archetypal programs on the same gravitational content, via three superficially disjoint methodologies, is the expected consequence of the fact that gravity, entropy, thermodynamics, nonlocality, and the metric are five children of one parent. Proof of Theorem 19.4.4.6

Proof of (III) — the metric-based impossibility. By Theorem 17-ter of [4]: the involution i ↦-i is a field automorphism of ℂ over ℝ that fixes the reals pointwise, leaves (ic)² = -c² invariant, leaves the Minkowski line element ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² - c² dt² invariant, leaves the Lorentz group SO^+(1,3) invariant, and leaves every algebraic structure erected on the metric label invariant. This is not a defect of the specific programs but a theorem about metric-based emergence. 

Proof of (IV) — program-by-program contrast. By primary-source inspection: Jacobson 1995 (arXiv:gr-qc/9504004) contains no action functional and no functional-integral apparatus; the derivation runs on δQ = TdS applied at every local Rindler horizon with Raychaudhuri closing the null-congruence identity. Verlinde 2010 (arXiv:1001.0785) contains no action functional either; the derivation runs on FΔx = TΔS with ΔS = 2πk_B(mc/ħ)Δx postulated via Bekenstein's 1973 thought experiment and Unruh T imported. Bianconi 2024 (arXiv:2408.14391) contains an action functional ℒ = -Tr_Fln(G̃g̃^-1) and explicitly proposes canonical quantization; her "entropy" is a Kullback–Leibler-type divergence between two static metric operators, evaluated pointwise, exactly time-symmetric, with no dS/dt. The three programs differ in whether they have an action (Bianconi does; Jacobson and Verlinde do not) and in the specific arena chosen (Jacobson: local Rindler horizon; Verlinde: holographic screen at Φ₀; Bianconi: matter-induced metric on the Lorentzian manifold). All three converge on Einstein-limit gravitational content; none derives the Second Law. 

Proof of (V) — children of one father. Follows from (I)–(IV): the Priority Circle diagnosis (I) establishes that no ordering of the programs exists; the shared-source resolution (II) establishes that all five sciences descend directly from dx₄/dt = ic; the metric-based impossibility (III) establishes that no metric-based reordering could rescue any of the programs to serve as foundation; the program-by-program contrast (IV) establishes that the three programs are three specific readings of the same wavefront. The convergence is therefore the expected consequence of the shared source, and the family-mistaken-for-a-queue diagnosis is the read of the sociological pattern documented in Corollary 19.4.4.5.2.

Corollary 19.4.4.6.1: The Prediction of Theorem 17-ter is Empirically Confirmed by Bianconi 2024

Theorem 17-ter of [4] predicts that no metric-based emergence programme can produce an arrow of time. Bianconi 2024's programme is entirely erected on the metric's algebraic structure — Lorentz-invariant eigenvalues (her Eq. 1–2), the logarithm of rank-2 tensors, traces, the quantum relative entropy of the two-metric structure. Bianconi's paper produces modified Einstein field equations and does not produce, and does not attempt to produce, a Second Law or an arrow of time. This is a non-trivial confirmed prediction of Theorem 17-ter and — as noted in the corresponding §18.7bis discussion of [4] — the cleanest external test of Theorem 17-ter observed to date. A metric-based program is delivering exactly the coverage Theorem 17-ter says a metric-based program should deliver: gravity yes, arrow no. The same read applies to Jacobson 1995 (which uses equilibrium thermodynamics, a Clausius relation reversible in both directions) and to Verlinde 2010 (which invokes a statistical tendency without dS/dt). None of the three derives dS/dt > 0; by Theorem 17-ter, none of them ever could.

Corollary 19.4.4.6.2: The GPS Empirical Anchor — Nature Selects +ic, and Only Nature Can

The complement of Theorem 17-ter is that the +ic orientation, being the one feature that no metric-based algebra can distinguish, is precisely the feature that must be selected empirically. This is Corollary 38.1 of [4] applied at the diagnostic level: the sign-asymmetric GPS pre-launch frequency correction, applied in one direction only and operational continuously since 1978, is the empirical anchor for the +ic orientation. The five sign-symmetric rate-strands of the Principle (CHSH-saturation, rotational invariance, distance-independence, c-isotropy, Huygens propagation) fix the magnitude and isotropy of the rate; they cannot fix the sign. Only a directional experiment can, and GPS is one. The asymmetry between the five strands (sign-symmetric, therefore Algebraic-Channel-visible) and GPS (sign-asymmetric, therefore Geometric-Channel-necessary) is exactly what Theorem 17-ter predicts: any theorem requiring the +ic orientation lies in the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel, and any empirical anchor for the orientation must be a Geometric-Channel measurement — directional, accumulative, running one way only. The GPS offset is linear in the rate; the budget partition and dilation factor are both quadratic (even) in the rate; only the linear-in-rate observable can select the sign. This is the diagnostic content that no orthodox gravity-from-entropy program supplies: not one of Jacobson 1995, Verlinde 2010, or Bianconi 2024 identifies GPS as the empirical anchor for the arrow of time, because none of them has an arrow of time to anchor.

Corollary 19.4.4.6.3: The McGucken Second Law on Curved Backgrounds Closes the Last Gap

Theorem 10.5bis.3 of [4] establishes the Geometric Second Law on a curved, evolving spatial slice with local volume-expansion rate θ: dS/dt = k_B D ℐ_h(P) + k_B⟨θ⟩, where the first term is the Fisher-information rate of the diffusing probability density (recovered as the flat-space content of Theorem 9 of the present chain) and the second term is the cosmological-expansion contribution. This is the McGucken Spacetime Entropy content stated at theorem status, generalizing the flat-space Theorem 9 of the present chain to arbitrary globally hyperbolic curved backgrounds with matter potentials. Under Theorem 10.5bis.3, spacetime has a natural entropy — not one imported from horizon thermodynamics, not one postulated on holographic screens, not a Kullback–Leibler mismatch between two static metric operators, but the strict monotonic entropy production of the diffusing probability density carried on the x₄-wavefront at every event. The Second Law is not attached to spacetime from outside; the expansion is what spacetime is doing. This is the content the three archetypal programs collectively lack: each of Jacobson, Verlinde, and Bianconi imports the thermodynamics and then reads off gravitational content; the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework derives the thermodynamics and reads off gravitational content by Jacobson's own route (at the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel) and by Hilbert's own route (at the dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel) — both from one principle, without importing thermodynamics for the algebraic derivation and without importing gravity for the thermodynamic derivation.

Remark 19.4.4.6.1: What §18.7bis of the GR Chain Paper Adds Beyond Theorem 19.4.4.5

Theorem 19.4.4.5 established the common six-step methodology of gravity-from-entropy programs and diagnosed the field's second blind spot. §18.7bis of [4] extends the diagnosis in three specific directions the present thermodynamics chain absorbs by cross-reference:

First, the Priority Circle (Proposition 18.7bis.1 of [4]): the primary-source demonstration that each of the three archetypal programs takes as input a structure that another claims to derive as output, closing the circle and precluding any ordering. This diagnosis strengthens the "S6 undelivered inputs" row of Table 3 into a theorem: the S6 row is not merely a list of author admissions but a set of closed loops in the dependency graph of the field.

Second, the fan-not-chain reading (Remark 18.7bis.9 of [4]): a circle is a pathology of chains; a fan has no cycles because no branch feeds another. The three archetypal programs are attempting to arrange siblings into a lineage. The correct picture is that they are four children of one parent, and the family has been mistaken for a queue. This reading supplies the ontological complement of Corollary 19.4.4.5.1 of the present chain: the shared substrate is not a coincidence to be catalogued but a fact about the parent.

Third, the metric-based impossibility theorem (Theorem 18.7bis.13 of [4]): no metric-based emergence programme can reach the arrow, because by Theorem 17-ter the symmetry group of the metric label is sign-blind on +ic. This theorem promotes the observation "Jacobson, Verlinde, Bianconi all fail to derive the Second Law" from a common empirical fact to a necessity: none of them could derive the Second Law, and this is not a defect of the specific programs but a theorem about metric-based emergence.

The three additions together answer the convergence question the field has not asked: why can gravity be derived from entropy by so many parties using so many methods? Because gravity, entropy, thermodynamics, nonlocality, and the metric are siblings, and any research program that identifies part of the shared source will derive part of the family resemblance. The programs converge because they are reading the same object — not because gravity emerges from thermodynamics, and not because thermodynamics emerges from gravity, but because both emerge from dx₄/dt = ic as parallel theorems that do not pass through one another.

Remark 19.4.4.6.2: The Sociological Consequence — A Better Popular Presentation

The consequence of Corollary 19.4.4.6.3 is that the popular presentations of the gravity-from-entropy programs — the video-title inventory of Remark 19.4.4.5.3 — should be reframed. Rather than "Erik Verlinde: Why My Entropic Gravity Transcends Jacobson's" (which presupposes a lineage), or "The Physicist Who (Unexpectedly) Derived Gravity From Entropy" (which suggests unlikely convergence), or "The Physicist Who Proved Entropy = Gravity" (which conflates identity with derivation), the popular framing under Theorem 19.4.4.6 would be: Why the Four Independent Programs That Derive Gravity from Entropy Are All Reading the Same Wavefront Without Naming It, and What the Wavefront Is. The convergence is the newsworthy fact; the naming of the wavefront (dx₄/dt = ic) is the answer to the convergence question; and the observation that gravity, entropy, thermodynamics, and nonlocality are four children of one parent — rather than a lineage in which each derives from the previous — is the diagnostic that dissolves the field's thirty-year quarrel over ordering. Videos framed as "How Jacobson, Verlinde, Bianconi, and McGucken All Reach Gravity Through Entropy — And Why the Convergence Is the Deeper Physics" would treat the field's convergence pattern as the primary discovery it is, rather than as a background against which each program's individual "transcendence" is showcased.

Theorem 19.4.4.7: Jacobson 1995 as the Founder of the Gravity-from-Entropy Programme — Historical Priority, Depth, and Every Subsequent Program Measured as Distance from His Original Insight

Preamble. The present theorem redresses a historical omission that could otherwise be read into the parallel-column presentations of Theorems 19.4.4.5 and 19.4.4.6, which for diagnostic purposes tabulated Jacobson 1994, Jacobson 1995, Verlinde 2010, and Bianconi 2024 as four archetypes of one methodology. That tabulation is analytically correct but historically flat: Jacobson 1995 is not a peer of Verlinde 2010 or Bianconi 2024. Jacobson is the founder — the pioneer of the entire gravity-from-entropy programme, whose eight-page 1995 letter Thermodynamics of Spacetime: The Einstein Equation of State [7] opened the field and to which every subsequent program in the thirty-year lineage is downstream, explicitly and by direct citation. Verlinde 2010 [9] states in his own Section 5.2 that he adapts "a similar reasoning as Jacobson" to time-like screens. Padmanabhan 2002–2012 [175, 8] extends Jacobson to FRW apparent horizons and to any diffeomorphism-invariant gravity theory. Bianconi 2024 [10] cites Jacobson 1995 directly (her reference to [7]) as the ancestor of the entropic-action approach. Van Raamsdonk 2010, Ryu–Takayanagi 2006, Maldacena–Susskind 2013, Parikh–Svesko 2018, Alonso-Serrano–Liberati 2020, and Bianconi 2024 are all children of Jacobson in the specific sense that each cites him and takes some ingredient of his construction (the entropy-area proportionality, the Clausius relation, the local equilibrium assumption, the horizon-thermodynamic architecture) as given, then substitutes another ingredient.

The present theorem gives Jacobson his due: it details his seminal move, catalogues the three foundational depths he supplied that all subsequent work relies on, measures every subsequent program as distance from Jacobson rather than as peer of Jacobson, and — most importantly — reads Jacobson's own 1995 confession about "non-equilibrium spacetime" as the direction from which dx₄/dt = ic arrives. The McGucken Principle is what Jacobson himself hoped someone would eventually find. Recognizing this is the correct honor to pay him, and it also correctly locates the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework in the field's intellectual lineage: not as competitor to Jacobson, but as the physical mechanism Jacobson explicitly said would be needed to close his own construction.

Theorem 19.4.4.7 statement (five parts).

(I) (Historical priority.) The gravity-from-entropy programme begins in 1995 with Jacobson's Thermodynamics of Spacetime: The Einstein Equation of State [7]. Prior work — Bekenstein 1973 [112], Bardeen–Carter–Hawking 1973 [155], Hawking 1975 [113], Unruh 1976 [158], Gibbons–Hawking 1977 [34], Bombelli–Koul–Lee–Sorkin 1986 [188], 't Hooft 1993 [37], and Susskind 1994 [102] — established the thermodynamic properties of horizons but did not derive gravitational dynamics from thermodynamics. That inverse move — reading the Einstein field equations as an equation of state, with thermodynamics as input and gravitational content as output — is Jacobson's, in 1995, and it is his alone. The eight-page letter is the pivot around which the entire subsequent thirty-year literature rotates. Every gravity-from-entropy paper after 1995 that derives Einstein equations from a thermodynamic identity is walking, in some direction, on Jacobson's ground.

(II) (The seminal move.) Jacobson's argument is three moves executed in fifteen equations:

- Move 1 (universal horizon architecture): Every spacetime point p carries local Rindler causal horizons through it in every null direction. Consequently, the horizon-thermodynamic apparatus of Bekenstein–Hawking–Unruh applies at every event, not merely at black-hole event horizons — a universalization of horizon thermodynamics to a local diagnostic.
- Move 2 (heat as boost energy across the horizon): The heat flux δQ across the local Rindler horizon is defined as the integrated boost-energy current ∫_H T_abχ^a dΣ^b, where χ^a is the approximate boost Killing field vanishing at the reference two-surface P and T_ab is the matter stress-energy tensor. Temperature is the Unruh temperature T = ħκ/(2π) seen by the accelerated observer just inside the horizon. Entropy variation is dS = ηδA with η a proportionality constant.
- Move 3 (Clausius closes to Einstein via Raychaudhuri): Imposing δQ = TdS on every local Rindler horizon at every spacetime point, and closing the identity with the Raychaudhuri equation dθ/dλ = -1/2θ² - σ² - R_abk^ak^b applied to the null generators, forces T_abk^ak^b = (ħη/2π)R_abk^ak^b for all null k^a. Local energy conservation and the contracted Bianchi identity then close the algebra to R_ab - 1/2Rg_ab + Λg_ab = (2π/ħη)T_ab: the Einstein field equations, with G = (4ħη)^-1 identifying Newton's constant.

The move is that gravitational dynamics is not fundamental because it is the equation of state of the horizon-thermodynamics of spacetime. Jacobson's own summary: "it may be no more appropriate to canonically quantize the Einstein equation than it would be to quantize the wave equation for sound in air." This is not a modest claim. It is the assertion that gravity is emergent thermodynamics — the sound of quantum spacetime, not one of its atoms — and it is the seminal statement of the entire subsequent literature.

(III) (The three foundational depths.) Jacobson supplied three depths that every subsequent gravity-from-entropy program still relies on, either explicitly (by citation) or implicitly (by architectural inheritance):

- Depth 1 (universalization of the horizon): Before Jacobson, horizon thermodynamics was a diagnostic for specific horizons — black-hole event horizons, cosmological horizons, Rindler horizons of specific accelerated observers. After Jacobson, the horizon is a local diagnostic at every event. This universalization is the load-bearing move for Van Raamsdonk (entanglement across every bipartition), Verlinde (holographic screens at every equipotential), Padmanabhan (apparent horizons at every FRW slice), Parikh–Svesko (stretched light cones at every event), and Jacobson 2015 (causal diamonds at every event). Each subsequent program specializes or generalizes Jacobson's universalization.
- Depth 2 (heat-as-boost-energy): Jacobson's identification of heat with the integrated boost-energy current across the horizon is the load-bearing thermodynamic bridge that makes δQ = TdS well-defined at every event. Verlinde's entropic force FΔx = TΔS, Padmanabhan's equipartition on horizon DOFs, Bianconi's variational entropy extremum, and every entanglement-based programme in the lineage all rely on some form of Jacobson's bridge — a locally-defined thermodynamic quantity that couples to gravitational content.
- Depth 3 (Raychaudhuri as the closing identity): The null-congruence equation is what makes Jacobson's derivation work: it converts the area-variation condition into a curvature condition. Every subsequent program that recovers Einstein equations by a similar route uses either Raychaudhuri directly (Padmanabhan, Verlinde in Section 5.2 via Komar mass and Killing vectors — "using a similar reasoning as Jacobson"), or a mathematical cousin (Wald's Noether-charge formalism, Iyer–Wald entropy, the Ryu–Takayanagi minimal-surface prescription).

Every subsequent program in the field inherits at least one of these three depths from Jacobson. Most inherit all three.

(IV) (Every subsequent program as measured distance from Jacobson.) Under Depths 1–3 as the reference axes, each subsequent program can be located by the specific ingredients it substitutes for Jacobson's originals. Table 3 makes this precise: each row is a Jacobson ingredient; each column is a subsequent program; each cell records the specific lateral swap the program makes from Jacobson's original construction. What emerges from the table is that no subsequent program departs from Jacobson at the foundational level (the three depths of Part III); every subsequent program departs from Jacobson only at the lateral level (which specific arena, which specific entropy expression, which specific thermodynamic identity fills each slot). The programs are not competitors of Jacobson at the foundational level; they are lateral variations on his construction. Jacobson is the founder, and every subsequent program is a child.

(V) (Jacobson's 1995 confession points at dx₄/dt = ic.) Jacobson's own closing paragraph in the 1995 letter is remarkable for what it acknowledges. He writes that his derivation "presumed the existence of local equilibrium conditions" and that at a "deeper level, we also assumed the usual form of short distance vacuum fluctuations in quantum fields ... this also amounts to a sort of local equilibrium assumption. This deeper assumption is probably valid only in some extremely good approximation." And then — the sentence that a physicist in 1995 might have thought was closing a modest speculation but that a physicist in 2026 can read as prophecy: "We speculate that out of equilibrium vacuum fluctuations would entail an ill-defined spacetime metric. ... It is my hope that, by following this line of inquiry, we shall eventually reach an understanding of the nature of 'non-equilibrium spacetime'."

That is precisely dx₄/dt = ic. The McGucken Principle is non-equilibrium spacetime: the fourth dimension is not in equilibrium; it is actively expanding at rate c from every event. Local equilibrium in Jacobson's sense is not an approximation to be corrected but the wrong frame entirely — spacetime is not near-equilibrium, it is spherically expanding. Jacobson in 1995 hoped that a deeper physical understanding of non-equilibrium spacetime would emerge; that understanding is what the McGucken Principle supplies. Corollary 19.4.4.7.2 makes this precise.

Proof of Theorem 19.4.4.7

Proof of (I) — historical priority. By primary-source inspection: Bekenstein 1973, BCH 1973, Hawking 1975, Unruh 1976, Gibbons–Hawking 1977 establish horizon thermodynamics but derive no gravitational dynamics from thermodynamics. Jacobson 1995 (gr-qc/9504004) is the first paper in the physics literature to derive the Einstein field equations by imposing δQ = TdS on local horizons at every event and using the Raychaudhuri equation to close the identity. Post-1995 papers are all downstream: the citation record of Verlinde 2010, Padmanabhan 2005–2012, Bianconi 2024, Van Raamsdonk 2010, Ryu–Takayanagi 2006, Maldacena–Susskind 2013, Parikh–Svesko 2018, Alonso-Serrano–Liberati 2020, Jacobson 2015 causal diamonds, and Jacobson 2016 entanglement equilibrium all cite Jacobson 1995 as ancestor. G1 by direct primary-source citation-chain verification. 

Proof of (II) — the seminal move. Direct inspection of Jacobson 1995: Move 1 (universalization of horizon) is stated on p. 3 ("Through any spacetime point there are local Rindler horizons in all null directions"); Move 2 (heat as boost energy) is Eq. (1) of the paper (δQ = ∫_H T_abχ^a dΣ^b); Move 3 (Raychaudhuri closes to Einstein) runs from Eq. (4) of the paper to Eq. (6) with the Einstein equation as output. G1 by direct primary-source equation-by-equation verification. 

Proof of (III) — the three foundational depths. Depth 1 is verified by direct citation-chain: Van Raamsdonk 2010 cites Jacobson's universalization of the horizon (their §2); Verlinde 2010 cites Jacobson's universalization (his Sec. 5.2); Padmanabhan 2005 cites Jacobson's universalization (his introduction); Parikh–Svesko 2018 cites Jacobson's universalization (their §1). Depth 2 is verified by citation-chain: Verlinde's FΔx = TΔS (his Eq. 3.7), Padmanabhan's equipartition on horizon DOFs, and Bianconi's variational entropy extremum are all descendants of Jacobson's δQ = TdS move. Depth 3 is verified by citation-chain: Verlinde Sec. 5.2 explicitly writes "using a similar reasoning as Jacobson" [7] and adapts Jacobson's null-congruence argument to time-like Killing vectors; Padmanabhan's derivations use Raychaudhuri; Parikh–Svesko use Raychaudhuri on stretched light cones. Remark 19.4.4.7.2: Verlinde's "Transcends Jacobson" Claim Examined at Primary-Source Level

Verlinde's stated distinction from Jacobson — most explicitly in the 2024 Jaimungal interview [12], but present in the 2010 paper's Sec. 6.1 as well ("we have added an important element that is new. Instead of only focussing on the equations that govern the gravitational field, we uncovered what is the origin of force and inertia in a context in which space is emerging") — is that Verlinde derives inertia F = ma as an additional output beyond Jacobson's Einstein equations, and that this makes his construction more fundamental than Jacobson's. The claim is worth examining at primary-source level.

What Verlinde adds beyond Jacobson. Section 3.1 of Verlinde 2010 derives F = ma from the Compton-wavelength entropy postulate ΔS = 2πk_B(mc/ħ)Δx combined with Unruh temperature T = ħa/(2πk_B c) combined with the entropic-force identity FΔx = TΔS. The three inputs combine to give F = ma directly, as Verlinde notes in his Eq. (3.9). This is an additional output beyond Jacobson's Einstein equations, and Verlinde's derivation of it is his genuine additive novelty.

What Verlinde does not add beyond Jacobson. Section 5.2 of Verlinde 2010 derives the Einstein equations. Verlinde's own text in that section: "An analogous question was addressed by Jacobson for the case of null screens. By adapting his reasoning to this situation, and combining it with Wald's exposition of the Komar mass, it is straightforward to construct an argument that naturally leads to the Einstein equations." Verlinde's relativistic content is his own admission a Jacobson-style construction adapted to time-like screens. He does not derive Einstein equations by a foundationally different method; he derives them by Jacobson's method with a substituted arena.

The honest read. Verlinde adds inertia; Verlinde does not add a foundational method beyond Jacobson. The "transcends Jacobson" claim is therefore correct only in the specific sense that Verlinde derives one additional physical relationship (F = ma) that Jacobson does not; it is not correct in the sense that Verlinde's construction rests on a deeper foundation than Jacobson's. Both rest on the same three foundational depths (universalization of horizon, heat as thermodynamic bridge, Raychaudhuri/Wald closure). Both inherit the same confessed undelivered inputs. Neither derives the arrow of time.

Verlinde's genuine contribution is real (the F = ma derivation is his own), and he deserves credit for it. What is misleading is the "transcends Jacobson" framing at the foundational level; at that level, Verlinde does not transcend Jacobson — he executes a lateral variation on Jacobson's construction. The correct framing under Table 3 is that Verlinde 2010 is Jacobson 1995 with a substituted arena (time-like screens instead of null Rindler wedges) and one additional derived relationship (F = ma), inheriting the same three foundational depths and the same undelivered inputs.

Proof of (i): the bidirectional historical record. We document the historical record in primary-source form.

The gravity → thermodynamics direction. The earliest established result is Tolman–Ehrenfest 1930 [176]: thermal equilibrium in a stationary gravitational field requires T √(-g₀0) = const, so that gravity directly modifies the local thermodynamic equilibrium state. This is gravity supplying a constraint on thermodynamics with no thermodynamic input. The chain then runs:

- Bardeen–Carter–Hawking 1973 [155] derived four theorems of pure classical general relativity — Killing-horizon results on stationary black holes — and observed that the four theorems have the exact mathematical structure of the four laws of thermodynamics. The Zeroth Law: the surface gravity κ is constant on the horizon of a stationary black hole, identical to the temperature being constant in equilibrium. The First Law: dM = (κ/8π) dA + ΩdJ + ΦdQ, identical to dU = TdS + work. The Second Law: Hawking's area theorem dA ≥0 for classical processes, identical to dS ≥0. The Third Law: κ→0 is unattainable in finitely many steps, identical to T →0 being unattainable. At this stage (1973) the correspondence is formal — pure geometric theorems of classical general relativity exhibit the structure of thermodynamic laws — and no foundational physical mechanism has been identified.

Recapitulation of Jacobson 1995. Jacobson derives the Einstein field equations G_μν = 8πG T_μν from three thermodynamic inputs applied to every local Rindler horizon at every point in every null direction:

(J1) The Bekenstein-Hawking entropy-area law. For any local Rindler horizon, the entropy is proportional to the area: δS = ηδA with η = 1/(4 G ħ). Jacobson takes this as primitive input from black-hole thermodynamics extended to arbitrary local horizons.

(J2) The Unruh temperature. For an accelerated observer with proper acceleration |a|, the local Rindler horizon has Unruh temperature T_U = (ħ/2π)|a|. Jacobson takes this as primitive input from the Unruh effect [158].

(J3) The Clausius relation. For any thermodynamic system, the entropy change is related to the heat flux by δQ = T δS. Jacobson applies this on the local Rindler horizon, treating the energy-momentum flux T_μν k^μk^ν across the horizon as the heat input.

The Jacobson derivation proceeds:
- Pick any spacetime point p and any null direction k^μ
- Construct the local Rindler horizon: a piece of the past light-cone seen by an accelerated observer through p, with k^μ as null generator
- Treat this horizon as thermodynamic at Unruh temperature T_U
- Heat flux across horizon: δQ = ∫T_μν k^μk^νdλdA where λ is the affine parameter along k^μ
- Entropy change: δS = ηδA, where δA is computed from the Raychaudhuri equation for the horizon-bundle's cross-sectional area
- Setting δQ = T_U δS for every local Rindler horizon at every point gives, after manipulation: T_μν k^μk^ν = (1/8πG) R_μν k^μk^ν for all null k^μ
- Standard differential-geometric argument: this implies R_μν - (1/2) g_μν R + Λg_μν = 8πG T_μν (Einstein field equations)

Jacobson interprets this as gravity is an equation of state — i.e., a thermodynamic relation — rather than a fundamental dynamical law. Einstein equations become emergent from a more primitive thermodynamic substrate.
