7.0 The 1995 letter read in full: each stated assumption derived from the Principle

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic states that from every event p a McGucken Sphere Σ_+(p) expands at c, its radius r = ct growing with the x₄-advance x₄ = ict, its wavelength at the massive tier λ_C = h/mc carrying the action h per Compton tick. Every quantity Jacobson's letter assumes — a causal horizon, a heat crossing it, an entropy proportional to its area, a cutoff, a temperature, local equilibrium, and the time-reversal invariance of the output — is a property of this expanding McGucken Sphere, and the derivation below is carried out item by item on Jacobson's own statements [7] (verified-read, full text).

(1) The question. Jacobson: "How did classical General Relativity know that horizon area would turn out to be a form of entropy, and that surface gravity is a temperature?" and, after reversing the logic, "Viewed in this way, the Einstein equation is an equation of state" [7, ¶1].

Derivation from the Principle. The null cone of Σ_+(p) has cross-sectional area A(t) = 4πc²t² and is tiled by N = A/ℓ_P² independent modes of the advance (Theorem 3.5), so S = k_BN/4 is a property of the cone the expansion of the McGucken Sphere generates. The same cone's generators k^μ are the objects whose focusing R_μνk^μk^ν enters the field equations (Theorem 4.7 Step 3), and the surface gravity κ is the rate at which the boost parameter of the Sphere's x₄-advance accumulates along a generator, whose Euclidean period 2π/κ is a temperature by KMS (Theorem 4.6). General relativity "knew" because the area, the surface gravity, and the field equations are three readings of one cone: in the Algebraic Channel the field equations describe how neighbouring cones focus (Theorem 4.1), in the Geometric Channel the same focusing is the Clausius balance of the cone's state count (Theorem 4.7), and Corollary 5.3 states the agreement as forced. The equation-of-state form is the Geometric-Channel derivation; the Algebraic-Channel derivation of the identical equation is the reason the equation of state has a time-reversal-invariant form (item 12).

(2) Heat. Jacobson: "In spacetime dynamics, we shall define heat as energy that flows across a causal horizon. It can be felt via the gravitational field it generates, but its particular form will be unobservable from outside the horizon" [7, ¶3].

Derivation from the Principle. A massive particle at rest carries its entire four-velocity along x₄ and accumulates phase at ω_C = mc²/ħ (Theorem 3.1), one tick of action h and energy ħω_C = mc² per Compton period Δt_C = h/mc². For matter crossing the null cone H with generators k^μ, the energy carried across per unit affine parameter and area is T_μνk^μk^ν, and for a dust of n particles per unit volume this is n mc² (u·k)²/c²: the sum of the Compton-tick energies of the McGucken Spheres crossing the cone, weighted by the projection of their advance onto the generator. Jacobson's δQ (his Eq. (1)) is therefore the integrated Compton-tick energy crossing the Principle-generated null surface (Theorem 4.7 Step 1). The form of that energy is unobservable from outside because H is the boundary of Σ_+(p)'s causal contact (§2.2): an event inside the cone of the crossing Spheres sends no Sphere that reaches the outside observer before the horizon, so only the aggregate — the focusing it produces on H, item (7) — is seen.

(3) Entropy proportional to area, with a cutoff. Jacobson: the entanglement entropy of vacuum correlations across the horizon "is divergent in continuum quantum field theory. If, on the other hand, there is a fundamental cutoff length l_c, then the entanglement entropy is finite and proportional to the horizon area in units of l_c²"; "We shall thus assume for most of this letter that the entropy is proportional to horizon area"; and "consistency with thermodynamics requires that l_c must be of order the Planck length (10^-33 cm)" [7, ¶4–5].

Derivation from the Principle. The continuum divergence arises because a field with no smallest advance has modes of arbitrarily short wavelength straddling the horizon. Under dx₄/dt = ic the advance proceeds in ticks: a McGucken Sphere of mass m advances Δx₄ = iλ_C per tick, so no mode of that Sphere has wavelength below λ_C = h/mc, and the count of modes straddling a surface of area A is finite, N∼A/λ², for every tier of the advance. The cutoff at the horizon tier is derived in Theorem 3.5 Step 1 from the crossing of the Compton wavelength h/mc with the Schwarzschild radius 2Gm/c² at m² = hc/2G, where λ_C = r_s = 2√(π)ℓ_P: the finest horizon-tiling mode of the advance has wavelength of order ℓ_P≈1.6×10^-33 cm, which is Jacobson's l_c, derived in place of inferred. Theorem 3.5 Steps 2–3 then give N = A/ℓ_P² and S = k_BA/4ℓ_P².

(4) The coefficient. Jacobson: "The dimensional constant η is undetermined by anything we have said so far (although given a microscopic theory of spacetime structure one may someday be able to compute η in terms of a fundamental length scale.)" [7, after Eq. (3)]; and at the end, "G = (4ħη)^-1, which identifies the length η^-1/2 as twice the Planck length (ħG)¹/2" [7, after Eq. (6)].

Derivation from the Principle. The fundamental length is ℓ_P of item (3), and η is computed two ways. In the Geometric Channel, the Clausius identity of Theorem 4.7 Step 4 gives the coupling η/2π in front of R_μνk^μk^ν, and the Newtonian matching of Theorem 4.1 Step 6 — the same matching Jacobson performs — fixes η = 1/4G in natural units, i.e. η = 1/4ℓ_P² with ħ = c = 1, which is Jacobson's G = (4ħη)^-1. In the Algebraic Channel the number 1/4 is computed: on the Euclidean Schwarzschild section the bulk Einstein–Hilbert term vanishes and the Gibbons–Hawking–York boundary term gives I_E = βMc²/2; the free-energy relation S = k_B(β⟨E⟩- I_E)/ħ with β = 8πGM/c³ gives S = 4πGM²k_B/ħc = k_BA/4ℓ_P² (Theorem 4.5 Step C). The 1/4 is the 1/2 of the boundary term carried through the free-energy relation, and the microscopic theory Jacobson's parenthesis asks for is the McGucken Sphere whose action is that Einstein–Hilbert action (Theorem 4.1) and whose horizon-tier wavelength is ℓ_P.

(5) Temperature. Jacobson takes the temperature to be the Unruh temperature of an observer hovering just inside the horizon, the Minkowski vacuum being thermal with respect to the boost Hamiltonian at T = ħκ/2π, with the diverging temperature and diverging energy flux having a finite ratio in the horizon limit [7, ¶6, ¶9].

Derivation from the Principle. Integrating dx₄/dt = ic gives x₄ = ict; in Euclidean units τ = x₄/c the Lorentz boost of rapidity η_b becomes a rotation by θ = -iη_b in the (x, cτ) plane, the accelerated worldline becomes a circle, and regularity at the rotation's fixed point requires 2π-periodicity, so the Euclidean proper-time period is 2πc/a (Theorem 4.6). The KMS condition (Appendix B) identifies periodicity ħβ in imaginary time with a thermal state at 1/β, giving T_U = ħa/2πck_B; for a horizon, a→κ gives Jacobson's ħκ/2π. The finite ratio Jacobson needs follows in Theorem 4.7 Step 4: the heat flux carries one factor a through χ^μ = -(a/c²)λk^μ and the temperature carries one factor a, so δQ/T_U is independent of a before the horizon limit is taken. The "vacuum" whose thermality Jacobson invokes is the overlap of McGucken Spheres expanding at +ic from neighbouring events (Theorem 10.1), and its boost-thermality is the Euclidean reading of the one advance.

(6) Local equilibrium at every point. Jacobson: "The equivalence principle is invoked to view a small neighborhood of each spacetime point p as a piece of flat spacetime"; a 2-surface element 𝒫 is chosen with vanishing expansion and shear of its past null normal congruence, defining a local Rindler horizon "that is instantaneously stationary (in 'local equilibrium') at p"; "Through any spacetime point there are local Rindler horizons in all null directions" [7, ¶7].

Derivation from the Principle. The flat neighbourhood is the exact metric of §2.1, ds² = (ic dt)² + dx⃗², the squared form of the rate; no equivalence-principle approximation is needed because the McGucken Sphere's expansion at c from p supplies the local Minkowski structure as a theorem. The local Rindler horizon through p is the null cone of a source event q at affine distance R behind p: the null normals of a round Sphere have expansion θ = 2/R and, by the spherical symmetry of Σ_+(q), exactly zero shear σ_μν = 0; as R→∞ the cone is a null plane with θ→0, σ = 0, which are Jacobson's equilibrium conditions at p (Theorem 4.7, preamble). The horizons "in all null directions" are the generators of Σ_+(p) itself, one per point of its S² cross-section, distributed by the unique SO(3)-invariant measure dμ = sinθdθdϕ/4π of Theorem 3.2 — the same measure that supplies the Born rule on the directional cross-section (Theorem 6bis.3), which is why the identity of Step 5 below holds for every null k^μ.

(7) The principle at play. Jacobson: "The fundamental principle at play in our analysis is this: The equilibrium thermodynamic relation δQ = T dS, as interpreted here in terms of energy flux and area of local Rindler horizons, can only be satisfied if gravitational lensing by matter energy distorts the causal structure of spacetime in just such a way that the Einstein equation holds" [7, ¶8].

Derivation from the Principle. The causal structure being distorted is the family of null cones that dx₄/dt = ic generates at every event, and "gravitational lensing by matter energy" is the convergence of neighbouring Spheres' lightfronts in the presence of Compton-tick energy. In §2.4 the expansion of the McGucken Sphere is primitive and the curvature is the derived description of how the lightfronts of Σ_+(p) and Σ_+(p') for nearby p, p' fail to remain parallel: the Raychaudhuri equation dθ/dλ = -1/2θ² - σ² - R_μνk^μk^ν is the statement that the cross-sectional area of a bundle of Sphere generators decreases at a rate set by the energy they cross. Jacobson's "can only be satisfied if" is then the identity of Theorem 4.7 Step 4: the Compton-tick heat crossing the cone equals the x₄-period temperature times the increment of the cone's cell count, and the cell count changes only through the focusing of the generators, so the focusing is fixed by the heat. The Einstein equation is the unique local relation that makes the Sphere's own count balance its own heat.

(8) The derivation, Eqs. (1)–(6). Jacobson: δQ = ∫_ℋT_abχ^a dΣ^b with χ^a = -κλk^a, giving δQ = -κ∫_ℋλT_abk^ak^b dλd𝒜; dS = ηδ𝒜 with δ𝒜 = ∫_ℋθdλd𝒜; the Raychaudhuri equation with θ² and σ² neglected giving θ = -λR_abk^ak^b; the Clausius relation then requiring T_abk^ak^b = (ħη/2π)R_abk^ak^b for all null k^a, hence (2π/ħη)T_ab = R_ab + fg_ab; local conservation and the contracted Bianchi identity fixing f = -R/2 + Λ [7, Eqs. (1)–(6)].

Derivation from the Principle. Theorem 4.7 Steps 1–5 reproduce this chain with each input a theorem: Eq. (1) is item (2); η in Eq. (3) is item (4); the equilibrium conditions that let θ² and σ² be dropped are item (6); the temperature is item (5); the local conservation ∇^μT_μν = 0 that selects f is Theorem 4.1 Step 4, derived on shell from the constitutive identity u^μu_μ = -c² by the energy and Euler projections, and is one of the two inputs the channels share (Corollary 4.8). The step "for all null k^a" is the statement that the Clausius identity holds on every generator of Σ_+(p); since the generators exhaust the S² of directions with the SO(3)-invariant measure of Theorem 3.2, the quadratic form (T_μν - (η/2π)R_μν)k^μk^ν vanishing on the whole null cone forces the symmetric tensor to be a multiple of g_μν, which is Jacobson's f g_ab. The unit bookkeeping, ħc/8πℓ_P² = c⁴/8πG, is carried in Theorem 4.7 Step 4. Padmanabhan's extremization over null vectors (§9.1) is the same "for all null k^a" written variationally.

(9) The cosmological constant. Jacobson: "The undetermined cosmological constant Λ remains as enigmatic as ever" [7, after Eq. (6)].

Derivation from the Principle. In both channels Λ enters as the integration constant allowed by ∇^μG_μν = 0 together with ∇^μT_μν = 0 (Theorem 4.1 Step 5 via Lovelock's βg_μν; Theorem 4.7 Step 5 via f = -R/2 + Λ), so its value is fixed by neither derivation. The McGucken cosmology determines the dark-energy sector from the advance: w(z) = -1 + Ω_m(z)/(6π), first stated in [31] §10 and in [27] §III.2 (verified-read), which attributes it to Proposition V.1 of the companion manuscript [32]; Theorem 12.1 of the present paper derives it — w = -1 exactly for the rigid advance, the departure as the contraction rate of the spatial sector, and the coefficient 6π = 3×2π from V/A = R_H/3 and the McGucken Sphere's acceleration scale a₀ = cH₀/2π. At Ω_m,0 = 0.315 this gives w₀ = -0.983 with no free parameter, which replaces an undetermined constant by a derived function of the matter density.

(10) Holography declined as circular. Jacobson, note [5]: "Another argument that might be advanced in support of the proportionality of entropy and area comes from the holographic hypothesis," which he declines to use because its primary support is black hole thermodynamics, the phenomenon the letter sets out to account for.

Derivation from the Principle. The circularity is removed because holography is a theorem of the McGucken Sphere: every Σ_+(p) is a Huygens wavefront — each of its points the source of a new Sphere, with dx₄/dt = ic supplying the physical mechanism (the spherical expansion at c from every event) that Huygens' construction states without mechanism — and the data on the wavefront determine the field inside by the Kirchhoff integral, so the state of the region is specified on its boundary (Lemma 7.4.4; Theorem 21 of [3], §11). The cell count N = A/ℓ_P² of item (3) is the count of independent Huygens sources on the wavefront, which is the bound on the states inside; area-proportionality therefore rests on the Sphere's mode count, and black hole thermodynamics is one of its consequences.

(11) Local equilibrium as the deeper assumption, and the ill-defined metric. Jacobson records that local equilibrium is presumed twice: in the instantaneous stationarity of the Rindler horizons, and in the usual form of the short-distance vacuum fluctuations, viewed as a zero-temperature thermal state; "We speculate that out of equilibrium vacuum fluctuations would entail an ill-defined spacetime metric" [7, ¶16].

Derivation from the Principle. The short-distance vacuum fluctuations are the isotropic Compton-tick displacements of Theorem 3.2, of length λ_C per tick in a direction drawn from the SO(3)-invariant measure; their "usual form" is the stationary reduced state of the forward diffusion with D = h/6m (Theorem 3.3), and the full state is unitary (§6.3). Equilibrium is the regime in which the aggregate over many ticks has reached that stationary form on the scale of the horizon patch. Out of equilibrium the metric remains defined, because the metric is the squared form of the rate, (ic)² = -c² (§2.1), and exists at every event independently of the state of the fluctuations; what fails is the Clausius identity at tick resolution, where the per-event count Ω has not reached its ensemble value. The residual of that failure is computable: the reduced-state generator of §6.3 gives the diffusion residual D_x^(McG) = ε²c²Ω_mod/2γ² (QM T22 of [5]: D_x^(McG) = ε²c²Ω/2γ², with total D = kT/mγ+ D_x^(McG)), which is the first measurable departure from the equilibrium metric relation and the quantity Jacobson's speculation points to.

(12) Time-reversal invariance, the sound analogy, and quantization. Jacobson notes that the Einstein equation is time-reversal invariant with propagating-wave solutions, compares it to the adiabatic sound equation in a gas — which "should not be canonically quantized as if it were a fundamental field, even though there is no question that the underlying dynamics is quantum" — and concludes that "it may not be correct to canonically quantize the Einstein equations, even if they describe a phenomenon that is ultimately quantum mechanical" [7, ¶17].

Derivation from the Principle. The time-reversal invariance of the output is Theorem 5.1(i) and Corollary 5.4: the field equations have an Algebraic-Channel derivation from symmetry and the calculus of variations, in which x₄→-x₄ leaves the Euclidean action, a function of (∂ϕ/∂x₄)², invariant (Lemma 7.4.6; Theorem 19 of [21]; Consequence 6 of Theorem 22.1 of [56]); the arrow enters only the Geometric-Channel route through the +ic orientation. The Einstein equation is the equation of the horizon-area reading of the count Ω at ensemble resolution (§7.3), and the Compton-tick events of the McGucken Spheres are the per-event dynamics beneath that reading. What is quantized is the advance: ħ is the action per Compton tick (§2.3), and quantum mechanics is derived from the Sphere along the Algebraic Channel (twenty-three results, [5]). Jacobson's conclusion follows as a theorem: canonically quantizing the Einstein equation would quantize the ensemble reading of a count whose per-event quantum dynamics are already those of the Sphere, and the correct quantum theory is the one derived in [5] and [6], of which the Einstein equation is the thermodynamic limit in the Geometric Channel and the symmetry output in the Algebraic Channel.

(13) Non-equilibrium spacetime. Jacobson: "It is my hope that, by following this line of inquiry, we shall eventually reach an understanding of the nature of 'non-equilibrium spacetime'" [7, ¶18], where high-frequency or large-amplitude disturbances fall outside the Einstein equation because the local equilibrium condition fails.

Derivation from the Principle. Non-equilibrium spacetime is the regime in which the Compton-tick resolution of the McGucken Sphere is no longer negligible against the aggregate: disturbances with frequency approaching ω_C = mc²/ħ or with amplitude such that the cell count on the horizon patch changes by order one per tick. There the Clausius identity is replaced by the per-event unitary dynamics of §6.3, whose reduced-state reading carries the residual D_x^(McG) of item (11) and whose tidal Born shift δp∼p R₀i0jL^iL^j (§13) is the second signature. The understanding Jacobson hopes for is the Sphere's per-event dynamics, of which his equilibrium equation of state is the ensemble reading.

Summary of the attribution. Each of Jacobson's thirteen statements descends from dx₄/dt = ic as follows: (1) area, surface gravity, and field equations as three readings of one cone, their agreement forced by common descent (Corollary 5.3); (2) heat as Compton-tick energy across the Principle-generated null cone (Theorems 3.1, 4.7 Step 1); (3) the area-proportional count with cutoff ℓ_P from the crossing of λ_C and r_s (Theorem 3.5); (4) η = 1/4ℓ_P² matched in the Geometric Channel and computed in the Algebraic Channel (Theorems 4.5, 4.7); (5) T = ħκ/2π as the Euclidean x₄-period (Theorem 4.6); (6) local equilibrium as the shear-free, asymptotically expansion-free null cone of a distant McGucken Sphere, in all directions of the SO(3) measure (§2.1, Theorem 3.2); (7) lensing as the derived focusing of Sphere lightfronts (§2.4, Theorem 4.7 Step 3); (8) Eqs. (1)–(6) as Theorem 4.7 Steps 1–5 with the shared conservation input of Corollary 4.8; (9) Λ as the common integration constant, with the dark-energy equation of state derived in [27]; (10) holography as a Huygens theorem of the Sphere (§11); (11) equilibrium as the stationary reduced state of the Compton-tick diffusion, with the metric defined throughout and the residual D_x^(McG) computed (§6.3); (12) time-reversal invariance from the Algebraic Channel and quantization of the advance, with the ensemble equation left classical (Theorem 5.1, [5]); (13) non-equilibrium spacetime as the per-event regime of the Sphere (§6.3, §13).

7.1 Seven contrasts

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic predicts that every input of the equation-of-state derivation is a theorem of the McGucken Sphere. Each contrast names Jacobson's input and the theorem that derives it; the quotations are those of §7.0.

1. Thermodynamics. Jacobson assumes "that the entropy is proportional to horizon area" [7, ¶4], with η "undetermined by anything we have said so far," together with the Unruh temperature and the Clausius relation. The Second Law, the area law, and the Unruh temperature are Theorems 3.3, 3.5, 4.6; the Clausius relation is derived in Theorem 4.7 Step 4.
2. The null Rindler horizon. Jacobson invokes the equivalence principle to treat each neighbourhood as flat and constructs local Rindler horizons on that background. The McGucken Sphere expanding at c from every event is the null surface, and the metric on which the horizon lives is the theorem of §2.1.
3. The Unruh effect, which presupposes quantum field theory, i, and ħ. Jacobson's temperature is that of the Minkowski vacuum with respect to the boost Hamiltonian, presupposing the imaginary unit of the quantum phase, the KMS structure, and the quantum of action. The i is the perpendicularity of x₄ = ict (§2.1), ħ is the action per Compton tick (§2.3), and quantum mechanics is derived along two channels (twenty-three results, forty-six derivations, [5]).
4. The cutoff. Jacobson requires l_c for finiteness and finds that consistency requires it to be of order the Planck length. The advance proceeds one Compton tick at a time and tiles the horizon by Planck-area cells (§2.3, §3.5); the scale is derived.
5. One derivation versus two. Jacobson gives one thermodynamic route. The Principle derives the same equations along two disjoint channels (Corollary 4.8); convergence through disjoint machinery is evidence that the Principle sits beneath the law.
6. Scope. Jacobson's result is confined to gravity as an equation of state. The Principle derives general relativity as a twenty-four-theorem chain [4], quantum mechanics as a twenty-three-theorem chain [5], thermodynamics as its own chain [3], and explains why the three connect (Theorem 5.1).
7. The microphysics. Jacobson defers η to a future microscopic theory of spacetime structure and closes on non-equilibrium spacetime. The Principle is that microphysics: the substrate whose state-counting statistics are the thermodynamics Jacobson assumed.

Jacobson inverted the logic of general relativity once, from curvature → thermodynamics to thermodynamics → curvature, and stopped at thermodynamics as bedrock. dx₄/dt = ic performs the second inversion: one geometric principle → both thermodynamics and curvature.
