7.1bis The 2015 entanglement-equilibrium paper read in full: each stated assumption derived from the Principle

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic states that the McGucken Sphere expands at c from every event, its wavelength setting the action h and its volume defining a nonlocality. The 2015 paper [33] (verified-read, full text) replaces the 1995 horizon with a small causal diamond — the region swept by the Sphere from a past vertex and bounded by the past cone of a future vertex — and replaces the Clausius relation with a maximization of entanglement entropy at fixed volume. Each of its stated assumptions is derived below from the Sphere, and the paper's fixed-volume restriction, which its author leaves unexplained, is the Principle's own statement that the Sphere's volume defines the nonlocality.

(1) The hypothesis. Jacobson: "When the geometry and quantum fields are simultaneously varied from maximal symmetry, the entanglement entropy in a small geodesic ball is maximal at fixed volume" [33, §I], motivated "by the notion of vacuum as an equilibrium state".

Derivation from the Principle. Maximal symmetry at an event is the statement that the McGucken Sphere expands at the same rate c in every spatial direction (isotropy, SO(3)) and in every inertial frame (Lorentz covariance, Lemma 7.4.1; Theorem 8 of [4]). The reduced state of the Compton-tick advance in that geometry is the one carried by the unique SO(3)-invariant measure on S² (Theorem 3.2), and the uniform measure maximizes the entropy -∫plnp dμ over all measures on S² with the same support, by the Gibbs inequality. The vacuum, the overlap of Spheres expanding at +ic from neighbouring events (Theorem 10.1), is therefore the maximum-entropy state of the advance at fixed geometry; varying the geometry away from maximal symmetry breaks the isotropy of the measure and lowers the entropy. The hypothesis is the Gibbs-inequality statement about the Sphere's measure, and the fixed-volume condition is item (8).

(2) The assumption behind it. Jacobson: "The area density of vacuum entanglement entropy η is finite and universal", which "involves UV aspects of quantum gravity that are not currently understood, so it remains an assumption" [33, §I]; and in §IV, "The scaling with area is natural in any theory with a large density of states at short distances. The assumption that η is universal is motivated by the idea that the UV structure of the vacuum is common to all states in the class being considered."

Derivation from the Principle. Finiteness is the Compton tick: the advance of a McGucken Sphere of mass m proceeds in steps Δx₄ = iλ_C, and at the horizon tier the step is ℓ_P (§7.0 item 3), so the density of states at short distances is large but finite, one mode per Planck cell, and η = 1/4ℓ_P² (Theorem 3.5). Universality follows from the invariance of the rate: dx₄/dt = ic holds with the same c at every event and in every frame, and ℓ_P = √(ħG/c³) is built from that rate, the action per tick, and the coupling fixed once by Newtonian matching (Theorem 4.1 Step 6), so the UV structure of the vacuum is the same Sphere at every event. The "states in the class being considered" are the reduced states of the advance.

(3) Hamilton's principle versus entropy maximization. Jacobson: "It is well known that diffeomorphism invariance selects the Einstein equation, at second order in derivatives, as the unique gravitational field equation in a metric theory. Since the MVEH is formulated in a diffeomorphism-invariant fashion, it is therefore not surprising that the Einstein equation would arise. Nevertheless, entropy maximization is quite different from Hamilton's principle of stationary action, so something new is learned here. Moreover, the Newton constant that appears in the derived Einstein equation—which is not fixed by diffeomorphism invariance—has precisely the value required in order for η to correspond to the Bekenstein-Hawking value, 1/4ħG. This is a nontrivial and essential consistency property of the derivation" [33, §I].

Derivation from the Principle. The two routes Jacobson contrasts are the two channels of Theorem 5.1. Hamilton's principle with diffeomorphism invariance and Lovelock uniqueness is the Algebraic Channel (Theorem 4.1, Steps 4′–5); entropy maximization is the Geometric Channel (Theorem 4.7 in its diamond form, item (7) below). Corollary 4.8 states what Jacobson observes: the two derivations share only local conservation and the Newtonian matching, and otherwise disjoint machinery, M(Π_A)∩M(Π_B) = ∅. The consistency he calls nontrivial — that the matched G makes η the Bekenstein–Hawking value — is Theorem 4.5 Step C, where the 1/4 is computed from the Algebraic-Channel action by the Euclidean cigar and agrees with the Geometric-Channel matching. The agreement is forced because both channels read the McGucken Sphere (Corollary 5.3); the "something new" is the second channel.

(4) The area deficit. Jacobson: "Central to our story is the equivalence of (1) to the statement that the surface area deficit of any small, spacelike geodesic ball of fixed volume is proportional to the energy density in the ball" [33, §II]; his Eqs. (5)–(8) give, at fixed volume, δA|_V = -Ω_d-2ℓ^d ℛ/2(d²-1) with ℛ = 2G₀0, hence δA|_V = -8πG Ω_d-2ℓ^d T₀0/(d²-1); and "this simple geometrical relation contains the full content of Einstein's equation, if it holds at all spacetime points and for all timelike unit vectors."

Derivation from the Principle. The geodesic ball of radius ℓ is the t = 0 slice of the diamond whose lower null boundary is Σ_+(o_-), the McGucken Sphere expanded from the past vertex for coordinate time ℓ/c, and whose upper boundary is the past cone of the future vertex. The area of ∂Σ is the cross-sectional area of that Sphere at r = ℓ, and its deficit relative to 4πℓ² is the integrated focusing of the Sphere's generators by the Compton-tick energy inside, the Raychaudhuri statement of §7.0 item (7) carried from θ to A: with θ = -λR_μνk^μk^ν on the generators and the SO(3) average ∫dΩn^kn^l = Ω_d-2δ^kl/(d-1) (his Eq. (30), the second moment of the measure of Theorem 3.2), the angular average of R_ikjln^kn^l is ℛ/(d-1), which produces his coefficient. "At all spacetime points" is the Principle's "from every event"; "for all timelike unit vectors" is the Lorentz covariance of the rate c (Lemma 7.4.1; Theorem 8 of [4]): the ball is defined by the choice of u^a, and because the Sphere expands at c in every frame, the deficit relation holds for every u^a, which is what upgrades the 00-component to the tensor equation. Jacobson's Appendix A traces the radius-excess form ℓ- √(A/4π) = GM/3c² to Feynman and the deficit relations to Pauli and Riemann; in the Principle the excess is the delay of the Sphere's lightfront, the quantity Theorem 4.7 Step 3 integrates.

(5) The qubit argument. Jacobson: "To localize the qbit within a region of size ℓ we must give it an energy of at least ħ/ℓ which, according to (8), will contribute an area deficit of order ħG, hence a surface entropy decrease of order unity, offsetting the added qbit" [33, §II].

Derivation from the Principle. A system localized to ℓ is a McGucken Sphere of wavelength ℓ, and ħc/ℓ is its Compton-tick energy (Theorem 3.1 with λ_C→ℓ). Its energy density ∼ħc/ℓ⁴ in his Eq. (8) with d = 4 gives δA|_V∼-8πG·(4π/15)·ħ/c³ ∼-ℓ_P², one Planck cell, and by Theorem 3.5 one cell carries 1/4 nat. The order-unity offset is the statement that adding one state to the interior removes one cell from the bounding count: S = k_BN/4 on the horizon and the state count inside are the same count Ω read on two surfaces (Theorem 6bis.3), so the bookkeeping balances cell for state. Jacobson's remark that a highly entropic object "makes its mark in the vacuum as well" is the same statement: the object's internal states are Sphere states, already in the vacuum count.

(6) The conformal Killing vector. Jacobson: the diamond's unique spherically symmetric conformal isometry is generated by ζ = 1/(2ℓ)[(ℓ² - u²)∂_u + (ℓ² - v²)∂_v] (his Eq. (9)), with ℒ_ζη_ab = -(2t/ℓ)η_ab (Eq. (11)); "The vector ζ is tangent to the null generators on the past and future null boundaries of the diamond, so those boundaries are conformal Killing horizons"; the edge ∂Σ "is a bifurcation surface", and the surface gravity is unity [33, §III].

Derivation from the Principle. The null boundaries are McGucken Spheres: u = -ℓ is Σ_+(o_-) and v = ℓ is the past cone of o_+, and ζ is tangent to their generators because it is the flow along the Sphere's own lightfront. The symmetry is conformal because the Sphere's radius grows, r = ct: a flow that follows the expanding wavefront rescales the metric, and the conformal factor -2t/ℓ in Eq. (11) is the expansion rate ṙ/r of the Sphere at time t, scaled to the diamond, read as a dilation. A true Killing vector exists for the Rindler wedge because the wedge is the ℓ→∞ limit (§7.0 item 6), where the rescaling vanishes; at finite ℓ the Principle's expansion is visible and only a conformal symmetry survives. The bifurcation surface ∂Σ is where the expanding Sphere from o_- meets the contracting Sphere onto o_+ — the surface on which the advance from the two vertices has equal radius — and the unit surface gravity is the normalization of the x₄-advance along the generators.

(7) The modular Hamiltonian and the Clausius relation. Jacobson: "The vacuum state of any QFT, restricted to the diamond, can be expressed (formally) as a thermal density matrix, ρ = Z^-1exp(-K/T), T = ħ/2π"; K "will be the generator of Lorentz boosts, i.e. hyperbolic angle shifts, at the edge of the diamond"; the vanishing of the modular free energy variation gives δS = (2π/ħ) δ⟨K⟩: "This is just the usual Clausius relation for a 'thermal' state"; and for a CFT, K = H_ζ = ∫_ΣT_abζ^b dΣ^a [33, §IV, Eqs. (14)–(17)].

Derivation from the Principle. Theorem 10.1 (ii): the modular flow of the wedge algebra is the boost, the x₄-advance read in the accelerated frame, with modular Hamiltonian K = 2π∫U⟨:T_UU:⟩dU on the horizon; the temperature ħ/2π in boost units is Theorem 4.6, the Euclidean x₄-period. The diamond result of Hislop–Longo that Jacobson cites is the conformal image of the wedge result, which in the Principle is the finite-ℓ McGucken Sphere mapped to its ℓ→∞ null plane (item 6). The Clausius relation δS = (2π/ħ)δ⟨K⟩ is Corollary 10.2(i) — the first-order vanishing of the Araki–Uhlmann relative entropy on the Sphere-cogenerated algebra — written on the diamond, and it is the relation Theorem 4.7 Step 4 uses: the Compton-tick energy of the excitation, weighted by the boost generator ζ along the Sphere's lightfront, equals the x₄-period temperature times the change in the count. H_ζ is the 1995 heat of §7.0 item (2) integrated over the ball instead of over the horizon.

(8) The fixed-volume restriction. Jacobson: "The MVEH is analogous, but with the additional feature that the energy vanishes. That the free energy of a diamond has no energy term can be motivated by comparison with de Sitter spacetime, and the restriction to fixed volume arises from the fact that the diamond has a conformal Killing vector rather than a true Killing vector"; and at the end of §V, "The coefficient would have been off by the factor (d+1)/3 had we used the area variation at fixed radius (4) rather than at fixed volume (5)" [33, §IV–V]. In Appendix D he derives the gravitational contribution δH_ζ = -(d-2)κδV/8πGℓ, which converts the area variation to δA|_V.

Derivation from the Principle. The McGucken Principle states that the McGucken Sphere's volume defines a nonlocality: the count Ω is a count of the advance-states within the Sphere's volume, and the horizon-area reading of that count (Theorem 3.5) is its holographic form (§11). The fixed-volume variation is therefore the variation that holds the nonlocal region fixed and asks how its bounding count changes; the fixed-radius variation changes the region itself and mixes the count with a change of the nonlocality, which is the origin of the spurious factor (d+1)/3 = 5/3. Appendix A.3bis shows the volume-fixed count and the horizon-area count to be the same count of the same Sphere. The conformal Killing vector that Jacobson identifies as the cause is item (6): the Sphere's expansion rescales the metric, and the extra term -(d-2)κδV/8πGℓ of his Appendix D is the gravitational Hamiltonian's response to that rescaling, i.e. the work done by the expansion of the McGucken Sphere against the volume, which the fixed-volume condition removes. The de Sitter comparison is the cosmological Sphere R₄ = ct of §12, whose Euclidean section is closed and whose free energy is -TS (Gibbons–Hawking [34], as Jacobson's Appendix C states), so that maximizing S at fixed V is minimizing the free energy of the Sphere.

(9) The nonconformal conjecture. Jacobson: "If the matter field is not conformal, K is not given by (17)"; for a QFT with a UV fixed point and ℓ≪L_QFT, "we conjecture—and we shall assume—that δ⟨K⟩ has the form of (19) with an additional term δX that is a spacetime scalar"; "Our entanglement variation assumption for nonconformal matter (21) concerns only standard QFT, and is either true or false" [33, §IV, §VI]. The divergence of Eq. (24) then ties the scalar to the local curvature scale, λ = (2π/ħ)ηδX + Λ (Eq. (25)).

Derivation from the Principle. Jacobson states the conjecture for any QFT with a UV fixed point; the derivation here is given for the case of a massive free field, whose departure from conformality is its mass term. Under Theorem 3.1 the mass is the Compton tick rate ω_C = mc²/ħ, so L_QFT = λ_C and the condition ℓ≪λ_C places the diamond below one Compton tick, where the massive McGucken Sphere is read at the massless tier, which is why the field is asymptotically conformal there. For this case δX is a spacetime scalar because it is built from m, hence from ω_C, an invariant of the Sphere (the same in every frame by dx₄/dt = ic), and its ℓ-dependence is that of the tick count on the diamond size; whether this form holds for every nonconformal QFT in Jacobson's class is, as he says, true or false of standard QFT and is left open here. Its absorption into λ by Eq. (25) is the same step as f = -R/2 + Λ in §7.0 item (8): the trace part of the Compton-tick energy enters the equation only through the integration constant, so the field equations of Theorem 4.7 hold for massive matter with Λ carrying the scalar.

(10) The coherent-state challenge. Jacobson: "The example of a coherent state reveals a challenge in this regard: Such a state can have nonzero energy density while leaving entanglement entropy unchanged. That is, not all energy registers as a change of entanglement. … Unless a further consequence of that hypothesis is found, or the hypothesis is refined and strengthened in some way, the Einstein equation does not appear to follow from it in all generality" [33, §VI].

Derivation from the Principle. The energy of a coherent state gravitates through the Algebraic Channel, which uses no entropy: Theorem 4.1 derives the field equations from Diff_McG, the constitutive identity, and Lovelock uniqueness, and the coherent state's T_μν enters there directly. Theorem 5.1(iii) states that gravity has both derivations, so a case in which the Geometric-Channel count is unchanged while the energy is nonzero is a case the Algebraic Channel carries alone; the Einstein equation follows in all generality because it has the second derivation. Within the Geometric Channel itself, the count that registers the coherent state is the relative entropy: Theorem 10.1(iii) gives, for a coherent excitation ω_φ of the wedge vacuum, S(ω₀ω_φ) = -2π∫U⟨:T_ab:⟩_ω_φξ^aξ^b dU dvol, which is nonzero and equal to 2πδ⟨K⟩/ħ — the Clausius relation of item (7) with the relative entropy as the count of Compton-tick states by which the excitation differs from the vacuum. The refinement Jacobson asks for is the replacement of δS_vN by S(ω₀ω_φ), which the McGucken Sphere supplies as its count (§10).

(11) The closing questions. Jacobson asks: "Do graviton fluctuations contribute to the entanglement entropy?"; "Can a gravitational field equation with higher curvature corrections be derived along these lines?"; how the assumptions relate to Lloyd's quantum geometric limit [35]; and "According to our derivation the Einstein equation is a property of vacuum equilibrium. Does this suggest how to include nonequilibrium effects?" [33, §VI].

Derivation from the Principle. Gravitons: Corollary 7.4(iii) of [19] (verified-read) states, "There is no graviton: gravity is the geometry of h_ij, not a force mediated by particles", following from its Theorem 7.1, under which only the spatial-slice metric h_ij carries dynamical degrees of freedom. The UV part ηA that Jacobson calls inscrutable is the count N = A/ℓ_P² of modes of the McGucken Sphere's own expansion at the horizon tier (Theorem 3.5, Lemma 7.4.4), which are features of the geometry and not quanta of a mediating field; Jacobson's observation that including graviton energy would double-count is then the statement that there is no separate graviton energy to add, the whole gravitational side being the geometry already on the left of his equation. Higher curvature: in the Algebraic Channel, Lovelock's theorem in d = 4 (Theorem 4.1 Step 5) gives G_μν + Λg_μν and nothing else, so no curvature-squared term with coefficient ℓ₁² arises from the Principle; corrections at the tick scale are the per-event departures of §6.3, with ℓ₁∼ℓ_P. Lloyd's limit bounds the number of events per unit four-volume by ħ and G; in the Principle that number is the density ρ_x₄ of Sphere-apex events of Theorem 3.6, bounded by one per Planck four-volume. Non-equilibrium: §7.0 item (13), the per-event regime of the Sphere with residual D_x^(McG).

Summary of the attribution. (1) the hypothesis is the Gibbs inequality for the SO(3)-invariant measure of Theorem 3.2; (2) finiteness and universality of η are the Compton tick and the frame-invariance of the rate (Theorem 3.5); (3) Hamilton's principle and entropy maximization are the two channels, with the Bekenstein–Hawking consistency computed in Theorem 4.5 (Corollary 4.8); (4) the area deficit is the integrated focusing of the McGucken Sphere's generators, holding for all u^a by Lorentz covariance of c (Theorem 4.7 Step 3, Lemma 7.4.1); (5) the qubit balance is one state for one Planck cell (Theorems 3.5, 6bis.3); (6) the conformal Killing vector is the Sphere's growth r = ct read as a dilation; (7) the modular Clausius relation is Theorem 10.1 with Theorem 4.6; (8) fixed volume is the Principle's statement that the Sphere's volume defines the nonlocality (Appendix A.3bis); (9) for a massive free field δX is a scalar built from the Compton tick rate, absorbed into Λ as in Theorem 4.7 Step 5; (10) coherent states gravitate through the Algebraic Channel and are counted by the relative entropy of Theorem 10.1; (11) there is no graviton (Corollary 7.4(iii) of [19]) and the UV count is the Sphere's horizon-tier modes, no higher-curvature term arises in d = 4, Lloyd's bound is ρ_x₄, and non-equilibrium is the per-event regime.

7.1ter The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Reading of Jacobson's own account of the 2015 paper: the move from the Rindler horizon to the ball, the statistical reading, and the two items he states he lacks

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic states that a McGucken Sphere expands at c from every event; the Rindler wedge of Jacobson 1995 is the ℓ→∞ limit of a Sphere's null cone (§7.0 item 6), and the causal diamond of Jacobson 2015 is a Sphere at finite radius ℓ together with the past cone of its future vertex (§7.1bis item (6)). What Jacobson describes as the improvement of 2015 over 1995 is, under the Principle, the move from the limit of the Sphere to the Sphere itself, and the two items he states he still lacks — the reason for the fixed volume, and generality against the coherent state — are the volume clause of the Principle and the Algebraic Channel. The quotations below are from the 2015 paper [33] (verified against the full text) and from the 2025 interview [1] (verified against the full transcript).

(1) The arena. Jacobson, interview [1]: "I took it in a different direction in a paper in 2015, 10 years ago, which I think was a significant improvement of what I did back in 1995, which was to focus not on local Rindler horizons, but to focus on regions of space that are ball-shaped." The 2015 paper [33, §III]: the ball Σ is generated "by sending out geodesics of length ℓ from o in all directions orthogonal to u^a"; its causal diamond "is the intersection of the future of a past vertex and the past of a future vertex"; in null coordinates the diamond "consists of the intersection of the regions u > -ℓ and v < ℓ"; and "The vector ζ is tangent to the null generators on the past and future null boundaries of the diamond, so those boundaries are conformal Killing horizons."

Derivation from the Principle. The boundary u = -ℓ is the McGucken Sphere Σ_+(o_-) expanded from the past vertex o_- for coordinate time ℓ/c (Definition 2 of [4], §2.2), and v = ℓ is the past cone of the future vertex o_+; the ball is the equatorial slice t = 0 of that Sphere. The conformal Killing vector ζ is tangent to the null boundaries because it follows the Sphere's own lightfront, and the symmetry is conformal rather than isometric because the Sphere's radius grows, r = ct: the conformal factor in Jacobson's Eq. (11), ℒ_ζη_ab = -(2t/ℓ)η_ab, is the growth of the Sphere read as a dilation (§7.1bis item (6)). In 1995 the arena was the Rindler wedge, the ℓ→∞ limit of this Sphere's null cone, where the dilation vanishes and a true Killing vector exists (§7.0 item 6). The improvement Jacobson names is therefore the replacement of the Sphere's limit by the Sphere at finite radius; the object was present in both derivations, named in neither.

(2) Statistical versus thermodynamic. Jacobson, interview [1]: "it's a more statistical approach to this relation as opposed to thermodynamic one." The 2015 paper [33, §I], on the holographic work it combines with 1995: "This approach treats the entropy statistically, rather than thermodynamically, and it concerns entropy of a compact region in the CFT at one time, rather than following the change of horizon entropy. The present work combines the local spacetime setting of the equation of state approach, with the statistical, compact region setting of the holographic analysis, but it proceeds directly in spacetime, making no use of holography."

Derivation from the Principle. The McGucken Entropy Identity (Theorem 6.1, Theorem (The McGucken Entropy Identity) of [3], reproduced in §6) states that the horizon count — reading (4), Bekenstein–Hawking, which 1995 follows as "the change of horizon entropy" — and the compact-region count — reading (3), von Neumann, "entropy of a compact region … at one time" — are two readings of the SO(3)-invariant Haar-measure count on the McGucken Sphere. The thermodynamic derivation of 1995 and the statistical derivation of 2015 count the same Sphere, on its horizon and within its volume; the holographic form of the identity, that the count within the volume is read on the bounding surface, is §11. The consistency Jacobson calls essential — [33, §I]: "the Newton constant that appears in the derived Einstein equation—which is not fixed by diffeomorphism invariance—has precisely the value required in order for η to correspond to the Bekenstein-Hawking value, 1/4ħG. This is a nontrivial and essential consistency property of the derivation" — is Theorem 4.5 Step C, where the coefficient 1/4 is computed from the Euclidean Einstein–Hilbert action on the Sphere's cigar, so the horizon reading and the volume reading of the count carry the same G (§7.1bis item (3)).

(3) "Something new." Jacobson [33, §I]: "It is well known that diffeomorphism invariance selects the Einstein equation, at second order in derivatives, as the unique gravitational field equation in a metric theory. Since the MVEH is formulated in a diffeomorphism-invariant fashion, it is therefore not surprising that the Einstein equation would arise. Nevertheless, entropy maximization is quite different from Hamilton's principle of stationary action, so something new is learned here."

Derivation from the Principle. The two routes Jacobson sets side by side are the two channels of Theorem 5.1 (Theorems 19.5–19.5.2 of [3]). Hamilton's principle with diffeomorphism invariance and Lovelock uniqueness is the Algebraic Channel, Theorem 4.1 (Theorem 9 of [4]), reading x₄ = ict as a label; entropy extremization at fixed volume is the Geometric Channel, Theorem 4.7 (Theorem 14 of [4]) in its diamond form, reading dx₄/dt = ic as the active expansion of the McGucken Sphere. That both routes derive the same field equation with the same G, sharing only local conservation and the Newtonian matching, is Corollary 4.8, the Hilbert–Jacobson agreement (Theorem 19.4 of [3], §4.9). What Jacobson learns as new is derived in the Principle as the agreement of two channels descending from one rate.

(4) The first item he states he lacks: the reason for the fixed volume. Jacobson, interview [1]: "I had to hold the spatial volume of the ball fixed in order for the Einstein equation I inferred to have the correct relationship between the gravitational constant and the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of the boundary. I find that really striking because it means that there's something special about holding the volume fixed. I have no idea why I should hold it fixed … the fact that that choice was the volume requires explanation, and I don't have the explanation." The 2015 paper [33, §IV–V]: "the restriction to fixed volume arises from the fact that the diamond has a conformal Killing vector rather than a true Killing vector"; "The coefficient would have been off by the factor (d+1)/3 had we used the area variation at fixed radius (4) rather than at fixed volume (5)"; and Appendix D: "If ζ is only a conformal Killing vector, δH_ζ does not vanish. … the gravitational field contribution to δH_ζ turns out to be -(d-2)κδV/8πGℓ."

Derivation from the Principle. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic states that the McGucken Sphere's volume defines a nonlocality. The count Ω whose extremum Jacobson takes is a count of the advance-states within the Sphere's volume (§6), and its horizon-area reading is the holographic form of the same count (Theorem 3.5, §11). The variation that holds the volume fixed holds the counted region fixed; the variation at fixed radius changes the region while counting, which is the origin of the spurious factor (d+1)/3 = 5/3 in d = 4 (§7.1bis item (8)). Appendix A.3bis shows the volume-fixed count and the horizon-area count to be the same count of the same Sphere. Appendix D's gravitational term -(d-2)κδV/8πGℓ is the correction that converts the fixed-radius area variation to the fixed-volume one; under the Principle it is the bookkeeping of the Sphere's growth, r = ct, read as the dilation of Eq. (11): because the Sphere's radius changes along the flow of ζ, the Hamiltonian H_ζ receives a volume term, and holding the volume fixed removes exactly that term. The explanation Jacobson states he does not have is the volume clause of the Principle.

(5) The second item he states he lacks: generality against the coherent state. Jacobson [33, §VI]: "The example of a coherent state reveals a challenge in this regard Varadarajan 2016: Such a state can have nonzero energy density while leaving entanglement entropy unchanged. … That is, not all energy registers as a change of entanglement. This is consistent with the hypothesis of maximal vacuum entanglement, although the Einstein equation implies that the entropy has decreased — relative to vacuum — by more than it needs to in order to satisfy the hypothesis. Unless a further consequence of that hypothesis is found, or the hypothesis is refined and strengthened in some way, the Einstein equation does not appear to follow from it in all generality."

Derivation from the Principle. The Einstein field equations have two derivations from dx₄/dt = ic (Theorem 5.1(iii); Theorem 19.4 of [3]). A coherent state's energy density enters the Algebraic Channel directly: Theorem 4.1 derives the field equations from Diff_McG, the constitutive identity u^μu_μ = -c², Noether's second theorem, and Lovelock uniqueness, with T_μν as source and no entropy anywhere in the derivation. The case Jacobson describes — nonzero energy with unchanged entanglement entropy — is a case the Geometric Channel's count does not register and the Algebraic Channel carries alone; the Einstein equation follows in all generality because it has the second derivation (§7.1bis item (10)). Within the Geometric Channel, the quantity that does register the coherent state is the Araki–Uhlmann relative entropy S(ω_φω₀) of Theorem 10.1, which is positive for any state distinct from the vacuum whether or not the von Neumann entropy changes; Corollary 10.2 is derived from its first-order vanishing, so the Geometric Channel's first law is the relative-entropy statement and the "entropy has decreased by more than it needs to" is the second-order positivity of S(ω_φω₀) (§10). Jacobson's observation that this "is consistent with the hypothesis" is read as the inequality δ² S ≤0 that the positivity of the relative entropy supplies.

(6) What Jacobson says the thermodynamic method cannot see. Jacobson, interview [1]: "the level I'm thinking about with this thermodynamic reasoning or even the statistical one using quantum field theory is kind of immune or blind to the fundamental substructure." The 2015 paper [33, §I] names the substructure's one required property: "To match the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, vacuum entanglement entropy should be cut off at the Planck scale. Considering the gravitational backreaction of vacuum fluctuations, such a cutoff appears natural, but it lies deep in the regime of poorly understood quantum gravity effects."

Derivation from the Principle. The substructure is the McGucken Sphere, and the cutoff is its wavelength: a Sphere carried by mass m has wavelength λ_C = h/mc (Theorem 3.1), and at the mass whose Compton wavelength equals its Schwarzschild radius the wavelength equals ℓ_P up to 2√(π) (Theorem 3.5 Step 1). The Planck-scale cutoff Jacobson places "deep in the regime of poorly understood quantum gravity effects" is derived as the Sphere's wavelength at the horizon tier, from the same rate c and the same action h that the anchor sentence states. The 2015 paper's ηA with η = 1/4ħG is the Planck-cell count of Theorem 3.5, and both of Jacobson's derivations are, on this reading, counts of the Sphere whose existence they are blind to.

Closing attribution. (1) The 2015 arena is a McGucken Sphere at finite radius, the 1995 arena its ℓ→∞ limit: Definition 2 of [4], §7.0 item 6, §7.1bis item (6). (2) The statistical and the thermodynamic readings are readings (3) and (4) of the count: Theorem 6.1, with the shared G from Theorem 4.5 Step C. (3) Hamilton's principle and entropy extremization are the two channels: Theorem 5.1, Theorem 4.1, Theorem 4.7, Corollary 4.8. (4) The fixed volume is the volume clause of the Principle: §7.1bis item (8), Appendix A.3bis. (5) Generality against the coherent state is the Algebraic Channel, Theorem 4.1, with the relative entropy of Theorem 10.1 as the Geometric-Channel quantity that registers it. (6) The Planck cutoff is the Sphere's horizon-tier wavelength: Theorem 3.5 Step 1.

7.2 Jacobson's own stated open problems, each resolved

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic predicts that an originator who derives gravity from assumed thermodynamics will, across the life of the programme, name the assumed items as the open ones. Jacobson has done so across three decades and three venues: the 1995 closing paragraph naming non-equilibrium spacetime as the open understanding [7, §7.0 item 13]; the 2015 entanglement-equilibrium paper, whose hypothesis is that "the entanglement entropy in a small geodesic ball is maximal at fixed volume" [33, introduction] and which states that the UV cutoff fixing η lies in a regime of quantum gravity it calls poorly understood [33]; and the 2025 interview [1]. The 1995 letter is quoted item by item in §7.0 and the 2015 paper in §7.1bis; the interview is quoted in full, item by item, in §7.2bis; here the items are given at the level of their stated criterion with the resolving theorem named, and the longer verbatim record is reproduced in [14, §5.6] and in §6.6.9.18 of [6].

(a) Gravity "already knows" thermodynamics. Criterion: why should the field equations be such that the Second Law holds? Resolution: Corollary 5.3 — the Second Law is derived from the physical expansion of the McGucken Sphere (Theorem 3.3) and the field equations are derived from the focusing of the Spheres from neighbouring events by matter (Theorem 4.7), so the two are theorems of one premise and their agreement is forced.

(b) The local Rindler horizon posited at every point. Criterion: Jacobson invented the construction in which every point can be treated as sitting on a horizon. Resolution: §2.2 with §7.0 item (6) — every event carries an expanding McGucken Sphere whose null cone is that horizon, and the local Rindler horizon is the R→∞ limit of the cone of a Sphere at affine distance R, with θ = 2/R→0 and σ = 0 (GR T11 of [4]).

(c) "Interpretive fuzziness" in the definitions of heat and horizon. Criterion: the heat in the Clausius relation and the horizon under curvature lack controlled definitions. Resolution: Theorem 4.7, Steps 1–4 — heat is the Compton-tick action crossing the null cone, the temperature is the Euclidean x₄-period, the entropy is the Planck-cell count; each is defined by the McGucken Sphere.

(d) Finiteness of the entanglement entropy. Criterion: "To match the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, vacuum entanglement entropy should be cut off at the Planck scale. Considering the gravitational backreaction of vacuum fluctuations, such a cutoff appears natural, but it lies deep in the regime of poorly understood quantum gravity effects" [33, §I]. Resolution: §2.3 — the count is finite from the outset because the advance proceeds one tick at a time; N = A/ℓ_P² cells, one quarter nat each.

(e) Discreteness versus the continuum. Criterion: Jacobson's stated uncertainty whether spacetime is discrete. Resolution: Lemma 7.4.2 (Proposition 10.8 of [6]) — the geometry is continuous (the coordinate x₄ = ict is a real continuum) and the action is discrete (one h per cycle); the finiteness of horizon entropy comes from the discreteness of the action count, derived there from e^-iω_Ct = e^-(mc/ħ)x₄ and E T_C = h.

(f) The metric as redundant given the vacuum fluctuations. Criterion: the metric is encoded in the correlations of the vacuum and may be no separate degree of freedom. Resolution: Lemma 7.4.3 ([6]) — the metric is the square of x₄ = ict, dx₄² = -c²dt², and the quantum phase is its exponential, e^-iEt/ħ = e^-(mc/ħ)x₄; the vacuum correlations and the metric are generated together by the advance, so the metric is encoded in the correlations as Jacobson says, as a second reading of the same coordinate.

(g) Entanglement makes space connected. Criterion: removing vacuum entanglement across a surface would cleave space. Resolution: Lemma 7.4.5 ([20]) — the McGucken Sphere's volume defines the nonlocality, a joint state requires a region within both systems' Spheres, so only systems with intersecting Spheres can be entangled; the vacuum across a surface is entangled because the Spheres of events on either side intersect across it, and a surface across which none intersected would bound two regions with no joint state.

(h) Holding the spatial volume fixed. Criterion: the 2015 extremization reproduces the Bekenstein–Hawking coefficient only at fixed volume — "off by the factor (d+1)/3 had we used the area variation at fixed radius" — and attributes the restriction to the diamond having "a conformal Killing vector rather than a true Killing vector" [33, §IV–V]; in the 2025 interview Jacobson states he has no idea why the volume should be held fixed [1]. Resolution: §7.1bis item (8) — the McGucken Principle states that the McGucken Sphere's volume defines a nonlocality, so the count Ω is a count within that volume, the fixed-volume variation holds the nonlocal region fixed, and the volume-fixed count equals the horizon-area count of the same Sphere (Appendix A.3bis); the conformal Killing vector is the Sphere's growth r = ct read as a dilation (§7.1bis item (6)).

Closing attribution. Each of (a)–(h) is resolved by a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic: (a) Corollary 5.3; (b) §2.2; (c) Theorem 4.7; (d) §2.3 with Theorem 3.5; (e) Lemma 7.4.2; (f) Lemma 7.4.3; (g) Lemma 7.4.5; (h) §7.1bis item (8) with Appendix A.3bis.

7.2bis The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Reading of Jacobson's interview, read in full: ten connections between gravity, thermodynamics, and entanglement, each derived from the Principle

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic states one physical process — a McGucken Sphere expanding at the velocity of light from every event, its wavelength setting the action h, its volume defining a nonlocality — and derives from it both of the things Jacobson describes as filling empty space, the metric and the quantum vacuum. Jacobson states his frame in the interview [1]: "Spacetime in the vacuum is filled with two independent things … the metric of spacetime exists everywhere in space and time, and the vacuum of quantum fields exists everywhere in space and time, and there's an intimate connection between them." The ten connections he draws between those two things are quoted below in his words and read as theorems of the Principle. The quotations are from the interview transcript (verified against the full transcript); where a reading cites a theorem of this paper, the theorem number is given.

(1) "Gravity somehow already knows about thermodynamics." Jacobson: "When a black hole evaporates, the horizon area shrinks. Bekenstein had proposed and supported with good arguments that the area of a black hole horizon is a measure of entropy, and yet the second law of thermodynamics says entropy can't decrease. So, if a black hole is shrinking, then it must be that the entropy of everything else is growing by enough to counterbalance that. The Hawking radiation is carrying entropy away. … That involves the Einstein equation, because the outflux of Hawking radiation is accompanied by an influx of negative energy across the horizon. And the relation between the energy flux across the horizon and the change in the black hole area is governed by Einstein's equation. Only if Einstein's equation works the way it does would the second law of thermodynamics be upheld. But that's crazy, it seemed. That means that gravity somehow already knows about thermodynamics."

McGucken reading. The Second Law arises from the physical expansion of the McGucken Sphere: because every Sphere expands at c in one direction, the count of its Compton-tick cells on any resolving surface increases in that direction, and dS/dt > 0 is derived (Theorem 3.3, Theorem 9 of [3]). The Einstein field equations are derived from the same expansion: matter focuses the McGucken Spheres from neighbouring events, and the Clausius relation on their null cones, with the area law and the Unruh temperature, closes to G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG/c⁴)T_μν (Theorem 4.7, Theorem 14 of [4]). The two laws agree because both are derived from one premise; the Generalized Second Law that Jacobson describes — horizon area plus radiation entropy non-decreasing — is Theorem 3.6 (Theorem 17 of [3]), derived from the same expansion. Gravity knows thermodynamics in the sense that both are theorems of dx₄/dt = ic.

(2) The local Rindler horizon at every point. Jacobson: "there's a black hole somewhere that formed, but gravity's everywhere. So, it had to be that everywhere could be like a black hole. So, I invented this idea of a local Rindler horizon. Basically, it's a perspective by which you can, at any point in spacetime, you have the light cone that governs the limits of causality, and you have light-like surfaces that look like little pieces of event horizons of black holes."

McGucken reading. A McGucken Sphere expands from every event, and its null cone is a horizon. §7.0 item (6) derives Jacobson's construction: the local Rindler horizon through an event p is the null cone of a Sphere from a source event at affine distance R behind p, with expansion θ = 2/R →0 as R →∞ and shear exactly zero by the spherical symmetry of the Sphere. The construction Jacobson had to invent at every point is supplied at every event by the Principle, because the Sphere is at every event.

(3) The thermal vacuum in the wedge and the boost as time. Jacobson: "If you just take the ground state of a quantum field, relativistic quantum field theory, and you restrict it to that wedge here between the two light cones … then that state no longer looks like a ground state, it looks like a thermal state." The relevant generator: "this boost symmetry, it's like a hyperbolic rotation, it's also a symmetry, and it also has conserved quantity associated with it, and that's called the boost energy. And the Hamiltonian that is the generator of the boost symmetry is the Hamiltonian with respect to which the vacuum is thermal inside this wedge." And: "This is a little bit non-intuitive for somebody who's not used to thinking about hyperbolic angle as a form of time."

McGucken reading. The boost is the x₄-advance of the McGucken Sphere seen from an accelerated frame, and the hyperbolic angle is a form of time because x₄ = ict turns a Lorentz boost into a rotation — the McGucken–Wick rotation (§4.5). A rotation is periodic; the period 2π/κ of the Euclidean x₄-boost is a temperature by the KMS condition, and the Unruh temperature k_BT = ħκ/2πc is derived from it (Theorem 4.6, Theorem 13 of [4]). The KMS condition on the wedge algebra cogenerated by the Sphere is Theorem 10.1, and the Bisognano–Wichmann theorem Jacobson names is the statement that the modular flow of that algebra is the boost. The thermal character of the restricted vacuum is a consequence of the Sphere's expansion read from the accelerated frame.

(4) Entanglement across an imaginary wall, and the partner's negative energy. Jacobson: "the quantum vacuum of fields is a pure quantum state … but the degrees of freedom on different sides of my imaginary wall are entangled with each other. So if I have access only to one side of my wall, then those entangled degrees of freedom are no longer in a pure state taken by themselves. They become in a mixed state, and that mixed state has a thermal character. … this wall is not a physical wall. It's an artifact of my choice of coordinates." On the partner mode across the wall: "It is an anti-correlation in terms of a globally defined boost Hamiltonian. … because we take [time] down on one side, we count this as negative energy, but it's actually locally measured as positive," which he relates to "that Wheeler interpretation that it's an antiparticle, like when you go backward in time," adding "I think that's a confusing perspective to try to take."

McGucken reading. A McGucken Sphere from any event crosses any wall one draws; the two sides are correlated because they are two sides of one Sphere. Restricting observation to one side gives a count over the half of the Sphere on that side, and that count is the von Neumann entropy — reading (3) of the McGucken Entropy Identity (Theorem 6.1, from [3]) — which is why the restricted state is mixed and thermal. The partner's "negative energy" is the other half of the Sphere read with time reversed; the +ic orientation of the Principle fixes the forward reading (Theorem 5.1, Theorem 19.5 of [3]: the Geometric Channel is +ic-oriented, the Algebraic Channel time-symmetric), so the time-reversed description is the Algebraic-Channel reading of a +ic-oriented process, which is the source of the confusion Jacobson names.

(5) The infinite entanglement entropy and the cutoff from gravity. Jacobson: "there are an infinite number of modes of the field … packed up very close to the corner of that wedge, right up next to the horizon. … in standard quantum field theory, there's no shortest wavelength of modes. … So because there's an infinite number of them, it looks like there's an infinite entanglement entropy. … the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy is finite. It's the area divided by four times the Planck length squared. … once the fluctuation and its partner get so close together that the gravitational fluctuation they create engulfs them both in like a miniature horizon, then it's not any more possible to separate them. … So it has to cut itself off because of gravity. And the place it cuts itself off is, you can argue in a hand-waving way, is at the right scale to match the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy."

McGucken reading. The McGucken Sphere has a wavelength, and the wavelength sets the action h (§2.3, from [4] §6.9). Carried by a mass m, the Sphere's wavelength is the Compton wavelength h/mc (Theorem 3.1); at the mass whose Compton wavelength equals its Schwarzschild radius, the wavelength equals ℓ_P up to the factor 2√(π) (Theorem 3.5 Step 1). The entanglement entropy is finite because the Sphere's cells have a size, and at the horizon tier that size is the Planck length; the count is A/4ℓ_P² with coefficient 1/4 (Theorem 3.5). Jacobson's "miniature horizon" that engulfs a fluctuation and its partner is the Sphere at the tier where Compton and Schwarzschild wavelengths coincide, derived, with its scale, from the Principle; the species independence of the resulting entropy with the physical G is Proposition 10.3.

(6) The Einstein equation as an equation of state, by the ideal-gas analogy. Jacobson: "for the gas, I would need to know, okay, how does the entropy of the gas depend on the total amount of energy in the gas and the volume of the gas, let's say. Then I also need to know that energy is conserved. … And I need to know what's called the Clausius relation … So I was emulating that by saying, okay, my system is the world on one side of this local Rindler horizon. The entropy is the area times some fundamental constant. I'm going to apply energy conservation by demanding that the stress-energy tensor is divergence-free … And I'm going to apply the Clausius relation that relates the amount of heat that goes into the system to the amount of entropy change. … I found that the area of the horizon must evolve in a way consistent with or determined by Einstein's equation."

McGucken reading. Each of the three inputs is derived from the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic. The entropy as area times a constant: Theorem 3.5, the Planck-cell count of the McGucken Sphere's horizon, with the constant k_B/4ℓ_P² fixed by the Sphere's horizon-tier wavelength. Energy conservation: the Noether identity ∇_μT^μν = 0 of Theorem 4.1 Step 4, from the symmetry group of the Sphere. The Clausius relation: Corollary 10.2(i), derived from the first-order vanishing of the Araki–Uhlmann relative entropy on the wedge algebra cogenerated by the Sphere, with the Bisognano–Wichmann modular Hamiltonian as the boost energy Jacobson calls heat. With the three inputs derived, Theorem 4.7 derives the Einstein field equations as the equation of state of the Sphere's horizon, and the Hilbert–Jacobson agreement (Theorem 19.4 of [3], §4.9) shows the same equations derived by the variational route with no thermodynamic input.

(7) Continuum versus discreteness, and Marolf's constraint. Jacobson: "It doesn't sound like anything here implies spacetime is not continuous." On discretization: "I don't imagine it could be a naive one where you just discretize space, because then you would break some of the other symmetries that are important. … Moreover, it actually has to be non-local in some sense." On Marolf: "He made a pretty cogent argument that gravity cannot emerge … from a system which has locally defined observables that can be simultaneously precise at space-like separation. … the concept of it is that there must be a non-locality built into the very structure from which spacetime and gravity are emerging. … I don't know what it is, frankly." And: "what would be the simplest discrete thing I could build a universe out of?"

McGucken reading. The McGucken Sphere expands continuously at c and carries a discrete wavelength; it breaks no Lorentz symmetry because c is the invariant rate by which the Sphere is defined (§2.1, Definition 2 of [4]), and the Sphere Uniqueness Theorem [17] shows dx₄/dt = ic is the unique law generating a Lorentz-covariant family of such expanding spheres. The nonlocality Marolf requires is in the Principle's statement — the Sphere's volume defines a nonlocality — so the constraint is satisfied before gravity is derived; this is Theorem 19.4.2 of [3], reproduced in §4.9, where the constraint is stated in the words Jacobson uses in this interview. The simplest thing one can build a universe out of, on this reading, is a McGucken Sphere expanding at c from every event.

(8) Entanglement as the connectivity of space, and the metric as redundant. Jacobson: "The fact that space in this room is connected from this side of my imaginary boundary to this side has something to do with the fact that empty space is full of entangled vacuum fluctuations." On disentangling: "Actually, I would have an infinite negative energy density. I would have a state whose gravitational back reaction is so big that it probably sort of cleaves space into two halves." On the metric: "there isn't really a separate metric degree of freedom. In fact, if you just show me the vacuum fluctuations, I can measure the metric in the behavior of the vacuum fluctuations. The metric is encoded in the nature of the correlations of the vacuum fluctuations. So the metric is kind of superfluous and redundant in the description if I just knew the vacuum fluctuations." And: "I suspect in the future we'll find that the metric needs to go as a fundamental ingredient in the recipe."

McGucken reading. Two regions are connected because McGucken Spheres from shared source events pass through both; the entanglement between the regions is derived as the intersection of those Spheres, the First McGucken Law of Nonlocality (Lemma 7.4.5, [20]). Remove the shared Spheres and the connection is removed with them. The metric is derived from the Sphere's expansion as its squared rate: dx₄/dt = ic with x₄ = ict gives dx₄² = -c²dt², the spherical symmetry gives the spatial part, and the Minkowski interval is the statement that a Sphere of radius r = ct expands from each event (§2.1, §2.2). The quantum vacuum is derived from the same expansion: the Wightman axioms — Hilbert space, Poincaré covariance, locality, the vacuum, the spectrum condition — are derived from dx₄/dt = ic in §16.15 of [6] (Appendix E), and the vacuum correlations Jacobson reads the metric from — the Bisognano–Wichmann thermal structure and the entanglement across any surface — are Theorem 10.1 and Lemma 7.4.5. Jacobson's observation that the metric can be read off the vacuum correlations is explained: both are derived from the Sphere, and two theorems of one premise agree. His inference is corrected: the metric does not go while the quantum state stays as the fundamental ingredient; neither is fundamental, and the one fundamental ingredient is the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, of whose Sphere the quantum state is a state. The program Jacobson describes — "rewrite quantum field theory and get rid of the metric and … put in the metric that you extract from the quantum field state itself" — is carried out in [6] in the other order: the Principle is written down and the metric and the field theory are both derived from it, which is what the title of [6], the cogeneration of Minkowski space and Hilbert space, states.

(9) Why the volume must be held fixed in the 2015 derivation. Jacobson: "when I said that I assumed the entropy is maximized, I had to say maximum with something held fixed. … it turned out I had to hold the spatial volume of the ball fixed in order for the Einstein equation I inferred to have the correct relationship between the gravitational constant and the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of the boundary. I find that really striking because it means that there's something special about holding the volume fixed. I have no idea why I should hold it fixed … the fact that that choice was the volume requires explanation, and I don't have the explanation."

McGucken reading. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic states that the McGucken Sphere's volume defines the nonlocality. The count Ω is a count within the Sphere's volume, so the variation that holds the counted region fixed is the volume-fixed variation, and the volume-fixed count is shown equal to the horizon-area count of the same Sphere (§7.1bis item (8), Appendix A.3bis). The conformal Killing vector Jacobson had to use in place of a true Killing vector is the Sphere's growth r = ct read as a dilation (§7.1bis item (6)). The explanation Jacobson states he lacks is the volume clause of the Principle.

(10) Thermodynamics as a fault-tolerant theory, and the test of a microscopic picture. Jacobson: "Thermodynamics is a very, I call it, fault-tolerant theory. It can get some things right without actually having the correct foundational microscopic picture. … I'm using robust thermodynamic concepts that are probably going to be correct, no matter what the right microscopic picture of spacetime and quantum gravity is. And some of what I'm trying to do is probably nonsense, the way Carnot, some of what he was doing was nonsense. But it's pushing us into the right place, asking the right questions." And on his own derivations: "the level I'm thinking about with this thermodynamic reasoning or even the statistical one using quantum field theory is kind of immune or blind to the fundamental substructure."

McGucken reading. Carnot derived the efficiency bound without the molecules; Jacobson derived the equation of state without the McGucken Sphere. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic supplies the microscopic process whose counting is the thermodynamics — the Sphere's Haar-measure cell count, of which the five entropies are readings (Theorem 6.1) — and Carnot's bound is derived from it (Theorem 3.4bis, from [3]). Jacobson's own test for a microscopic picture is that it derive the inputs his thermodynamic reasoning had to assume: the area law, the Unruh temperature, the Clausius relation, the cutoff, the fixed-volume choice. The Principle derives each (Theorems 3.5, 4.6; Corollary 10.2; Theorem 3.5 Step 1; §7.1bis item (8)), and in addition derives what Jacobson says his reasoning is blind to — the substructure itself.

Closing attribution. Jacobson's two things filling spacetime, the metric and the quantum vacuum, are both derived from the expansion of the McGucken Sphere at c from every event, and each of the ten connections he draws between them is a theorem of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic: (1) Theorems 3.3, 3.6, 4.7; (2) §7.0 item (6); (3) Theorems 4.6, 10.1, §4.5; (4) Theorems 6.1, 5.1; (5) Theorem 3.5 with Step 1, Proposition 10.3; (6) Theorems 3.5, 4.1 Step 4, Corollary 10.2, Theorem 4.7, Theorem 19.4 of [3]; (7) §2.1, [17], Theorem 19.4.2 of [3]; (8) Lemma 7.4.5, §2.1–2.2, Appendix E, Theorem 10.1; (9) §7.1bis item (8), Appendix A.3bis; (10) Theorems 6.1, 3.4bis.

7.2ter The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Reading of the arrow of time in Jacobson's thermodynamics of spacetime: used as a convention in the construction, absent from the output, and deferred to non-equilibrium spacetime

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality. This subsection asks of Jacobson's three texts — the 1995 letter [7], the 2015 entanglement-equilibrium paper [33], and the 2025 interview [1] — whether the direction of time is considered in either the thermodynamics or the gravity he relates, and answers from his sentences. Evidence levels: the §7.0 quotations of [7] are verified-read; the additional sentences of [7] quoted here were obtained by a full-text search of the letter for the words "past," "future," "time," "arrow," "irrevers," "revers," "second law," "increase," "decrease," "boost," and "direction" (web-digest), each sentence quoted in full as it stands in the letter; [33] and [1] are verified-read (§7.1bis, §7.2bis).

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic predicts that the field equations derived through the Clausius relation on a causal horizon carry no arrow of time (Theorem 5.1(i): the Algebraic Channel reads the squared form (ic)² = -c²), that the horizon on which the derivation is run is a McGucken Sphere whether it is taken as the forward cone of an event or as the past horizon of an observer (§2.2: the past cone Σ_-(p) is the locus of forward McGucken Spheres Σ_+(q) from earlier events q arriving at p), that the focusing of its generators is the same under reversal of the generators (Lemma 5.1bis.1(ii)), and that the arrow of time is a separate theorem of the same expansion, dS/dt > 0 from the sign of +ic (Theorem 3.3), with the generalized second law as Theorem 3.6. The prediction for Jacobson's texts is therefore: an orientation will be used to set up the horizon, the output will be time-reversal invariant, and the Second Law will appear only where it is taken from outside.

Lemma 7.2ter.1 (The 1995 letter uses a time orientation as a construction convention and contains no statement of an arrow). (i) The words "second law" and "arrow" do not occur in [7]. (ii) The horizon of the derivation is the past horizon of the observer or of the 2-surface 𝒫, with the heat flux and the focusing both taken to the past of 𝒫 and the Killing field chosen future pointing. (iii) Entropy increase is mentioned twice, both times as a case outside the derivation.

Proof. (i) Full-text search of [7] for "second law" and "arrow" returns no occurrence (web-digest). (ii) Jacobson's horizon: "It can be simply the boundary of the past of any set 𝒪 (for 'observer')," "This sort of horizon is a null hypersurface (not necessarily smooth) and, assuming cosmic censorship, it is composed of generators which are null geodesic segments emanating backwards in time from the set 𝒪." At a point p: "Through p we consider a small spacelike 2-surface element 𝒫 whose past directed null normal congruence to one side (which we call the 'inside') has vanishing expansion and shear at p." "We call the past horizon of such a 𝒫 the 'local Rindler horizon of 𝒫', and we think of it as defining a system — the part of spacetime beyond the Rindler horizon — that is instantaneously stationary (in 'local equilibrium') at p." "Through any spacetime point there are local Rindler horizons in all null directions." The orientation of the boost field: "Let χ^a be an approximate local boost Killing field generating this horizon, with the direction of χ^a chosen to be future pointing to the 'inside' past of 𝒫." The heat: "We assume that all the heat flow across the horizon is (boost) energy carried by matter"; "This heat flux to the past of 𝒫 is given by" his Eq. (4), where "The integral is over a pencil of generators of the 'inside' past horizon ℋ of 𝒫," and "If k^a is the tangent vector to the horizon generators for an affine parameter λ that vanishes at 𝒫 and is negative to the past of 𝒫, then χ^a = -κλk^a and dΣ^a = k^a dλdA where dA is the area element on a cross section of the horizon." The focusing: "At 𝒫 the local Rindler horizon has vanishing expansion, so the focussing to the past of 𝒫 must bring an expansion to zero at just the right rate so that the area increase of a portion of the horizon will be proportional to the energy flux across it." Every oriented quantity — the past horizon, the past-directed congruence, the flux to the past, the future-pointing χ^a — is fixed by a choice made in setting up the construction. (iii) The two mentions of entropy increase: "For instance, in free expansion of a gas, entropy increase is not associated with any heat flow, and this relation is not valid." And, in the closing analogy with sound in a gas: "For sufficiently high sound frequency or intensity one knows that the local equilibrium condition breaks down, entropy increases, and sound no longer propagates in a time reversal invariant manner." Both are given as processes to which δQ = T dS does not apply, and the letter closes with "It is my hope that, by following this line of inquiry, we shall eventually reach an understanding of the nature of 'non-equilibrium spacetime'" (§7.0 item 13, verified-read). □

Lemma 7.2ter.2 (The output of the construction is time-reversal invariant, and the past-horizon construction and the forward-Sphere construction of Theorem 4.7 give the same field equation). The Einstein equation obtained in [7] is invariant under t →-t; and Theorem 4.7, which runs the Clausius relation on the forward McGucken Sphere Σ_+(p), yields the same equation as Jacobson's past-horizon construction.

Proof. The Einstein equation G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG/c⁴)T_μν is built from the metric and its first two derivatives and from T_μν, each even under t →-t for the matter in question; this is Theorem 5.1(i). The equality of the two constructions: both use the Raychaudhuri equation dθ/dλ = -1/2θ² - σ_μνσ^μν - R_μνk^μk^ν on a null congruence with θ = σ = 0 at p, Jacobson on the past-directed generators of the past horizon, Theorem 4.7 on the future-directed generators of Σ_+(p). By Lemma 5.1bis.1(ii) the Raychaudhuri equation is carried to itself under k^μ→-k^μ, λ→-λ, so θ(λ) = -λR_μνk^μk^ν and δA = -∫λR_μνk^μk^νdA dλ hold with the same sign on either congruence; with δQ = T dS, T = ħκ/2πc k_B and dS = ηδA, both constructions give R_μνk^μk^ν = (2π/ħη) T_μνk^μk^ν for all null k^μ, hence the Einstein equation with G = c³/4ħη (Theorem 4.7 Steps 3–5). The direction chosen for the generators therefore drops out of the result, which is why the orientation Jacobson fixes in Lemma 7.2ter.1(ii) leaves no trace in his output. □

Reading under the Principle. Jacobson's past horizon of 𝒫 is composed of forward McGucken Spheres: the "null geodesic segments emanating backwards in time" from 𝒪 are the generators of the Spheres Σ_+(q) from earlier events q that arrive at 𝒫 (§2.2), and his "local Rindler horizons in all null directions" through p are the generators of Σ_+(p) read from p (§7.0 item 5). The heat he integrates "to the past of 𝒫" is the Compton-tick energy those Spheres cross before reaching 𝒫 (Theorem 4.7 Step 3). The Principle supplies the orientation he chooses by convention as a physical fact — every McGucken Sphere is generated at its apex and expands at +ic — and then shows, by Lemma 7.2ter.2, why the convention does no work in his output: the Clausius route to the field equation reads the squared form of the rate, in which the sign of +ic is absent (Theorem 5.1 anchor; §5.1bis Step 5).

Lemma 7.2ter.3 (The 2015 paper is stated as an equilibrium hypothesis, and the interview takes the generalized second law from Bekenstein and Hawking). (i) [33] is built on the hypothesis that the entanglement entropy of a small causal diamond is maximal in the vacuum (§7.1bis), an equilibrium condition by name, with no statement about the direction of time. (ii) In [1] the Second Law occurs once, as the motivation Jacobson gives for Bekenstein's entropy: "the second law of thermodynamics says entropy can't decrease. So, if a black hole is shrinking, then it must be that the entropy of everything else is growing by enough to counterbalance that. The Hawking radiation is carrying entropy away" (§7.2bis, verified-read).

Proof. (i) is §7.1bis: every quoted hypothesis of [33] is an extremum condition on the vacuum state at fixed volume, and the derivation is of the semiclassical Einstein equation from first-order variations about that extremum; a first-order variation about an equilibrium has no sign of dt. (ii) is the quoted sentence: the generalized second law — horizon area plus radiation entropy non-decreasing — is stated as a known law from which Bekenstein's identification follows, and no derivation of it is offered or claimed in [1], [7], or [33]. □

Reading under the Principle. The generalized second law Jacobson takes as given is Theorem 3.6 (Theorem 17 of [3]), derived from the forward propagation of the Compton-tick count on the horizon McGucken Sphere; its strict form for the matter sector is Theorem 3.3. The entanglement-equilibrium hypothesis of [33] is the ensemble reading of the same count at the instant t (§7.1bis), and the Principle adds to it the direction in which the instant advances.

Theorem 7.2ter.4 (In Jacobson's texts the arrow of time is neither in the thermodynamics nor in the gravity; under the Principle it is a theorem beneath both). (i) The thermodynamics Jacobson uses is the equilibrium relation δQ = T dS at a local Rindler horizon and the equilibrium hypothesis of [33]; the irreversible processes — "entropy increase is not associated with any heat flow," local-equilibrium failure in which "entropy increases, and sound no longer propagates in a time reversal invariant manner" — are the processes he places outside the derivation and in "non-equilibrium spacetime." (ii) The gravity he obtains is time-reversal invariant (Lemma 7.2ter.2), with the orientation used in the construction removed by the evenness of the focusing equation. (iii) Under dx₄/dt = ic the arrow is Theorem 3.3, the generalized second law is Theorem 3.6, the attraction stated on the forward McGucken Sphere is one-way (Theorem 5.1bis.2), and the equilibrium relation Jacobson uses is the Algebraic-Channel reading of the same expansion (Theorem 4.7, Corollary 5.3); the "non-equilibrium spacetime" he hopes for is the Geometric Channel at Compton-tick resolution (§7.2).

Proof. (i) Lemma 7.2ter.1(iii) and Lemma 7.2ter.3. (ii) Lemma 7.2ter.2. (iii) Theorem 3.3 derives dS/dt > 0 from the forward Compton-tick propagator selected by +ic; Theorem 3.6 derives horizon-area-plus-radiation monotonicity on the forward cone; Theorem 5.1bis.2 states attraction on Σ_+(p) and shows the reversed statement has no carrier; Theorem 5.1 places the Clausius-route field equation in the Algebraic Channel, and §7.2 identifies the processes Jacobson excludes — entropy increase without heat flow — as the Compton-tick diffusion of the reduced state (Theorem 3.3, §6.3), derived from the same +ic orientation and lying below the equilibrium relation he uses. □

Closing attribution. Orientation as convention, arrow absent, entropy increase placed outside the derivation: Lemma 7.2ter.1 on [7]. Time-reversal invariance of the output and equality of the past-horizon and forward-Sphere constructions: Lemma 7.2ter.2 through Lemma 5.1bis.1(ii), Theorem 4.7, Theorem 5.1(i). Equilibrium hypothesis and borrowed generalized second law: Lemma 7.2ter.3 on [33] and [1]. The arrow as a theorem of the expansion: Theorem 7.2ter.4 through Theorem 3.3, Theorem 3.6, Theorem 5.1bis.2, Corollary 5.3, §7.2; the past horizon as forward McGucken Spheres of earlier events: §2.2, §7.0 item 5.

7.3 Counting versus dynamics: why Jacobson unified two pillars and not three

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic supplies both a counting (the Geometric-Channel mode count on the McGucken Sphere) and a dynamics (the Algebraic-Channel Schrödinger evolution and commutator), and predicts that a programme built on counting alone will unify the two counting sciences and leave the dynamical one out.

The chain Carnot → Clausius → Boltzmann → Bekenstein → Jacobson → 't Hooft/Susskind is a counting programme: S = k_BlnΩ, δQ = T dS, S = A/4ℓ_P², the holographic bound, and the equation of state are statements about how many states there are. The Schrödinger equation, the commutator, the Born rule, and the Wigner classification are statements about how individual states evolve. Jacobson's unification ran along the counting seam and could not include quantum dynamics within a counting formalism. Padmanabhan's variational principle on null vectors (§9.1) reaches gravitational-field dynamics, which is ensemble-level dynamics of a metric that is itself a leveled average over ∼10⁵7 atoms, and so still sits above per-state dynamics. The McGucken Duality supplies both seams from one source — counting through the Geometric Channel, dynamics through the Algebraic Channel — and this is the sense in which the three pillars are three resolution-readings of one fact: thermodynamics at ensemble resolution through the Geometric Channel, gravity-as-thermodynamics at horizon resolution through the Geometric Channel, quantum mechanics at single-event resolution through the Algebraic Channel. The historical order of discovery is the order in which the leveling cascade of the central limit theorem over ∼10²3 Compton-coupled wavefronts was instrumentally accessible: the most-leveled signatures (planetary orbits, heat engines) first, the per-event signatures (Stern–Gerlach, Davisson–Germer) last. The Feynman–Wiener correspondence — the identity of ∫𝒟x e^iS/ħ and ∫𝒟x e^-βE under β = it/ħ, called a coincidence since 1948 and posed as a question by Stay and Baez in 2010 — is the empirical signature of the two channels being readings of one Principle under the McGucken–Wick rotation. The full historical treatment is §6.6.9.18.F of [6], reproduced in [14, §5.6.10].

7.4 The corpus results used in §7, derived here from the Principle

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic states that the fourth dimension expands at c from every event as a McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality. Six results of the corpus are used in §§7.0–7.2 by citation; each is derived here from the Principle so that the reading of Jacobson rests on derivations present in this paper. The corpus citations are kept beside each lemma.

Lemma 7.4.1 (Lorentz covariance of the rate; Theorem 8 of [4], [17]; reproduced in full). The statement and proof are the author's, verbatim, from [4]; the present paper's restatement in its own numbering, and any steps it adds, follow the quotation.

From [4], verbatim — Theorem 8 (Poincaré invariance of dx₄/dt = ic), statement and proof: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list)

Theorem 8 (Poincaré invariance of dx₄/dt = ic). The combined invariance group of dx₄/dt = ic acting on M_G is the Poincaré group ISO(1,3) = ℝ⁴ ⋊SO^+(1,3) at the four-dimensional level.

Proof. By items (i)--(iii) of Definition 7, the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic is invariant under the four-dimensional translation subgroup ℝ⁴. By items (iv) and (v), it is invariant under the proper orthochronous Lorentz group SO^+(1,3). The Lorentzian signature on the constraint surface arises from the pullback of the holomorphic quadratic form g_E = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² + dx₄² on the complexified cotangent bundle along the embedding ι: (t, x₁, x₂, x₃) ↦(x₁, x₂, x₃, ict), producing ι^* g_E = -c² dt² + dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² (Theorem 4(a)). The full derivation of the Poincaré invariance group as the product of dx₄/dt = ic and the embedding ι appears in [82, §2.2, Theorem 12]. The priority statement --- that dx₄/dt = ic generates the Poincaré group rather than being a representation of it --- is the content of [22, Theorem 1], where the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic is established as the father symmetry from which Lorentz, Poincaré, Noether, Wigner, gauge, quantum-unitary, CPT, diffeomorphism, and supersymmetry all descend as theorems. The semidirect-product structure ISO(1,3) = ℝ⁴ ⋊SO^+(1,3) follows from the standard composition of translations with Lorentz transformations [66]. □

Restatement in the present paper's notation. Every inertial observer measures the McGucken Sphere Σ_+(p) expanding at the rate c.

Proof. By §2.1 the Principle gives the quadratic form Q(dx) = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² + (ic dt)² = dx⃗² - c²dt², and by §2.2 the McGucken Sphere is its null set Q = 0. A linear change of inertial coordinates x↦Λx that preserves the form of the Principle must carry the Euclidean four-form dx₁² + …+ dx₄² to itself, since the Principle contains no preferred direction among the four coordinates once x₄ = ict is admitted; the maps preserving dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² + dx₄² with x₄ imaginary are the maps preserving Q, which is the Lorentz group O(1,3) (its proper orthochronous part SO^+(1,3) preserving the +ic orientation of §2.2). Since Q is invariant, so is its null set: Λ carries {Q = 0} to {Q = 0}, i.e. the Sphere r = ct to the Sphere r' = ct' with the same c. Together with the four translations, which leave dx₄/dt unchanged because the rate is the same at every event, the invariance group is the Poincaré group ISO(1,3). □

This is the lemma invoked for "for all timelike unit vectors" in §7.1bis item (4) and for the universality of η in item (2): the choice of u^a selects an inertial frame, and in every such frame the McGucken Sphere expands at c.

Lemma 7.4.2 (Continuous geometry, discrete action; Proposition 10.8 of [6]; reproduced in full). The statement and proof are the author's, verbatim, from [6]; the present paper's restatement in its own numbering, and any steps it adds, follow the quotation.

From [6], verbatim — Proposition 10.8 (Continuum-discrete duality), statement and proof: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list)

Proposition 10.8 (Continuum-discrete duality: geometric continuity and action discreteness as complementary aspects of dx₄/dt = ic). The McGucken framework provides simultaneously the geometric continuity of spacetime structure and the action-quantization discreteness of quantum-mechanical content, at different cascade-level aspects of the single principle dx₄/dt = ic. Specifically:

(i) (Geometric continuity is preserved at all cascade levels.) The spatial slice of Minkowski Space 𝕄₁,3 at parameter time t is a continuous 3-manifold (cardinality 2^ℵ₀ for the spatial points; topologically ℝ³ with the standard Lorentzian-metric-induced smooth structure, Lemma 2.5). The McGucken Sphere 𝓜_E(t) at every event E ∈ Minkowski Space 𝕄₁,3 is a continuous 2-sphere with a continuum of perpendicular x_4-radii (Proposition 10.7 (i)–(ii)). The position and momentum operators q̂_i, p̂_i on 𝓗 have continuous spectra σ(q̂_i) = σ(p̂_i) = ℝ (Remark 10.9, Wielandt–Wintner 1948). The Lorentzian metric η_μν is a smooth tensor field on Minkowski Space 𝕄₁,3 (Lemma 2.5). (ii) (Action discreteness is forced at every Planck-frequency oscillation.) At every event of Minkowski Space 𝕄₁,3, the x_4-advance along any radial direction of the local McGucken Sphere accumulates action in discrete units of ℏ per Planck-frequency oscillation (Proposition 2.2 of the present paper). λ_dB(E) = ℏc/E,

the spatial scale at which one full x_4-oscillation accumulates one action quantum ℏ. For a massive particle of rest energy mc², this specializes to the reduced Compton wavelength

λ_P = √(ℏG/c³) ≈ 1.616 × 10⁻³⁵ m,

equivalently the reduced Compton wavelength of a particle of Planck mass m_P = √(ℏc/G) ≈ 2.176 × 10⁻⁸ kg. The Planck length is the universal regime at which the geometry of the McGucken Sphere cannot be separated from the action quantization carried by each oscillation; below this scale, the dx₄/dt = ic framework’s continuum-discrete duality becomes inseparable.

(iv) (Resolution of the orthodox discrete-vs-continuous debate.) The orthodox tradition has treated geometric discreteness and geometric continuity as competing alternatives. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework dissolves the competition. Geometry (positions, radii, spectra of canonical operators, smooth metric tensor) is continuous, supplying Lorentz invariance and the high-precision continuum tests of relativity. Action content (oscillations along any worldline, accumulating ℏ per oscillation) is discrete, supplying the quantum-mechanical character of every empirically observed quantum interference effect. The two are complementary aspects of dx₄/dt = ic, not competing alternatives — and the dx₄/dt = ic framework’s success in deriving both QM and SR from one principle is tied to its providing both continuity and discreteness simultaneously at different cascade-level positions.

Restatement in the present paper's notation. The coordinate x₄ = ict is a real continuum, and the action of a Compton-coupled system is integer-valued in units of h when resolved on complete cycles; the finiteness of the horizon count comes from the second property and does not require discretizing the first.

Proof. x₄ = ict is the integral of a constant rate over the real variable t, so x₄/i ranges over ℝ and the metric of §2.1 is a smooth Lorentzian metric with no minimum length. The phase of a system of rest energy mc² is e^-iω_Ct = e^-(mc/ħ)x₄ with ω_C = mc²/ħ (§2.3), and the action accumulated over an interval Δt is mc²Δt; on a complete cycle Δt = T_C this is exactly h, so the number of cycles in any interval is an integer plus a fraction of one cycle, and the number of distinguishable Compton-tick states of the advance resolved on a region is the integer count Ω of §2.3. The horizon count N = A/ℓ_P² of Theorem 3.5 is the number of complete cycles of the horizon-tier advance (wavelength ℓ_P, §7.0 item 3) across the area A; it is finite because cycles are counted, while the coordinate on which they are counted is continuous. □
