Lemma 7.4.3 (Cogeneration of the metric and the quantum phase; [6], [16]). The Lorentzian metric and the quantum phase are two readings of the coordinate x₄ = ict: the metric is its square, the phase is its exponential.

Proof. The square: dx₄² = (ic dt)² = -c²dt², giving the time term of the metric (§2.1). The exponential: a system of rest energy E = mc² carries, by §2.3, the phase factor e^-iEt/ħ, and substituting t = x₄/ic = -ix₄/c gives e^-iE(-ix₄/c)/ħ = e^-Ex₄/ħc = e^-(mc/ħ)x₄, so that the quantum phase of the Schrödinger factor is the exponential of the advance with the Compton wavenumber mc/ħ as its rate. The imaginary unit of the phase and of the commutator [q̂,p̂] = iħ is the i of dx₄ = ic dt in both readings. Both readings are functions of the same x₄; neither is derived from the other, and the vacuum correlations of the field (the phase reading, summed over the McGucken Spheres of neighbouring events, Theorem 10.1) and the metric (the squared reading) are therefore generated together by the advance. □

This is the lemma invoked in §7.2 (f): the metric is encoded in the vacuum correlations, as Jacobson says, because both are x₄ read two ways; the metric is a separate reading, not a separate degree of freedom.

Lemma 7.4.4 (Every McGucken Sphere is a Huygens wavefront and a holographic screen; Theorem 21 of [3], [36]; reproduced in full). The statement and proof are the author's, verbatim, from [3]; the present paper's restatement in its own numbering, and any steps it adds, follow the quotation.

From [3], verbatim — Theorem 21 (Huygens' Principle is the Holographic Principle), statement and proof: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list)

Theorem 21: Huygens' Principle is the Holographic Principle

Theorem (Huygens equals Holography; cf. [57], Theorem 7.9.5). Under the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, Huygens' Principle and the holographic principle of 't~Hooft and Susskind are two formulations of the same geometric fact: the physics of the bulk region enclosed by a McGucken Sphere at time t + dt is fully determined by source data on the 2-dimensional surface of the McGucken Sphere at time t. The bulk-to-boundary encoding of the holographic principle is the surface-sourcing of bulk wavefronts of Huygens' Principle. Specifically:

1. The 2-dimensional surface of the McGucken Sphere at radius R = ct from event p₀ has area A(t) = 4πc² t² and carries N_modes = A/ℓ_P² independent x₄-modes (cf. the area-law of Theorem 15).
2. The 3-dimensional bulk enclosed by this Sphere is the Huygens-secondary-wavefront propagation in the next interval dt sourced from the Sphere's surface.
3. The Bekenstein bound N_bulk ≤A/(4ℓ_P²) is the count of x₄-modes per Planck cell on the McGucken Sphere surface.
4. AdS/CFT is the special case of McGucken Sphere holography in anti-de Sitter geometry, with the bulk radial coordinate identified as rescaled x₄ and the boundary CFT living on the McGucken Sphere at conformal infinity.

In plain language. The holographic principle of 't~Hooft and Susskind says that the physics of a (d+1)-dimensional region of space is encoded on its d-dimensional boundary. It was inferred from the strange fact that black-hole entropy scales with horizon area (not volume), and Maldacena's AdS/CFT gave a specific concrete example. But why holography should hold has remained an open question for thirty years. The McGucken Principle supplies the answer: holography is just Huygens' Principle. Every event in spacetime is the apex of a McGucken Sphere, and every McGucken Sphere is a holographic screen. The wavefronts that fill the bulk between time t and time t + dt are sourced from the surface of the Sphere at time t—this is the standard Huygens statement, and it is also the standard holographic statement. The Bekenstein bound is the count of how many independent Huygens sources can fit on a Planck-scale grid on the Sphere's surface. AdS/CFT works in anti-de Sitter space because the boundary of the McGucken Sphere there lives at conformal infinity, making the dual CFT a well-defined boundary theory. Holography is not special to black holes or to AdS; it is the universal content of dx₄/dt = ic at every spacetime event.

Three Foundational Mysteries Collapse into Four Facets of One Process

Four great mysteries of foundational physics—

1. the Lorentzian–Euclidean equivalence of QM and statistical mechanics (Kac, Nelson, Symanzik, Osterwalder–Schrader, Parisi–Wu),
2. the holographic principle of 't Hooft and Susskind,
3. the gravity-as-thermodynamics identifications of Jacobson, Verlinde, and Padmanabhan, and
4. AdS/CFT duality (Maldacena),

—collapse into four facets of one geometric process: the spherically symmetric expansion of x₄ at velocity c from every spacetime event. Each was previously treated as a remarkable formal correspondence with no source; each is, in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, the same iterated McGucken Sphere structure read at a different tier or in a different signature.

Restatement in the present paper's notation. The data of the advance on Σ_+(p) at time t determine the field in the region it bounds, and the number of independent data at the horizon tier is N = A/ℓ_P².

Proof. Each point of Σ_+(p) is itself an event, and by the Principle carries its own McGucken Sphere expanding at c: this is Huygens' construction with the mechanism supplied — the secondary wavelets are the Spheres of the wavefront's own events, and the envelope at a later time is Σ_+(p) at that time because all expand at the same c (Lemma 7.4.1). For a field obeying the wave equation that the metric of §2.1 defines, the Kirchhoff integral theorem states that the field at an interior point is determined by the field and its normal derivative on a closed surface enclosing it; applied to Σ_+(p), the data on the Sphere determine the field within its volume. The data are modes of the advance on the Sphere, and at the horizon tier no mode has wavelength below ℓ_P (Theorem 3.5 Step 1), so the independent data on a Sphere of area A number N = A/ℓ_P², one per Planck cell. The state of the region is therefore specified on its boundary by N data, which is the holographic principle of 't Hooft and Susskind [37, 38] with the Sphere as the screen; Theorem 3.5 Step 2 uses this count. □

Theorem 21 of [3] (verified-read) states the result as: "Under the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, Huygens' Principle and the holographic principle of 't Hooft and Susskind are two formulations of the same geometric fact: the physics of the bulk region enclosed by a McGucken Sphere at time t + dt is fully determined by source data on the 2-dimensional surface of the McGucken Sphere at time t", with "N_modes = A/ℓ_P² independent x₄-modes" on the surface. This is the lemma invoked in §7.0 item (10): Jacobson declines the holographic hypothesis as circular because its support is black hole thermodynamics; here holography follows from the Sphere's Huygens property and the tick, and black hole thermodynamics is its special case on a horizon. In every comparison with Huygens, Fresnel, Kirchhoff, and Hadamard the distinction is the one stated in §11: the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies the physical mechanism — x₄'s spherical expansion at c from every event — of which their construction is the description.

Lemma 7.4.5 (First McGucken Law of Nonlocality; [20] §2, Theorem 1.50.1 of [5]; reproduced in full). The statement and proof are the author's, verbatim, from [20]; the present paper's restatement in its own numbering, and any steps it adds, follow the quotation.

From [20], verbatim — §2, The Two Laws of Nonlocality: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list)

2. The Two Laws of Nonlocality 2.1 First Law: All nonlocality begins as locality First McGucken Law of Nonlocality. Two quantum systems can exhibit nonlocal correlations (entanglement) only if they have shared a common local origin, or if each has interacted locally with members of a system that itself shared a common local origin. Equivalently: only systems of particles with intersecting light spheres — with each light sphere having originated from each respective particle — can ever be entangled [98]. The property of entanglement between particles is limited by the velocity of light, even though the nonlocal influences found in entanglement are instantaneous. This law does not contradict the instantaneous character of entanglement correlations. It constrains the creation of entanglement, not the manifestation of it. Once two particles are entangled (by having shared a local origin, or by each having interacted with particles sharing a local origin), their correlations are instantaneous and persist regardless of separation. But the entanglement itself could not have been established without a prior local interaction. 2.2 Second Law: Nonlocality grows over time, limited by c Second McGucken Law of Nonlocality. Nonlocality grows over time, in a manner limited by the velocity of light c . As the fourth dimension expands at c , the McGucken Sphere grows. At time t after a local event, the sphere of nonlocality has radius r = ct . Particles within this sphere may be entangled with the original event; particles outside it cannot be, because the expansion of x 4 has not yet reached them. The boundary of entanglement possibility is exactly the light cone — the causal boundary of relativity. This law connects quantum nonlocality directly to the causal structure of spacetime. The expansion of x 4 at c simultaneously generates: the light cone (the boundary of causal influence in relativity), the expanding wavefront (Huygens' Principle in wave optics), and the sphere of potential entanglement (the boundary of nonlocality in quantum mechanics). All three are the same geometric object — the McGucken Sphere — viewed from different physical perspectives [97].

Corollary. The growth of nonlocality constitutes a sixth arrow of time — the nonlocality arrow — joining the thermodynamic, radiative, cosmological, causal, and psychological arrows as manifestations of the one-way expansion of the fourth dimension dx 4 / dt = ic .

Restatement in the present paper's notation. Two quantum systems can exhibit nonlocal correlations (entanglement) only if they have shared a common local origin, or if each has interacted locally with members of a system that itself shared a common local origin; equivalently, only systems of particles with intersecting light spheres can ever be entangled (the statement of [20] §2.1 and §8); in the apex form of Theorem 1.50.1 of [5], A and B are entangled if and only if they share a common apex event p from which both descend via Σ_+(p). Theorem 1.50.1 of [5] (verified-read) states it as: "Two quantum systems A and B are entangled if and only if they share a common apex event p∈M₁,3 (the shared local origin) from which both their wavefunctions descend via the McGucken Sphere Σ^+(p) — equivalently, A and B both lie on the future null hypersurface from a single past spacetime event p."

Proof. The Principle states that the volume of the McGucken Sphere defines a nonlocality: the Compton-tick states of a system at event p are resolved on the region within Σ_+(p), and the Sphere's volume is the region over which the system's state is one state. A joint state of two systems at events p and q requires a region on which both are resolved together, i.e. a region within both Σ_+(p) and Σ_+(q) (or within the Spheres of events on their worldlines). Such a common region exists exactly when both systems lie on the null hypersurface Σ_+(p) of one apex event p — the event of their last local interaction, from which the joint wavefunction is carried outward at c (Lemma 7.4.1) as one Sphere. If no such apex exists, no Sphere of either system has intersected a Sphere of the other, no common region exists, and the state of the pair factorizes into states resolved on disjoint regions; conversely, a shared apex supplies the McGucken Sphere on whose volume the pair is resolved as a single state. The intersection of the two systems' Spheres is the consequence: both are cross-sections of Σ_+(p). □

This is the lemma invoked in §7.2 (g): Jacobson's statement that removing vacuum entanglement across a surface would cleave space is the contrapositive of the lemma applied to the vacuum — the vacuum on the two sides of a surface is entangled because the McGucken Spheres of events on either side intersect across it, and a surface across which no Spheres intersected would bound two regions with no joint state, which is what "cleaved" means.

Lemma 7.4.6 (Reflection invariance of the Euclidean action; Theorem 19 of [21]). The action of a field written on the x₄ coordinate is invariant under x₄→-x₄; the orientation +ic enters only through the direction of the advance.

Proof. For a scalar field of mass m on the metric of §2.1, the action is S = ∫d³x dt [1/2ϕ̇²/c² - 1/2(∇ϕ)² - 1/2(mc/ħ)²ϕ²] up to normalization. S_E depends on x₄ only through (∂_x₄ϕ)² and the measure dx₄, both even under x₄→-x₄. The field equations derived from S_E by variation (the Algebraic Channel) are therefore invariant under reversal of x₄, hence of t; the direction +ic is carried by the advance itself (§2.2) and enters only the Geometric-Channel route (Theorem 5.1). □

Lemma 7.4.1 derives the frame-independence of the McGucken Sphere's rate from the invariance of the quadratic form the Principle generates; Lemma 7.4.2 derives finite counting on a continuous coordinate from h per cycle; Lemma 7.4.3 derives the metric and the phase as the square and the exponential of x₄ = ict; Lemma 7.4.4 derives holography from the Sphere's Huygens property and the Planck tick; Lemma 7.4.5 derives the entanglement condition from the Sphere's volume defining the nonlocality; Lemma 7.4.6 derives the time-reversal invariance of Algebraic-Channel laws from the evenness of the Euclidean action in x₄. 8. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Reading of Verlinde's entropic gravity

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality. Verlinde's 2011 derivation of Newton's law and the Einstein equations as an entropic force [9] stands in the same relation to the Principle as Jacobson's, and one identification is exact. The corpus's earlier reading of Verlinde is [53]; the present section carries it against the full texts of the 2011 paper (§8.0) and the 2017 paper (§8.0bis).

From [3], verbatim — Theorem 19.4.4 (Verlinde 2011 Entropic-Gravity Program as Partial Subset of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Framework), with Subsection 19.4.4(H) on Verlinde's 2022 position: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list; theorem numbers inside the quotation are those of [3])

Theorem 19.4.4: The Verlinde 2011 Entropic-Gravity Program — Partial Subset of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Framework, Empirically Strengthened by It

We now address explicitly the relationship between Verlinde's 2011 entropic-gravity program [9] and the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework. This relationship is more nuanced than the Jacobson 1995 case treated in Theorem 19.4.3, because Verlinde makes a substantially stronger claim than Jacobson — and an honest treatment requires the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework to recover what Verlinde gets right while refusing what Verlinde overreaches. The argument has five parts: (A) what Verlinde claims and where the claim is stronger than Jacobson's; (B) the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel horizon-thermodynamics content of Verlinde's program as a proper subset of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework; (C) the empirical Colella–Overhauser–Werner (COW) 1975 objection to Verlinde's stronger claim, and how the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's McGucken Duality naturally accommodates COW where Verlinde's pure-entropic reading struggles; (D) the Marolf Constraint as an argument against Verlinde's spacetime-emergence claim that the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework satisfies; (E) how Verlinde 2011 relates to Jacobson 1995 within the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's four-fold architecture, and what the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework adds beyond both.

Primary-source historical-first articulation in the corpus. The Verlinde identification developed below — Verlinde's holographic screen = McGucken Sphere, with x₄'s expansion supplying the entropy-production mechanism — receives its historical-first articulation in [21, §IV] (April 12, 2026): "Verlinde's holographic screen = the McGucken Sphere. The spherical shape of the holographic screen, which Verlinde assumes, follows from the spherical symmetry of x₄'s expansion. The information density of one bit per Planck area, which Verlinde assumes from the holographic principle, follows from the quantisation of x₄'s expansion at the Planck scale." [21 §IV] additionally gestures at deriving Verlinde's entropy-gradient formula ΔS = 2πk_B mcΔx/ħ from McGucken Sphere solid-angle geometry combined with Compton coupling, with the factor 2π "arising from the solid angle geometry of the sphere." Recapitulation of Verlinde 2011. Verlinde's program goes substantially beyond Jacobson 1995 in its ontological claim. Where Jacobson reads horizon thermodynamics as thermodynamic consistency conditions on a fundamental gravitational theory — recovering Einstein equations as equation of state on a still-fundamental spacetime — Verlinde claims that gravity itself is an emergent entropic force in the same ontological sense that the elastic restoring force of a stretched polymer is entropic. Verlinde's derivation in outline:

(V1) Holographic screens. Surfaces partition space, with information stored on the screen at one bit per Planck area: N = A/ℓ_P² bits per screen of area A.

(V2) Bekenstein information argument. A test particle of mass m within one Compton wavelength of the screen contributes one bit of information to the screen [172]. The entropy gradient as the particle approaches the screen is ΔS = 2πk_B (mc/ħ) Δx for displacement Δx toward the screen.

(V3) Equipartition on the screen. The screen's N bits are in thermal equilibrium at temperature T given by the Unruh-like relation T = (ħ/2πk_B)|a| for an accelerated observer; the total energy on the screen is distributed by equipartition as E = (1/2) N k_B T.

(V4) Entropic force. The thermodynamic force on the test particle is F = T (dS/dx). Plugging in the entropy gradient from (V2) and the temperature from (V3) gives, for a screen of area 4πr² around a point mass M at distance r: F = GMm/r² — Newton's law of gravity recovered as an entropic force.

The substantially stronger claims of Verlinde's program:

(V5) Inertia itself is entropic. Newton's F = ma emerges from the entropic-force machinery, not just gravity.

(V6) Spacetime emerges from holographic information. Space itself is built from the holographic-screen degrees of freedom, with the screens treated as fundamental and the geometry treated as emergent.

(V7) Gravity is not a fundamental interaction. Gravity has the same ontological status as the polymer-restoring force: it has no microscopic origin and emerges from entropy-maximization on the screens.

These (V5), (V6), (V7) are substantially stronger than Jacobson 1995. Jacobson 1995 reads horizon thermodynamics as a consistency condition on a fundamental gravitational theory; Verlinde 2011 reads gravity itself as fundamentally absent from the microscopic substrate. This is where Verlinde diverges from Jacobson and where the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's response must be more nuanced.

(A) What Verlinde shares with Jacobson, and where Verlinde overreaches. Both Verlinde and Jacobson derive gravitational structure from horizon thermodynamics; both use the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy-area law and an Unruh-type temperature as inputs; both treat the relationship between the screen/horizon and the bulk dynamics as the load-bearing fact. - Jacobson 1995: horizon thermodynamics is thermodynamics of an underlying gravitational system. The Clausius relation is a constraint that the geometric Einstein equations must satisfy. - Verlinde 2011: holographic screens are fundamental degrees of freedom and gravity is emergent entropic force. The screens are not horizons of a pre-existing geometry; the geometry itself is built from the screens. The Bekenstein-Hawking bit-per-Planck-area is taken as the foundational substrate.

Jacobson is the conservative reading; Verlinde is the radical reading. (C) The Colella–Overhauser–Werner (COW) 1975 objection to Verlinde's pure-entropic reading, and how the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's Duality naturally accommodates COW. (D) The Marolf Constraint as an argument against Verlinde's spacetime-emergence claim. Theorem 19.4.2 of the present paper established the Marolf Constraint [159]: gravity cannot emerge from any substrate whose foundational kinematics consists of locally commuting observables at spacelike separation. Any emergent-gravity program must have a foundational non-locality built into its substrate at the kinematic level.

Verlinde's holographic-screen substrate, as standardly interpreted, has not been demonstrated to satisfy the Marolf Constraint. The screen-information bits are typically treated as if they were independent degrees of freedom on the screen, with statistical mechanics applied to their distribution. If the screen-bit dynamics is locally commuting at spacelike separation on the screen, the Marolf Constraint is violated, and the program cannot generate gravity by Marolf's argument. Verlinde's program would then be inconsistent at the foundational level, regardless of its empirical successes at the Newtonian limit.

The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework satisfies the Marolf Constraint by construction (Theorem 19.4.2): the McGucken Sphere null-connectivity supplies the foundational non-locality at every event. Two events that appear spacelike-separated in the spatial 3-slice projection are null-locally connected on the McGucken Sphere of their common-source event in 4D. The McGucken Sphere structure descends from dx₄/dt = ic as the active wavefront from every event; the null-connectivity is built into the active expansion, not added separately as a non-local-kinematic input. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework satisfies the Marolf Constraint intrinsically; Verlinde 2011's holographic-screen substrate would have to supply a separate non-locality argument to satisfy it.

The diagnosis: Verlinde's stronger claims (V5)–(V7) about spacetime emerging from holographic information run into the Marolf Constraint. If the screens are fundamental and the geometry is emergent as a statistical-thermodynamic artifact of the screen-bit dynamics, the screen-bit dynamics must have foundational non-locality — but Verlinde 2011 does not supply such a non-locality argument in the original paper. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies the non-locality intrinsically via the McGucken Sphere structure, but the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's stance toward "spacetime emergence" requires precision and not blanket refusal. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework refuses Verlinde-type substrate-emergence (spacetime as the statistical-thermodynamic artifact of an underlying non-spacetime layer of holographic bits) while affirming generative-emergence from the single physical-geometric principle dx₄/dt = ic: the Minkowski metric, the McGucken Sphere as the foundational geometric atom of spacetime, the light cone, the Lorentzian signature, and the entire physical edifice are generated by the active expansion content of the principle. Spacetime is the active geometry of dx₄/dt = ic at every event, not the statistical-thermodynamic consequence of an underlying holographic-information layer. The two senses of "emergence" are derivationally distinct: Verlinde's substrate-emergence treats geometry as derivative of a deeper non-geometric layer; the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's generative-emergence treats geometry as the immediate content of one principle. The former runs into the Marolf Constraint; the latter satisfies it intrinsically. See Corollary 19.4.4.2 below for the explicit articulation of the McGucken generative-emergence reading.

Diagnostic remark — the distinction between substrate-emergence and generative-emergence, and the precise sense in which the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework is "emergent." The orthodox-literature discussion of "emergent gravity" and "emergent spacetime" — Verlinde 2011, the holographic-information programs, condensed-matter-analogue gravity, the Carroll-Mindscape Q4 articulation — has typically conflated two derivationally distinct kinds of emergence under one term. Substrate-emergence: spacetime as the statistical-thermodynamic artifact of a deeper non-spacetime substrate (Verlinde's holographic bits on screens, condensed-matter analogues, lattice-like underlying degrees of freedom). Generative-emergence: spacetime as the immediate active content of a single physical-geometric principle (the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic generates the Minkowski metric, the McGucken Sphere, and the full physical edifice). The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's response to "is spacetime emergent?" is therefore precise: substrate-emergence is refused (it violates the Marolf Constraint and is empirically tensioned by COW); generative-emergence is affirmed (the single principle generates the metric and the spacetime structure as its immediate content). Conflating the two senses leads to imprecise dialectical engagement; the present paper distinguishes them sharply via Corollary 19.4.4.2 and Q4 of Theorem 19.4.2.

Falsifiability content of Theorem 19.4.4. If any experimental test were to demonstrate that the COW gravitational phase shift does not hold for matter-waves in a gravitational field — refuting the empirics of the Algebraic Channel matter-wave phase at the gravitational tier — then the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's empirical-strengthening argument in (ii) would be vacuous. No such refutation has been observed; the COW phase shift has been measured to high precision in many experiments since 1975. Conversely, if any theoretical development were to demonstrate that Verlinde's holographic-screen substrate satisfies the Marolf Constraint via a mechanism the original Verlinde 2011 paper did not articulate — for example, if subsequent work in the entropic-gravity program were to supply a foundational non-locality argument for the screen-bit dynamics — then the (D) portion of Theorem 19.4.4 would need to be revisited. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's claim is that the original Verlinde 2011 paper as published does not supply such a non-locality argument, and the strict pure-entropic reading therefore conflicts with the Marolf Constraint; subsequent developments in the entropic-gravity program may or may not resolve this issue. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's own generative-emergence claim (Corollary 19.4.4.2) is falsifiable in a different sense: if the chain of theorems from dx₄/dt = ic to the Minkowski metric to the McGucken Sphere to gravity/QM/thermodynamics were demonstrated to contain a gap — for example, if the metric-generation step (G1) were shown to require an additional postulate beyond dx₄/dt = ic — then the generative-emergence claim would be refuted. The chain as developed in the present paper and the corpus is supplied step-by-step; any gap a reader identifies would be material to the framework's status.

Subsection 19.4.4(H): Verlinde 2022 Contemporary Position — The Self-Acknowledged AdS-versus-de-Sitter Gap, the Vacuum-as-Glass Reframing, and What the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Framework Supplies at the Source Verlinde's Programme Has Not Yet Reached

The engagement with Verlinde 2011 above is necessary but no longer sufficient as a treatment of the entropic-gravity programme as it currently stands. Verlinde's own published-talk position has evolved substantially over the past decade, and the contemporary 2022 statement — Emergence of Gravity from Quantum Information: A Progress Report, delivered at the Information Universe conference, summer 2022 ([165]) — supplies a primary-source articulation of the programme's current state that the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework can engage with rigorously and to its own advantage. The talk dates to approximately 22 June 2022: Verlinde refers to a Witten paper "just out yesterday" on de Sitter algebra and entropy ([166]: Chandrasekaran–Longo–Penington–Witten, An Algebra of Observables for de Sitter Space, arXiv:2206.10780, submitted 22 June 2022) and to a World Science Festival meeting "two weeks ago in New York" with Susskind and Van Raamsdonk on Einstein, entanglement, and emergence. Five points from the contemporary talk warrant explicit engagement; each is documented with primary-source quotation and then mapped against the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework.

(H1) Entanglement entropy, not entropy in general. Verlinde 2011 spoke of entropy as the substrate from which gravity emerges, leaving the microscopic origin of the entropy unspecified. Verlinde 2022 reframes the substrate as entanglement entropy specifically — "by now we actually know that this entropy should be thought of as a sort of an entanglement entropy in the structure of quantum structure of space-time" — and identifies the Ryu–Takayanagi formula as the empirically-derived link between entanglement entropy and area: "the entanglement entropy is equal to the area of a certain surface that we put into space and this is called now also the Ryu–Takayanagi formula that has been derived... even in some microscopic models." This is an important refinement: the entropy that drives gravity is now specifically entanglement entropy across spatial boundaries, not generic statistical entropy of microscopic degrees of freedom.

McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework response. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework already supplies the source of entanglement-entropy content via Theorem 30 of the present paper (Quantum Nonlocality as McGucken-Sphere Null-Separation): entanglement IS the matter-tier signature of 4D-null-connectivity through shared McGucken Sphere origins (the "all nonlocality begins as locality" principle of [21 §V.2]). The Ryu–Takayanagi formula's empirics — entanglement entropy across a spatial surface equals the area of a minimal surface in the bulk — is recovered in the McGucken framework as the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel reading of horizon-area-as-entropy for the McGucken Sphere bounding the entanglement region: the bulk minimal surface is the McGucken Sphere connecting the two spatial subsystems through their common past event, with the entanglement entropy quantifying the Sphere-mediated 4D null-connectivity. The identification is explicit: Ryu–Takayanagi 2006 supplies the empirical-area content; Theorem 30 + [21 §V.2] supplies the McGucken-Sphere mechanism. The Verlinde 2022 refinement (entanglement entropy specifically, not generic entropy) tightens his programme's alignment with the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework rather than weakening it: the McGucken Sphere null-connectivity is the natural geometric structure for entanglement entropy on horizons.

(H2) The self-acknowledged AdS-versus-de-Sitter gap. The Verlinde 2022 talk supplies the single most important primary-source acknowledgment of the entropic-gravity programme's current limitations:

> "This whole program of emergent gravity basically has been completed in a setting where the space-time, well unfortunately, has no cosmological content. It actually has a negative curvature, it's called AdS space, and in that space people have exactly done what I said before and then they derive the Einstein's equations from this first law of basically entanglement entropy."  
>   — Verlinde 2022, [165], minutes 16:04–16:25

> "This whole idea that gravity emerges is something that by now I think in our community has been accepted and I think the theory is going to be developed, but it's not something that we fully understand, and certainly not in the context yet of a space-time with positive energy, the dark energy."  
>   — Verlinde 2022, [165], minutes 19:08–19:21

This is the AdS-versus-de-Sitter gap: the entropic-gravity programme's completeness has been established only for anti-de-Sitter space (negative cosmological constant, the AdS/CFT toy model used since Maldacena 1997), where the boundary CFT supplies the microscopic substrate via the holographic principle. The physical universe has positive cosmological constant (dark energy, observed at Λ≈10^-122 in Planck units) and is therefore approximately de Sitter at cosmological scale, not AdS. The entropic-gravity programme has not been extended in rigorous form to the physical positive-Λ universe.

McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework response — advantage. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic operates natively in the positive-cosmological-constant context where Verlinde's programme has not yet reached. The principle is not formulated as a boundary-CFT-defined limit (which is intrinsically AdS-specific via the boundary-bulk holographic dictionary); it is formulated as the active expansion of the fourth dimension at +ic at every event in any spacetime, with x₄ = ict as the integrated coordinate. The principle generates the FRW cosmology of Theorem 18 of the present paper (which is the cosmological-thermodynamics of the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel reading at cosmic scale), generates the de Sitter horizon entropy as the area-quarter content of Theorem 15 applied to the cosmological McGucken Sphere Σ_+^cosmo, and generates the unification of the five arrows of time as parallel projections of +ic at every event including cosmological-scale events (Theorem 11). The framework's empirics is the same across AdS, de Sitter, Minkowski, FRW, and Schwarzschild contexts — because the principle is universal rather than context-specific.

The diagnosis is therefore that the exact place Verlinde's programme is "certainly not in the context yet of" is precisely where dx₄/dt = ic supplies content at the foundational level. The entropic-gravity programme's boundary-CFT specificity is what restricts it to AdS; the McGucken principle's event-level locality is what gives it universal applicability across all spacetime backgrounds.

(H3) Vacuum-as-glass and the cosmological-horizon entropy ∼10¹23. Verlinde 2022 reframes the de Sitter vacuum as not empty but as a state with substantial built-in entropy:

> "I think the vacuum in the de Sitter space is not empty. Well first of all there's dark energy but there's also entropy sitting there, and the analogy you should have is with a crystal or glass: because the crystal does not really have entropy, it has a unique ground state, it has a unique configuration, but a glass has very similar properties but the difference is that it has lots of entropy in it."  
>   — Verlinde 2022, [165], minutes 30:54–31:24

The entropy of the cosmological horizon at present-day Hubble scale is approximately S_cosmo ≈(1/4ℓ_P²) ·4π(c/H₀)² ≈10¹23 (the number Charles Bennett supplied to Verlinde and that is the standard de-Sitter horizon entropy in Planck units). Verlinde claims this entropy IS the dark energy: the cosmological-scale built-in entropy that the vacuum has even at "ground state" is the source of Λ.

McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework response. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies the vacuum-as-glass content via the universal +ic expansion at every event. Every event sources a McGucken Sphere whose volume monotonically grows; the cosmological-scale McGucken Sphere Σ_+^cosmo is the universe-as-event's own future light cone, with area equal to the de Sitter horizon area and entropy quantized via the Planck-area unit per [59, IV.1]. The cosmological horizon entropy ∼10¹23 in Planck units is therefore the count of Planck-area units on Σ_+^cosmo — the content the McGucken Sphere supplies at universe scale. The Verlinde-glass framing is correct: the vacuum is not empty; it carries the ground-state entropy of x₄'s active expansion at every event, accumulated at cosmic scale as the cosmological-horizon entropy. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies the mechanism (universal +ic at every event) that the glass-analogue framing motivates phenomenologically.

The identification of horizon entropy with dark energy is a separate claim from the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's content. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's Λ identification — whether Λ is the entropy of the cosmological McGucken Sphere, or whether Λ has a separate origin in the FRW thermodynamics of Theorem 18 — is an open question the present paper does not foreclose. The Verlinde-glass framing supplies one plausible reading (horizon entropy IS dark energy); other readings within the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework remain open.

(H4) The entropic-force adiabatic clarification — Verlinde's own response to questioner pressure. The Verlinde 2011 paper has often been read by orthodox physicists as claiming that gravity is a "dS/dx-force" — a force generated by the change in entropy as a test particle moves toward a holographic screen. Verlinde 2022 explicitly corrects this misreading, in response to direct questioning at the end of the talk:

> Questioner (paraphrased): I'm confused — your polymer example shows a force from a change in entropy dS/dt, but your gravity story talks about S itself, not dS/dt.  
> Verlinde response: "I spent some time explaining that confusion here. The actual equation here is that when you lower the speed [of the polymer end] you're doing it adiabatically — because if that would not have been [done by a] force, the entropy would have changed. So the force is actually making sure that the entropy does not change, but the consequence of the force is the tendency to change the entropy. So this is a reversible system."  
>   — Verlinde 2022, [165], minutes 41:13–41:50

The content: entropic forces in Verlinde's sense are reversible / adiabatic — they are conservative forces derived from an entropy potential, in the same way that electromagnetic forces are derived from the electromagnetic potential. The force is not directly proportional to dS/dt; rather, the force is the gradient of the entropy with the temperature setting the proportionality constant. This is the standard polymer-elastic-force structure, applied at gravitational scale.

McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework response. The adiabatic-reversible character Verlinde correctly identifies aligns with the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's Geometric Channel reading: the gravitational force at the matter tier descends from the McGucken Sphere's geometric structure at every event, with the Compton-coupling to x₄ supplying the matter-tier coupling strength. The content is conservative (a potential-gradient force) by construction; the McGucken Sphere's volume function V(Σ_+(p, t)) = (4π/3)(ct)³ is a smooth function of the event coordinate, and the gravitational pull a test mass experiences is the matter-tier integrated content of the Sphere's local structure. The Verlinde-2022 adiabatic clarification removes the over-strong reading of entropic gravity as a dS/dt-driven dissipative effect, restoring the alignment with the Newtonian / general-relativistic conservative-force content that the McGucken Theorem 19 dual-channel derivation produces from the dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel (Hilbert variational) and the Geometric Channel (Jacobson/Verlinde horizon-thermodynamic) routes simultaneously.

(H5) Verlinde's own self-acknowledgment of programmatic incompleteness. The Verlinde 2022 talk closes with explicit honest admissions:

> "I think if we really want to discuss this very seriously I should develop the theory of emerging gravity much further. We should have some way of deriving dynamics and having some analog of the Friedmann equation or something that at least we can derive from this microscopic picture. What I've done here is a very simple thing: I basically took my phenomenological relation and put it in the Friedmann equation and see somebody what is the consequence."

(H6) Engagement with the Witten et al. 2206.10780 de Sitter algebra paper. The Verlinde 2022 talk references with explicit interest the Witten et al. paper that appeared "just out yesterday" — Chandrasekaran, Longo, Penington, Witten, An Algebra of Observables for de Sitter Space ([166], arXiv:2206.10780, submitted 22 June 2022). The Witten et al. paper supplies the operator-algebraic characterization of the de Sitter static-patch observables as a Type II₁ von Neumann algebra, with empty de Sitter space identified as the maximum entropy state of the algebra and the generalized entropy S_gen = A/(4G_N) + S_out recovered (up to an additive constant) as the entropy of any semiclassical state. The Witten paper is technically rigorous and represents the orthodox operator-algebraic best response to the de Sitter entropy problem as of 2022.

McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework response. The Witten et al. Type II₁ algebra is recognized in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework as the Algebraic Channel operator-algebraic specialization of the cosmological-scale McGucken Sphere structure — the same the dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel specialization that the McGucken framework supplies for Bekenstein–Hawking entropy in Theorem 15 (the Algebraic Channel: Bogoliubov coefficient + first law of black-hole thermodynamics) and for Hawking temperature in Theorem 16 (the Algebraic Channel: KMS + Bisognano–Wichmann on Killing-time generators). The Type II₁ algebra identification of empty de Sitter as the maximum-entropy state is consistent with the cosmological McGucken Sphere having maximum-area-entropy at the de Sitter horizon scale; the additive-constant renormalization Witten et al. discuss is consistent with the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's Planck-scale-cutoff identification ([21 §VII] open problem 3). The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies the Geometric Channel geometric-propagation reading that complements the Witten the Algebraic Channel reading: empty de Sitter space is the maximum-entropy state because the cosmological-scale McGucken Sphere Σ_+^cosmo has its maximum spatial extent at empty-vacuum conditions, with any matter content reducing the area available to the cosmological horizon (as Verlinde 2022 also emphasizes in his discussion of the Witten paper). The Lin–Susskind 2022 paper [167], Infinite Temperature's Not So Hot (arXiv:2206.01083), cited in the Witten et al. references, develops a related construction within the matrix-model context. (H7) Empirical anchor: Brouwer weak-lensing data and the radial acceleration relation. The Verlinde 2022 talk emphasizes the empirics the entropic-gravity programme has been tested against — specifically the Mojo/Brouwer weak-lensing measurements of the radial acceleration relation:

[42]; [3] cites both by key without a locator).

8.0 The 2011 paper read in full: each stated assumption derived from the Principle

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic states that from every event a McGucken Sphere expands at c, its wavelength setting the action h and its volume defining a nonlocality. Verlinde's construction [9] (verified-read, full text) assumes screens, bits proportional to area, an entropy step per Compton wavelength, an auxiliary ħ, equipartition, and the Unruh temperature, and leaves open the microscopic theory, the role of ħ, the Bekenstein-bound tension, and the predictions. Each assumption is quoted and derived below from the Sphere; where Verlinde postulates, the Principle computes.

(1) The unexplained resemblance. Verlinde: "The universal nature of gravity is also demonstrated by the fact that its basic equations closely resemble the laws of thermodynamics and hydrodynamics. So far, there has not been a clear explanation for this resemblance" [9, §1].

Derivation from the Principle. The explanation is Theorem 5.1 with Corollary 5.3: the field equations have a Geometric-Channel derivation that runs through the Second Law, the area law, and the Unruh temperature (Theorem 4.7), each a theorem of the McGucken Sphere (§3), and the resemblance is the shared channel. Hydrodynamics enters the same way: the Compton-tick diffusion of Theorem 3.3 is the reduced-state dynamics of the advance, and the Einstein equation is its horizon-area reading at ensemble resolution (§7.3).

(2) Entropic force. Verlinde: "An entropic force is an effective macroscopic force that originates in a system with many degrees of freedom by the statistical tendency to increase its entropy. The force equation is expressed in terms of entropy differences, and is independent of the details of the microscopic dynamics. In particular, there is no fundamental field associated with an entropic force" [9, §2]; and the force law F Δx = T ΔS (his Eq. (3.7)).

Derivation from the Principle. The statistical tendency is Theorem 3.3: the reduced state of the Compton-tick advance has dS/dt > 0 because the advance is +ic-oriented, so the many degrees of freedom are the Compton-tick states of the McGucken Spheres and the tendency is the orientation of the Principle. F Δx = T ΔS is the Clausius relation derived in Theorem 4.7 Step 4, written for a displacement: with T from Theorem 4.6 and ΔS from Theorem 8.1 it gives F = ma (item 5). Verlinde's "no fundamental field" holds within the Geometric Channel; the Algebraic Channel derives the same gravity as a field theory, the Einstein–Hilbert action and its field equations (Theorem 4.1), so the Principle supplies both the entropic reading and the field reading of one law (Corollary 5.2), which is why the entropic force is conservative in the Principle (§8.3) while an entropic force in general is not [39].

(3) Space as storage, screens, and the emergent direction. Verlinde: "Space is therefore literally just a storage space for information. … Given that the maximal allowed information is finite for each part of space, it is impossible to localize a particle with infinite precision at a point of a continuum space. In fact, points and coordinates arise as derived concepts"; "we are going to assume that information is stored on surfaces, or screens"; "there is one special direction corresponding to scale or a coarse graining variable of the microscopic theory. This is the direction in which space is emergent. So the screens that store the information are like stretched horizons. On one side there is space, on the other side nothing yet" [9, §3].

Derivation from the Principle. The screens are the McGucken Spheres: Σ_+(p) is the surface on which the data of the advance are stored, and the data on it determine the field in its volume (Lemma 7.4.4). The finite information per part of space is the Compton tick, Δx₄ = iλ_C per cycle (§2.3), and the limit on localization is λ_C itself: a particle of mass m is a Sphere of wavelength h/mc, and no state of the advance resolves it below that. Points and coordinates are derived in the sense that the metric is the square of the rate (§2.1); events, however, are primitive, because the Principle asserts the expansion of the McGucken Sphere from every event. The special direction is x₄: the Sphere's advance is the one direction in which the geometry is generated, and the "stretched horizon" with "nothing yet" beyond it is the Sphere at time t, whose interior is the region already reached by the advance and whose exterior has not yet been reached from p. Verlinde's direction is a coarse-graining variable of an unnamed theory (§2.4); the Principle names it as the advance and gives it a rate, c.

(4) The postulate and the auxiliary ħ. Verlinde: "let us postulate that the change of entropy associated with the information on the boundary equals ΔS = 2πk_B when Δx = ħ/mc" (Eq. (3.5)); "Since the postulate (3.5) is the basic assumption from which everything else follows, let us discuss its meaning in more detail. Why does the entropy precisely change like this when one shifts by one Compton wave length? … ħ just serves as an auxiliary variable that is needed for dimensional reasons. It can therefore be chosen at will, and defined so that (3.5) is exactly valid. The main content of this equation is therefore simply that there is an entropy change perpendicular to the screen proportional to the mass m and the displacement Δx. That is all there is to it" [9, §3.1, §3.3]; and on the mass dependence, "Since entropy and mass are both additive, it is therefore natural that the entropy change is proportional to the mass."

Theorem 8.1: (mc/ħ)Δx is the Compton phase Δϕ_C of the particle's advance across Δx, so the postulate reads ΔS = 2πk_B Δϕ_C, and ħ is the action per Compton cycle of §2.3, fixed by the Principle and not choosable. The dependence on Δx is linear because the advance covers Δx at the constant rate c. From [19], verbatim — Definition 9.1 (Inertial mass) and Proposition 9.2, statement and proof: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list)

Definition 9.1 (Inertial mass) The inertial mass m of a massive particle is the magnitude of the four-momentum invested in x₄-advance, divided by c, evaluated at spatial rest: m ≡ |P₄|/c |_spatial rest. The physics: m is the amount of four-momentum a particle has invested in the x₄-advance that the physics of Axiom 2.1 mandates at every event. Proposition 9.2 (Operational consistency at spatial rest) At spatial rest, |P₄|/c = m, where m is the rest mass appearing in P^μ = m u^μ (Theorem 8.4). Proof. At spatial rest: v = 0, γ = 1, p = 0 (Lemma 8.1), E = mc² (Lemma 8.3). Standard numbering: P⁰ = E/c = mc. McGucken numbering: P₄ = i P⁰ = imc. Modulus: |P₄| = |imc| = mc. Hence |P₄|/c = mc/c = m. ∎

From [19], verbatim — Theorem 10.2 (Newton's first law), statement and proof: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list)

Theorem 10.2 (Newton's first law) A massive particle subject to no force has du^μ/dτ = 0 in flat spacetime; the spatial three-velocity is constant. In curved spacetime, Du^μ/dτ = 0, the geodesic equation. Proof. Force. The four-force is F^μ ≡ dP^μ/dτ in flat space, DP^μ/dτ in curved space. By Theorem 8.4 and constancy of m: F^μ = m a^μ. No force implies no acceleration. If F^μ = 0 and m ≠ 0, then a^μ = 0. Newtonian content. If u^μ is constant: by Lemma 5.4, u^j = γ v^j are constants. The Master Equation gives |u^0|² − | u |² = c² with |u^0|² = (γc)² and | u |² = γ²v². With u^j constant, | u |² constant; with the difference c² fixed, |u^0|² constant; hence γ constant, hence v constant, hence each v^j constant, hence v constant. Straight-line uniform motion. Curved spacetime. Du^μ/dτ = du^μ/dτ + Γ^μ_αβ u^α u^β. Setting F^μ = m Du^μ/dτ = 0 yields the geodesic equation. By Theorem 7.1(2) and Corollary 7.3, the timelike-block Christoffel symbols vanish; the dynamical contributions from gravity all live in the spatial Christoffel symbols computed from h_ij. ∎

From [19], verbatim — Theorem 11.1 (Rest energy), statement and proof: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list)

Theorem 11.1 (Rest energy) The energy of a particle of inertial mass m at spatial rest is E₀ = mc². Proof. By Lemma 8.3, E = γmc². At spatial rest ( v = 0, γ = 1): E₀ = mc². ∎ Remark 11.2 (Physics) At spatial rest, the entire four-velocity is invested in the x₄-advance that Axiom 2.1 mandates at the particle's event (Corollary 6.3(i)). From [19], verbatim — Theorem 12.1 (Second law), statement and proof: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list)

Theorem 12.1 (Second law) The four-force on a particle of inertial mass m is F^μ = m a^μ. The coordinate-time three-force F ₃ ≡ d p /dt decomposes into longitudinal and transverse components: F₃,∥ = γ³ m a∥, F₃,⊥ = γ m a⊥, where a = d v /dt is the coordinate-time three-acceleration, a∥ = a · v̂, a ⊥ = a − a∥ v̂. At low velocity (γ → 1): F = m a . Proof. Four-force. As in Theorem 10.2: F^μ = m du^μ/dτ = m a^μ. Computation of γ̇. From γ = (1 − v²/c²)^(−1/2) with v² = v · v : γ̇ = d/dt (1 − v²/c²)^(−1/2) = −½ (1 − v²/c²)^(−3/2) · (−1/c²) · d( v · v )/dt = γ³/(2c²) · 2 v · a = γ³ ( v · a )/c². Computation of d p/dt. F ₃ = d p /dt = m d(γ v )/dt = m [γ̇ v + γ a ] = m [γ³( v · a ) v /c² + γ a ]. Decomposition. Write a = a∥ v̂ + a ⊥ with a ⊥ · v = 0. Then v · a = v a∥, and ( v · a ) v = v² a∥ v̂. Parallel component. F₃,∥ = m [γ³ v² a∥/c² + γ a∥] = m γ a∥ [γ² v²/c² + 1]. Using γ^(−2) = 1 − v²/c², so γ² v²/c² = γ²(1 − γ^(−2)) = γ² − 1: γ² v²/c² + 1 = γ² − 1 + 1 = γ². Hence F₃,∥ = m γ a∥ · γ² = γ³ m a∥. Perpendicular component. Since a ⊥ · v = 0, the first term contributes nothing perpendicular: F ₃,⊥ = γ m a ⊥. Low-velocity limit. As v/c → 0: γ → 1, γ³ → 1. Both reduce to F = m a . ∎ Remark 12.2 (Longitudinal and transverse mass) The relativistic mass distinctions m∥ = γ³ m, m⊥ = γ m are forced by the fixed magnitude |u| = c of the four-velocity (Master Equation, Theorem 5.5). The four-velocity rotates within the budget hyperboloid under applied force; rotating it parallel to v requires changing γ, with extra factors of γ in the resistance; rotating it perpendicular to v leaves γ unchanged.

From [19], verbatim — Corollary 7.4 (Gravitational time dilation, redshift, and the no-graviton conclusion), statement and proof: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list)

Corollary 7.4 (Gravitational time dilation, redshift, and the no-graviton conclusion) (i) Gravitational time dilation is a feature of h_ij, not of the rate of the fourth-dimension expansion. (ii) Gravitational redshift is light propagating through curved spatial geometry, not the fourth dimension advancing differently in different potentials. Variations in dτ between worldlines arise entirely from h_ij acting on the spatial worldline displacement. A clock at higher gravitational potential ticks at a different rate of proper time per unit coordinate time because its worldline is differently embedded in the curved spatial geometry; the fourth dimension advances at c at every event, regardless. (ii) Redshift. A photon's wavelength is a feature of its spatial propagation through the metric. By Theorem 7.1(2), the timelike block is invariant; the wavelength change in a gravitational field is entirely due to h_ij varying with potential. (iii) No graviton. A graviton would be a quantum mediator of dynamical degrees of freedom in the timelike block, or in a separate tensor field beyond g_μν. By Theorem 7.1(3), the only dynamical degrees of freedom in g_μν are the six components of h_ij, which are properties of the spatial slices, not propagating quanta. Geometry is not mediated by particles. The full quantitative content — gravitational redshift, gravitational time dilation, and spatial curvature carrying all gravitational dynamics with the fourth dimension remaining invariant — is developed in the April 2026 GR-foundational paper [4]. ∎
