The "statistical averaged random dynamics at the microscopic level" is the isotropic Compton-tick displacement of Theorem 3.2 with the SO(3)-invariant measure, and the entropy differences "in whatever way defined" are defined: S = k_BlnΩ with Ω the Compton-tick state count of the McGucken Sphere (§6). The cause of gravity in the Geometric Channel is the focusing of the Sphere's generators by that count (Theorem 4.7 Step 3); in the Algebraic Channel it is the field equation of the derived action. Verlinde's mechanism is one channel of the Principle's two.

(11) The role of ħ, the Bekenstein bound, and the rescaling freedom. Verlinde: "This brings us to a somewhat subtle and not yet fully understood aspect. Namely, the role of ħ"; the screen entropy S = (c³/4Għ)∫_𝒮dA "appears to be very high, and violates the Bekenstein bound"; "there may also be other ways to reconcile these statements, for example by making use of the freedom to rescale the value of ħ … one can even multiply ħ by a function f(Φ₀) of the Newton potential on the screen" [9, §6.4].

Derivation from the Principle. ħ has no rescaling freedom: it is the action per Compton cycle, E T_C = h (§2.3), and Theorem 8.1 makes the entropy step a count of cycles. The Bekenstein tension is resolved by distinguishing the McGucken Sphere's capacity from its occupation: N = A/ℓ_P² (Theorem 3.5, Lemma 7.4.4) is the number of modes of the advance a Sphere of area A can carry, and the Bekenstein bound S≤2πk_BER/ħc bounds the entropy of matter states inside; the two coincide only when the Sphere is a horizon, where every mode is occupied, which is Jacobson's and Verlinde's horizon case. For an equipotential Sphere far from a horizon the capacity exceeds the occupied matter entropy, and no bound is violated because the capacity is not the state of the matter. Multiplying ħ by f(Φ₀) would alter the cycle count by position, contradicting the invariance of the rate (Lemma 7.4.1); what varies with Φ₀ is the fraction of ticks resolved per coordinate time (item 8), which is the redshift, already in the metric.

(12) Predictions. Verlinde: "Does this view of gravity lead to predictions? The statistical average should give the usual laws, hence one has to study the fluctuations in the gravitational force. Their size depends on the effective temperature, which may not be universal and depends on the effective value of ħ. … But clearly, we need a better understanding of the theory to turn this in to a prediction" [9, §6.4].

Derivation from the Principle. With ħ fixed and the temperature derived, the fluctuation scale is derived: the Compton-tick diffusion has D = h/6m (Theorem 3.3), and the residual on a coherent state is D_x^(McG) = ε²c²Ω_mod/2γ² (§6.3); the tidal Born shift δp∼p R₀i0jL^iL^j and the four further tests of §13 are the predictions Verlinde asks for. The published falsifications of an entropic force with unfixed noise [39, 40] are the measurements of exactly these fluctuations (§8.3), and the Principle survives them because its unitary full state carries no thermal noise beyond the bounded residual.

(13) Action at a distance. Verlinde: "What Newton did not know, and certainly Hooke didn't, is that the universe is holographic. Holography is also an hypothesis, of course, and may appear just as absurd as an action at a distance. One of the main points of this paper is that the holographic hypothesis provides a natural mechanism for gravity to emerge. It allows direct 'contact' interactions between degrees of freedom associated with one material body and another, since all bodies inside a volume can be mapped on the same holographic screen" [9, §6.4].

Derivation from the Principle. Holography is a theorem (Lemma 7.4.4), and the "contact" is the Principle's nonlocality: the McGucken Sphere's volume defines the region on which bodies share one state (Lemma 7.4.5), so two bodies within one Sphere interact through the joint count on that Sphere, and the screen on which "all bodies inside a volume can be mapped" is Σ_+(p) itself. The mechanism Newton lacked and Hooke demanded is the expansion of the McGucken Sphere at c from every event: a local event becomes a nonlocal surface, and the gravitational interaction is the focusing of that surface's generators by the Compton-tick energy of the bodies it encloses (Theorem 4.7 Step 3).

Summary of the attribution. (1) the resemblance is the shared Geometric Channel (Theorem 5.1, Corollary 5.3); (2) the entropic force is the Clausius relation of Theorem 4.7 Step 4 with the orientation of Theorem 3.3, and the field reading is Theorem 4.1; (3) screens are McGucken Spheres, finite information is the tick, the emergent direction is x₄ (Lemma 7.4.4, §2.3); (4) the postulate is 2πk_B per radian of Compton phase with ħ fixed (Theorem 8.1, Theorem 3.1); (5) temperature and acceleration are one Euclidean period (Theorem 4.6), giving F = ma; (6) N = A/ℓ_P² and equipartition over free horizon-tier modes give 1/2Nk_BT = Mc² as an identity (Theorem 3.5, Lemma 7.4.4); (7) the admitted circularity is removed because the inputs are derived without Newton; (8) inertia is m = |P₄|/c and the redshift is dτ/dt, both from the advance ([19], Theorem 3.1 Step 1); (9) the Komar sketch is completed by Theorem 4.7 with the trace-reversed combination fixed by conservation (Corollary 4.8); (10) geometry and gravity are both derived (§2.1, Theorem 5.1); (11) ħ is fixed and the Bekenstein tension is capacity versus occupation (§2.3, Theorem 3.5); (12) the fluctuations are D = h/6m and the residual D_x^(McG) (§6.3, §13); (13) holography and contact are Lemmas 7.4.4 and 7.4.5.

8.0bis The 2017 paper read in full: the dark sector of emergent gravity derived from the Principle

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic states that from every event a McGucken Sphere expands at c, its wavelength setting the action h and its volume defining a nonlocality. Verlinde's 2017 paper [101] (verified-read, full text) extends the 2011 construction to de Sitter space: it takes the cosmological horizon's entropy and temperature as input, postulates that the de Sitter entropy is distributed over the bulk as a volume law, computes the entropy a mass removes from the horizon, and from the elastic response of the "dark energy medium" estimates an apparent dark-matter acceleration g_D = √(a_Mg_B) with a_M = a₀/6, a₀ = cH₀. It lists the conditions under which the estimate holds and the cosmological questions it leaves open. Each step is quoted and derived below from the cosmological Sphere; the one place where the two programmes differ numerically is stated with its size.

(1) The cosmological horizon and the acceleration scale. Verlinde: "The most important aspect we have to deal with is that de Sitter space has a cosmological horizon. Hence, it carries a finite entropy and temperature given by (1.1), where the surface acceleration κ is given in terms of the Hubble parameter H₀ and Hubble scale L by κ = cH₀ = c²/L = a₀ (1.2). The acceleration scale a₀ will play a particularly important role in this paper" [101, §1.2]; and "we propose that the thermal excitations responsible for the de Sitter entropy constitute the positive dark energy. In this physical picture the positive dark energy and accelerated expansion are caused by the slow thermalization of the emergent spacetime" [101, §1.2].

Derivation from the Principle. The cosmological horizon is the Hubble Sphere, the McGucken Sphere of radius R_H = c/H expanding from the cosmological origin event; its entropy k_BA_dS/4ℓ_P² and temperature ħH/2πk_B are Theorem 18 of [3] (quoted in §9.0 item 1), the cosmological instance of Theorems 3.5 and 4.5 with the cigar period β_dS = 2π/H. The dark energy is identified by Theorem 12.1(i): the energy density of the unperturbed advance has w = -1 exactly, by the rigidity of the rate (Lemma 7.4.1), with no thermalization hypothesis. The acceleration scale differs by the factor that separates a cycle from a radian: Verlinde's a₀ = cH₀ is the surface gravity of the de Sitter horizon; the Principle's galactic scale is a₀ = cH₀/2π (Theorem 12.1(iii), [27]), the Hubble Sphere's expansion rate per radian of its cycle, the same radian that converts λ_C to ħ/mc in Theorem 8.1. Verlinde's Milgrom scale is then a_M = a₀/6 = cH₀/6 (item 6), the Principle's is cH₀/2π; the two differ by 2π/6 = 1.047, 4.7%, which lies inside the present empirical uncertainty on a₀ ([27] §X, falsifier F1, verified-read: "If precision converges on a₀ outside [1.04, 1.13]×10^-10 m/s², the asymmetry-based prediction fails").

(2) The entropic criterion for the missing-mass regime. Verlinde: "Empirically the directly observed gravitational phenomena attributed to dark matter, such as the flattening of rotation curves in spiral galaxies and the evidence from weak lensing data, occur when the surface mass density falls below a universal value determined by the acceleration scale a₀: Σ(r) = M/A(r) < a₀/8πG (1.3). … let us rewrite the above inequality as S_M = 2πM/ħa₀ < A(r)/4Għ (1.4). The quantity on the l.h.s. represents the change in the de Sitter entropy caused by adding the mass M, while the r.h.s. is the entropy of a black hole that would fit inside the region bounded by the area A" [101, §1.3].

Derivation from the Principle. S_M = 2πM/ħa₀ = 2πML/ħc is Theorem 8.1 evaluated across the Hubble length: ΔS = 2πk_B (Mc/ħ) Δx with Δx = L = R_H, the Compton phase the mass M accumulates over one Hubble radius of the advance. The right-hand side is Theorem 3.5. The criterion compares two counts on the same McGucken Sphere — the Compton-phase count a mass M carries across the region (Theorem 3.1, Theorem 8.1) and the Planck-cell count of its boundary (Theorem 3.5) — and in the Principle it is the statement that the matter's x₄-coupling and the cosmological Sphere's coupling are comparable, g_N ∼a₀, which is the transition of the interpolation g = g_N + √(g_Na₀) of [27] (item 6).

(3) The two postulates: area law and volume law. Verlinde: "(i) There exists a microscopic bulk perspective in which the area law for the entanglement entropy is due to the short distance entanglement of neighboring degrees of freedom that build the emergent bulk spacetime. (ii) The de Sitter entropy is evenly divided over the same microscopic degrees of freedom that build the emergent spacetime through their entanglement, and is caused by the long range entanglement of part of these degrees of freedom" [101, §2]; and the resulting volume law, "a ball of radius r centered around the origin contains an entropy S_DE(r) proportional to its volume S_DE(r) = V(r)/V₀ with V(r) = Ω_d-2r^d-1/(d-1) (2.13) … V₀ = 4GħL/(d-1) (2.14) … An alternative way to write the entropy S_DE(r) is in terms of the area A(r) as S_DE(r) = (r/L) A(r)/4Għ (2.15)" [101, §2.2].

Derivation from the Principle. Postulate (i) is Theorem 3.5 Step 2 with Lemma 7.4.4: the independent data of the advance on a McGucken Sphere are one per cell of the tier's squared wavelength, so the count is of the surface, and the "neighboring degrees of freedom" are the adjacent cells of one wavefront. Postulate (ii) is the volume of the anchor sentence — the Sphere's volume defines a nonlocality — read on the Hubble Sphere: the region reached by the cosmological advance is the interior of the Hubble Sphere, and every event in it shares the common origin that Lemma 7.4.5 requires for nonlocal correlation. The volume law's normalization is then a geometric identity: in d = 4, V₀ = 4GħL/3 and S_DE(r) = V(r)/V₀ = (r/L) A(r)/4Għ because V/A = r/3 — the same surface-to-volume conversion that Theorem 12.1(iii) uses, V/(AR_H) = 1/3, and that supplies the factor 3 of 6π = 3×2π. Verlinde's "evenly divided" is the Principle's isotropy (Theorem 3.2): the advance reaches every direction of the Hubble Sphere's interior at the same rate.

(4) The entropy a mass removes, and mass as relative entropy. Verlinde: "the total de Sitter entropy changes by a negative amount S_M(L) given by S_M(L) = u(L) d/dL((A(L))/(4Għ)) = -(2πML)/(ħ) (4.25) … Apparently, adding matter to spacetime reduces the amount of entanglement entropy. Our interpretation of general relativity and the Einstein equations is that it describes the response of the area law entanglement of the vacuum spacetime to matter" [101, §4.1]; "dS_M(r)/dr = -2πM/ħ (4.27) … by integrating this equation one finds S_M(r) = -2πMr/ħ (4.28), which up to a sign is the familiar Bekenstein bound, which together with the results of [57] suggests that the definition of mass in emergent gravity is given in terms of relative entropy" [101, §4.1].

Derivation from the Principle. Equation (4.27) is Theorem 8.1 per unit length, dS/dr = 2πk_B Mc/ħ, the Compton phase rate of the mass along the advance; the sign is Theorem 4.7 Step 3, Raychaudhuri focusing, by which matter crossing a McGucken Sphere's generators reduces the area they span, δA = -∫λR_μνk^μk^νdλdA, and with it the Planck-cell count of Theorem 3.5. "The response of the area law entanglement of the vacuum spacetime to matter" is Theorem 4.7 in full: Clausius on every generator of every Sphere. Mass as relative entropy is Theorem 10.1(iii): the Araki–Uhlmann relative entropy of a coherent excitation from the vacuum on the Sphere-cogenerated wedge equals -2π∫U⟨:T_ab:⟩ξ^aξ^b dU dvol, the count of Compton-tick states by which the excitation is distinguished from the vacuum — Verlinde's 2πMr/ħ is its evaluation for a mass M over the length r, with M = |P₄|/c the x₄-momentum of the Compton coupling (Definition 9.1 and Proposition 9.2 of [19]).

(5) The elastic medium and the ħ-free volume. Verlinde: "The central idea of this paper is that the volume law contribution to the entanglement entropy, associated with the positive dark energy, turns the otherwise 'stiff' geometry of spacetime into an elastic medium. We find that the elastic response of this 'dark energy' medium takes the form of an extra 'dark' gravitational force that appears to be due to 'dark matter'" [101, §1.4]; "V_M(r) = 8πGMr^d-1/a₀ (4.33). Here we replaced the Hubble length L by the acceleration scale a₀ to arrive at a formula that is dimensionally correct. In other words, this volume does not depend on ħ or c. In fact, as we will see, the elastic description that we are about to present only depends on the constants G and a₀" [101, §4.2].

Derivation from the Principle. The ħ-independence is Lemma 7.4.2: the cell count ∝1/ħ and the phase per cell ∝ħ cancel, as in Padmanabhan's equipartition energy (§9.0bis item 3), so the macroscopic law carries G and a₀ only. The medium that responds is named: it is the spatial sector x₁x₂x₃, which in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework is stretched radially by aggregated mass while x₄ advances rigidly (Scenario A of [27] §X.3b.1, h_rr = (1 - r_s/r)^-1; Theorem 12.1(ii)–(iii)). Verlinde's "stiff" geometry made "elastic" by the volume law is, in the Principle, the asymmetry between the rigid advance of x₄ and the stretchable spatial three; the "displacement of entropy" is the contraction ψ of the slice, and the "memory effect" is the accumulated δR/R_H = Ω_m/6 of Theorem 12.1(iii), which is cumulative because the advance does not reverse (+ic, Theorem 5.1).

(6) The main formula and the Tully–Fisher scaling. Verlinde: "∫₀^r (GM_D²(r'))/(r'²) dr' = (M_B(r) a₀ r)/6 (7.40). This is the main formula and central result of our paper … In the special case that the baryonic mass M_B is entirely centered in the origin … this leads to the relation g_D(r) = √(a_M g_B(r)) with a_M = a₀/6 (7.43). The parameter a_M is the famous acceleration scale introduced by Milgrom … We like to emphasize that we have not derived the theory of modified Newtonian dynamics as proposed by Milgrom. In our description there is no modification of the law of inertia, nor is our result (7.43) to be interpreted as a modified gravitational field equation. It is derived from an estimate" [101, §7.2]; and the total acceleration "g(r) = g_B(r) + g_D(r) (7.41)". The conditions: "one is dealing with a centralized, spherically symmetric mass distribution, which has been in dynamical equilibrium during its evolution. Dynamical situations as those that occur in the Bullet cluster are not described by these same equations. The system should also be sufficiently isolated … Finally, in the previous subsection we actually derived an inequality" [101, §7.2].

Derivation from the Principle. For a point mass Verlinde's total acceleration is g = g_B + √(a_Mg_B) with a_M = cH₀/6. The interpolation of [27], tested against the SPARC radial-acceleration relation at χ²/N = 0.46, is g = g_N + √(g_Na₀) with a₀ = cH₀/2π (verified-read, [27] §IV.4: "the geometric mean of the two scales the framework has — local mass acceleration GM/r² and cosmological background a₀"). The functional form is the same; the scale differs by 2π/6 (item 1). The derivations differ in kind. Verlinde's is "an estimate" of an elastic response, holding "only when certain conditions are being satisfied" and reducing to an inequality outside them; the Principle's √(g_Na₀) is the geometric mean of the matter McGucken Sphere's acceleration GM/r² (Theorem 3.1 at the horizon tier, Theorem 4.1 Step 6) and the Hubble Sphere's acceleration per radian cH₀/2π (Theorem 12.1(iii)), the two accelerations the Principle has, and it carries no equilibrium, isolation, or point-mass condition because both Spheres are present at every event (§2.2). The baryonic Tully–Fisher slope of exactly 4, v_f⁴ = GM_Ba₀, follows in the regime g_N ≪a₀ from either form; in the Principle it is the projection of x₄'s SO(3) expansion ([27] Test 7, Theorem 3.2). The Bullet-cluster offset that Verlinde excludes is a prediction of [27] (the lensing follows the galaxies, the gas lags, through the asymmetric coupling) and is listed there as Test 10.

(7) The stated open questions. Verlinde: "the arguments and calculations that we presented in this paper are not yet sufficient to answer the questions regarding the cosmological evolution of our equations. In particular, we made use of the value of the present-day Hubble parameter H₀ in our equations, which immediately raises the question whether one should use another value for the Hubble parameter at other cosmological times. In our calculations the parameter H₀ was assumed to be constant, since we made the approximation that our universe is entirely dominated by dark energy and that ordinary matter only leads to a small perturbation. … This poses again the question whether a theory in which (apparent) dark matter is explained via emergent gravity would be able to reproduce the successful description of the CMB spectrum, the large scale structure and galaxy formation. These questions need to be understood before we can make any claim that our description of dark matter phenomena is as successful as the ΛCDM paradigm … one should be able to derive the cosmological evolution equations from emergent gravity. For this one needs to first properly understand the role of quantum entanglement and the evolution of the total entropy of our universe. So it is still an open question" [101, §8.2].

Derivation from the Principle. Each question is answered by a theorem stated earlier in this paper, cited below. The Hubble parameter at other times: Theorem 12.1(iii) is written with Ω_m(z), so w(z) = -1 + Ω_m(z)/6π evolves, rising toward -1 + 1/6π at high z, with no assumption that dark energy dominates. The cosmological evolution equations: the Friedmann equations are Theorem 18 of [3], Step A1, from the Einstein equations of Theorems 4.1 and 4.7 with homogeneity and isotropy. The evolution of the total entropy: Theorem 18 item 1 and Theorem 3.3, dS/dt > 0 by the +ic orientation. The CMB and structure formation: [27] tests 2–6 and 9 (Planck 2018 CMB, Pantheon+, DESI BAO, fσ₈, cosmic chronometers, the H₀ tension as the 8.3% contraction ψ(t_rec)/ψ(t₀)), with zero free dark-sector parameters. The role of entanglement: Lemma 7.4.5, every entangled pair sharing an origin event inside one McGucken Sphere, and Theorem 10.1 for the wedge algebra. Verlinde's programme requires these from a microscopic theory it names as future work; in the Principle they are the same theorems that gave the 2011 results.

Closing attribution for §8.0bis. Item 1: Theorem 18 of [3] (Theorems 3.5, 4.5), Theorem 12.1(i), (iii), Theorem 8.1, Lemma 7.4.1. Item 2: Theorems 8.1, 3.5, 3.1. Item 3: Theorem 3.5 Step 2, Lemma 7.4.4, Lemma 7.4.5, Theorem 3.2, Theorem 12.1(iii). Item 4: Theorem 8.1, Theorem 4.7 Step 3, Theorem 10.1(iii), Definition 9.1 of [19]. Item 5: Lemma 7.4.2, Theorem 12.1(ii)–(iii), Theorem 5.1. Item 6: Theorem 12.1(iii), Theorems 3.1, 3.2, 4.1 Step 6, [27]. Item 7: Theorem 12.1(iii), Theorem 18 of [3], Theorem 3.3, Lemma 7.4.5, Theorem 10.1, [27].

8.0ter The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Reading of what Verlinde's identification of gravity with entropy asserts, why his construction carries no arrow of time, and why it requires a holographic screen

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality. This subsection takes three questions to Verlinde's text [9] (verified-read, full text) and [165] (verified-read, transcript): what his sentence "gravity is an entropic force" asserts and what he says it means; where the direction of time leaves his construction; and why the construction cannot be written without a holographic screen. Each answer is quoted from his page, proved as a statement about his equations, and followed by the theorem of the Principle that supplies what the construction lacks.

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic states that every event p is the apex of a McGucken Sphere Σ_+(p) of radius R = ct expanding at c; the area law on that Sphere is Theorem 3.5, its holographic property is Lemma 7.4.4, the Unruh temperature on an accelerated worldline is Theorem 4.6, the entropy step per Compton wavelength is Theorem 8.1, and the one-way tendency dS/dt > 0 is Theorem 3.3, from the +ic orientation. Verlinde's screen, bits, temperature, entropy step, and tendency are these five theorems taken as five assumptions, and the single quantity his construction omits is the one the Principle makes primary: the rate dR/dt = c at which the screen expands, which carries the direction of time.

8.0ter.1 What the identification asserts, in his words. Verlinde [9, §2]: "An entropic force is an effective macroscopic force that originates in a system with many degrees of freedom by the statistical tendency to increase its entropy. The force equation is expressed in terms of entropy differences, and is independent of the details of the microscopic dynamics. In particular, there is no fundamental field associated with an entropic force"; "The statistical tendency to return to a maximal entropy state translates into a macroscopic force." On what it means, [9, §6.1]: "We identified a cause, a mechanism, for gravity. It is driven by differences in entropy, in whatever way defined, and a consequence of the statistical averaged random dynamics at the microscopic level"; "It is time we not only notice the analogy, and talk about the similarity, but finally do away with gravity as a fundamental force"; "If gravity is emergent, so is space time geometry. Einstein tied these two concepts together, and both have to be given up if we want to understand one or the other at a more fundamental level." The phrase "Entropy = Gravity" is the title of the 2025 interview [12], supplied by the interviewer; it does not occur in [9].

Lemma 8.0ter.1 (The identification in [9] is a consequence relation, with gravity on one side and entropy differences on the other). In [9] gravity is derived from entropy differences through F Δx = T ΔS (his Eq. (3.7)); no equation of [9] equates a gravitational quantity to an entropy.

Proof. Eq. (3.7) has a force on the left and an entropy difference on the right, related by a temperature. Eq. (3.13), F = GMm/R², is obtained from (3.7) by eliminating T and ΔS through (3.6), (3.10)–(3.12) and A = 4πR²; in the result no entropy appears. Eq. (5.33), M = 1/2∫_𝒮T dN, relates mass to temperature and bit count. The entropy S of the screen is defined (Eq. (3.10) with N = A c³/Għ) and the Newton potential "keeps track of the depletion of the entropy per bit" (§3.4); in each case entropy is the quantity from which a gravitational quantity is computed. His own summary, "driven by differences in entropy … and a consequence of the statistical averaged random dynamics," names the relation as cause and consequence. □

Reading under the Principle. The two quantities Verlinde relates by cause and consequence are two readings of one McGucken Entropy S = k_BlnΩ (Theorem 6.1): the area count is reading (4) and the field equation is its horizon reading through the Clausius relation derived in Theorem 4.7 Step 4, which is Verlinde's (3.7) with T from Theorem 4.6 and ΔS from Theorem 8.1 (§8.0 item 2). The field reading in the Algebraic Channel (Theorem 4.1) and the entropic reading in the Geometric Channel (Theorem 4.7) are both kept (Corollary 5.2), so "do away with gravity as a fundamental force" is replaced by common descent: gravity and entropy are theorems of the expansion of the McGucken Sphere, with neither the cause of the other (Corollary 5.3). Geometry is kept as the square of the rate (§2.1).

8.0ter.2 Where the direction of time leaves the construction.

Lemma 8.0ter.2 (Every relation of [9] §3 holds at a single instant). The equations from which Verlinde derives Newton's second law F = ma and Newton's law of gravitation F = GMm/R² — his (3.6), (3.7), (3.8), (3.10), (3.11), (3.12) — contain no time derivative and no sign of dt; the only one-way element of the construction, the "statistical tendency to increase its entropy," is an assumption imported from statistical mechanics; and the construction assigns no orientation to any coordinate, because spacetime as a whole is placed downstream of the thermodynamics.

Proof. (i) Eq. (3.6), ΔS = 2πk_B (mc/ħ) Δx: the increment is in x, perpendicular to the screen, at one instant; Verlinde's gloss is "there is an entropy change perpendicular to the screen proportional to the mass m and the displacement Δx. That is all there is to it" [9, §3.3]. (ii) Eq. (3.7), F Δx = T ΔS: a virtual-work relation between two increments taken at the same instant. (iii) Eq. (3.8), k_BT = ħa/2πc: the acceleration a is a second derivative, even under t →-t (Lemma 5.1bis.1(i)). (iv) Eq. (3.10), N = Ac³/Għ: A is the area of a closed 2-surface at one instant. (v) Eq. (3.11), E = 1/2 N k_BT: the equipartition rule of equilibrium statistical mechanics, which holds when nothing changes in time. (vi) Eq. (3.12), E = Mc²: a rest energy. None of (i)–(vi) contains d/dt. (vii) The force equation "is independent of the details of the microscopic dynamics" [9, §2]: independence from the dynamics is independence from the time evolution, so the direction of that evolution cannot enter through the force equation. (viii) The tendency: "the statistical tendency to increase its entropy" [9, §2] is stated and used; no equation of [9] derives it. (ix) Orientation: "If gravity is emergent, so is space time geometry" [9, §6.1]; the "one special direction" of §3 is "a coarse graining variable of the microscopic theory," a direction of emergence of space, with no orientation in time assigned to it. □

Verlinde's own word for the resulting process, from the 2022 keynote in reply to a questioner on the polymer example ([165], 41:13–41:50, verified-read, quoted in full in §8 (H4)): "the force is actually making sure that the entropy does not change, but the consequence of the force is the tendency to change the entropy. So this is a reversible system." The reversibility he asserts is that of the adiabatic process: the entropic force is the gradient of an entropy potential, conservative, with the process run slowly enough that the entropy of the system is held fixed. The tendency that would make the process one-way is, again, named as a consequence and supplied by statistics.

Proposition 8.0ter.3 (The standing of the force in [9]; a consequence of his premises, stated here and not in [9]). In [9] the entropic force has the standing of Boltzmann's H-theorem: it holds with overwhelming probability and is excluded by no theorem of the construction from reversing. On a fluctuation of the screen entropy toward a lower value, ∂S/∂x changes sign and with it F = T ∂S/∂x, with the probability of a Loschmidt fluctuation.

Proof. By Lemma 8.0ter.2(viii) the tendency is statistical and imported. A statistical tendency to increase entropy is the H-theorem's conclusion, and Loschmidt's objection (§6.2, [74, 75]) applies to it: the time-symmetric microdynamics produces entropy-decreasing trajectories with the same measure as the time-reverses of the entropy-increasing ones. The force equation (3.7) is linear in ΔS, so on a trajectory along which the screen entropy decreases across Δx the force reverses. No equation of [9] excludes such a trajectory; the construction is "independent of the details of the microscopic dynamics" and so cannot contain the exclusion. Verlinde does not state this consequence; its derivation here uses only his stated premises. □

Reading under the Principle. The Second Law of the Principle is strict, dS/dt > 0 (Theorem 3.3), because the Compton-tick walk is propagated forward by the sign of +ic and the reversed walk is the -ic process, which is forbidden (Theorem 19.5.1(iii) of [3], §5.1); Loschmidt's objection is resolved by the two channels (§6.2, Theorem 12 of [3]). Attraction is stated on the forward McGucken Sphere (Theorem 5.1bis.2), and the reversed statement has no carrier. So the fluctuation of Proposition 8.0ter.3 has no realization in the Principle: the entropy count on a McGucken Sphere is monotone in t and the force toward the mass that sources the stretching of h_ij does not reverse (Corollary 5.1bis.3). The direction of time enters at the first step, as the sign of the rate, and is read by every later theorem; in [9] it enters nowhere and is borrowed once.

8.0ter.3 Why the construction requires a holographic screen.

Theorem 8.0ter.4 (The screen is the premise of every step of Newton's law of gravitation in [9]). Verlinde derives two laws of Newton. Newton's second law, F = ma (3.9), is derived in his §3.1 from the entropy step (3.6), the virtual-work relation (3.7), and the Unruh temperature (3.8). Newton's law of gravitation, F = GMm/R² (3.13), is derived in his §3.2 from exactly the equations (3.6), (3.7), (3.10), (3.11), (3.12) and A = 4πR², with the Unruh law set aside. Each of the five equations and the area formula presupposes a closed 2-surface, and with the surface removed no equation of [9] relates the test mass m to the source mass M.

Proof. Verlinde's chain, in his order [9, §3.2]: "Now suppose our boundary is not infinitely extended, but forms a closed surface. More specifically, let us assume it is a sphere. For the following it is best to forget about the Unruh law (3.8), since we don't need it. It only served as a further motivation for (3.6). The key statement is simply that we need to have a temperature in order to have a force." Then: "Assuming that the holographic principle holds, the maximal storage space, or total number of bits, is proportional to the area A," N = Ac³/Għ (3.10); "Let us now just make the simple assumption that the energy is divided evenly over the bits N. The temperature is then determined by the equipartition rule" E = 1/2 Nk_BT (3.11); "After this we need only one more equation:" E = Mc² (3.12), "Here M represents the mass that would emerge in the part of space enclosed by the screen"; "The rest is straightforward: one eliminates E and inserts the expression for the number of bits to determine T. Next one uses the postulate (3.6) for the change of entropy to determine the force. Finally one inserts A = 4πR² and one obtains the familiar law: F = GMm/R²" (3.13).

The computation: from (3.11), (3.12), (3.10), T = 2E/Nk_B = 2Mc² Għ/(Ac³k_B) = 2GMħ/(Ac k_B); from (3.7) and (3.6), F = T ΔS/Δx = T·2πk_B mc/ħ = 4πGMm/A; with A = 4πR², F = GMm/R².

The role of the surface in each line. (a) Eq. (3.6) defines ΔS as the entropy change "near the screen" for a displacement perpendicular to it (Bekenstein's lowering of a mass toward a horizon); a gas has an entropy and no entropy gradient along a particle's path, so without a surface there is no ΔS to take and (3.7) has no right-hand side. (b) Eq. (3.10) defines N as proportional to an area, which requires a 2-surface, and Verlinde's "the only assumption made here is that the number of bits is proportional to the area. Nothing more" places the whole microscopic description of the construction on that surface. (c) Eq. (3.11) distributes the energy over the N bits of (3.10); without N there is no T. (d) Eq. (3.12) is the energy "enclosed by the screen"; the source mass M enters the construction only as what the surface encloses. (e) A = 4πR² requires the surface to be a sphere of radius R, which is where R — the distance in the law of gravitation — enters. Deleting the surface deletes ΔS, N, T, the enclosure that introduces M, and the radius R; what remains is a particle of mass m and a mass M with no equation between them. Holography is thus the premise that the microscopic degrees of freedom live on 2-surfaces at one bit per ℓ_P², and in [9] it is assumed: "Holography is also an hypothesis, of course, and may appear just as absurd as an action at a distance" [9, §6.4]. □

Theorem 8.0ter.5 (Verlinde's screen is the McGucken Sphere read at one instant, with its expansion removed). Each of the six inputs of Theorem 8.0ter.4, and the imported tendency of Lemma 8.0ter.2(viii), is a theorem of the McGucken Sphere; the single quantity of the Sphere absent from the screen is its rate of expansion dR/dt = c.

Proof. (i) The surface and its radius. Σ_+(p) is "the 2-sphere swept out by x₄'s spherically symmetric expansion at radius R = ct from O," with "area A = 4πR² = 4πc²t²" (Theorem 3.5, proof, verbatim from [6]); Verlinde's "let us assume it is a sphere" and A = 4πR² are this surface at the instant t = R/c. (ii) Bits proportional to area, (3.10). Theorem 3.5: one mode of the advance per cell of area ℓ_P², S = k_BA/4ℓ_P², so N = A/ℓ_P² = Ac³/Għ is the cell count of the Sphere (§8.0 item 6). (iii) The holographic principle. Lemma 7.4.4 (Theorem 21 of [3]): "the physics of the bulk region enclosed by a McGucken Sphere at time t + dt is fully determined by source data on the 2-dimensional surface of the McGucken Sphere at time t"; Verlinde's hypothesis is this theorem with dt deleted. (iv) The entropy step, (3.6). Theorem 8.1: (mc/ħ)Δx is the Compton phase of the particle's advance across Δx, so ΔS = 2πk_B Δϕ_C, with ħ the action per Compton cycle fixed by the Principle (§8.0 item 4). (v) The temperature, (3.8) and the T of (3.11). Theorem 4.6 derives T = ħa/2πck_B as the Euclidean period of the x₄-advance on the accelerated worldline, and the equipartition identity 1/2Nk_BT = Mc² is derived among the quantities of (ii), (v), and the law of gravitation a = GM/R² (§8.0 item 6). (vi) The enclosed mass, (3.12). The Sphere's volume defines the nonlocality (Lemma 7.4.5): the bodies inside Σ_+(p) share one state on it, and their energy is the Compton-tick energy crossed by its generators (Theorem 4.7 Step 3), which is the M "enclosed by the screen." (vii) The tendency. Theorem 3.3, dS/dt > 0 from +ic. Every input is now a theorem of the Sphere at the instant t; the Sphere's one further property, that R increases at c, appears in none of (3.6)–(3.12), and it is the property whose sign is the arrow of time (Lemma 8.0ter.2, Proposition 8.0ter.3). □

Reading under the Principle. The screen is needed in [9] because the construction has no event from which a surface is generated; the surface must be posited, together with everything on it. Under the Principle the surface is generated: every event emits a McGucken Sphere, the Sphere carries the count, the count has the area law, and the Sphere's advance at c supplies the tendency, the temperature's period, and the direction of time. Verlinde's "mechanism for gravity to emerge" through "direct 'contact' interactions … since all bodies inside a volume can be mapped on the same holographic screen" [9, §6.4] is the nonlocality of the Sphere's volume (Lemma 7.4.5, §8.0 item 13), with the mechanism Hooke demanded and Newton lacked supplied as the expansion of the McGucken Sphere at c from every event.

Closing attribution. What the identification asserts: Lemma 8.0ter.1 on [9] §§2, 3, 5, 6.1; the two-readings resolution is Theorem 6.1 with Corollaries 5.2–5.3 and Theorem 4.7 Step 4. Absence of the arrow: Lemma 8.0ter.2 on his (3.6)–(3.12) and [165]; the Principle's strict Second Law is Theorem 3.3 with Theorem 19.5.1(iii) of [3], and one-way attraction is Theorem 5.1bis.2 with Corollary 5.1bis.3. Standing of the force: Proposition 8.0ter.3, derived here from his premises, resolved by §6.2. Necessity of the screen: Theorem 8.0ter.4 on [9] §3.2. Screen as McGucken Sphere at one instant: Theorem 8.0ter.5 through Theorem 3.5, Lemma 7.4.4, Theorem 8.1, Theorem 4.6, Lemma 7.4.5, Theorem 4.7 Step 3, Theorem 3.3.

8.0quater The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Reading of whether Verlinde's text does what it states: the claim, the inputs, the coefficient, the absent state count, and the published tests

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality. This subsection compares the claim Verlinde states for [9] with what the equations of [9] do, using only his text (verified-read, full text) and the criticisms already quoted in §10bis.4. The comparison has four parts: the inputs from which Newton's laws are recovered; the numerical coefficient; the state count that an entropic force requires and that [9] does not supply; and the published tests. Each part closes with the theorem of the Principle that supplies the missing item.

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic derives the area count (Theorem 3.5), the Compton entropy step (Theorem 8.1), the Unruh temperature (Theorem 4.6), the one-way tendency (Theorem 3.3), and the field equations (Theorems 4.1, 4.7) from the expansion of the McGucken Sphere, with G matched once to Newton's law of gravitation in the weak-field limit (Theorem 4.1 Step 6) and ħ fixed as the action per Compton cycle (§2.3). The state count whose gradient an entropic force requires is Ω, the number of Compton-tick states on the McGucken Sphere (Theorem 6.1, §6.1), and the Principle predicts that the quantities Verlinde assumes are theorems and that the quantity he leaves undefined is defined.

The claim, verbatim. [9, §6.1]: "We identified a cause, a mechanism, for gravity. It is driven by differences in entropy, in whatever way defined, and a consequence of the statistical averaged random dynamics at the microscopic level." [9, §3.2]: "We have recovered Newton's law of gravitation, practically from first principles!" The title: "On the Origin of Gravity and the Laws of Newton."

Lemma 8.0quater.1 (The inputs of [9] §3 are results of the theory being derived, by Verlinde's own statement). The entropy step (3.5) is Bekenstein's black-hole result; the bit count (3.10) introduces G by definition; and Verlinde states that the arguments have been run in reverse.

Proof. (i) Eq. (3.5) is introduced as "Motivated by Bekenstein's argument, let us postulate that the change of entropy associated with the information on the boundary equals ΔS = 2πk_B when Δx = ħ/mc" [9, §3.1]. Bekenstein's argument concerns the entropy increase of a black hole when a particle of mass m is lowered to within one Compton wavelength of its horizon; the horizon, its area, and the relation of area to mass are results of general relativity. (ii) Eq. (3.10), N = Ac³/Għ: "where we introduced a new constant G. Eventually this constant is going to be identified with Newton's constant, of course. But since we have not assumed anything yet about the existence a gravitational force, one can simply regard this equation as the definition of G" [9, §3.2]. The constant that appears in the derived law is placed in the input by definition. (iii) Verlinde's own statement of the direction of the argument, two sentences after the claim of first principles: "It had to work, partly for dimensional reasons, and also because the laws of Newton have been ingredients in the steps that lead to black hole thermodynamics and the holographic principle. In a sense we have reversed these arguments" [9, §3.2]. □

Reading under the Principle. The reversal is removed because the inputs are derived without Newton's laws (§8.0 item 7): the area law is the Planck-cell count of the McGucken Sphere (Theorem 3.5), the entropy step is the Compton phase of the advance (Theorem 8.1), and G enters once, as the matching constant of the weak-field limit (Theorem 4.1 Step 6, Corollary 4.8), after the field equations have been derived.

Lemma 8.0quater.2 (The form of the law of gravitation is fixed by the chain, and its coefficient equals one because three borrowed conventions multiply to one). In the chain (3.6), (3.7), (3.10)–(3.12), A = 4πR², the constants ħ and c cancel identically, the dependence F ∝GMm/A is fixed by the chain's form, and the coefficient is (2π)·2/(4π) = 1, where 2π is Bekenstein's constant in (3.6), 2 is the reciprocal of the equipartition 1/2 in (3.11), and 4π is the area of the unit sphere.

Proof. From (3.11) and (3.12), T = 2Mc²/(Nk_B); from (3.10), T = 2Mc² Għ/(Ac³k_B) = 2GMħ/(Ac k_B). From (3.7) and (3.6), F = T ΔS/Δx = T·2πk_B mc/ħ. Substituting, F = (2GMħ/Ac k_B)(2πk_B mc/ħ) = 4πGMm/A: ħ cancels between the entropy step and the bit count, c cancels between the rest energy and the bit count, k_B cancels between the entropy step and the temperature. The exponents of G, M, m, and A are each fixed by the chain's form: G and M enter once through T, m once through ΔS, A once through N. With A = 4πR², F = GMm/R², and the coefficient is 2π·2/4π = 1. Verlinde's "partly for dimensional reasons" is this cancellation; the coefficient is the product of Bekenstein's 2π, the equipartition 1/2, and the sphere's 4π, each taken from outside the construction. □

Reading under the Principle. The same three numbers are derived: the 2π is one full cycle of Compton phase per tick of length λ_C = h/mc, with ħ/mc one radian of it (Theorem 8.1, §8.0 item 4); the 1/2 Nk_BT = Mc² identity is derived among the quantities of Theorem 3.5, Theorem 4.6, and the law of gravitation (§8.0 item 6); and 4πR² is the area of the McGucken Sphere at R = ct (Theorem 3.5, proof).

Lemma 8.0quater.3 (No state count is supplied for gravity in [9]). Verlinde defines an entropic force through a configuration count, S(E,x) = k_BlogΩ(E,x) with F/T = ∂S/∂x (his Eqs. (2.1), (2.3)), and computes Ω for the polymer; for gravity he supplies no Ω, no microscopic state space, and no dynamics on it.

Proof. [9, §2], the polymer: "S(E,x) = k_BlogΩ(E,x)" (2.1), where "Ω(E,x) denotes the volume of the configuration space for the entire system," "Each of these configurations has the same energy," and "There are many more such configurations when the molecule is short compared to when it is stretched"; the force is "F/T = ∂S/∂x" (2.3), and "An entropic force is recognized by the facts that it points in the direction of increasing entropy." The mechanism of the polymer's force is therefore the count Ω(E,x) of configurations at fixed energy, which is computable and whose x-dependence is the source of the force. For gravity, [9] §§3–5 contain no state space, no Ω, and no computation of S from a count; the screen entropy is assigned by postulate (3.5)–(3.6) and by N = Ac³/Għ; and the summary is "driven by differences in entropy, in whatever way defined" [9, §6.1]. The "statistical averaged random dynamics at the microscopic level" is named and no equation of motion on any microscopic space is written. The item that makes the polymer example a mechanism is absent from the gravitational case. □

Reading under the Principle. The count is supplied. Ω is the number of Compton-tick states of the McGucken Sphere (Theorem 6.1; the five readings of §6.1), the microscopic dynamics is the isotropic Compton-tick displacement with the SO(3)-invariant measure (Theorem 3.2), the one-way tendency is derived from it (Theorem 3.3), and the horizon-area reading of the same count gives the field equations (Theorem 4.7). The gradient whose existence Verlinde postulates is the gradient of a count that is written down (§8.0 item 10).

Lemma 8.0quater.4 (The items Verlinde lists as open are the items a mechanism would have to supply). [9] names as open: equipartition, the role of ħ, the Bekenstein bound, the predictions, and the Einstein equations beyond a sketch.

Proof. Equipartition: "Perhaps the least obvious assumption is equipartition, which in general holds only for free systems" [9, §3.3]. ħ: "This brings us to a somewhat subtle and not yet fully understood aspect. Namely, the role of ħ" [9, §6.4]. Bekenstein bound: the screen entropy "appears to be very high, and violates the Bekenstein bound," with the proposed repair "the freedom to rescale the value of ħ" [9, §6.4]. Predictions: "But clearly, we need a better understanding of the theory to turn this in to a prediction" [9, §6.4]. Einstein equations: "The key question at this point is whether the equation (5.34) is sufficient to derive the full Einstein equations"; "We will present a sketch of this" [9, §5.2]. Each item is a property of the microscopic theory — the energy distribution over the states, the quantum of action, the state-count bound, the fluctuations, the full dynamics — and the microscopic theory is the item Lemma 8.0quater.3 finds absent. □

Reading under the Principle. Each is derived in §8.0: equipartition as an identity among derived quantities (item 6), ħ as the action per Compton cycle with no rescaling freedom (item 11), the Bekenstein tension as capacity against occupation on the McGucken Sphere (item 11), the fluctuation scale D = h/6m and the residual D_x^(McG) (item 12), and the Einstein equations in full along both channels (item 9, Theorems 4.1 and 4.7).

The published tests. The criticisms are quoted in full in §10bis.4; the record is in §8.3. Kobakhidze [39] (verified-read, abstract): "We argue that neutron interference experiments and experiments on gravitational bound states of neutron unambiguously disprove entropic origin of gravitation"; body: "Thus, Verlinde's theory implies practically complete decoherence of neutron waves." Visser [171] (verified-read, abstract): the conservative character of Newtonian gravity "places significant constraints on the form of the entropy and temperature functions. … The constraints I will establish are sufficient to present real and significant problems for any reasonable variant of Verlinde's entropic gravity proposal." The 2017 dark-sector extension [101] has been tested against weak lensing [42] and galaxy and cluster data [41, 43], with the results described in §8.3.

Reading under the Principle. The neutron carries a coherent phase because the force is the geodesic motion in h_ij derived in the Algebraic Channel (Theorem 4.1, Corollary 7.4 of [19]) and the matter wave is the Compton phase of the same advance (Theorem 8.1), so no thermal noise is imposed beyond the bounded residual of §6.3 (§8.3, §10bis.4(a)); the force is conservative because it is the field equation's weak-field limit, and the entropy function Visser constrains is the derived count of Theorem 6.1 (§10bis.4).

What the text establishes. Lemmas 8.0quater.1–4 locate what [9] does: it rewrites Newton's second law and Newton's law of gravitation in thermodynamic variables — entropy step, bit count, temperature — whose definitions were extracted from black-hole thermodynamics and from Newton's constant, and it shows the rewriting is consistent, with the coefficient fixed by three borrowed conventions. Jacobson [7] had shown in 1995 that the Einstein equation is consistent with the same rewriting at the level of the field equations (§7). The claim of a mechanism and of first principles exceeds this: a mechanism for an entropic force is, by Verlinde's own definition (2.1), a configuration count whose gradient is the force, and none is given for gravity. The Principle supplies the count, the surface on which it lives, the temperature, the step, the tendency, and the direction of time, each as a theorem of the expansion of the McGucken Sphere at c from every event (Theorem 8.0ter.5), and the consistency Verlinde demonstrates becomes the statement that the Geometric-Channel reading of one law agrees with its Algebraic-Channel reading (Corollary 5.2).

Closing attribution. The claim: [9] §§3.2, 6.1. Inputs as borrowed results: Lemma 8.0quater.1, resolved by Theorem 3.5, Theorem 8.1, Theorem 4.1 Step 6. Coefficient: Lemma 8.0quater.2, the three numbers derived in Theorem 8.1, §8.0 item 6, Theorem 3.5. Absent state count: Lemma 8.0quater.3, supplied by Theorem 6.1, Theorem 3.2, Theorem 3.3, Theorem 4.7. Open items: Lemma 8.0quater.4, resolved in §8.0 items 6, 9, 11, 12. Tests: [39], [171], [41]–[43], §8.3 and §10bis.4, resolved by Theorem 4.1, Corollary 7.4 of [19], Theorem 8.1, §6.3. Jacobson's prior consistency result: [7], §7.

8.1 Verlinde's entropy step is the Compton phase of the advance

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic predicts that the elementary entropy increment of any holographic-screen construction is set by the Compton phase accumulated by a particle's advance, because the advance is what carries the particle's action h per cycle.

Verlinde's postulate — "the basic assumption from which everything else follows" [9, §3.3] — is quoted in full in §8.0 item (4): the entropy of a holographic screen changes by ΔS = 2πk_B when a particle of mass m is displaced by Δx = ħ/mc, i.e. ΔS = 2πk_B (mc/ħ) Δx, linear in the displacement, with ħ "an auxiliary variable that is needed for dimensional reasons" that "can therefore be chosen at will" [9, §3.3].

Theorem 8.1 (The Verlinde step as a theorem of the Compton phase). The quantity (mc/ħ)Δx is the Compton phase Δϕ_C accumulated by the particle's x₄-advance across the displacement, and Verlinde's postulate reads ΔS = 2πk_B Δϕ_C. Under dx₄/dt = ic the phase accumulates at ω_C = mc²/ħ (Theorem 3.1), one full cycle of 2π per Compton tick of length λ_C = h/mc carrying the action h (§2.3); the displacement unit ħ/mc = λ_C/2π is one radian of that cycle. The entropy increment per unit displacement is therefore fixed by the Compton coupling, and ħ is the action per Compton cycle.

Proof. The rest-frame phase of a massive particle is ϕ = ω_Ct = mc²t/ħ (Theorem 3.1). Along a spatial displacement Δx traversed in the time the advance takes to cover it at c, Δt = Δx/c, the phase increment is Δϕ_C = mc Δx/ħ. Hence (mc/ħ)Δx = Δϕ_C, and Δx = ħ/mc corresponds to Δϕ_C = 1 radian; a full tick λ_C = 2πħ/mc corresponds to 2π radians and carries ΔS_action = h (§2.3). Verlinde's linear relation is the statement that the screen's entropy is proportional to the Compton phase, with proportionality constant 2πk_B per radian; the phase itself, its rate, and the constant ħ setting it are supplied by the Principle, and the constant 2πk_B per radian is computed in Corollary 10.2(ii) from the modular Hamiltonian of the McGucken Sphere-cogenerated wedge. □

The remaining inputs of the construction — holographic screens, equipartition of energy over N = Ac³/Għ bits, the Unruh temperature — are respectively the McGucken Sphere's causal boundaries (§2.2, §11), the Planck-area tiling of Theorem 3.5, and Theorem 4.6. Verlinde's entropy is S = k_BlogΩ with Ω the configuration count on the screen; it is the same count as §6 read on the same kind of surface.
