8.2 Verlinde's stated open items, each resolved

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic predicts that an entropic-force programme will require (i) a derivation of spacetime, (ii) a derivation of inertia, (iii) a microscopic theory it cannot name, (iv) an account of entanglement as the connectivity of space, (v) a formulation without a boundary, and (vi) an answer to why thermodynamics yields dissipation while gravity yields structure. Verlinde states each of these in his 2025 interview [12]; the one verbatim phrase from that source used in this paper is "something more fundamental, more microscopic." The items are given at the level of their criterion.

(i) Deriving spacetime and inertia, beyond Jacobson. Criterion: assuming spacetime assumes its geometry; a derivation of the Einstein equations does not say how inertia works. Resolution: the metric is the theorem of §2.1; inertial mass is the magnitude of the fourth-momentum at spatial rest, m = |P₄|/c, from which the mass shell, E₀ = mc², Newton's first and second laws in full relativistic generality, and the weak, Einstein, and strong equivalence principles are derived (Theorem 12.1 of [19]).

(ii) The unnamed microscopic theory. Criterion: the laws are emergent from something more microscopic that may remain unknown. Resolution: the expanding McGucken Sphere with its Compton-tick states is that theory (§2, §6).

(iii) Entropy as counting what is unknown. Resolution: S = k_BlnΩ with Ω the physical count of Compton-tick states (§6), ontic (§3.2).

(iv) Spacetime stitched by entanglement. Resolution: nonlocality is created by the expansion of the McGucken Sphere itself — a local event becomes a nonlocal surface at c — and the entanglement that connects two regions is the intersection of their Spheres from a shared origin, the First McGucken Law of Nonlocality (Lemma 7.4.5; [20]); the same nonlocal surface, counted on the horizon, is the gravitational entropy, so the stitching and the emergence of gravity are one surface counted two ways (§11).

(v) The boundary that the universe lacks. Criterion: AdS/CFT and the screen construction require a boundary, and the real universe has none. Resolution: the McGucken Sphere expands from every event, so every event carries its own local horizon; the Principle applies at every point of the boundary-free, expanding universe (§2.2).

(vi) Dissipation from thermodynamics, structure from gravity. Criterion (posed in the interview by the interviewer): if gravity and thermodynamics are the same, why does one give the Second Law and the other the field equations? Resolution: Theorem 5.1 — the Geometric Channel read in full gives the dissipative, +ic-oriented Second Law; the same McGucken Sphere read at frozen slices gives the symmetric field equations; both readings exist for gravity, only the first for thermodynamics.

8.2bis The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Reading of Verlinde's claim that his entropic gravity transcends Jacobson's

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic states what spacetime is before any area, screen, or horizon is named: the metric is the squared rate of the McGucken Sphere's expansion (§2.1), its wavelength is the action (§2.3), and mass is the Compton coupling to the advance (Theorem 3.1). Verlinde's charge against Jacobson is that Jacobson assumes spacetime; the Principle's reading is that the charge is correct, that Verlinde's own construction assumes the same spacetime, and that dx₄/dt = ic is the statement both are missing.

Verlinde's claim, verbatim (interview with Curt Jaimungal [12], transcript verified-read). On Jacobson: "what Jacobson showed is that if you assume that the entanglement entropy, this quantity that we've been talking about, is equal to the area of some horizon surface, then you can derive the Einstein equations." On the circularity: "Jacobson basically already assumed spacetime. He assumed that there is an area. He said there is an entanglement entropy that goes like the area. Let's write down the first law, and then it becomes Einstein's equations. But I think there's something circular about the reasoning, because assuming spacetime also is assuming its geometry. You cannot derive its geometry from something there." On inertia: "In a certain way, what Jacobson does, he derives the third law. Because if you derive Einstein's equations, you also derive Newton's third law. But you don't tell me how inertia arises. Inertia is a much more fundamental concept that basically tells you what mass means. When we move something, why do we apply a force, need to apply a force, to accelerate it? So F equals ma, that's the law that I derived." On the ordering: "we're eventually not deriving only Einstein's equations. We need to derive first what space and time are." On the claim itself: "So there's some way that my paper transcends his equations, his results. And I think it also contains it in some form." On the area assumption as assumption: "if we assume that entanglement goes like the area, we can derive the Einstein equations. But this is an assumption, and you may wonder whether that assumption is always true. And I think that there are situations where that might not be true." On equilibrium: "they are in equilibrium at horizons of black holes. They are at equilibrium at the horizon of a cosmological horizon. They're not in equilibrium in some arbitrary point of spacetime." On the real universe: "in a universe where there is dark energy, which is more like our own universe, that there can be deviations from it."

The criteria stated. (a) A derivation of gravity that begins from an area, a horizon, and S ∝A has assumed spacetime and its geometry. (b) A derivation of the Einstein equations is a derivation of the force law; inertia, F = ma, is prior to it and must be derived separately. (c) Space and time must be derived before the gravitational law. (d) S_ent ∝A is an assumption that may fail, in particular in a universe with dark energy.

The McGucken Principle reading, point by point.

(a) The charge against Jacobson is correct, and it applies to Verlinde. Jacobson's 1995 letter takes a spacetime point, a local Rindler horizon through it, an area element, and S = ηA as its inputs; Jacobson says so, and §7.0 quotes him. Verlinde's 2011 §3.1 takes a holographic screen — a surface of area A in a space — a bit count N = Ac³/Għ on it, the equipartition E = 1/2Nk_BT, and the Unruh temperature k_BT = ħa/2πc of a worldline accelerating in that space (§8.0 items (1)–(5), each quoted). A screen with an area and a worldline with an acceleration are spacetime with its geometry. The arena Verlinde substitutes for Jacobson's — a time-like screen for a null Rindler wedge — is a different surface in the same assumed spacetime; Theorem 19.4.4 of [3] (reproduced in §8) records Verlinde's own statement for the Einstein equations: "By adapting his reasoning to this situation, and combining it with Wald's exposition of the Komar mass, it is straightforward to construct an argument that naturally leads to the Einstein equations."

(b) What the inertia derivation contains. Verlinde's F = ma follows from three inputs: ΔS = 2πk_B(mc/ħ)Δx, k_BT = ħa/2πc, and FΔx = TΔS. The second input is the Unruh relation, in which a is the proper acceleration of a worldline in Minkowski space; substituting it gives F = ma because a was supplied. Newton's first law is the statement that inertial frames exist; the Unruh formula is written in those frames. The derivation is therefore a derivation of the coefficient m in F = ma — the identification of the inertial mass with the Compton coupling mc/ħ of the entropy step — and that identification is Verlinde's own result, which Theorem 19.4.4 of [3] credits: "This is an additional output beyond Jacobson's Einstein equations, and Verlinde's derivation of it is his genuine additive novelty." It is not a derivation of inertia from something prior to spacetime. In the Principle the three inputs are theorems: ΔS = 2πk_B(mc/ħ)Δx is Corollary 10.2(ii), the Bisognano–Wichmann modular Hamiltonian evaluated per Compton wavelength; the Unruh temperature is Theorem 4.6, the Euclidean period of the x₄-boost; and the entropic-force identity is the first law on the McGucken Sphere-cogenerated wedge, Corollary 10.2(i). Inertial mass is the Compton coupling rate ω_C = mc²/ħ to the advance (Theorem 3.1), the magnitude of the fourth-momentum at spatial rest, m = |P₄|/c, from which Newton's first and second laws follow (Theorem 12.1 of [19], cited in §8.2(i)); the equality of inertial and gravitational mass is the two channels reading one x₄ budget (Theorem 19.4.5(iii) of [3], §6ter).

(c) "We need to derive first what space and time are." This is the ordering the Principle has: dx₄/dt = ic is a statement about what the fourth dimension does, the Minkowski interval is its squared rate (§2.1), the Hilbert space is cogenerated with it (Appendix E, [6]), and the Einstein equations come after, by either channel (Theorem 4.1, Theorem 4.7). Verlinde's construction does not have this ordering; it begins at the screen. Verlinde's own "I think it also contains it in some form" is read here at the level Theorem 19.4.4 of [3] gives it: Verlinde 2011 is Jacobson 1995 with a substituted arena and one additional derived relationship, resting on the same three depths (universalization of the horizon, heat as boost energy, Raychaudhuri or Wald closure) and the same undelivered inputs.

(d) Whether S ∝A can fail. In the Principle S = k_BA/4ℓ_P² on a horizon is Theorem 3.5, with ℓ_P the McGucken Sphere's wavelength at the horizon tier, and S_ent equals that count by Theorem 6.1 (readings (3) and (4) of one measure) and Proposition 10.3 (species independence, with the physical G). The area law is a theorem on every horizon, including the cosmological horizon of the de Sitter McGucken Sphere (§8.0bis item (1), §12). Verlinde's remark that equilibrium holds "at horizons" and "not in equilibrium in some arbitrary point of spacetime" is the KMS condition of Theorem 10.1 on the wedge algebra, which holds for the Rindler wedge at every event because every event launches a McGucken Sphere whose null cone is the local horizon (§7.0); the equilibrium is local, as Jacobson required and as Verlinde allows. The deviations Verlinde expects in a dark-energy universe are, in the Principle, the dark-sector terms of Theorem 12.1 — a₀ = cH₀/2π and w(z) = -1 + Ω_m(z)/6π — which are consequences of the cosmological McGucken Sphere's area law, so the law is kept and the deviation Verlinde anticipates is derived from it with its constant fixed.

Closing attribution. Verlinde is correct that Jacobson assumes spacetime, correct that inertia is prior to the field equations, and correct that space and time must be derived first; his own construction assumes the same spacetime through the screen and the Unruh relation, and derives the mass coefficient of F = ma, not inertia. The item each of his criteria asks for is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic: spacetime, §2.1; inertia, Theorem 3.1 with Theorem 12.1 of [19]; the ordering, §2 before §4; the area law, Theorem 3.5 with Theorem 6.1 and Proposition 10.3; the dark-energy deviation, Theorem 12.1.

8.3 The published falsifications of entropic gravity, and the McGucken dark sector with zero free parameters

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic treats gravity as the horizon-area reading of the McGucken Sphere's count, and so predicts that the specific failures of the entropic-force construction — non-conservativity, thermal noise on coherent states, boundary dependence, absence of cosmology — are absent.

The published record: the entropic force is not strictly conservative [39]; neutron interference and gravitationally bound ultracold-neutron states (qBounce) are inconsistent with an entropic, noisy origin of gravity [39]; the decoherence an entropic force would impose on coherent states exceeds what is observed, requiring special open-system models to evade [40]; and the programme is scope-limited to isolated spherically symmetric systems in a dark-energy-dominated background, with no lensing or CMB sector of its own and mixed cluster-scale results [41, 42, 43]. In the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework gravity derives the Einstein field equations (conservative, §4); unitary evolution is the frozen reading of the same McGucken Sphere, so coherent states carry no thermal noise (§6.3, with the residual D_x as the only, bounded, departure); no boundary is required (§8.2 (v)); and the cosmology is complete [27]. On the shared MOND phenomenology — both programmes obtain an acceleration scale from cH₀ with zero free dark-sector parameters, Verlinde's a_M = cH₀/6 [101, Eq. (7.43)] and the Principle's a₀ = cH₀/2π (Theorem 12.1(iii)), 4.7% apart (§8.0bis item 1) — the McGucken cosmology derives the baryonic Tully–Fisher slope of exactly 4 as the projection of x₄'s SO(3) expansion, fits the SPARC radial-acceleration relation at χ²/N = 0.46 against the McGaugh–Lelli MOND benchmark χ²/N = 1.46, and takes first place in twelve independent tests including w₀ = -0.983 from cumulative spatial contraction, within 1% of the DESI 2024 combined fit [27, §VI.5]. The reason is the invariance of x₄'s expansion at c against x₁,x₂,x₃: Verlinde's construction lives on a symmetric Lorentzian manifold taken as input, whereas the Principle derives that manifold and retains the asymmetry between the advancing x₄ and the stretchable spatial three, from which the twelve divergences enumerated in [27, §VI.5.3] follow. In the thermodynamic limit the two agree: Verlinde's entropic gravity is the macroscopic shadow of the Principle's microscopic mechanism, which is why they coincide on Newton's law, the Einstein equations, the Bekenstein–Hawking formula, and a₀ [27, §VI.5.1].

Closing attribution. The thirteen statements of the 2011 paper: §8.0, each derived. The seven statements of the 2017 paper: §8.0bis, each derived. The Verlinde step: Theorem 8.1. Spacetime and inertia: §2.1, §8.0 item (8), [19]. The microscopic theory: §2, §6. Entanglement and connectivity: Lemma 7.4.5, §11. Boundary-free formulation: §2.2. Dissipation versus structure: Theorem 5.1. Dark sector: [27].

9. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Reading of Padmanabhan's horizon thermodynamics and Bianconi's entropic action

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality. Padmanabhan's programme generalizes Jacobson's to every diffeomorphism-invariant theory and recasts it as an extremum principle over null vectors; Bianconi's treats the metric as a density matrix and derives gravity from a relative entropy. Padmanabhan's review [8] and his equipartition paper [44] are read in full in §§9.0–9.0bis, each quoted step followed by its derivation from the Principle; §9.1 collects the criterion-level items and the comparison table; §9.2 reads Bianconi. Each item each author states is read here as a theorem of the Principle.

9.0 The 2010 review read in full: each stated step derived from the Principle

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic states that from every event a McGucken Sphere expands at c, its wavelength setting the action h and its volume defining a nonlocality. Padmanabhan's review [8] (verified-read, full text, §§5.2, 6.1, 7.1, 7.2, 7.5, 7.6, 8) establishes that the field equations evaluated on any horizon are a thermodynamic identity, that local Rindler observers at every event constrain the geometry, that the field equations follow from extremizing an entropy functional over all null vectors with the metric held fixed, that the cosmological constant then enters as an integration constant, and that the microscopic theory behind all of this is open. Each step is quoted and derived below from the Sphere. Padmanabhan's units are ħ = c = k_B = 1, G = L_P², signature -+++; his 𝒢_ab is 1/(16πG)(R_ab - 1/2 R g_ab) in Einstein gravity, so that his 2𝒢_ab = T_ab is G_ab = 8πG T_ab.

(1) The identity on every horizon. Padmanabhan: "the equality — between field equations on the horizon and the thermodynamic identity — should have a more general validity. This has now been demonstrated for an impressively wide class of models like the cases of stationary axisymmetric horizons and evolving spherically symmetric horizons in Einstein gravity, static spherically symmetric horizons and dynamical apparent horizons in Lanczos-Lovelock gravity, generic, static horizon in Lanczos-Lovelock gravity, three dimensional BTZ black hole horizons, FRW cosmological models in various gravity theories and even in the case Horava-Lifshitz gravity" [8, §5.2]; and for a static horizon in Einstein's theory his Eq. (122), (κ)/(2π) ∂_λ(1/4√(σ))δλ- {…}δλ² = T_n̂n̂√(σ)δλ, read as T dS - dE = P dV.

Derivation from the Principle. The identity is Theorem 4.7 Step 4 evaluated on a horizon. Its three ingredients are each a theorem of the McGucken Sphere: the temperature κ/2π is Theorem 4.6 (the Wick-rotated x₄-boost of the accelerated observer), the entropy 1/4√(σ) per unit transverse coordinate area is Theorem 3.5 (one x₄-mode per Planck-area cell with the coefficient of Theorem 4.5), and the flux T_n̂n̂ is the Compton-tick action crossing the null cone (Theorem 4.7 Step 1, Theorem 3.1). The reason the identity holds on horizons of every kind in Padmanabhan's list — stationary, evolving, cosmological — is that every horizon is a null surface, every null surface is ruled by generators of McGucken Spheres, and the Clausius relation of Step 4 is stated per generator at each event with no reference to the global geometry. The Lanczos–Lovelock entries of his list are a mathematical family indexed by D; the Principle fixes D. The dimension is physical — three spatial directions and the one expanding x₄, D = 4 — and in D = 4 Lovelock's theorem makes the Einstein tensor the unique divergence-free symmetric second-order tensor (Theorem 4.1 Step 5), the Gauss–Bonnet term being topological. The Principle therefore predicts that of Padmanabhan's family only the Einstein member has a physical instance, and the horizon thermodynamics of the D > 4 members describes no spacetime of expanding Spheres. Padmanabhan reaches the same selection: "we are led to Lanczos-Lovelock model of gravity in general and to Einstein gravity (uniquely) in D = 4" [8, §7.6].

From [3], verbatim — Theorem 18, statement items 1–2 and Step A3 (de Sitter horizon entropy): (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list)

Theorem (FRW thermodynamics from McGucken Principle with empirical first-place ranking). In a Friedmann-Robertson-Walker (FRW) cosmology with scale factor a(t), the cosmological McGucken Sphere expansion forces the thermodynamic relations:

1. Cosmological entropy increase: the total entropy within the cosmological horizon increases monotonically: dS_cosmo/dt > 0.
2. de Sitter horizon entropy: in a de Sitter phase with Hubble parameter H, the horizon entropy is S_dS = k_B A_dS/(4ℓ_P²) where A_dS = 4π/H² is the de Sitter horizon area.

Step A3 (de Sitter horizon entropy from Theorems 15–16 of the present paper). In a de Sitter phase with Hubble parameter H constant, the de Sitter horizon at proper distance R_dS = c/H has entropy derived through the derivation of Theorems 15 and 16 of the present paper applied to the de Sitter Killing-time generator, with the Euclidean cigar period β_dS = 2π/H replacing the Schwarzschild β = 2π/κ but with identical Gibbons–Hawking–York boundary-action evaluation (Proposition V.1 of [24] adapted to the de Sitter geometry):

S_dS = k_B A_dS/4ℓ_P² = (πk_B c²)/(H² ℓ_P²).

This is the Gibbons–Hawking de Sitter entropy [99], derived from the Algebraic Channel as a corollary of the present paper's Theorems 15–16.

The FRW and de Sitter entries of Padmanabhan's list are therefore the cosmological-McGucken Sphere instance of the same two theorems (Theorems 15–16 of [3] are Theorems 3.5 and 4.5 of the present paper), with the de Sitter temperature T_dS = ħH/2πk_B as the cigar period β_dS = 2π/H and the horizon surface term computed in [100].

From [3], verbatim — the four-dimensions statement and the geometric forcing of x₄ (Father-Symmetry classification and the Disjunctive Forcing import): (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list)

- Lovelock 1971 in physics is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic. The uniqueness of the Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian in four spacetime dimensions is a McGucken theorem. The four-spacetime-dimensions content is forced by the Disjunctive Forcing Theorem of [27, §X.7]; the diffeomorphism-invariance content is forced by the moving-dimension geometry of [58]; the Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian as the unique diffeomorphism-invariant second-order scalar action is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic via [84, Proposition 45].

- Geometric forcing — sphere-surface x₄-locality. Every point on the future null cone Σ^+(p) of an event p has x₄(q; p) = 0. The three-spatial separation |𝐱 - 𝐱₀| = c(t - t₀) grows linearly in time; the x₄-separation stays at zero. The x₄-coordinate is the one that has been driven outward and reached every surface point simultaneously; the spatial dimensions are the slice on which the shadow of that advance is observed. The McGucken Sphere is not symmetric between x₄ and the spatial dimensions; if the spatial dimensions were also expanding at c isotropically, the structure of the Sphere as a record of x₄-advance through a stationary spatial slice would collapse.

(2) Local Rindler observers at every event. Padmanabhan: "At every event in spacetime, we will introduce uniformly accelerating local Rindler observers and use the horizon thermodynamics perceived by these Rindler observers to constrain the background geometry. We shall begin by making the notion of local Rindler observers and their coordinate system well defined. Let us choose any event 𝒫 and introduce a local inertial frame (LIF) around it with Riemann normal coordinates X^a = (T, 𝐗) such that 𝒫 has the coordinates X^a = 0 in the LIF. Let k^a be a future directed null vector at 𝒫 and we align the coordinates of LIF such that it lies in the X–T plane at 𝒫. We next transform from the LIF to a local Rindler frame (LRF) coordinates x^a by accelerating along the X-axis with an acceleration κ by the usual transformation" [8, §6.1].

Derivation from the Principle. The construction is read off the McGucken Sphere at 𝒫. The LIF exists and is Minkowskian because the metric at 𝒫 is the square of the rate, ds² = (dx₄)² + d𝐱² = -c²dt² + d𝐱² (§2.1), with dx₄/dt = ic the same in every inertial frame (Lemma 7.4.1). The future-directed null vector k^a is a generator of Σ_+(𝒫), and every direction on the Sphere's cross-section supplies one, which is why "at every event" and "for all null vectors" (item 4) are both available: the Sphere is spherically symmetric and expands in every spatial direction at once. The LRF is the accelerated observer's description of that generator as a horizon; the acceleration κ fixes the temperature of item 1 by Theorem 4.6. Padmanabhan introduces the observers as a device; the Principle supplies the object they observe — the Sphere's null cone at 𝒫 — and the rate c at which it is generated.

(3) The matter entropy functional. Padmanabhan: "if we can determine the form of entropy functional for gravity (S_grav) in terms of the normal to the null surface, then it seems natural to demand that the dynamics should follow from the extremum prescription δ[S_grav + S_matter] = 0 for all null surfaces in the spacetime where S_matter is the relevant matter entropy. … If T_ab is the matter energy-momentum tensor in a general D(≥4) dimensional spacetime then an expression for matter entropy relevant for our purpose can be taken to be

S_matt = ∫_𝒱 d^Dx √(-g) T_abn^an^b (202)

where n^a is a null vector field. From our Eq. (193) we see that the entropy density associated with proper 3-volume is β(T_abξ^aξ^b) dV_prop where — on the horizon — the vector ξ^a becomes proportional to a null vector n^a. If we now use the Rindler coordinates in Eq. (7) in which √(-g) = 1 and interpret the factor β as arising from an integration of dt in the range (0, β) we find that the entropy density associated with a proper four volume is (T_abn^an^b)" [8, §7.1].

Derivation from the Principle. T_abn^an^b is the integrand of Theorem 4.7 Step 1: the boost-energy flux of matter across the generator k^μ is δQ = ∫T_μνχ^μdΣ^ν with χ^μ = -aλk^μ the approximate boost Killing vector, so δQ = -∫T_μν(aλ)k^μk^νdλdA, and the Clausius relation of Step 4 converts it to entropy at the Unruh inverse temperature β = 2πc k_B/ħa of Theorem 4.6. Padmanabhan's "integration of dt in the range (0, β)" is the Euclidean period of the McGucken–Wick rotation (Theorem 4.5, §10): the thermal circle of the Rindler observer is the Compton-phase cycle of the x₄-boost, so the factor β multiplying the energy flux is the one period of the advance seen by that observer. In the Principle the energy crossing the McGucken Sphere is carried in Compton ticks, ħω_C = mc² per cycle (Theorem 3.1), and T_abn^an^b is the density of that action flux through the null cone; its integral over one Euclidean period is the increment of the horizon count Ω (§6).

(4) The gravitational entropy functional and the two conditions. Padmanabhan: "The simplest choice is to postulate S_grav to be a quadratic expression in the derivatives of the normal:

S_grav = -4∫_𝒱 d^Dx √(-g) P_ab^ cd ∇_cn^a ∇_dn^b (204)

where the explicit form of P_ab^ cd is ascertained below. … We expect the variational principle to hold for all null vectors n^a thereby leading to a condition on the background metric. Obviously, the functional in Eq. (205) must be rather special to accomplish this … two conditions are sufficient to ensure this. First, the tensor P_abcd should have the same algebraic symmetries as the Riemann tensor R_abcd of the D-dimensional spacetime. This condition can be ensured if we define P^a_ bcd as P^a_ bcd = ∂L/∂R^a_ bcd (206) where L = L(R^a_ bcd, g^ik) is some scalar. … Second, we will postulate the condition: ∇_aP^abcd = 0 (207)" [8, §7.1]; and, in §7.2, the identity that explains the construction: "4P_ab^ cd∇_cn^a∇_dn^b = 4∇_c[P_ab^ cdn^a∇_dn^b] - 4n^aP_ab^ cd∇_c∇_dn^b = … = 4∇_c[P_ab^ cdn^a∇_dn^b] + 2n^a𝒢_ain^i (213) … So, when we consider variations ignoring the surface term we are effectively varying (2𝒢_ab - T_ab)n^an^b with respect to n^a and demanding that it holds for all n^a" [8, §7.2].

Derivation from the Principle. Identity (213) is the bridge: on a null n^a in Einstein gravity, 2𝒢_abn^an^b = 1/(8πG)R_abn^an^b, so up to a surface term Padmanabhan's postulated S_grav is -1/(8πG)∫√(-g) R_abn^an^b. That contraction is exactly what Theorem 4.7 Step 3 integrates: the Raychaudhuri equation at leading order about θ(0) = σ(0) = 0 gives θ(λ) = -λR_μνk^μk^ν, hence δA = -∫λR_μνk^μk^νdλdA, and Step 2 converts δA to entropy by the area law of Theorem 3.5, δS = (k_B/4ℓ_P²) δA = -(k_Bc³/4ħG)∫λR_μνk^μk^νdλdA. The gravitational entropy "in terms of the normal to the null surface" is therefore derived, with its coefficient: it is the change in the Compton-tick cell count on the McGucken Sphere's null cone produced by the focusing of its generators, and the overall scaling of n^a that Padmanabhan notes is "arbitrary" is harmless for the same reason it is harmless in Theorem 4.7: both sides of the Clausius relation, the flux δQ of Step 1 and the focusing δA of Step 3, are quadratic in k^μ, so a rescaling k^μ→f k^μ multiplies the identity by f². The quadratic form is derived as well: with the horizon through the event chosen so that θ = σ = 0 there (the equilibrium condition of Theorem 4.7 Step 3), the first-order terms vanish and the leading term of Raychaudhuri is the Ricci focusing, second order in the generator's derivatives — which is why "the leading term for entropy function in the correct theory is likely to be quadratic" [8, §7.6]. Condition (206), P with the Riemann symmetries, and condition (207), ∇_aP^abcd = 0, hold for Einstein gravity with P^ab_ cd = 1/(32πG)(δ^a_cδ^b_d - δ^a_dδ^b_c), the tensor Theorem 4.1 Step 5 selects by Lovelock's theorem; in the Principle they are consequences of the Algebraic Channel, with Padmanabhan's postulated "elastic constants of spacetime solid" being the single constant G that Theorem 4.1's Newtonian matching fixes.

(5) The field equations with Λ as an integration constant. Padmanabhan: "the condition that S[n^a] be an extremum for arbitrary variations of n^a then becomes

2P_ab^ cd(∇_c∇_d - ∇_d∇_c)n^a - (T_ab + λg_ab)n^a = 0, (210)

… the above expression reduces to

(2ℛ^a_ b - T^a_ b + λδ^a_b)n^a = (2𝒢^a_ b - T^a_ b + (L + λ)δ^a_b)n^a = 0, (211)

… We see that the equations of motion do not contain derivatives with respect to n^a which is, of course, the crucial point. … We need the condition in Eq. (211) holds for arbitrary vector fields n^a. One can easily show using ∇_a𝒢^a_ b = 0 = ∇_aT^a_ b that this requires λ+ L = constant leading to the field equation 𝒢^a_ b = 1/2T^a_ b + Λδ^a_b (212) where Λ is a constant. … One crucial difference between the two equations is the introduction of the cosmological constant Λ as an integration constant in Eq. (212). … We have now shown that we will get the same field equations (but with a cosmological constant) if we start with the expression in Eq. (205), maximize it with respect to n^a and demand that it holds for all n^a. This result might appear a little mysterious at first sight" [8, §7.2].

Derivation from the Principle. Equation (211) on all null n^a is Theorem 4.7 Step 5. Padmanabhan's "for arbitrary vector fields n^a" is, in the Principle, "for every generator of every McGucken Sphere at every event": because Σ_+(p) expands in every spatial direction, the null directions available at p fill the full two-sphere of the cross-section, and these span the tangent space, so a symmetric bilinear form vanishing on all of them vanishes identically — this is the completeness statement Step 5 uses. The passage from "= 0 on all null n^a" to the tensor equation leaves exactly one term undetermined, the multiple of g_ab, because g_abn^an^b = 0; local conservation ∇^aT_ab = 0 (Theorem 4.1 Step 4) with the contracted Bianchi identity ∇^aG_ab = 0 then forces that multiple to be constant — this is the Λ that Theorem 4.7 Step 5 records as "an integration constant (allowed because ∇^μg_μν = 0 identically)". The result is "mysterious" only if the equations of motion are expected to govern n^a; in the Principle n^a is a generator of a Sphere, whose dynamics is already fixed — it advances at c — and the extremum condition is a constraint on the geometry through which the Spheres advance. That is why "the equations of motion do not contain derivatives with respect to n^a": the Principle has no dynamics for n^a to supply.

(6) The shift symmetry and the no-go theorem. Padmanabhan: "Eq. (205) is clearly invariant under the shift L_m →L_m - ρ₀ or equivalently, T_ab →T_ab + ρ₀g_ab, since it only introduces a term -ρ₀n^an_a = 0 for any null vector n^a. In other words, one cannot introduce the cosmological constant as a low energy parameter in the action in this approach. We saw, however, that the cosmological constant can re-appear as an integration constant when the equations are solved. … This extra symmetry under the shift T_ab →T_ab + ρ₀g_ab arises because we are not treating metric as a dynamical variable in an action principle. In fact one can state a stronger result. Consider any model of gravity satisfying the following three conditions: (1) The metric is varied in a local action to obtain the equations of motion. (2) We demand full general covariance of the equations of motion. (3) The equations of motion for matter sector are invariant under the addition of a constant to the matter Lagrangian. Then, we can prove a 'no-go' theorem that the cosmological constant problem cannot be solved in such model. … So the only hope we have is to introduce an approach in which gravitational field equations are obtained by varying some degrees of freedom other than g_ab in a maximization principle" [8, §7.5].

Derivation from the Principle. The Principle has both routes, and Theorem 5.1 states their relation. The Algebraic Channel (Theorem 4.1) varies the metric and satisfies Padmanabhan's conditions (1)–(3); the Geometric Channel (Theorem 4.7) varies nothing — it reads the Clausius relation on the McGucken Sphere's generators — and the shift symmetry T_ab →T_ab + ρ₀g_ab is the statement that a term proportional to g_ab carries no flux across a null cone, g_abk^ak^b = 0, so the Compton-tick action crossing the horizon in Theorem 4.7 Step 1 is blind to it. Padmanabhan's "degrees of freedom other than g_ab" are named: they are the generators k^a of the Spheres. The integration constant that his approach leaves "much less troublesome to choose" is then given a physical identification by Theorem 12.1: the energy density of the unperturbed x₄-advance has w = -1 exactly, by the rigidity of the rate (Lemma 7.4.1, Theorem 7.1 of [19]), and its equation of state on the matter-contracted slice is w = -1 + Ω_m/6π. The constant Padmanabhan can only set by observation is, in the Principle, the energy density of the advance itself; Theorem 12.1 fixes its equation of state, and its magnitude is the subject of [31] §10 and [27] §III.2, outside the present paper.

(7) "Spacetime has an entropy density," and what is missing. Padmanabhan: "The key idea is that the behaviour of bulk spacetime is similar to the behaviour of a macroscopic body of, say, gas and can be usefully described through thermodynamic concepts — even though these concepts may not have any meaning in terms of the true microscopic degrees of freedom. … leading to the central theme: 'Spacetime has an entropy density' from the top. The form of the entropy function encodes the information about dynamics and its extremisation leads to the field equations. … In the complete description (statistical mechanics of the 'atoms of spacetime') one should be able to obtain the form of the entropy in terms of the microscopic degrees of freedom. … In the absence of such a theory, we are relying on a thermodynamic description" [8, §7.6].

Derivation from the Principle. The entropy density is the count Ω of Compton-tick states of the McGucken Spheres (§6, Theorem 6.1): one direction on the cross-section per tick, one h per cycle (§2.3), one mode per Planck-area cell at the horizon tier (Theorem 3.5). The "atoms of spacetime" are the ticks of the advance, and the form of the entropy in terms of them is S = k_BlogΩ with Ω counted on the Sphere. The thermodynamic description's validity "even though these concepts may not have any meaning in terms of the true microscopic degrees of freedom" is Theorem 5.1: the Geometric Channel reads the advance at ensemble resolution and yields the Second Law and the field equations; the Algebraic Channel reads the same advance at single-event resolution and yields the time-reversal-invariant laws. The microscopic theory Padmanabhan's §7.6 lacks is the Principle itself.

(8) The Conclusions: microstructure, observer dependence, quantum and thermal. Padmanabhan: "To provide a physical picture behind these mathematical results, it is necessary to invoke certain effective degrees of freedom which can participate in the (observer dependent) thermodynamic interactions near any local patch of a null surface that acts as a horizon for certain class of observers. At present we have no deep understanding of how this comes about … Assume that the spacetime is endowed with certain microscopic degrees of freedom capable of exhibiting thermal phenomena. This is just the Boltzmann paradigm: If one can heat it, it must have microstructure!; and one can heat up a spacetime. … we are forced to accept that the notion of entropy is an observer dependent concept. … We do not yet have a similar set of rules for quantum field theory in noninertial frames. … This requires an intriguing relationship between quantum fluctuations and thermal fluctuations" [8, §8].

Derivation from the Principle. The microstructure is item 7. Observer dependence of the entropy is a theorem of the McGucken Sphere: every inertial observer measures the same rate c (Lemma 7.4.1), so the inertial observer sees the whole cross-section of Σ_+(p) and counts no horizon; the accelerated observer's Wick-rotated x₄-boost (Theorem 4.6) places part of the cross-section behind a null surface, and the entropy that observer assigns is the count Ω of the generators so hidden. The "rules for quantum field theory in noninertial frames" are Theorem 10.1: the algebra of the Sphere-cogenerated wedge is type III₁, its modular flow is the x₄-boost, and the Rindler observer's thermal state at T_U is the KMS state of that flow (Bisognano–Wichmann [45], Theorem 10.1). The "intriguing relationship between quantum fluctuations and thermal fluctuations" is Lemma 7.4.3 with the McGucken–Wick rotation: the quantum phase is e^iωt = e^ωx₄/c, the exponential of the coordinate whose square is the metric, and the thermal period βħ in Euclidean time is the Compton cycle of the same coordinate under x₄ → real (Theorem 4.5, §10). The two kinds of fluctuation are two readings of the advance of x₄.

9.0bis The equipartition paper read in full: E = 1/2 nk_BT derived

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic states that from every event a McGucken Sphere expands at c, its wavelength setting the action h and its volume defining a nonlocality. Padmanabhan's equipartition paper [44] (verified-read, full text) reinterprets the static-horizon relation S = E/2T as equipartition over n = ΔA/L_P² horizon cells, derives Newton's law from it, and closes with the statement that the distinction between quantum and thermal fluctuations should fade in the correct description. Each step is quoted and derived below.

(1) The relation and its reinterpretation. Padmanabhan: "the relation S = E/2T between the entropy (S), active gravitational mass (E) and temperature (T) — obtained previously in gr-qc/0308070 — can be reinterpreted as the law of equipartition E = (1/2)nk_BT where n = ΔA/L_P² is the number (density) of microscopic horizon degrees of freedom in an area ΔA" [44, Abstract]; and "Suppose we have any formalism of quantum gravity in which there is a minimum quantum of length or area, of the order of L_P² ≡Għ/c³. Given this result, a patch of horizon having an area A can be divided into n = (A/c₁L_P²) microscopic cells where c₁ is a numerical factor. If each cell has c₂ internal states then the total number of microscopic states is c₂^n and the resulting entropy is S = nlnc₂ = (4lnc₂/c₁)(A/4L_P²). This will lead to the standard result in Einstein's theory, S = (A/4L_P²) if we choose (4lnc₂/c₁) = 1" [44, §2].

Derivation from the Principle. The two free numbers c₁, c₂ are fixed. The cell is the horizon-tier wavelength of the advance: Theorem 3.5 Step 1 derives ℓ_P as the wavelength of the advance at the horizon tier (the Compton wavelength and the Schwarzschild radius cross at λ_C = r_s = 2√(π)ℓ_P), and Step 2 counts one x₄-mode per cell of area ℓ_P² by the Kirchhoff count of Lemma 7.4.4, so c₁ = 1; the coefficient 1/4 is computed in Theorem 3.5 Step 3 twice — by the Euclidean cigar of Theorem 4.5 (Proposition V.1 of [24]) in the Algebraic Channel and by the Newtonian matching of Theorem 4.1 Step 6 carried through Theorem 4.7 in the Geometric Channel — with no state-counting input, so lnc₂ = 1/4 follows from S = k_BA/4ℓ_P² with n = A/ℓ_P². Padmanabhan's choice 4lnc₂/c₁ = 1 is the output of Theorem 3.5. The relation S = E/2T itself follows for a Schwarzschild horizon from the same two theorems: with S = k_BA/4ℓ_P² = 4πGk_BM²/ħc (Theorem 3.5, A = 4πr_s², r_s = 2GM/c²) and T_H = ħc³/8πGk_BM (Theorem 4.5), 2ST_H = 2·(4πGk_BM²)/(ħc)·(ħc³)/(8πGk_BM) = Mc² = E. The general static case rests on Padmanabhan's Noether-charge definitions of S and E (his Eqs. (10)–(11)); the Principle supplies the Schwarzschild instance from its two theorems and the identification of E as the rest energy of the Compton coupling, E = mc² = ħω_C (Theorem 3.1).

(2) Equipartition and the active mass. Padmanabhan: "we will assume that the each cell of area c₁L_P² contributes an energy (1/2)T in accordance with the standard thermodynamic equipartition law. Then the total energy is

ℰ ≡1/2 nT = 1/2 ST/(lnc₂) = 2ST/c₁ = E/c₁ (7)

… if we take the patches to be of size L_P² (that is, c₁ = 1), then the equipartition energy of the horizon maches with the active gravitational mass producing the horizon!" [44, §2].

Derivation from the Principle. With c₁ = 1 and lnc₂ = 1/4 from item 1, Eq. (7) is an identity: 1/2 n k_BT = 1/2(A/ℓ_P²)k_BT = 2(k_BA/4ℓ_P²)T = 2ST = E. The physical input in Padmanabhan's step is the assumption of 1/2k_BT per cell. The Principle does not assume it; it derives the three quantities the assumption relates — n = A/ℓ_P² (Theorem 3.5 Steps 1–2), S = k_Bn/4 (Theorem 3.5 Step 3), T (Theorems 4.5, 4.6) — and E = Mc² for the Schwarzschild horizon (item 1), so that E = 1/2nk_BT holds as an identity among derived quantities. The per-cell statement is then derived without any equipartition assumption: Theorem 3.5 Step 3 gives entropy k_B/4 per cell, S = k_Bn/4, and E = 2ST (item 1) gives the energy per cell E/n = 2ST/n = 1/2k_BT. Each x₄-mode of the horizon tier carries entropy k_B/4 and energy 1/2k_BT, with the thermal state supplied by Theorem 10.1 at the temperature of Theorem 4.6; the scope of the derivation is the Schwarzschild horizon, where E = Mc² = 2ST is computed, and Padmanabhan's general static case rests on his Eq. (1).

(3) Newton's law and the ħ-independence. Padmanabhan: "Hence the equipartition energy for the degrees of freedom associated with this surface will give (taking c₁ = 1 or, equivalently, attributing (1/2)k_BT per Planck area), in normal units,

ℰ = 1/2A/(L_P²)k_BT = 1/2A/(L_P²)(ħκ)/(2πc) = A/(4π)(c²κ)/G (8)

… Note that ℰ is independent of ħ if we treat, as is usually done, G and ħ as unrelated independent constants. The effective number of degrees of freedom on the surface n ∝1/ħ while the Rindler temperature T ∝ħ making the equipartition energy (1/2)nk_BT independent of ħ. Equating the equipartition energy ℰ to the energy of active gravitational mass Mc², we find that the acceleration induced on a body at rest on a surface of area A is given by

κ = GM((4π)/A) = GM/(r²) = ((𝒜_Pc³)/(ħ))M/(r²) (9)

which is just the Newton's law of gravity. … The last equality in Eq. (9) shows that, in this holographic approach to gravity, the Planck area 𝒜_P = L_P² is what determines the gravitational force. … If we keep 𝒜_P finite and take the limit ħ→0 then the coupling constant diverges in the Newton's law, showing that gravity is intrinsically a quantum phenomenon" [44, §2].

Derivation from the Principle. Eq. (8) is Theorem 3.5 (n = A/ℓ_P²) times Theorem 4.6 (k_BT = ħκ/2πc) with ℓ_P² = ħG/c³ from Theorem 3.5 Step 1; the ħ cancels because the cell area is proportional to h and the temperature is proportional to h — Lemma 7.4.2, continuous geometry with discrete action: the field equation is h-free while every cell it is built from is h-sized. Eq. (9) is the Newtonian matching of Theorem 4.1 Step 6 and Theorem 4.7 reached by the horizon-count route, and Padmanabhan's "intrinsically a quantum phenomenon" is Theorem 3.5 Step 1 read in reverse: G = ℓ_P²c³/ħ is a Compton-wavelength statement, the horizon-tier instance of λ_C = h/mc (Theorem 3.1), so the coupling of gravity is set by the action h of the McGucken Sphere's wavelength and has no ħ→0 limit at fixed cell size.

(4) The local form and the degrees of freedom. Padmanabhan: "the equipartition law S = βE/2 of ref.[4] itself takes the interesting form of an integral over the local acceleration temperature T_loc ≡(Na_μn^μ)/2π and is given by

E = 1/2k_B∫_∂𝒱(√(σ)d²x)/(L_P²){(Na_μn^μ)/(2π)} ≡1/2k_B∫_∂𝒱dn T_loc (12)

thereby identifying the number of degrees of freedom to be dn = √(σ)d²x/L_P² in an area element √(σ)d²x. … The validity of the equipartition condition in Eq. (1), for arbitrary three-volumes 𝒱 leads to the field equation ∇_ia^i ≡R_abu^au^b = 8πGT̅_abu^au^b for the static observers which is essentially the 00 component of the Einstein equation" [44, §2].

Derivation from the Principle. dn = √(σ)d²x/ℓ_P² is Theorem 3.5 applied to each area element — one x₄-mode per Planck cell of each McGucken Sphere's cross-section — and T_loc is Theorem 4.6 for the redshifted acceleration of the static observer at that element; the redshift factor N is the static observer's share v_x₄(r)/c = √(1 - r_s/r) of the advance, the rate dx₄/dt = ic being the same at every r (Appendix D, A.3.2). The passage from "arbitrary three-volumes" to the 00 component of the field equation is the static-observer instance of Theorem 4.7 Step 5: the Clausius identity per Sphere at every event, summed over the cells of any closed surface, is the field equation projected on the observers' four-velocity, and "demanding local Lorentz invariance" to reach the full tensor is Lemma 7.4.1, every inertial observer measuring the same rate c.

(5) The Conclusions: quantum and thermal, and the Compton-wavelength force. Padmanabhan: "all these thermodynamical features arise because the local Rindler observers attribute a density matrix to a pure quantum state after integrating out the unobservable modes. From this point of view, all these thermal effects are intrinsically quantum mechanical … But our results suggest that this distinction between quantum fluctuations and thermal fluctuations is artificial (like e.g., the distinction between energy and momentum of a particle) and should fade away in the correct description of spacetime" [44, §3]; and "If one assumes that (i) ΔS/k_B has to be quantized … in units of 2π and (ii) ⟨δx⟩≈ħ/mc for a particle of mass m, then we reproduce F = mg on using the Rindler temperature k_BT = ħg/2πc" [44, §3].

Derivation from the Principle. The first statement is Lemma 7.4.3 with Theorem 4.5: the quantum phase is the exponential of x₄ and the metric is its square, and under the McGucken–Wick rotation the thermal period of the Rindler observer is the Compton cycle of the same coordinate, so the two kinds of fluctuation are two readings of the advance — Padmanabhan's own comparison, "like the distinction between energy and momentum of a particle," is the four-vector statement of Theorem 3.1, where E/c and 𝐩 are the x₄ and spatial components of the momentum of the advance. The density matrix "after integrating out the unobservable modes" is the reduced state of Theorem 3.3 and the type III₁ wedge algebra of Theorem 10.1. The second statement is Theorem 8.1 verbatim in Padmanabhan's notation: ⟨δx⟩ = ħ/mc = λ_C/2π is one radian of the Compton phase accumulated by the x₄-advance across the displacement (Theorem 3.1), the quantum of ΔS/k_B in units of 2π is one Compton cycle carrying the action h (§2.3), and F = T ΔS/⟨δx⟩ = (ħg)/(2πc k_B)·(2πk_B)/(ħ/mc) = mg. The two assumptions Padmanabhan lists are the two theorems named.

9.1 Padmanabhan: the field equations on a horizon as TdS = dE + PdV, and the entropy extremum over null vectors

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic predicts that any diffeomorphism-invariant gravitational theory evaluated on a horizon will exhibit the Clausius-type identity, because the horizon is the McGucken Sphere's null cone and the field equations are the Clausius relation on it (Theorem 4.7); and that the field equations will follow from extremizing an entropy over all null vectors, because the Clausius identity holds for every null generator of every Sphere at every event (Theorem 4.7, Step 5).

Padmanabhan's review [8] states five items at the level of its §1 (verified-read); each is given here at the level of its criterion, with the full-text derivations in §9.0 cited per item.

1. The field equations on a horizon reduce to TdS = dE + PdV in Einstein gravity, Lovelock gravity, BTZ, FRW, and Hořava–Lifshitz settings (his §1, §5.1). LTD reading: Theorem 4.7 Step 4 is this identity on the McGucken Sphere's null cone with PdV the work term of the horizon's expansion; its universality across theories is the universality of the null cone that dx₄/dt = ic generates at every event regardless of the gravitational Lagrangian, and the Lovelock extension is the D > 4 form of Theorem 4.1 Step 5, Lovelock's theorem being the uniqueness statement used there.

2. The surface term of the gravitational action, evaluated on the horizon, gives the horizon entropy, through a holographic relation between surface and bulk terms that the conventional approach leaves unexplained (his §1). LTD reading: Theorem 4.5 Step C computes this directly — the bulk Einstein–Hilbert term vanishes on the Ricci-flat section and the Gibbons–Hawking–York surface term carries the whole entropy, its 1/2 becoming the 1/4 — and §11 states why the surface carries the bulk's information: every McGucken Sphere is both a Huygens wavefront and a holographic screen (Theorem 21 of [3]).

3. Entropy extremization for all local Rindler observers gives (G_ab - 8πT_ab)n^an^b = 0 for all null n^a (his Eq. 3), hence G_ab = 8πT_ab + ρ₀g_ab with ρ₀ constant by the Bianchi identity, and a new invariance T_ab→T_ab + λg_ab (his §1, §7). LTD reading: this is Theorem 4.7 Step 5 — the Clausius identity holds for every null k^μ at every event, and the all-null-vectors argument with local conservation and the Bianchi identity yields the Einstein tensor and the cosmological constant as an integration constant. The invariance T_ab→T_ab + λg_ab is a property of the null-projected form: g_abn^an^b = 0. In the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework the extremum runs in the Geometric Channel (Theorem 5.1): the entropy being extremized is the McGucken Sphere's count Ω on the horizon, and "for all local Rindler observers" is "for every null generator of every Sphere."

4. The construction LIF → LRF, with matter δE near the horizon transferring δS = (2π/κ)δE (his §1, §6). LTD reading: the local inertial frame is the Minkowski metric of §2.1 at the event, exact; the local Rindler frame is the accelerated observer's view of the McGucken Sphere's null cone (Theorem 4.7 preamble); and δS = (2π/κ)δE = δE/T_U with T_U from Theorem 4.6 in natural units — the entropy transferred is the increment of Ω that the Compton-tick action δE adds to the horizon count.

5. Microstructure inferred, and unknown. Padmanabhan infers, since horizons can be heated by Hawking radiation or by acceleration, that spacetime has microstructure, and writes that "we have no clue about its microstructure" [8, §1]. LTD reading: the microstructure is the Compton-tick state of the expanding McGucken Sphere — one direction on the cross-section per cycle, one h per cycle (§2.3) — and its count Ω is the entropy (§6). The thermodynamic description's insensitivity to microstructure, which Padmanabhan notes allows the universal form TdS = dE + PdV, is the Geometric-Channel reading at ensemble resolution (§7.3); the microstructure itself is accessible at single-event resolution through the Algebraic Channel.

The equipartition reading of the field equations — E = 1/2Nk_BT over N = A/L_P² horizon degrees of freedom [44] — is the Planck-area tiling of Theorem 3.5 with the temperature of Theorem 4.6: each of the N cells is one Compton-tick mode, and equipartition over them at T_U is the horizon-tier statement of the Compton coupling of Theorem 3.1; the full derivation, step by step against the text of [44], is §9.0bis.

9.2 Bianconi: the metric as a density matrix, and gravity from the quantum relative entropy

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic predicts that a construction treating the metric as a density matrix will find the metric's own entropy to vanish and will recover the Einstein–Hilbert action only after inserting a curvature term by hand, because the metric is the frozen coordinate integral of the advance from which the ħ-cycles have been integrated away, and the curvature term is what the Algebraic Channel derives (Theorem 4.1).

Bianconi's letter [10] states five items (verified-read, arXiv:2408.14391v1); the one verbatim phrase used from it is in item 1.

1. The theory "treats the metric at each point of spacetime as a density matrix" [10], with eigenvalues defined Lorentz-invariantly by T̂_μν[V^(λ)]^ν = λV^(λ)_μ (his Eq. 1), so that all eigenvalues of g_μν equal one. LTD reading: the metric and the quantum state are cogenerated from the McGucken Sphere — the metric as the squared-rate reading (ic)² = -c² (§2.1), the state as the amplitude reading (§6bis) — so reading the metric as a density matrix reads one object through the other channel's vocabulary (the identification Jacobson also reached, §7.2 (f)).

2. The entropy of the metric vanishes identically, H = Tr glng^-1 = 0 (his Eq. 7), so the relative entropy reduces to the cross-entropy term. LTD reading: the coordinate integral x₄ = ict retains no trace of the ħ-sized cycles that composed it — relativity built on x₄ = ict is not manifestly quantum although the oscillation persists at every point [6] — so the metric alone carries zero entropy; the entropy sits in the McGucken Sphere's count Ω, which the metric's integration has frozen out (§6.1, §6.2).

3. The Lagrangian is ℒ = Tr g̃ln𝐆̃^-1 - Λ (his Eq. 36) with the induced metric 𝐆̃ = g̃ + α(D|Φ⟩⟨Φ|D + (m² + R)|Φ⟩⟨Φ|) - βℛ (his Eq. 32), the term -βℛ inserted so that the vacuum metric is determined. LTD reading: the curvature term that must be inserted is the Einstein–Hilbert sector the Algebraic Channel derives from the McGucken Sphere's Lorentz covariance and Lovelock uniqueness (Theorem 4.1 Steps 4′–5); the relative entropy between g̃ and 𝐆̃ is, on the type-III₁ algebra the Sphere cogenerates, the Araki–Uhlmann functional of §10, and the count it measures is Ω.

4. For α,β≪1 the action reduces to Einstein–Hilbert coupled to the scalar field (his Eqs. 39–40), with modified Einstein equations (his Eq. 45) beyond that limit and a rescaled constant Λ' = (Λ+ (d+1))/4β> 0 even at Λ = 0. LTD reading: Corollary 4.8 — both channels of the Principle converge on G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG/c⁴)T_μν with Λ an integration constant; Bianconi's low-coupling limit is the regime in which the Algebraic-Channel action is recovered, and her higher-order terms are the departures the Principle's two-channel disjointness constrains (Theorem 4.7 Step 5 forces the Einstein tensor at every order in the Geometric Channel).

5. Open items: solutions of Eq. 45 deferred; canonical quantization and the dark-matter role of the 𝐆-field left to future work. LTD reading: the dark sector is supplied with zero free parameters by the McGucken cosmology [27] (§8.3, §12), and the quantization question is answered by the cogeneration of ℋ and 𝕄₁,3 from the McGucken Sphere [6].

10. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Reading of Dorau–Much: the Araki–Uhlmann relative entropy as the count Ω on the McGucken Sphere-cogenerated wedge algebra

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality. Dorau and Much [11] replace Jacobson's classical entropy with the Araki–Uhlmann relative entropy of a scalar field on a bifurcate Killing horizon, find it equal to the energy flux across the horizon, and, assuming S_rel = δA/4, recover the semiclassical Einstein equations. Each input is a theorem of the Principle.

10.1 What Dorau and Much establish, and the McGucken reading

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic predicts that the quantum distinguishability of an excitation from the vacuum at a horizon equals the horizon-area variation, because both are the count Ω of Compton-tick states of the McGucken Sphere (Theorem 6bis.3); the proportionality Dorau and Much assume is derived as the equality of the two readings (Theorem 6bis.3).

Their chain (verified-read of the abstract and equations): the relative entropy of a coherent excitation against the vacuum equals the energy flux, S_rel = -2π∫U⟨:T_ab:⟩ξ^aξ^b dU dvol (their Eq. 13); matched to the Raychaudhuri area focusing (their Eq. 24), it gives R_ab - 1/2Rg_ab + Λg_ab = α⟨:T_ab:⟩ (their Eq. 28), with α = 8π fixed by assuming S_rel = δA/4. Their inputs: the local Minkowski metric via the equivalence principle, the Bekenstein–Hawking area law, the geometric modular flow Δ^it = D₂πt with the vacuum KMS at the Unruh temperature (Bisognano–Wichmann [45]), the quasifree Hadamard vacuum, and the bifurcate Killing horizon.

10.2 The relative entropy as a theorem of the Principle

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic supplies each object on which the Araki–Uhlmann functional rests, with the standard operator-algebra theorems invoked on hypotheses the Principle derives (Theorem D.1 of [14]; §§22.3.9–22.3.10 of [3]).

Theorem 10.1. Let 𝒩 be the von Neumann algebra of the McGucken field on the Rindler wedge W of a uniformly accelerated observer, with vacuum Ω₀. Then (i) 𝒩 is a hyperfinite type-III₁ factor; (ii) its Tomita–Takesaki modular flow is the boost, the x₄-advance read in the accelerated frame, with modular Hamiltonian K = 2π∫U⟨:T_UU:⟩dU on the horizon; (iii) for a coherent excitation ω_φ the Araki–Uhlmann relative entropy [55, 49] S(ω₀ω_φ) = -⟨Ω_φ|lnΔ_Ω₀|Ω_φ|Ω_φ⟩ equals -2π∫U⟨:T_ab:⟩_ω_φξ^aξ^b dU dvol, the count of Compton-tick states by which the excitation is distinguished from the vacuum on the McGucken Sphere.

From [6], verbatim — Theorem 7.11 (Complex conjugation as McGucken-Sphere PT-symmetry through the source event), statement and proof: (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list)

Theorem 7.11 (Complex conjugation as McGucken-Sphere PT-symmetry through the source event). Let particle A at event E ∈ 𝕄₁,3 propagate its McGucken Sphere outward at dx_4/dt = +ic by the canonical isotropic expansion of clause 3, §2.4. Then:

(i) (4D PT-symmetry through E.) The forward light cone of E admits a unique non-trivial discrete symmetry preserving the spherical isotropy of the McGucken-Sphere expansion: the 4D PT-reflection through E,

PT_E : (x^μ − x^μ_E) ↦ −(x^μ − x^μ_E), equivalently x ↦ 2x_E − x and t ↦ 2t_E − t.

The continuous symmetries of the forward light cone of E preserving isotropy are the spatial rotations SO(3) about x_E (which preserve the spherical symmetry of the wavefront); the additional discrete symmetry PT_E sends the forward light cone to the backward light cone, with the McGucken-Sphere wavefront (forward in t, outward in space from E) mapped to its time-reversed structure (backward in t, inward toward E) — geometrically the same wavefront with reversed orientation.

(ii) (Wavefunction transforms as ψ(PT_E · event) = ψ^(event), exactly.) The McGucken-derived wavefunction ψ on 𝕄₁,3, constructed by Definition 2.6 as the path-integral kernel from source events to target events, satisfies the symmetry identity

ψ(PT_E · event) = ψ^(event), i.e. ψ(2x_E − x, 2t_E − t) = ψ^(x, t),

exactly for any McGucken-derived wavefunction. The wavefunction’s complex-conjugation algebra is the shadow of the McGucken-Sphere PT-symmetry through the source event.

(iii) (Born density as multiplication of wavefunction at event and PT_E-reflected event.) The Born density |ψ(P, t)|² at any spatial-slice event (P, t) is the geometric multiplication of the wavefunction’s value at (P, t) with its PT_E-reflected value at the reflected event:

|ψ(P, t)|² = ψ(P, t) · ψ^(P, t) = ψ(P, t) · ψ(2x_E − P, 2t_E − t).

For normalized wavefunctions this reduces to the standard modulus-squared. The Born rule’s squaring operation is the cascade-level expression of the McGucken-Sphere PT-symmetry through the source event.

(iv) (Free-propagation reading.) For a free particle without external absorber, the conjugate factor ψ^ in the Born density is supplied by the McGucken Sphere’s intrinsic PT-symmetry through the source event, not by an external absorber. The Born density is well-defined at every event of the spatial slice without requiring a collision partner. The conjugate factor is therefore intrinsic to the single particle’s own forward light cone, supplied geometrically by the wavefront’s natural reflection symmetry through its emission event.

(v) (Spatial-slice corollary at fixed t.) The spatial-slice restriction of the 4D PT_E symmetry at fixed parameter time t is the spatial antipodal map P ↔ 2x_E − P through x_E. For energy-eigenstate wavefunctions ψ_n(x) · exp(−iE_n t/ℏ), the global temporal phase drops out of the Born density, and the spatial-slice corollary is exact: the antipodal map yields complex conjugation up to a global phase that drops out of |ψ|². For general (non-stationary) wavefunctions, the antipodal-at-fixed-t map yields complex conjugation only up to a residual temporal-phase factor; the exact symmetry statement is the 4D PT_E through E, with the spatial-slice antipodal map as its restriction at fixed t.

(vi) (Upstream connection to Principle 2.1.) The PT-symmetry through E is the geometric shadow of the Principle 2.1 (§2.1): the spherically symmetric wavefront expanding at velocity c from event E has reflection through E as its natural symmetry, and that reflection is exactly PT_E in 4D. The complex structure of QM (Theorem 3.1: i as the algebraic marker for x_4-perpendicularity) and the Born rule’s bilinearity (Lemma 7.1: rank-2 sesquilinear pairing inherited from the rank-2 Minkowski metric) are therefore both downstream consequences of this single geometric symmetry. The complex structure and the Born-rule bilinearity, previously two derivationally distinct facts in the cascade, are now placed on the same upstream foundation: the McGucken-Sphere PT-symmetry through the source event.

Proof.

(i) The McGucken Sphere 𝓜_E(t) at parameter time t centered at E is the locus of points reached by the spherically symmetric x_4-expansion from E at velocity c after proper time t in E’s rest frame (clause 3 of §2.4). The 4D structure (forward light cone of E plus the spheres at each future parameter time) is preserved under any symmetry preserving the isotropy of the expansion. The continuous symmetries through E preserving isotropy are the spatial rotations SO(3) about x_E. The discrete non-trivial symmetry through E is PT_E: the combined parity-and-time-reversal reflection sends (x − x_E, t − t_E) ↦ −(x − x_E, t − t_E), mapping the forward light cone of E to the backward light cone with geometric structure preserved up to orientation. The McGucken-Sphere wavefront (a 2-sphere in space at parameter time t) maps under PT_E to a 2-sphere of the same radius in space at parameter time −t (i.e., at time 2t_E − t, which lies in the backward light cone of E). The forward-and-outward expansion maps to backward-and-inward propagation — geometrically identical wavefront with reversed orientation in both space and time. Therefore PT_E is a discrete symmetry of the 4D McGucken-Sphere structure through E.

(ii) By Definition 2.6, the McGucken-derived wavefunction at any event (P, t) is the path-integral kernel

ψ(P, t) = ∑_{paths γ: E → (P, t)} exp(iS
γ

with the action S

The identity ψ(PT_E · event) = ψ^(event) is therefore exact for any McGucken-derived wavefunction. For explicit verification with a plane-wave component ψ_k(x, t) = exp(ik · (x − x_E) − iω(k)(t − t_E)):

ψ_k(PT_E · (P, t)) = exp(ik · (2x_E − P − x_E) − iω(k)(2t_E − t − t_E))
= exp(ik · (x_E − P) − iω(k)(t_E − t))

k · (P − x_E) − ω(k)(t − t_E)
)

By linearity, the symmetry identity extends to any Fourier superposition of plane-wave components, i.e., to any McGucken-derived wavefunction on 𝕄₁,3.

(iii) Direct substitution: |ψ(P, t)|² = ψ^(P, t) · ψ(P, t) = ψ(PT_E · (P, t)) · ψ(P, t) by clause (ii). The geometric reading identifies the Born density’s squaring as the multiplication of the wavefunction’s value at an event with its value at the PT_E-reflected event.

(iv) For a free particle, the source event E is the emission event (or the initial-condition event of the wavefunction). The wavefunction’s complex-conjugation symmetry ψ(PT_E · event) = ψ^(event) is intrinsic to the McGucken-Sphere PT-symmetry through E; no external absorber is required to supply the conjugate factor. The Born density at any event (P, t) is therefore well-defined as ψ(P, t) · ψ(2x_E − P, 2t_E − t), the multiplication of the wavefunction’s value at (P, t) with its value at the PT_E-reflected event. When a detector subsequently arrives at the spatial point P, the head-on collision of Theorem 7.7 supplies a second physical source of the conjugate factor (the absorber’s outgoing McGucken Sphere viewed in the emitter’s frame); the dx₄/dt = ic framework’s three readings (Theorem 7.4 cascade-level, Theorem 7.7 detection-event, Theorem 7.11 free-propagation) are then jointly consistent at the detection event, with the free-propagation reading describing the pre-detection state and the head-on-collision reading describing the detection event itself.

(v) Restrict the 4D PT_E symmetry to fixed parameter time t. The spatial-slice map is P ↦ 2x_E − P (spatial antipodal through x_E). For energy-eigenstate wavefunctions ψ(x, t) = ψ_n(x) · exp(−iE_n t/ℏ), the temporal factor exp(−iE_n t/ℏ) is global and drops out of the Born density |ψ(P, t)|² = |ψ_n(P)|². The spatial antipodal map applied to ψ_n yields ψ_n(2x_E − P), which equals ψ_n^(P) for ψ_n with definite spatial parity about x_E (a parity-symmetric Hamiltonian centered at x_E supports parity eigenstates with this property). For general non-stationary wavefunctions ψ(x, t) = ∑_k a_k exp(ik · (x − x_E) − iω(k)(t − t_E)), the spatial antipodal at fixed t gives ψ(2x_E − P, t) = ∑_k a_k exp(−ik · (P − x_E) − iω(k)(t − t_E)), while ψ^(P, t) = ∑_k a_k^* exp(−ik · (P − x_E) + iω(k)(t − t_E)). The two differ by both the conjugation a_k ↦ a_k^* and the temporal phase ω(t − t_E) ↔ −ω(t − t_E). The spatial-slice antipodal map at fixed t yields complex conjugation only when both: (a) the wavefunction has all-real Fourier coefficients a_k (i.e., spatial-parity-symmetric), AND (b) the wavefunction is monochromatic (single ω) or stationary. For general wavefunctions the exact symmetry is the 4D PT_E through E, with the spatial-slice antipodal map as its fixed-t restriction.

(vi) By Principle 2.1 (§2.1), the McGucken Principle dx_4/dt = ic states that x_4 advances as a spherically symmetric wavefront from every spacetime event E, carrying wavelength, frequency, phase, and therefore action. The natural symmetry of such a wavefront is reflection through E. In 4D, reflection through E is the PT_E operation. The wavefunction’s complex-conjugation algebra (Theorem 3.1: i as the algebraic marker for x_4-perpendicularity) and the Born rule’s bilinearity (Lemma 7.1: rank-2 sesquilinear pairing inherited from the rank-2 Minkowski metric) are therefore both downstream consequences of the McGucken-Sphere PT-symmetry through the source event. The chain extends:

dx_4/dt = ic → x_4 advances as a spherically symmetric wavefront from E → the wavefront has PT_E-reflection as its natural symmetry → the wavefunction satisfies ψ(PT_E · event) = ψ^(event) → the Born density at any event is the modulus-squared of a wavefunction whose phase structure is constrained by this symmetry.

The complex structure of QM and the bilinearity of the Born rule are placed on the same upstream foundation. The dynamics were in the premise (§2.1); so was the conjugate structure that the Born rule reads. ∎

From [5], verbatim — Lemma 8.7, Geometric Channel proof of QM T8 (the Klein–Gordon equation): (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list; four clauses that presented the rest-frame four-velocity normalization u^μu_μ = -c² as the four-vector form or Lorentz-covariant form of the Principle are replaced, in square brackets, by the statement that the normalization is a consequence of dx₄/dt = ic — the norm is a magnitude statement carrying no McGucken Sphere, no orientation, and no measure, and the Principle is the physical expansion itself)

Lemma 8.7 (Geometric Channel proof of QM T8). The wavefunction of a massive
spin-0 particle, modeled as the McGucken-Sphere wavefront with a
Compton-frequency rest-mass oscillation, satisfies
(- m² c²/ħ²)ψ = 0.

Proof. Everything below descends from the physical expansion of x₄ at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every event of M_G (dx₄dt = ic). The proof builds the Klein--Gordon equation along a Geometric Channel
chain in six steps, with the mass shell
P^μP_μ = -m² c² [a consequence of
dx₄dt = ic by
Lemma [4.7]]. The construction follows
the structure of  §9.1.5: the Klein--Gordon equation
falls out as the differential expression of the mass-shell constraint,
with no canonical-quantization step performed at any point in the chain.

Step 1: Mass shell from the McGucken Principle.
[By Lemma [4.7], the rest-frame four-velocity normalization
u^μu_μ = -c² follows from dx₄dt = ic (Theorem 3.1 Step 1 of the present paper),] holding identically at every spacetime
point in the rest frame of any massive particle at that point.
Multiplying both sides by the squared rest mass m² and using the
definition P^μ: = m u^μ:

P^μP_μ = m² u^μu_μ = m² (-c²) = -m² c².

This is the mass shell --- the geometric locus in four-momentum space
where the McGucken-Sphere wavefront is consistent with rest mass m.
The mass-shell condition is Lorentz-invariant: by Lorentz invariance of
the McGucken-derived Minkowski metric
(Theorem [9.2], descending from
Postulate [4.1] clause (iv), derived at Theorem 4.6), the relation
P^μP_μ = -m² c² holds in every Lorentz frame on M_G. The
mass shell [follows from the McGucken Principle:
u^μu_μ = -c² is a consequence of dx₄dt = ic,] and multiplying by m² promotes it to the four-momentum mass
shell.

Step 2: Compton frequency from action quantization of the wavefront.
By the physics of the principle
(Remark [4.2] of
Chapter [4]), the x₄-wavefront carries action ħ
per oscillatory cycle at the Planck frequency. For a particle of rest
mass m, the rest-frame wavefunction oscillates at the Compton angular
frequency ω_C = mc²/ħ along proper time
(Theorem [5.1],
derived from the rest-frame four-velocity budget of
Lemma [4.2] combined with the action quantum
per Sphere cycle of Theorem [3.2]). The four-wavevector k^μ: = P^μ/ħ carries
the mass shell into wavevector-frequency form:

k^μk_μ = (P^μP_μ)/(ħ²) = - (m² c²)/(ħ²),

holding in every Lorentz frame on M_G. The constants c and ħ
appearing in this relation are the twin properties of one wavefront
advance (Theorem [9.35]): c is the rate of x₄-advance and
ħ is the action per oscillatory cycle at the Planck frequency,
with both reading off the physics of dx₄dt = ic.

Step 3: Plane-wave wavefunction as elementary mode of the
McGucken-Sphere expansion at four-wavevector on the mass shell. On
M_G, an elementary mode of the McGucken-Sphere expansion at
four-wavevector k^μ is the plane-wave

ψ_k(x^μ) = exp(i k^νx_ν) = exp(i S[γ]/ħ),

where the second equality identifies the four-wavevector phase
k^νx_ν with the classical action S[γ] = P^νx_ν along
the straight worldline γ at four-wavevector k^μ, divided by
the action quantum ħ. The plane-wave mode ψ_k satisfies the
mass-shell constraint of Step 2 by construction:
k^μk_μ = -m² c²/ħ² is the Lorentz-invariant statement that
ψ_k propagates on the McGucken-Sphere expansion of a particle of
rest mass m.

Step 4: d'Alembertian applied --- Klein--Gordon as the differential
expression of the mass-shell constraint. The d'Alembertian
= η^μν∂_μ∂_ν acts on the plane-wave
mode ψ_k(x^μ) = exp(ik^νx_ν) by direct differentiation:

ψ_k = η^μν(ik_μ)(ik_ν) ψ_k = - k^μk_μψ_k = + (m² c²)/(ħ²) ψ_k,

using the mass-shell relation k^μk_μ = -m² c²/ħ² of Step 2
in the last equality. Rearranging:

(- (m² c²)/(ħ²)) ψ_k = 0,
 the
Klein--Gordon equation in plane-wave form, exactly
equation [
eq:Klein­-Gordon
]. Extension to general wavefunctions
follows by Fourier completeness: the Klein--Gordon operator
- m²c²/ħ² is linear, so every superposition
ψ(x) = ∫d³𝐤 ψ̃(𝐤) ψ_k(x) over
plane-wave modes on the mass shell satisfies the same equation. Since
plane-wave modes are dense in the matter-wavefunction space
L²(ℝ³, d³𝐱) by Fourier completeness
(Lemma [6.4] of
Chapter [2]), the Klein--Gordon equation
(- m²c²/ħ²)ψ = 0 holds for every massive spin-0
matter wavefunction.

No canonical-quantization step has been performed. The Geometric Channel chain
reads off the Klein--Gordon equation as the differential expression of
the mass-shell constraint, with the d'Alembertian acting on plane-wave
modes producing the mass-shell eigenvalue
-k^μk_μ = m²c²/ħ² by direct evaluation of
η^μν∂_μ∂_νexp(ik^νx_ν). The Algebraic
Channel quantization rule P̂^μ = -iħ∂^μ (Stone's
theorem applied to spacetime-translation invariance,
Lemma [8.4]) does not appear in Geometric Channel: the
role of mapping classical four-momentum to operator action that Algebraic
Channel executes through Stone-quantization is replaced in Geometric Channel by the
role of reading off the differential action of  on McGucken-Sphere
plane-wave kernels through direct evaluation. The two channels arrive at
the same Klein--Gordon equation through derivationally disjoint chains.

Step 5: Huygens--Fresnel--Kirchhoff integral form of the same
content. The differential form (- m²c²/ħ²)ψ = 0 has a
corresponding integral form: the McGucken-Sphere wavefront
M^+_p(t) from each Cauchy-surface event p is the elementary
secondary wavefront, with rest-frame Compton-phase
exp(-iω_C τ) along proper time
(Lemma [7.8]), and the Klein--Gordon equation
is the self-consistency condition on the superposition of secondary
wavefronts. This is the massive-case generalization of Huygens's
principle (Theorem [1.1], QM T1): each McGucken Sphere from a
Cauchy-surface point carries its rest-frame Compton-phase
forward, and the Kirchhoff diffraction integral over the Cauchy surface
reproduces the wavefunction at any subsequent event on M_G. The
differential form (Klein--Gordon) and the integral form
(Huygens--Fresnel--Kirchhoff superposition over McGucken Spheres) are
two expressions of the same dynamical content of
dx₄dt = ic, related by Stokes' theorem on the spacetime
slab between successive Cauchy surfaces. The massless case (m = 0,
ω_C = 0) recovers the standard Huygens construction of QM T1
Geometric Channel; the massive case adds the Compton-phase to each
secondary wavefront.

Step 6: Massless limit and Geometric Channel characterisation. In the
massless limit m →0, the mass shell collapses to the null cone
k^μk_μ = 0 at every event of M_G, and the Klein--Gordon
equation reduces to the massless wave equation ψ = 0
(Lemma [8.5], QM T1 Geometric Channel). Photons and other
massless particles propagate on the null cone with no Compton frequency:
the rest-frame phase oscillation has rate zero
(ω_C = mc²/ħ = 0 when m = 0), the rest-frame wavefunction
degenerates to a constant phase, and the wavefront's x₄-advance has
no associated rest-mass cycling. The massless limit recovers the
spherical-wavefront of QM T1 Geometric Channel as a consistent special
case of the massive Klein--Gordon equation.
