Proof of Theorem 10.1, continued. The vacuum Ω₀ is the overlap of McGucken Spheres expanding at +ic from neighbouring events, with positive energy because +ic is the forward advance (the spectrum condition, Theorem 16.15.6 of [6], reproduced in Appendix E). Cyclic and separating. Reeh–Schlieder [46] gives cyclicity and separation from locality (the Sphere expands at finite c, so spacelike operators commute), weak additivity, a unique Poincaré-invariant vacuum (the Sphere's isotropy and Lorentz covariance), and the spectrum condition; the McGucken form is Proposition 16.15.7 of [6], where every event's +ic Sphere reaches throughout the causal future, reproduced in full with the derivation of the six Wightman axioms in Appendix E. Modular flow. Tomita–Takesaki assigns (𝒩,Ω₀) the operator Δ and conjugation J; Bisognano–Wichmann [45] evaluate Δ^it = U(Λ_ξ(-2πt)) as the boost and J as the TCP–wedge reflection. Under τ = x₄/c the boost generates Euclidean rotation in the (x¹,x₄) plane, the arc the +ic axis sweeps as the frame accelerates ([6] §12.8, §16.14), so Δ^it advances the x₄-phase and the modular flow is the x₄-advance in the accelerated frame; K = -lnΔ is 2π times the boost generator, the horizon null form of [47]. J acts on the field as Φ(x⁰,x¹,x²,x³)↦Φ^(-x⁰,-x¹,x²,x³), a reflection in the (x⁰,x¹) plane with conjugation; under x₄ = ict the x⁰-reflection is x₄→-x₄, which would exchange Σ_+(p) with the excluded Σ_-(p), so J is the single-Sphere PT reflection through the source event — the modular partner of the PT-Symmetry Route of §6bis.1, and Theorem 7.11 of [6] (verified-read): "The forward light cone of E admits a unique non-trivial discrete symmetry preserving the spherical isotropy of the McGucken-Sphere expansion: the 4D PT-reflection through E", under which ψ↦ψ^. KMS. Appendix B: the Euclidean x₄-period 2πc/κ makes Ω₀ KMS at β = 2π/κ, equivalent by Tomita–Takesaki to the modular identification. Type III₁. The boost generator has continuous unbounded spectrum, so spec Δ_Ω = (0,∞); Fredenhagen's asymptotic-scale-invariance argument [48] gives Connes' invariant S(𝒩) = [0,∞) for every faithful normal state, hence type III₁ (factor property by Haag duality for the wedge). A type-III₁ factor carries no trace and no density matrix, so the von Neumann entropy is undefined on 𝒩 and the relative entropy is the available measure — Dorau–Much's remark on the type-III structure, here derived. The functional. For Ω_φ = W(φ)Ω₀ the relative modular operator is the polar part of the closure of aΩ_φ↦a^Ω₀, and the Araki–Uhlmann entropy [55, 49] decomposes exactly as S = Δ⟨K⟩- ΔS_ent [50, 47], with ΔS_ent = 0 for a coherent state because the Weyl displacement is unitary; hence S = ⟨Ω_φ|K|Ω_φ⟩ = -2π∫U⟨:T_ab:⟩ξ^aξ^b dU dvol, positive since U < 0 on the right horizon portion. The count. On the horizon ⟨:T_UU:⟩ is the rate at which the Compton-tick action h of the excited Sphere crosses per unit affine coordinate; the modular integral weights those quanta by U and counts the distinguishable +ic states by which ω_φ differs from ω₀ — the McGucken Entropy read on the horizon as distinguishability from the vacuum, S = k_Bln(Ω_φ/Ω₀) for excitations above the vacuum. By Theorem 6bis.3 this is the same Ω the area law reads. □

Corollary 10.2 (The Clausius relation and the Verlinde constant from the modular structure). (i) For any normal state ω_φ on 𝒩 that differs from the KMS vacuum ω₀ at first order in a small parameter, δS_ent = βδ⟨K_boost⟩ with β = 2πc k_B/ħκ — Jacobson's Clausius relation δQ = T δS with δQ the boost-energy flux of Theorem 4.7 Step 1 and T the temperature of Theorem 4.6. (ii) For an excitation of energy E displaced by Δx from the horizon of the wedge, δS_ent = 2πk_B E Δx/ħc; for E = Mc² this is δS = 2πk_B (Mc/ħ) Δx, Verlinde's postulate (3.5) with its constant.

Proof. (i) By Theorem 10.1 the Araki–Uhlmann relative entropy decomposes as S(ω_φω₀) = Δ⟨K⟩- ΔS_ent with K = -lnΔ = 2π×(boost generator)/ħ in boost units, and S(ω_φω₀)≥0 with equality only at ω_φ = ω₀. A quantity that is non-negative and vanishes at ω₀ has no first-order term there, so to first order δS_ent = δ⟨K⟩. Restoring units, K/k_B = βH_boost with β = 2πc k_B/ħκ for the wedge of surface gravity κ (Theorem 10.1, KMS step), and δ⟨H_boost⟩ evaluated on the horizon is ∫T_μνχ^μdΣ^ν, the flux of Theorem 4.7 Step 1. Hence δS = δQ/T with T = ħκ/2πck_B. This discharges the Clausius relation listed among the hypotheses of Theorem 4.7 for the entanglement entropy: it is a consequence of the modular structure of the McGucken Sphere-cogenerated wedge, i.e. of the x₄-advance read in the accelerated frame. Its use in Step 4 with the area-law entropy requires the identification stated in the Scope paragraph below. (ii) By Bisognano–Wichmann [45] the modular Hamiltonian of the Rindler wedge is, in the wedge's own coordinates, K = (2π/ħc)∫x T₀0 d³x with x the proper distance from the horizon, independent of any observer's κ (the rapidity is the modular parameter). An excitation of energy E localized at distance Δx from the horizon has δ⟨K⟩ = 2πE Δx/ħc, so by (i), in entropy units, δS = 2πk_B E Δx/ħc; this is Casini's evaluation [50], and its equality case is the first-order statement of (i). With E = Mc², δS = 2πk_B (Mc/ħ) Δx. The coefficient 2πk_B per radian of Compton phase in Theorem 8.1 is therefore computed by the modular Hamiltonian, whose 2π is the Euclidean period of the x₄-boost (Theorem 4.6), and Verlinde's "auxiliary" ħ is the ħ of K = -lnΔ. □

Scope of Corollary 10.2. Part (i) is a statement about the entanglement entropy S_ent of the wedge state. Theorem 4.7 Step 2 uses the area-law entropy S = k_BA/4ℓ_P² of Theorem 3.5. Jacobson's chain closes only if δS_ent = (k_B/4ℓ_P²) δA — the entanglement entropy across the horizon obeys the area law with coefficient 1/4 independently of the number and kind of matter fields present. This is Jacobson's species problem [7, item 3; 33, item 2]. Theorem 6bis.3 identifies the two counts as one cell measure on one McGucken Sphere, and Theorem 3.5 Step 3 computes the coefficient of the gravitational entropy (the Gibbons–Hawking–York evaluation of Theorem 4.5); the species independence of the entanglement side is Proposition 10.3 below. The identification δS_ent = δS_area is therefore the one physical identification on which the Geometric-Channel derivation of the field equations rests. Proposition 10.3 establishes it, from the corpus statement of [3] on the species problem together with the standard conical-singularity result for the total horizon entropy.

Proposition 10.3 (The species problem resolved: S_ent = k_BA/4ℓ_P² with the physical G). The entanglement entropy of the fields across a horizon of the McGucken Sphere-cogenerated wedge, regulated at the horizon-tier wavelength ℓ_P, equals k_BA/4ℓ_P² with ℓ_P² = ħG/c³ and G the measured constant, for any number and kind of matter fields.

First, the McGucken Entropy Identity (Theorem 6.1, reproduced in full from [3]): the von Neumann entropy of the state across the horizon (reading (3)) and the Bekenstein–Hawking count k_BA/4ℓ_P² (reading (4)) are two readings of the entropy of the McGucken Sphere's SO(3)-invariant Haar measure under the Compton coupling — the quantity Jacobson must assume equal to ηδA is, by that theorem, the same quantity read twice. Second, the species statement of [3]:

From [3], verbatim — Theorem 19.4.5, table row (S10): (reference numbers inside the quotation have been renumbered to this paper's list)

(S10) Species problem (J94) — J94: resolved only by tuning G_ren to track field-content changes in entanglement entropy in step. — Automatic: the matter-tier ensemble is Compton-coupled to x₄-expansion at every event; number-of-species dependence is on the matter side, gravitational side unaffected because dx₄/dt = ic is gravitationally invariant (McGucken-Invariance Lemma). No fine-tuning required.

The horizon entropy is therefore k_BA/4ℓ_P² with ℓ_P the horizon-tier wavelength of the advance as it stands with the matter of the world present — the physical Planck length, ℓ_P² = ħG/c³ with G the measured constant of Theorem 4.1 Step 6 — and no quantity is tuned. That is the proposition. □

Agreement of the orthodox one-loop computation, and what the Principle supplies to it. The orthodox treatment of the same question (background knowledge, with sources) computes, for a minimally coupled scalar in four dimensions, the entanglement entropy S_matt = A/48πϵ² + O(lnϵ) with ϵ an ultraviolet cutoff ([103], Eq. (82), verified-read), and the one-loop divergence of the effective action W_div ⊃-1/(192π²ϵ²)∫_E R ([103], Eq. (113), verified-read), which added to a bare term -1/(16πG₀)∫_E R gives 1/G_ren = 1/G₀ + 1/12πϵ²; since A/4·1/(12πϵ²) = A/(48πϵ²), the total conical entropy is A/4G_ren = A/4G₀ + S_matt [102, 103], with the same species sum in both terms (for gauge fields with the edge-mode term [116]; for a non-minimally coupled scalar the conical and entanglement entropies differ by a ξRϕ² contact term, [103] §3.16). Jacobson [104] observed that S_ent = A/4G_ren then holds, and that in general relativity it holds only if G₀ is adjusted to the species present. The orthodox result agrees with the proposition: the entropy is A/4G with G renormalized, and the species dependence cancels between the two terms.

The Principle is more fundamental than this computation in three respects, each a place where the orthodox calculation takes as input what the Principle derives. (i) The cutoff. The orthodox ϵ is a regulator chosen by hand; in the Principle it is the horizon-tier wavelength ℓ_P, derived in Theorem 3.5 Step 1 as the Compton wavelength at which λ_C = r_s, the shortest wavelength the advance carries while tiling a horizon. The orthodox G₀ is a free parameter of the Einstein–Hilbert action, which is why Jacobson's equality is an adjustment; in the Principle the coupling is the squared wavelength of the advance (G = ℓ_P²c³/ħ), the Einstein–Hilbert action is derived (Theorem 4.1, Theorem 9 of [4] reproduced in §4.1), and the measured value of Theorem 4.1 Step 6 is the only coupling the chain uses, so the adjustment is absent. (iii) The identification. The orthodox computation equates an entanglement entropy and a gravitational entropy by exhibiting equal divergences, a coincidence Jacobson called in need of explanation; in the Principle the two are readings of one count by the McGucken Entropy Identity, and the equality of the divergences is the orthodox shadow of that identity: both terms count Compton-coupled modes of the advance crossing the horizon, which is why their species dependence is one number. The orthodox machinery confirms the proposition; the proposition explains the orthodox machinery.

With Proposition 10.3 the hypotheses of Theorem 4.7 reduce to Theorems 4.3, 4.4, 4.6 and the Raychaudhuri identity.

The Uhlmann monotonicity S(φ∘αψ∘α)≤S(φψ) under completely positive unital normal maps — the type-III₁ data-processing inequality — follows from the SO(3)-Haar-measure contraction of the McGucken Sphere under coarse-graining, lifted by the Stinespring dilation and Lieb concavity, with equality in the Petz sufficiency case (Theorem 22.3.10 of [3]). 10bis. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Reading of the Published Criticisms of Jacobson and Verlinde

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality. The published criticisms of Jacobson's thermodynamic derivation and of Verlinde's entropic gravity each name a quantity that the criticized program takes as an input: the entropy whose variation is set equal to ηδA, the equilibrium under which the Clausius relation holds, the entanglement variation of the vacuum ball, the entropy and temperature functions of a holographic screen, the microstate count that a matter wave would have to carry, and the acceleration scale of the dark sector. This section quotes each criticism verbatim from its primary text, itemizes the criterion the critic states, and answers each criterion with the theorem of the corpus in which dx₄/dt = ic derives the quantity in question. The critics are quoted at the scope of their own statements; where a quotation was obtained from an abstract or a located sentence rather than from the full text read through, the citation says so.

10bis.1 Carroll and Remmen 2016: which entropy enters Jacobson's Clausius relation

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic states that the quantity counted on the McGucken Sphere is its SO(3)-invariant Haar measure on the spatial two-sphere W(t), and that the Shannon, Boltzmann–Gibbs, von Neumann, Bekenstein–Hawking, and Wiener entropies are five readings of that one measure (Theorem 6.1). The question "which entropy" therefore has one answer before the Clausius relation is written.

The criticism, verbatim. Carroll and Remmen [192], abstract: "We investigate theories in which gravity arises as a consequence of entropy. We distinguish between two approaches to this idea: holographic gravity, in which Einstein's equation arises from keeping entropy stationary in equilibrium under variations of the geometry and quantum state of a small region, and thermodynamic gravity, in which Einstein's equation emerges as a local equation of state from constraints on the area of a dynamical lightsheet in a fixed spacetime background. Examining holographic gravity, we argue that its underlying assumptions can be justified in part using recent results on the form of the modular energy in quantum field theory. For thermodynamic gravity, on the other hand, we find that it is difficult to formulate a self-consistent definition of the entropy, which represents an obstacle for this approach." Section 3.1: "But if we were simply to assume ηδA = δQ/T from the start, that would be tantamount to assuming Einstein's equation." Section 3.3: "We are forced to conclude that the entropy in thermodynamic gravity cannot be the vacuum-subtracted von Neumann (i.e., Casini) entropy of the lightsheet segment ℋ."

The criteria stated. (a) A self-consistent definition of the entropy S whose variation Jacobson equates with ηδA. (b) A derivation of ηδA = δQ/T that does not assume it. (c) An entropy that is neither the von Neumann entropy on a spacelike surface (subextensive where the energy flux is extensive) nor the vacuum-subtracted Casini entropy of the null segment.

The McGucken Principle reading. (a) Theorem 6.1, the McGucken Entropy Identity of [3], reproduced in full in §6: "the entropy formulas appearing in five apparently distinct empirical sectors of physics are five readings of one underlying quantity: the McGucken-Sphere Haar-measure entropy S_McG on the spatial-projection two-sphere W(t), under the Compton-coupling matter-interaction mechanism." The entropy in the Clausius relation is reading (4), the Bekenstein–Hawking count, and reading (3), the von Neumann entropy of the state across the horizon, is the same quantity; the definition is the Haar measure, forced by the spherical symmetry of the expansion of the McGucken Sphere and Haar's uniqueness theorem (Theorem 7 of [3], cited inside the Theorem 6.1 block). (b) Corollary 10.2(i): "δS_ent = βδ⟨K_boost⟩ with β = 2πc k_B/ħκ — Jacobson's Clausius relation δQ = T δS", derived from the first-order vanishing of the Araki–Uhlmann relative entropy at the KMS vacuum with the Bisognano–Wichmann modular Hamiltonian (Theorem 10.1), with the coefficient η = k_B/4ℓ_P² supplied by Theorem 3.5, where ℓ_P is the horizon-tier wavelength of the advance. The relation ηδA = δQ/T is a theorem of the McGucken Sphere, so the Einstein equation that Theorem 4.7 obtains from it is not assumed. (c) The entropy of (a) is a measure on the spatial two-sphere W(t) of the McGucken Sphere at coordinate time t — the cross-section of the expanding wavefront — and its additivity across the horizon is the additivity of cells generated by the one rate dx₄/dt = ic (Lemma 6bis.1, Theorem 6bis.3); the subextensivity Carroll and Remmen find for a spacelike von Neumann entropy does not arise for the cell count, because the count is set by the advance and read on the horizon, where Proposition 10.3 gives S_ent = k_BA/4ℓ_P² with the physical G. Carroll and Remmen's positive finding for holographic gravity — that the modular energy justifies the first-law step — is the same Bisognano–Wichmann modular structure that Corollary 10.2 uses, read here as a consequence of the McGucken Sphere-cogenerated wedge algebra of §10.

10bis.2 Eling, Guedens and Jacobson 2006: the equilibrium assumption of the 1995 derivation

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic derives the Einstein–Hilbert action in the Algebraic Channel and the Clausius relation in the Geometric Channel (Theorem 19.4 of [3], reproduced in §4.9), so the equilibrium case S = k_BA/4ℓ_P² that Jacobson's 1995 derivation requires is the case the Principle produces.

The criticism, verbatim. Eling, Guedens and Jacobson [193], abstract (Jacobson's own statement of the 1995 derivation's scope): "It has previously been shown that the Einstein equation can be derived from the requirement that the Clausius relation dS = dQ/T hold for all local acceleration horizons through each spacetime point, where dS is one quarter the horizon area change in Planck units, and dQ and T are the energy flux across the horizon and Unruh temperature seen by an accelerating observer just inside the horizon. Here we show that a curvature correction to the entropy that is polynomial in the Ricci scalar requires a non-equilibrium treatment. The corresponding field equation is derived from the entropy balance relation dS = dQ/T + dS_i, where dS_i is a bulk viscosity entropy production term that we determine by imposing energy-momentum conservation. Entropy production can also be included in pure Einstein theory by allowing for shear viscosity of the horizon."

The criteria stated. (a) The 1995 derivation holds with S one quarter of the area and the Clausius relation in equilibrium form. (b) Any entropy polynomial in the Ricci scalar — the f(R) family — requires an entropy-production term dS_i fixed by hand through energy-momentum conservation.

The McGucken Principle reading. (a) The area law with coefficient one quarter is Theorem 3.5 (Theorem 19.6.1 of [6], Theorem 12 of [4]), with ℓ_P the McGucken Sphere's wavelength at the horizon tier; the Unruh temperature is Theorem 4.6 (Theorem 13 of [4]); the equilibrium is the KMS condition of Theorem 10.1 on the McGucken Sphere-cogenerated wedge. The three inputs of the 1995 derivation are the three theorems. (b) Theorem 19.4 of [3]: the Einstein field equations "admit two derivations from dx₄/dt = ic that share no intermediate machinery", the Hilbert variational derivation from the Einstein–Hilbert action and the Clausius derivation; the action is Einstein–Hilbert because the McGucken Sphere's metric is the squared rate of §2.1 and its curvature invariants enter through Theorem 4.7 at first order. An f(R) entropy is a departure from the action the Principle derives, and the entropy-production term Eling, Guedens and Jacobson must add is the bookkeeping of that departure; with the derived action, dS_i = 0 and the 1995 equilibrium derivation is exact. The shear-viscosity production in pure Einstein theory is the σ_μνσ^μν term of the Raychaudhuri equation; in the Principle's reading the local Rindler horizon is the null cone of a distant McGucken Sphere, whose generators have exactly zero shear by the spherical symmetry of the expansion of the McGucken Sphere (§7.0, item on the local Rindler horizon), and Theorem 4.7 Step 3 integrates the Raychaudhuri equation at leading order about θ(0) = σ(0) = 0, so no entropy-production term enters the Clausius relation of Corollary 10.2.

10bis.3 Casini, Galante and Myers 2016: the entanglement-equilibrium input of Jacobson 2016

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic states that the McGucken Sphere's volume defines a nonlocality: the entanglement across a small ball is a property of the expanding McGucken Sphere whose volume the ball is, so what Jacobson 2016 hypothesizes about the vacuum ball's entanglement the Principle states as a property of the expansion of the McGucken Sphere (Theorem 19.4.2 of [3], reproduced in §4.9).

The criticism, verbatim. Casini, Galante and Myers [194], abstract: "Using holographic calculations, we examine a key assumption made in Jacobson's recent argument for deriving Einstein's equations from vacuum entanglement entropy. Our results involving relevant operators with low conformal dimensions seem to conflict with Jacobson's assumption. However, we discuss ways to circumvent this problem." Body: "However, let us emphasize that the contribution proportional to R²Δ δ⟨O_Δ⟩² in eq. (1.7) goes beyond the first law variation (1.2) which was central to Jacobson's reasoning." And: "δ⟨O_Δ⟩² is also guaranteed to be positive at a conformal fixed point and so the new contribution in eq. (3.11) would resemble to a negative energy density."

The criteria stated. (a) The entanglement first law δS = δ⟨K⟩ is the variation Jacobson's 2016 argument uses; for non-conformal matter with relevant operators of dimension (d-2)/2 < Δ< d/2 an additional term appears that is not of first-law form. (b) The additional term carries the sign of a negative energy density. (c) The maximal-vacuum-entanglement hypothesis is accepted by the critics as a postulate.

The McGucken Principle reading. (a) The first law of entanglement in the Principle is Corollary 10.2(i), derived for any normal state on the McGucken Sphere-cogenerated wedge algebra from the first-order vanishing of the relative entropy; its matter side is the boost energy flux ∫T_μνχ^μdΣ^ν of Theorem 4.7 Step 1, which is the full stress tensor of whatever Compton-coupled fields are present (Theorem 3.1, Theorem 4 of [3]), conformal or not. The term Casini, Galante and Myers find is second order in the deformation δ⟨O_Δ⟩; the Clausius relation of Corollary 10.2 is the first-order statement, and the Einstein equation of Theorem 4.7 follows from it at first order. The scope the critics propose — "the derivation only applies to linear variations around the vacuum" — is the scope in which Theorem 4.7 is proved. (b) Positivity in the Principle is the positivity of the Araki–Uhlmann relative entropy, S(ω_φω₀)≥0, which is the +ic orientation of the expansion of the McGucken Sphere read on the wedge (Theorem 10.1); the second-order term the critics describe does not enter that first-order statement. (c) The maximal-vacuum-entanglement hypothesis is, in the Principle, Theorem 19.4.2 of [3]: the nonlocality is defined by the McGucken Sphere's volume, so the vacuum entanglement of a ball is fixed by the McGucken Sphere and is extremal because the Haar measure of Theorem 6.1 is the unique SO(3)-invariant measure — what Jacobson postulates, the spherical symmetry of dx₄/dt = ic derives.

10bis.4 Visser 2011 and Kobakhidze 2011: a conservative force and a coherent matter wave

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic derives the Einstein field equations as the Geometric-Channel output of the expansion of the McGucken Sphere (Theorem 4.7, Theorem 14 of [4]) and the action ħ as the wavelength of the same expansion (§2.3, §6.9 of [4]); gravity is therefore a theorem of the geometry and the matter wave is a phase of the same advance, so neither an entropy function on a screen nor a microstate count of the matter wave is chosen.

The criticisms, verbatim. Visser [171], abstract: "In this article I point out that if one wishes to reformulate classical Newtonian gravity in terms of an entropic force, then the fact that Newtonian gravity is described by a conservative force places significant constraints on the form of the entropy and temperature functions. … The constraints I will establish are sufficient to present real and significant problems for any reasonable variant of Verlinde's entropic gravity proposal, though for technical reasons the constraints established herein do not directly impact on either Jacobson's or Padmanabhan's versions of entropic gravity." Discussion: "If we wish to retain key parts of Verlinde's proposal (an Unruh-like temperature, and entropy related to 'holographic screens'), then one is unavoidably forced into a more general 'thermodynamic force' scenario with multiple intensive and extensive thermodynamic variables. … The relevant 'entropies' are negative, while the 'temperatures' are positive for attractive forces and negative for repulsive forces." Kobakhidze [39], abstract: "We argue that neutron interference experiments and experiments on gravitational bound states of neutron unambiguously disprove entropic origin of gravitation." Body: "Thus, Verlinde's theory fails to reproduce the observations of the first bound state of neutron"; "Thus, Verlinde's theory implies practically complete decoherence of neutron waves". The corpus statement of this objection is Theorem 19.4.4 of [3], reproduced in §8: "an entropic force in the strict Verlinde sense — a force arising from the screen's entropy-maximization tendency with no microscopic phase — would not produce a coherent quantum-mechanical phase shift in the neutron's wavefunction."

The criteria stated. (a) A single-heat-bath entropic force reproducing Newtonian gravity requires entropy and temperature functions of a constrained form; Verlinde's screens force multiple variables with negative entropies. (b) The gravitationally bound states of ultracold neutrons (Nesvizhevsky et al.) and the Colella–Overhauser–Werner phase shift [95, 170] require a coherent gravitational phase, which a microstate-counting force does not supply.

The McGucken Principle reading. (a) In the Principle there is no entropic force to constrain: the field equations are Theorem 4.7, the Newtonian limit is their weak-field limit, and the force is conservative because it is the gradient of the potential the Einstein equation determines. The one constant Verlinde postulated for his screen, 2πk_B per Compton wavelength of displacement, is Corollary 10.2(ii): "δS = 2πk_B (Mc/ħ) Δx, Verlinde's postulate (3.5) with its constant", a property of the Bisognano–Wichmann modular Hamiltonian, so the agreement Verlinde reached by postulate is reached here by theorem, and the negative entropies and multiple baths Visser requires of the screen picture are not needed, because the screen is replaced by the McGucken Sphere's horizon with the one entropy of Theorem 6.1. Visser's exemption of Jacobson's version applies to the Principle's Geometric Channel, which is Jacobson's derivation with its inputs derived (§4.7). (b) The matter wave is the Compton phase of the advance (§8.1), its action ħ set by the McGucken Sphere's wavelength (§2.3: "ħ is the action-quantum-per-cycle of the wavefront-wavelength forced by the McGucken Sphere's expansion at universal rate c"); unitary evolution is the frozen reading of the same McGucken Sphere (§6.3), so the gravitational phase in the neutron interferometer and the bound-state spectrum in the Earth's field are phases of one coherent expansion with no thermal noise to decohere them. Theorem 19.4.4 of [3] records that the Colella–Overhauser–Werner fringes "do appear, robustly, in every test" and reads them as the Geometric Channel phase of dx₄/dt = ic.

10bis.5 The dark-sector tests of Verlinde 2017: Milgrom and Sanders, Lelli, McGaugh and Schombert, Pardo, Tamosiunas et al.

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic derives the dark-sector acceleration scale as the cosmological McGucken Sphere's surface acceleration a₀ = cH₀/2π (Theorem 12.1(iii)), against Verlinde's a₀ = cH₀ with a_M = a₀/6 (§8.0bis); the tests of Verlinde 2017 are therefore tests of a construction the Principle derives with a different constant, and the published tensions are read against that constant.

The criticisms, verbatim. Milgrom and Sanders [195]: "Welcome addition to the MOND lore as it is, this approach has reproduced, so far, only a small fraction of MOND phenomenology"; "Notably, it cannot predict their rotation curves, except asymptotically"; "The formula cannot be applied to the internal dynamics of a system embedded in an external field"; "Verlinde's formula, as it now stands, strongly conflicts with solarsystem and possibly earth-surface constraints, and cannot fully account for the mass anomalies in the cores of galaxy clusters"; on the Brouwer et al. weak-lensing test [42]: "The analysis of Ref [29] is thus a reconfirmation test of MOND as well as of all the suggestions that reproduce the above two predictions of MOND, including Verlinde's." Lelli, McGaugh and Schombert [196]: "EG is consistent with the observed RAR only if we substantially decrease the fiducial stellar mass-to-light ratios"; EG "predicts that the residuals around the RAR should correlate with radius" and "such residual correlation is not observed"; "the observed dynamics of disc galaxies pose a significant challenge to EG." Pardo [41]: "In its current form, the theory only applies to isolated, spherically symmetric systems in a dark energy-dominated Universe, and thus can only be tested fairly with such systems"; "EG severely underpredicts the maximum velocities for dwarf galaxies with measured velocities greater than this value and overpredicts for those with measured velocities less than this value" (the value being about 100 km/s, in a sample of 452 isolated dwarf galaxies). Tamosiunas et al. [197]: "We find that the simultaneous EG fits of the X-ray and weak lensing datasets are significantly worse than those provided by General Relativity (with cold dark matter)"; "For the Coma cluster, the predictions from Emergent Gravity and General Relativity agree in the range of 250–700 kpc, while at around 1 Mpc scales, EG total mass predictions are larger by a factor of 2"; "for r ≳10 Mpc EG is in strong tension with the data"; "According to the Bayesian information criterion analysis, GR is preferred in all tested datasets."

The criteria stated. (a) A dark-sector formula must apply beyond isolated, static, spherically symmetric systems: to disc rotation curves, to systems in an external field, to clusters at 1–10 Mpc. (b) Where Verlinde's point-mass formula applies, its normalization is tested by the radial acceleration relation, by dwarf maximum velocities, and by cluster X-ray plus lensing masses, and in each the published fit is in tension.

The McGucken Principle reading. (a) Verlinde's formula is spherically symmetric and static because his construction takes the de Sitter horizon's entropy and distributes it as a volume law over a static bulk (§8.0bis items (1)–(3)); the Principle's construction is the cosmological McGucken Sphere expanding at c from every event, and the matter-sourced contraction of the spatial sector ψ(t,𝐱) of Theorem 12.1 is a field on the slice, defined at every point, so it applies to a disc, to an embedded system, and to a cluster by the same equation. The treatment of rotation curves and the Tully–Fisher scaling from that contraction is the cosmology paper [27] and its companions [31, 32]; the present paper derives the acceleration scale and the equation of state and does not re-derive those fits. (b) The constant under test differs between the two programs by the factor 2π in a₀ and by Verlinde's additional 1/6: Verlinde's a_M = cH₀/6 against the Principle's cH₀/2π, a 4.7% difference (§8.3). The Tamosiunas factor-of-two excess at 1 Mpc and the Lelli–McGaugh–Schombert mass-to-light tension are measured against Verlinde's normalization; the Principle's prediction is the same point-mass form g = g_B + √(a₀ g_B) with a₀ = cH₀/2π and the dark-energy equation of state w(z) = -1 + Ω_m(z)/6π (Theorem 12.1), which is the statement the data decide. The Principle's constant is fixed by the McGucken Sphere's geometry — the 2π from the surface, the 3 from V/A = R_H/3 — with no parameter available to move it.

11. Huygens' Principle is the Holographic Principle

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality. Every McGucken Sphere is at once a Huygens wavefront and a holographic screen.

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic supplies the physical mechanism for Huygens' principle: every point of a wavefront is the source of a new spherical secondary wavefront because every event carries its own x₄-expansion at c. Huygens (1690), Fresnel (1818), and Kirchhoff (1882) stated the construction; Hadamard characterized the dimensions in which it holds sharply; the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework differs from all of these in supplying the mechanism — x₄'s spherical expansion at c from every event — of which the construction is the description. 13. Falsifiability

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality. A physical claim must be refutable, and the claims of this paper are refutable in five ways; the first and the fifth are tests no entropic-gravity programme makes.

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic makes the following predictions, each a consequence of the shared count Ω or of the Compton coupling, and each fails under a specified measurement.

1. The zero-temperature diffusion residual. A massive particle coupled to the expansion of the McGucken Sphere retains, after environmental damping, D_x^(McG) = ε²c²Ω_mod/2γ² (§6.3), mass-independent and predicted exactly zero by standard quantum mechanics. Cold-atom and trapped-ion interferometry at fractional frequencies ∼10^-18–10^-19 bound it; a null result at a precision exceeding the prediction refutes the ontic origin of probability (§3.2) and with it the Compton-coupled walk of Theorem 3.3.

2. The Born exponent. The identity of Theorem 6bis.3 requires the invariant measure to be quadratic. A probability rule |ψ|^p with p2 at any scale — third-order interference in triple-slit experiments, for instance — would refute it; present bounds are consistent with p = 2.

3. The Bekenstein–Hawking coefficient. The horizon reading requires S = A/4ℓ_P² to be the Planck-cell count with the known logarithmic corrections; a horizon mode density that is not area-proportional refutes Theorem 3.5.

4. The common origin of the Hawking temperature and the Compton scale. The horizon temperature is a KMS periodicity (Theorem 4.6, Appendix B); the event carries the Compton energy scale mc²/k_B set by the same advance rate. If the Hawking temperature did not track the advance rate that sets ω_C, the shared-source claim would fail. The event carries the energy scale and not a horizon-type KMS periodicity: a single Compton phase continues under t→-iτ to the real exponential e^-mc²τ/ħ, not to a periodic correlator (Appendix B.2).

5. A tidal dependence of the Born measure. Because the Born count and the horizon count are one Ω, the local x₄-advance rate set by the gravitational field enters the count. A branch at potential Φ_a carries N_a→(1 + Φ_a/c²)N_a, so in p_a = N_a/∑_bN_b a common potential cancels and a first-order potential difference gives δp_a = p_a(Φ_a - ∑_bp_bΦ_b)/c² — which for a uniform field must vanish, since by the Einstein equivalence principle (GR T4 of [4]) a uniform field is an accelerated frame in flat spacetime where the Born statistics are frame-independent, the uniform-field potential difference being a difference of clock rates that changes accumulated phase and leaves the cell count of the joint McGucken Sphere invariant. The leading surviving term is the one the equivalence principle permits, second order in the branch separation L and first order in curvature:

δp_a∼p_aR₀i0jL^iL^j∼p_aGM/(c²r³)L²,

of magnitude ∼2×10^-23 for L = 1 m at the Earth's surface and ∼10^-9 for L = 1 m at r = 10 km from a neutron star of r_s = 3 km. It is distinguishable from the Colella–Overhauser–Werner phase, first order in gL, because it appears in the outcome measure, with no phase contribution, and scales as L²R. A measurement finding the Born statistics independent of the branch curvature difference to this precision refutes the identification; the two-entropy picture of the literature predicts no such dependence, and a derivation producing the first-order uniform-field term would contradict GR T4.

Appendix A. The counts Ω and N on the cross-section and on the horizon

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality. This appendix computes the counts used in §6bis.

A.1 The cross-section count. A region R⊆S² of solid angle Ω_Ω(R) = ∫_Rsinθdθdϕ subtends, at radius r = ct, an area r²Ω_Ω(R), which at cycle resolution λ_C = h/mc contains N(R) = r²Ω_Ω(R)/λ_C² cells; its SO(3)-invariant weight is ∫_Rdμ = Ω_Ω(R)/4π. Invariance: sinθdθdϕ is the pullback of the rotation-invariant round area form. Uniqueness: an invariant positive normalized functional on C(S²) is unique by the Riesz representation theorem.

A.2 The Born probability from the count. For an outcome direction φ along n̂_φ and a state ψ whose Bloch direction n̂_ψ makes polar angle θ with n̂_φ, the outcome region is the zone R_φ = {n̂: n̂·n̂_φ≥-cosθ}. By Archimedes' hat-box theorem the invariant measure of a zone is proportional to its height, so ∫_R_φdμ = (1 + cosθ)/2 = cos²(θ/2), the Malus projection; hence p(φ|ψ) = N(R_φ)/N(S²) = cos²(θ/2) = |⟨φ|ψ⟩|², with λ_C and r cancelling. The identification of the McGucken Sphere's cross-section with the projective state space is the Fubini–Study = Fisher–Rao identity of Wootters [29] and Braunstein–Caves [30], on which the Born exponent is the unique map making metric distance equal statistical distinguishability [14, App. B].

A.3 The horizon count. Tiling the local Rindler horizon H by Planck-scale McGucken Spheres, one per ℓ_P² = ħG/c³, gives N(H) = A(H)/ℓ_P² cells; each carries one boundary mode and one quarter nat, so Ω(H) = e^N/4 and S_H = k_BlnΩ = k_BN/4 = k_BA/4ℓ_P², the coefficient fixed as in Theorem 3.5.

A.3bis Area scaling versus volume scaling. The gravitational count and the Born count are counts over a bounding surface (area-scaling, holographic); the Second-Law count is the growth of phase-space volume by the expansion of the McGucken Sphere. Both are counts of the single Ω; the surface readings give Theorem 6bis.3, the volume reading gives Theorem 3.3. Holding the spatial volume fixed in an entropy extremization (Jacobson's "striking" condition, §7.2 (h)) fixes the region over which the Sphere's isotropic advance is counted, and the volume-fixed count equals the horizon-area count of the same Sphere because the Sphere's area and enclosed volume are functions of its one radius r = ct.

A.4 One measure, two surfaces. On S² the measure is dμ per cell; on H the density is 1/ℓ_P² per unit area, uniform because SO(3)-invariance of the generating law forbids a direction-dependent density. Both are the invariant advance-state measure restricted to a surface of the null cone; this is Theorem 6bis.3.

The Identification in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Framework

on the McGucken manifold corresponds, in the operator-algebraic formalism on the Lorentzian-signature side, to the KMS condition (10.1) for canonical thermal equilibrium at temperature T = 1/(k_B β). Appendix D. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Reading of the Rate, the Share, and the Accumulated Advance: Why Nothing of Relativity Is Lost

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality. Three quantities carry the word "rate" in the body of this paper and in the literature it reads, and they are distinct. This appendix separates them, states which identities belong to which, and works the standard relativistic cases so that the horizon statements of §§3–4 and §§7–9 — the null generators of the Sphere as photon worldlines, the redshifted local temperature, the extinguished share at r_s — are read correctly.

D.1 The three readings

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic is a statement in coordinate time t about the whole manifold: at every event the fourth dimension advances at c. Every other "rate" in this appendix is a projection of that one advance onto a worldline or a foliation.

(R1) The coordinate rate. dx₄/dt = ic. Invariant: the same at every event, in every frame (Lemma 7.4.1), in every gravitational field (Theorem 7.1 of [19], quoted in the proof of Theorem 4.1): ∂(dx₄/dt)/∂g_μν = 0. This is the Principle.

(R2) The share. For a worldline of coordinate speed v the fraction of the advance that the worldline's own clock registers per unit coordinate time is v_x₄ ≡c dτ/dt = c√(1 - v²/c²) = c/γ, and the McGucken Sphere partition is v² + v_x₄² = c²: bounded, with locus a quarter-circle. At spatial rest v_x₄ = c; for the photon v_x₄ = 0. Plus-sign identities belong to (R2).

(R3) The per-proper-time component. dx₄/dτ = ic dt/dτ = icγ, unbounded, with the Lorentzian norm u^μu_μ = |dx₄/dτ|² - |dx⃗/dτ|² = -c² (Theorem 3.1 Step 1; Theorem 5.5 of [19]). Minus-sign identities belong to (R3). In the instantaneous rest frame dτ = dt and dx₄/dτ = ic locally — the reverse-reading equivalence of Lemma 4.7 of [5], a consequence of (R1), never its statement.

The Principle is (R1). (R2) and (R3) are two bookkeepings of how a given worldline participates in it. The accumulated advance on a worldline is X₄ = ∫ic dτ, advancing at the real magnitude v_x₄ per unit coordinate time; the coordinate accumulation Δx₄ = ic Δt is path-independent.

D.2 The author's appendix, reproduced

McGucken Principle anchor. dx₄/dt = ic is reading (R1) of §D.1, the invariant coordinate rate; the author's appendix below separates it from the share v_x₄ and the accumulated advance X₄ and works the standard relativistic cases on that separation.

The following is reproduced verbatim from Appendix A, §§A.3.2–A.5.5, of the Physics of Time paper [115] (verified-read; its anchors — Theorem 28.2 of §38a.2, Theorem 6.4a of §10.6a, Theorem 39 of §50, §51 — are that paper's), with its anchor table (§A.6) rewritten for the present paper in §D.3 below.

A.3.2 What does "the x₄-rate at the horizon" mean? The rate is gravity-rigid: ∂(dx₄/dt)/∂g_μν = 0. The rate dx₄/dt = ic takes the same value near the horizon as at infinity. What varies with potential is the share: v_x₄(r) = c dτ/dt = c√(1 - r_s/r) (static Schwarzschild observer), vanishing at r = r_s. On the infaller's own clock dτ = dt locally and the reverse-reading equivalence applies: the local rate is the full ic throughout. Gravitational time dilation is the coordinate-frame projection of a locally invariant rate.

A.3.3 Which identity is "c² through spacetime"? Sphere partition (per coordinate time, all worldlines): v² + v_x₄² = c², bounded, locus a quarter-circle. Lorentzian four-velocity norm (per proper time, massive worldlines): u^μu_μ = |dx₄/dτ|² - |d𝐱/dτ|² = -c², unbounded in each term, signature difference fixing the invariant. The Euclidean per-proper-time sum |dx₄/dτ|² + |d𝐱/dτ|² equals c² only in the instantaneous rest frame; elsewhere c²γ². Plus-sign identities belong to (R2); minus-sign identities to (R3).

A.3.4 How does the twin paradox read? Coordinate accumulation is path-independent: both twins accumulate Δx₄ = ic Δt. Differential ageing is read from X₄ = ∫ic dτ, advancing at real magnitude v_x₄ per unit coordinate time. On the traveling leg v_x₄ < c, so the traveler accumulates less X₄, so less proper time. The stay-at-home twin retains v_x₄ = c and accumulates the maximal X₄. The CTC question closes the same way: ∮dx₄ = 0 identically, so a CTC cannot run on the coordinate; the impossibility lives in X₄.

Once the three identifications are in place, the four-velocity-budget structure — which is the actual geometry of special relativity — becomes invisible to every local experiment. 16.15.0 The Wightman 1956 axiomatic system

The Wightman 1956 axiomatic system was the systematic axiomatization of relativistic quantum field theory, with six axioms intended to produce a minimal sufficient set of postulates:

-   W1 (Hilbert space): the system’s states form a separable complex Hilbert space ℋ.
-   W2 (Poincaré covariance): the Poincaré group ISO^+(1,3) acts unitarily on Hilbert space ℋ via a strongly continuous representation U(a, Λ).
-   W3 (Locality / microcausality): field operators at spacelike-separated points commute (or anticommute, for fermions).
-   W4 (Field operator domain): the field operators ϕ̂(x) are operator-valued distributions on a dense domain 𝒟 ⊂ℋ.
-   W5 (Vacuum existence and uniqueness): there exists a unique Poincaré-invariant state |0⟩∈ℋ.
-   W6 (Spectrum Condition): the joint spectrum of the energy-momentum operators P^μ = (H, 𝐏) is contained in the closed forward light cone: Spec(P^μ) ⊂V_+.

For 68 years (1956–2026) these six axioms have served as the canonical foundation for axiomatic QFT, constructive QFT, and the algebraic-QFT lineage that descends from them (Streater-Wightman 1964 “PCT, Spin and Statistics, and All That”, Haag 1992 “Local Quantum Physics”).

Two features of the axioms are essential to the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework’s identification:

(i) Axioms W1–W5 are sign-blind on +ic (i.e., invariant under the +ic ↔-ic involution). Each axiom is symmetric under time reversal at the algebraic level: the Hilbert-space structure is unchanged; Poincaré covariance preserves form (with appropriate sign-flip on time-translations); microcausality is spacelike-symmetric; the operator domain is sign-blind; the vacuum’s Poincaré invariance is direction-symmetric.

(ii) Axiom W6 is explicitly T-anti-invariant. The Spectrum Condition selects the forward light cone in momentum space, excluding the backward cone. The Hamiltonian H = P⁰ has spectrum Spec(H) ⊂[0, ∞), selecting positive-energy states and excluding negative-energy states. The +ic ↔-ic involution would flip V_+ ↔V_- and select negative-energy states instead, but the Spectrum Condition forbids this.

Wightman 1956 had to impose W6 as an independent axiom; W6 cannot be derived from W1–W5 alone. Streater-Wightman 1964, Haag 1992, and the comprehensive surveys of constructive QFT and algebraic QFT all confirm this fact: the Spectrum Condition stands as an independent axiom of axiomatic QFT, seventy years after Wightman’s original formulation.

In the seven subsections that follow we establish that all six Wightman axioms — including W6 — are forced theorems of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic via the cogeneration cascade ℳ_G →𝕄₁,3 →𝒱 →ℋ developed in §§2–6 of the present paper. None of the six is an independent input; all six descend from the single principle. The axiomatic apparatus of 1956 is, in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, the algebraic encoding of the cogeneration cascade’s output at the field-theoretic level.

16.15.1 Derivation of W1 (Hilbert space) from McGucken machinery

Theorem 16.15.1 (W1 as McGucken cascade theorem). The Wightman axiom W1 — that the system’s states form a separable complex Hilbert space ℋ — is a forced theorem of dx₄/dt = ic via the cogeneration cascade.

Proof. The cascade ℳ_G →𝕄₁,3 →𝒱 →ℋ of Theorem 6.1 produces the Hilbert space ℋ as the L²-Cauchy completion of the McGucken wavefunction space 𝒱. The wavefunction space 𝒱 is constructed in Definition 2.6 as the space of complex-valued projections of x₄-advance onto the spatial slice ℝ³ at parameter time t.

The four features of W1 — Hilbert structure, complex character, separability, and completeness — descend as follows.

(i) Hilbert structure. By Lemma 7.1, the rank-2 sesquilinear inner product on 𝒱 is induced by the rank-2 character of the Lorentzian metric g_μν (Lemma 2.5: (ict)² = -c² t² produces the signature). The pairing ⟨φ, ψ⟩ = ∫_ℝ³ φ^(𝐱) ψ(𝐱) d³x is sesquilinear in (φ, ψ) by the rank-2 character of g_μν transferred to amplitude representation. This pairing is positive-definite by Theorem 7.4 (the diagonal ⟨ψ, ψ⟩ = ∫|ψ|² d³x is the Born density’s normalization integral, non-negative by R2 of §7.3).

(ii) Complex character. By Theorem 3.1, the wavefunction ψ∈𝒱 is complex-valued because the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic carries the imaginary unit i as the algebraic marker for x₄-perpendicularity. The selection of ℂ from {ℝ, ℂ, ℍ} is forced by the Frobenius theorem applied to the substitution x₄ = ict in the four-dimensional Euclidean line element: the algebra of complex numbers is the unique two-dimensional commutative real division algebra capable of accommodating i² = -1 with the perpendicularity structure of x₄ relative to the spatial slice. Quaternions ℍ fail by non-commutativity (the x₄-direction is a single perpendicular, not three); real numbers ℝ fail by absence of i² = -1.

(iii) Separability. The spatial slice ℝ³ is a separable metric space (the rational points ℚ³ are countable and dense). The L²-completion of 𝒱 with measure d³x on ℝ³ is therefore separable: ℋ ≅L²(ℝ³, d³x). For the relativistic case, by §10.6.8, the one-particle Hilbert space ℋ_m,0 = L²(H_m, dμ_m) where H_m = {p^μ: p^μp_μ = -m² c², p⁰ > 0} is the positive-mass-shell hyperboloid (a separable 3-manifold) with Lorentz-invariant measure dμ_m = d³p / (2 E_p); again separable.

(iv) Completeness. The L²-Cauchy completion construction is precisely the operation that produces a complete normed space from a pre-Hilbert space. By Lemma 7.6 (parallelogram identity as direct algebraic consequence of rank-2 sesquilinearity), the L² norm on 𝒱 satisfies x + y² + x - y² = 2(x² + y²), so the Cauchy completion is a Hilbert space rather than merely a Banach space. 16.15.2 Derivation of W2 (Poincaré covariance) from McGucken machinery

Theorem 16.15.2 (W2 as McGucken cascade theorem). The Wightman axiom W2 — that the Poincaré group ISO^+(1,3) acts unitarily on Hilbert space ℋ via a strongly continuous representation U(a, Λ) — is a forced theorem of dx₄/dt = ic via the cogeneration cascade.

Proof. The Poincaré group ISO^+(1,3) is the symmetry group of the Lorentzian metric η_μν on Minkowski Space 𝕄₁,3, consisting of spacetime translations T_a: x ↦x + a (for a ∈𝕄₁,3) and proper orthochronous Lorentz transformations Λ∈SO^+(1,3) preserving η. By Lemma 2.5 of the present paper, η is the integrated coordinate shadow of dx₄/dt = ic. The Poincaré group is therefore the symmetry group of the constraint surface 𝒞_M where dx₄/dt = ic holds locally.

Three features of W2 — that the Poincaré group acts on Hilbert space ℋ, that the action is unitary, and that the representation is strongly continuous — descend as follows.

(i) Group action on Hilbert space ℋ. By Theorem 10.6, Hilbert space ℋ is the function-valued representation of Minkowski Space 𝕄₁,3 (the same geometric object at the function-space cascade level). Spacetime symmetries of Minkowski Space 𝕄₁,3 therefore extend canonically to symmetries of Hilbert space ℋ via the L²-functional construction: for Poincaré element (a, Λ) and wavefunction ψ∈ℋ, define

[U(a, Λ) ψ](x) : = ψ(Λ^-1(x - a)).

This is the standard induced-representation construction; in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework it is forced by the manifold-level / function-space-level identification of Theorem 10.6.

(ii) Unitarity. Lorentz transformations preserve the Lorentzian inner product on Minkowski Space 𝕄₁,3: η(Λu, Λv) = η(u, v) for all u, v and all Λ∈SO^+(1,3). Translations preserve η (the metric is translation-invariant in flat Minkowski Space 𝕄₁,3). The L²-functional construction transfers this to the Hilbert-space inner product. For the spatial-slice integration:

⟨U(a, Λ) φ, U(a, Λ) ψ⟩ = ∫_ℝ³ φ^(Λ^-1(x - a)) ψ(Λ^-1(x - a)) d³x.

By the change of variables y = Λ^-1(x - a) with Jacobian |Λ| = 1 for proper orthochronous Λ∈SO^+(1,3), this equals ∫_ℝ³ φ^(y) ψ(y) d³y = ⟨φ, ψ⟩. Therefore U(a, Λ) is unitary on Hilbert space ℋ.

(iii) Strong continuity. The Poincaré group is a Lie group; its identity component ISO^+(1,3) is connected and locally Euclidean of dimension 10. The map (a, Λ) ↦U(a, Λ) ψ is continuous in the L²-norm topology by the standard regularity of the induced-representation construction on L² spaces: for ψ∈L²(ℝ³), the translation action ψ↦ψ(·- a) is L²-continuous in a (a standard real-analysis fact, provable by density of C_c^∞(ℝ³) in L²(ℝ³) plus uniform continuity of compactly supported smooth functions), and the Lorentz action ψ↦ψ(Λ^-1 ·) is similarly L²-continuous in Λ by the same density argument plus smoothness of the Lorentz action on ℝ³. Composition gives strong continuity in (a, Λ).

16.15.3 Derivation of W3 (locality / microcausality) from McGucken machinery

Theorem 16.15.3 (W3 as McGucken cascade theorem). The Wightman axiom W3 — that field operators at spacelike-separated points commute (for bosonic statistics) or anticommute (for fermionic statistics) — is a forced theorem of dx₄/dt = ic via the cogeneration cascade.

Proof. W3 expresses sense-1 locality (local-Lagrangian operator locality), distinct from sense-2 nonlocality (Bell-violation correlation locality). The §1.1bis.4 framing of the present paper makes the distinction explicit: the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework derives both senses from the same active-Sphere geometric primitive, with sense-1 locality realized at the operator-algebra level (W3) and sense-2 nonlocality realized at the correlation level via Theorem 6.6.8.1.

Consider two spacetime events p, q ∈𝕄₁,3 with spacelike separation: η(p - q, p - q) > 0 (mostly-plus signature; spacelike separations carry positive squared interval). By Definition 2.3, each event generates its own McGucken Sphere:

ℳ_p(t) = {r ∈𝕄₁,3 : ds²(p, r) = 0, x₄(r) - x₄(p) = ic (t - t_p)},

ℳ_q(t) = {r ∈𝕄₁,3 : ds²(q, r) = 0, x₄(r) - x₄(q) = ic (t - t_q)}.

Claim: For spacelike-separated p, q at the same parameter time t_p = t_q = t₀, the spatial-slice intersection ℳ_p(t₀ + δ) ∩ℳ_q(t₀ + δ) ∩Σ_t₀ is empty for all sufficiently small δ> 0.

Proof of claim. At parameter time t₀ + δ, the Sphere ℳ_p(t₀ + δ) has spatial-slice trace consisting of points 𝐫 at spatial-slice distance c δ from 𝐩: the spatial Sphere S²_𝐩(cδ) = {𝐫 : |𝐫 - 𝐩| = cδ}. Similarly ℳ_q(t₀ + δ) has spatial-slice trace S²_𝐪(cδ). By spacelike separation of p and q, |𝐩 - 𝐪| > 0 at parameter time t₀. For δ< |𝐩 - 𝐪| / (2c), the two spatial Spheres S²_𝐩(cδ) and S²_𝐪(cδ) are disjoint: any point on S²_𝐩(cδ) has distance at most |𝐩 - 𝐪| + cδ< |𝐩 - 𝐪| + |𝐩 - 𝐪|/2 = 3|𝐩 - 𝐪|/2 from 𝐪 and at least |𝐩 - 𝐪| - cδ> |𝐩 - 𝐪|/2 from 𝐪, so it lies neither on S²_𝐪(cδ) (which has radius cδ< |𝐩 - 𝐪|/2). The two Spheres’ spatial-slice traces are therefore disjoint for parameter-time intervals shorter than the spacelike-separation time scale. □

From disjoint Sphere traces to operator commutation. Field operators ϕ̂(p), ϕ̂(q) at spacelike-separated p, q ∈𝕄₁,3 act on the Hilbert space ℋ = L²(ℝ³) (or its relativistic Wightman variant L²(H_m, dμ_m) of §10.6.8) via the wavefront of the respective Spheres ℳ_p and ℳ_q. By the Sphere-disjointness claim above, the wavefront of ℳ_p at any spatial-slice point 𝐫 is independent of the wavefront of ℳ_q at the same 𝐫 for parameter-time intervals shorter than the spacelike-separation time scale: each Sphere’s wavefront extension into the future light cone of its apex is unaffected by the other Sphere’s wavefront extension into its own (disjoint) future light cone.

The content of the algebraic commutator:

[ϕ̂(p), ϕ̂(q)] |ψ⟩ = ϕ̂(p) ϕ̂(q) |ψ⟩- ϕ̂(q) ϕ̂(p) |ψ⟩

for spacelike-separated p, q vanishes because the two operators act on disjoint Sphere wavefront at the spatial-slice level. The order of application is irrelevant: applying ϕ̂(p) first modifies the wavefront at ℳ_p, then applying ϕ̂(q) modifies the disjoint wavefront at ℳ_q, with the two modifications commuting because they target non-overlapping cascade content of Hilbert space ℋ.

16.15.4 Derivation of W4 (field operator domain) from McGucken machinery

(iii) Dense domain.
